# Leader barks: what each civilization says to each other

The port's own lines, not FFH2's: for every ordered pair of civilizations, what the speaker's
leader (an AI) says to the listener's (the human) at eleven diplomacy moments, three lines each
(21 civilizations, 420 pairs, 13,860 lines). In a game, a leader picks among these and FFH2's own
lines for that moment (`crates/ffh-play/src/view/speech.rs`); a game started with "Vanilla
experience" uses FFH2's alone.

The moments: **First contact** (they meet), **Declares war** (the speaker declares war),
**Refuses to talk** (at war, it will not negotiate yet), **Greeting (friendly)** and **Greeting
(hostile)** (you contact it; cautious to friendly, or annoyed to furious), **Accepts a deal**,
**Thanks for a gift**, **Turns down a deal**, **Agrees to peace**, **Refuses peace** and
**Rejects a demand** (you asked for something for nothing).

Format, read by the game: `### Speaker → Listener` sections (civilizations by their short
names), `#### Moment` headings as above, one line per `- ` bullet. `[CT_NAME]` is the listener's
leader's name, `[OUR_NAME]` the speaker's. A line fits any leader of either civilization: it
names neither and calls neither he or she.

## Amurites

### Amurites → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- So the Tower of Eyes did not hold. Our father built it for the one pupil he could neither cure nor kill, and we have read the inventories.
- The Children of Kylorin greet the circus. Keep your puppets on their strings and your fingers out of our thoughts, and we shall get along.
- Half your court once studied under our father, and the other half wears masks. Which half am I addressing?

#### Declares war
- Kylorin showed your court mercy once, in a sunken tower in the swamp. The faculty has voted not to repeat the error.
- Your puppets dance on threads of mind magic. Our adepts have spent a generation learning how threads are cut.
- The masquerade is over. Every Harlequin you send across the border will end up pinned and labelled in our lecture halls.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with minds that wear other minds. Your last envoy did not seem entirely himself.
- Your herald recited a riddle, wept, and then laughed. We have filed all three under evidence. No talks.
- Come back when the laughter stops. We do not expect to see you again.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. My wards are up, naturally, but do come in. What is the game today?
- Our masters of the mind would dearly love an hour with one of your Puppets. Purely for study, you understand.
- Two schools that sprang from the same master should not quarrel forever. Speak, and do let me finish my own sentences.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Something was rummaging in my thoughts just now. Was that you, or one of your many tenants?
- Your Taskmasters dragged Amurite students across the border in chains. Speak quickly; my patience is a very short spell.
- If this is another jest, I warn you the punchline will be a fireball.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Our scribes checked the seals three times for illusions, and they appear to be real.
- A fair exchange, oddly enough. Do not let it ruin your reputation.
- Done. We will keep two copies, in case the ink on one of them starts laughing.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Jubilee with no strings attached? We will search it for strings anyway, but thank you.
- Curious. Generous, even. The faculty will debate your motives for a decade.
- Our thanks. It will sit inside a warding circle until we are sure it does not bite.

#### Turns down a deal
- Your terms change every time I look away from the page. No.
- We do not sign anything drafted by a court that argues with itself in rhyme.
- Too clever by half, and the other half is mad. We decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well, the game is over. Pack up your Freaks and your wagons and go home.
- Peace, then. Kylorin would not have wanted his heirs and his pupils burning each other's libraries.
- We accept. May your court find a cheaper amusement than our border towns.

#### Refuses peace
- You offer peace with a smile painted on. We will wait until we see the face beneath it.
- No. Your Mimics have stolen enough of our training already, and we mean to take it back from their corpses.
- Our father left your founder alive in a cell, and see where that led. We would rather finish the work.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the jesters? Our archmages would die of embarrassment.
- You want our tomes for nothing. Here is a jest in return: no.
- The answer is no, and it does not rhyme, so you cannot mistake it for anything else.

### Amurites → Bannor

#### First contact
- So you are the Bannor. Your priests have written about us at length; we have read every page and corrected the grammar.
- The Children of Kylorin greet the soldiers of Junil. We study every kind of power. Yours, we are told, is obedience.
- We are scholars, not heretics, whatever your confessors say. Keep the crusade away from our schools and we will be good neighbours.

#### Declares war
- Your priesthood has finally added us to its list of the damned. Let us see how the Order's steel fares against the arcane.
- You wanted to teach us repentance. We will teach you what a fireball does to a shield wall.
- Every Bannor farm is a little castle, they say. Our siege-mages have been eager for the practice.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your envoy came with a confessor and a list of our sins. We kept the list and sent back the envoy. That will do.
- We will not debate theology with a battle line.
- Talk? Your heralds only preach, and we have lecturers enough of our own.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. We have been considering a show of support for the Order, should the Veil come for us both.
- Ah, the Bannor: disciplined, punctual, never late to an audience. How refreshing, after a week among my colleagues.
- Speak freely. Our adepts can sanctify a tainted field as well as any priest of Junil, and we would rather do it alongside you.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- If your confessors have come to inspect our necromancy licences again, they may wait outside in the rain.
- Your priests damn us because we regulate the dark arts instead of burning everyone who studies them. Say what you came to say.
- You march like a sermon and you speak like one. Be brief.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your Law is tiresome, but your contracts are dependable.
- Done. No one has ever accused the Bannor of reading a treaty loosely.
- A sound exchange. Record it in your codex, and we will record it in ours.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, with no sermon attached? You surprise me. Thank you.
- Our thanks. Tell your priests the godless mages were grateful; it will confuse them for weeks.
- Generous. Perhaps there is room for scholars in Junil's world after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- We do not trade our tomes to people who keep a list of books to burn.
- This offer comes with conditions on which schools of magic we may teach. No.
- The Order can buy obedience. It cannot buy research. We decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go back to watching for the end of the world, and we will go back to studying how it might work.
- We accept. Our siege-mages are weary of wet camps, and your fortress farms are tedious to burn.
- Very well. Let the confessors and the archmages argue in letters again, instead of in fire.

#### Refuses peace
- You came to cleanse us. We are not finished teaching you otherwise.
- A peace while your Crusade still marches? Your priests would call it a truce until the next sermon.
- No. When your Crusaders stop singing hymns over our burned schools, we may listen.

#### Rejects a demand
- A tithe for Junil? We tithe to curiosity, and the collection plate is closed.
- You have every right to ask, and we every right to laugh. We are laughing.
- Our gold builds universities, not penance. No.

### Amurites → Calabim

#### First contact
- Vampires who farm men. Fascinating, from a strictly academic distance. Kindly keep it a great distance.
- We have read about your Dark Gift. Our laws against prolonging life past its natural span would hang most of your nobility.
- Greetings, children of the Grand Broods. You will find our people well warded, and our blood far too full of magic to agree with you.

#### Declares war
- Our law on sustaining life past nature is merciless and spectacular, and your entire court is in breach of it.
- We have practised necromancy under strict licence for generations. You have never once filed the paperwork.
- The herds in your cities will be freed, and your nobility catalogued, pinned and labelled for our students.

#### Refuses to talk
- One of your envoys bit a junior archivist. There will be no more envoys.
- You want words. Our wards want your kind kept on your own side of the river. The wards win.
- The faculty has voted not to receive the undead today, or any other day.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Come in, [CT_NAME], but leave your thirst at the door. Our students are not refreshments.
- I confess a professional curiosity about how you persist. Not enough to volunteer, mind.
- Speak. We study every branch of magic, even the ones that drink.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Broods have been hunting on our side of the border. Explain yourself, and quickly.
- I can smell the cellar on you from here. What do you want?
- You are an unlicensed experiment in eternal life, and I sit on the licensing board. Talk.

#### Accepts a deal
- Acceptable. Payment in gold, please, not in anything that once had a pulse.
- Agreed. We will not ask how your goods were produced, or by whom.
- Done. A fair trade between those who study immortality and those who stole it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- How unexpected. We are honoured, and we are also counting our students.
- Thank you. Generosity is a surprise from people who keep men as cattle.
- Our thanks. We will examine it for curses and then, very probably, keep it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would pay us in bloodpets, and we keep no pets.
- Your offer is anaemic, if you will forgive the term.
- We decline. Some knowledge is regulated for a reason, and your court is that reason.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your herds, and keep them grazing on your own pastures.
- We accept. May your nights be long, and spent very far from ours.
- Very well. A truce between the living and the undying, until one of us reconsiders.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every night we wait, another village is drained to keep your nobles young.
- Your peace is a feeding schedule with a ribbon tied around it.
- Not yet. Our necromancers have only just been granted permission to practise on you.

#### Rejects a demand
- You ask for tribute as if we were one of your cattle towns. We are not.
- No. You have taken enough from the living already.
- Our answer is a ward, and it does not open for your kind.

### Amurites → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs who remember Bhall. Our father borrowed her fire to cleanse Patria, once. You are what was left in the hearth.
- The Clan of Embers. You worship fire, they tell me. So do we, in the hands of trained adepts.
- Keep your raiders away from our schools and we may even buy some of that fire mana you sit on.

#### Declares war
- Fire was always our father's favourite tool. Let us show you what an Amurite does with your fallen goddess's gift.
- Braduk burned once without any help from us. Your camps will burn now with it.
- Your warbands are gathering on the old roads toward our cities. The schools close; the siege-mages open.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not negotiate with axes.
- Your envoy could not read the treaty, and I suspect the one who sent him could not either.
- Go back to your fires. We will talk when there are fewer of you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. You are more civilised than your cousins in the wilds, which is to say, a little.
- Ah, the Ember Banner. What can scholars do for the children of a fallen goddess?
- Speak. Our pyromancers are curious how much of Bhall's old fire still burns in your people.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders burned one of our libraries last month. I take that personally.
- If you have come to threaten us, at least do it in more than three grunts.
- The smell of smoke arrived a day before you did. Say what you want.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A sound bargain, even if half the seal is a thumbprint in soot.
- Done. Even a warlord can count when it matters.
- Very well. Take the coin, and spend it far from our borders.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Clan? Thank you, and I will not ask whose village it came from.
- Our thanks. Few in Erebus would expect manners from Braduk.
- Generous. The faculty owes you a revised chapter on orcs.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That would arm your raiders against our own villages.
- We do not trade spellbooks to people who use paper for kindling.
- Your offer is mostly bluster and smoke. We decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and fight your barbarian cousins; they need the education more than we do.
- We accept. Our adepts would rather study fire than spend it on orcs.
- Very well, the war is over. Do try to burn something else.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your camps sit on our mana nodes, and the fire in them belongs to us.
- When the last of your warbands has learned to fear a robed figure on a hill, we will talk.
- Peace with an orc horde lasts until the next hungry winter. We will finish this now.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You have mistaken us for a village you have not burned yet.
- No. Our coin buys tomes, not axes.
- Ask again, and the answer will arrive on fire.

### Amurites → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. Our grandfathers met your pack in the snow, and the wolf learned to heel. We trust it remembers.
- You still smell of the long winter. The Children of Kylorin remember how it ended, and who ended it.
- We are scholars, not prey. Your ancestors made that mistake once, and Kylorin had to correct them.

#### Declares war
- The wolf has forgotten who broke it to the leash. We will remind it.
- Kylorin bested your pack and turned it on its old master. This time we will not bother turning you.
- You cull your weak, they say. Let us see how many of you are strong enough to survive a firestorm.

#### Refuses to talk
- Wolves do not parley; they circle. We are watching you circle.
- We will talk when the pack sits.
- Your envoy growled through the entire audience. Consider that our reply as well.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. The pack has done well in a warmth it never wanted.
- Ah, the Doviello. Our fathers fought yours in the ice; now we trade. Progress, of a sort.
- Speak. You helped end the winter in the end, even if a mage had to show you how. That earns you a seat.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders sniffed at our borders again. Does the pack need another lesson from the Amurites?
- I did not invite the wolves in. State your business, then go.
- You come here baring your teeth. Our adepts have teeth of fire.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. The pack bargains instead of biting, for once.
- Done. Spend it on something other than spears, if you can imagine such a thing.
- A fair trade. Kylorin would have been surprised.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The pack gives something away? That is new. Thank you.
- Our thanks. The wolf brings a bone; we shall not ask whose.
- Generous. Perhaps the pack has learned something since the Thaw.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That would feed your pack and starve our schools.
- Only the weak would accept terms like these, and your people despise the weak.
- Not good enough. Bring us a better kill.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to the tundra; the snow there suits you.
- We accept. The wolf heels again, as it once did for our father.
- Very well. Go and hunt someone who cannot set the forest on fire around you.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your pack still has too many teeth.
- You want peace because you are hungry. We know what the wolf does once it is fed.
- Not until the pack has learned this lesson as well as its grandfathers did.

#### Rejects a demand
- The last time the Doviello demanded something of the Amurites, it ended with a leash.
- No. Hunt somewhere else.
- The answer is no, and a wolf should know better than to ask a mage twice.

### Amurites → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim. You keep the holy places and the memory of the Compact. We would very much like to read your archives.
- You stood witness when the Godslayer passed to Finner. We have only one question: what did it look like?
- We are the Children of Kylorin. Your monks will find us curious, polite, and frequently in your libraries.

#### Declares war
- You sit on the fonts of power that Sucellus gave you, and you let no one study them. We are done asking permission.
- Your sacred sites hold more mana than prayer. We will put both to better use.
- Peaceful monks guarding secrets they will never use. We will take the secrets; keep your peace if you can.

#### Refuses to talk
- You lecture us on purity while we bury our students. There will be no talks.
- Your monks may meditate on our silence.
- Come back when you have something to say that is not a homily.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Of all the holy nations, only yours has never called our mages damned. We remember that.
- Ah, the keepers of the shrines. Tell me, do the seven firs still stand where the Compact was signed?
- Speak. Your monks tended the broken through every age of the world, and even mages are grateful for that.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your monks turned our scholars away from another shrine. What do you want now?
- Purity is easy for those who never study anything. Speak.
- You disapprove of us. We noticed. Is there anything else?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Honest dealing from honest keepers, as always.
- Done, and gladly. The word of the Elohim has outlasted empires.
- A fair bargain. We expected nothing less from the heirs of Immanuel Logos.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. The followers of Immanuel are as generous as the histories say.
- A gift! Our archmages will raise a toast to the Elohim at their next interminable meeting.
- Our gratitude, keeper. Should you ever wish to lend us your archives, it would be greater still.

#### Turns down a deal
- We cannot, not unless the offer comes with a map to Finner's tomb.
- Kind, but insufficient. We know what your vaults are hiding.
- No. Surely even saints can haggle better than that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. You were never meant for war, and we were never meant to fight you.
- We accept. Go and tend your shrines; the hells are rising, and Erebus needs its keepers more than its corpses.
- Gladly, then. Let no one say the Amurites stood against the Elohim while the Veil grew.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The shrines you guard sit on our nodes, and your monks are too stubborn to share.
- No. You hide too much behind your vows of peace.
- When you open your archives to us, we will open negotiations with you.

#### Rejects a demand
- Alms for the shrines? We give to our schools.
- No, keeper. Tend the poor with your own coin, as you always have.
- The Amurites do not tithe, not even to the kindest people in Erebus.

### Amurites → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori. You turned from the gods, and we never paid them much attention. I think we will understand each other.
- A Lanun captain once set out for our shores carrying a gift from your founder, and the ice swallowed him. We still wonder what it was.
- People without gods, meet people who worship magic. Shall we compare notes?

#### Declares war
- You preach that men should lead themselves. We will lead you, for a while.
- Your Adventurers grow too strong to leave unstudied. Consider this an invitation to our laboratories.
- No god will come to help you, and you would refuse one anyway. How very convenient for us.

#### Refuses to talk
- You wanted to be left alone. So be it.
- Your envoy urged us to think for ourselves. We did. The answer is no.
- We need no guidance from the Grigori, and we will not sit through it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Two peoples who do without the gods' favours; shall we also do without each other's enmity?
- Ah, the Grigori. Your Adventurers would make remarkable students, if they could bear to sit still.
- Your cities shelter the curious, and so do our schools. What brings you, friend?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You lecture the world about servitude, yet your spies sit in our academies. What is it?
- Your Luonnotar preach of a god above the gods. Our archmages call it unproven. Be quick.
- You came to tell us to think for ourselves? We do. Get to the point.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Clear terms, and no divine footnotes.
- Done. A bargain between two peoples who answer to no god.
- Fair enough. Reason prevails, for once.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. No strings, no gods, no sermon. Refreshing.
- A gift! The faculty is so rarely surprised.
- Our thanks. The last gift your people sent us sank in the ice; this one, at least, arrived.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Independence cuts both ways, and this deal cuts ours.
- We decline. Clever, but not clever enough for Amurite scholars.
- Your offer asks us to lean on you. You of all people should understand why we will not.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. We fight enough wars for the gods' sake; this one was for nobody's.
- We accept. Build your safe havens; we will build our schools.
- Agreed: free men may lead themselves, mages may study, and each may leave the other to it.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your Adventurers improve with every battle; we must end this before they become legends.
- Not yet. You taught the world self-reliance, and we rely on ourselves to finish this.
- Peace now would only give your heroes time to grow.

#### Rejects a demand
- Self-sufficiency is your creed, is it not? Practise it.
- No. Ask your god above the gods.
- You of all people should know we owe you nothing.

### Amurites → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus. Your riders hunted Patria's rogue mages at our father's call. We remember who answered Kylorin.
- Horse lords and sellswords. We may have work for you, and we pay in gold, not glory.
- Greetings. Keep your herds off the hills near our border; we suspect your shepherds already know to.

#### Declares war
- Your grandfathers charged down war-mages for Kylorin. Let us see how you fare against his children.
- A sword for hire is a sword pointed at someone. We have decided to break it before it points at us.
- Your raiders are swift. Lightning is swifter.

#### Refuses to talk
- You sold your lances to our enemies. Go and talk to them.
- We do not haggle with mercenaries in the middle of a contract.
- Ride on. The schools have nothing more to say to you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your companies have served us well, and we pay well. What do you need?
- Ah, Kylorin's old hunters. Sit, and tell me whose war you are riding in this season.
- Speak, horse lord. Our siege-mages could always use a few swift riders around them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your clans raid our herds and then offer to guard them for a fee. Bold. What now?
- Last season your mercenaries rode for our rival. Tell me why I should hear you.
- You smell of horse and broken contracts. Be brief.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Payment on delivery, as always with the Hippus.
- Done. Gold for speed is a good trade.
- Very well. May your herds grow, and your clans stop raiding each other.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, from a mercenary? Now that is a rarity worth recording.
- Our thanks. Kylorin's riders have not forgotten his children, it seems.
- Generous. I shall not tell your rival clans; they would never let you live it down.

#### Turns down a deal
- Too dear. Even good riders are not worth that much.
- No. That contract would set your lances on the wrong side of our walls.
- We decline. Come back when your price stops galloping.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and find a richer employer.
- We accept. The Hippus and the Amurites fought side by side once; let us remember it this time.
- Very well. Ride home and count what you have left.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You struck first and fled fast. This time we follow.
- Your peace comes with a price; we would rather pay in fire.
- Not until your clans learn that not every war is a business.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Hire yourselves out to someone else.
- No. We pay mercenaries for work, not for threats.
- You may ride around our walls as long as you like. The answer stays no.

### Amurites → Illians

#### First contact
- The men of Letum Frigus. Our father walked into the ice with a glowing blade, and the winter ended. You will remember it differently.
- You were the greatest of scholars once, before your god froze the world. Scholars should talk to scholars.
- We are the Children of Kylorin. Your old master knew that name well.

#### Declares war
- Kylorin ended your god's winter. His children will end your new lord's ambitions.
- Your ruler would be a god. We would prefer a footnote.
- The cold returns wherever your armies march. We have brought fire enough for all of it.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with the White Hand.
- Your envoy left frost on our doorframe. These talks are over.
- Go back to your caverns and dream of the old ice.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Leave your blizzard outside, if you would; our libraries are draughty enough.
- Ah, the Illians. What do the old scholars of Mulcarn want with the new ones?
- Speak. Your people knew magic before most of Erebus could spell the word, and we respect that, if little else.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your priests talk of a new winter. Our father did not walk into the ice so that you could bring it back.
- Your ruler would be a god; mine would be happy to be left alone. Speak.
- The room grows colder every time you visit. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even the winter has its uses in a bargain.
- Done. Pay us before the frost sets in.
- Very well. Ice and fire may trade, if nothing else.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Cold to the touch, but welcome. Our thanks to the north.
- Thank you. We will keep it near the fire.
- Our thanks. Perhaps the Illians remember being scholars after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargains thaw into nothing by spring.
- We decline. That would arm a god in waiting.
- Not enough. The fires of our schools cost more than that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Return to Letum Frigus and stay there.
- We accept. Let the snows stay where they belong.
- Very well. Kylorin would have preferred a spring to a war.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every frozen town is another reason to finish what Kylorin began.
- Your god is gone, and your would-be god will follow.
- Peace with the winter? The Children of Kylorin were born of the Thaw.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the winter? We paid it enough in the Age of Ice.
- No. You will have to freeze it out of us.
- Our answer is the one our father gave Mulcarn.

### Amurites → Infernal

#### First contact
- So the Veil's rituals did weaken the walls. We studied those rites as a warning, and you are the consequence.
- A demon lord walking Erebus. Our schools teach summoning under strict licence, and you, I fear, were not licensed.
- We know what you want; we have read the treatises. Keep your hounds away from our borders.

#### Declares war
- You want souls. We have trained a generation of adepts to sanctify every field you taint.
- We have summoned your lesser kin for study for centuries. Now we will dismiss the greater.
- Our firebows have been moved to the border we share with you. Let hell meet the arcane.

#### Refuses to talk
- Every word with a demon is a clause. We sign nothing.
- Go back through your Obsidian Gates.
- We need not hear the pit's offers. We have read them all, in the original.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- I will speak with you, [CT_NAME], but my wards are up and my adepts are watching.
- Curious. A demon who negotiates. Tell me why I should listen.
- Speak. We study every power, even yours. Especially yours.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The land along our border is withering. I know your work when I see it. What do you want?
- Hell knocks again. Say it and go.
- I can smell brimstone on your words before you speak them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, with every clause read twice. Twice.
- Done. The terms are written in ink, not blood, and they will stay that way.
- Very well. Even demons can be useful, under supervision.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from hell. It will be studied in a warded vault, far below the school.
- Our thanks, with reservations and a great many wards.
- Thank you. I shall not ask what it cost someone else.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Nothing from the pit comes without a price hidden in it.
- We decline. Your fine print is still smouldering.
- A demon's bargain? Even our first-year students know better.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. We both know it is only a pause.
- We accept. Turn your eyes elsewhere, and keep your hellhounds leashed.
- Very well. And may the Elohim never learn that we signed it.

#### Refuses peace
- No. A demon's peace is a weapon held in the other hand.
- Your truce is a smile with too many teeth in it.
- Not while your taint is still creeping across our fields.

#### Rejects a demand
- Souls are not a currency the Amurites deal in.
- No. Take your demands to the Ashen Veil; they enjoy your bargains.
- Here is our answer: a circle of salt and a closed door.

### Amurites → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad. We know your people distrust magic, so let us say at once that our gold is entirely real.
- Greetings from the surface, dwarves. You slept through the winter under your mountains; we were born of its ending.
- We admire your clockwork, and you will not admire our spells. Let us trade anyway.

#### Declares war
- You call all magic a swindle. Allow us to demonstrate that it is not.
- Your walls are stone and your black powder is clever. Our siege-mages need neither.
- The Khazad hoard gold and distrust spells. We will relieve you of both problems at once.

#### Refuses to talk
- You bar our scholars from your halls, and we bar your envoys from ours.
- Go back under your mountain.
- We will not haggle with people who weigh every word on a scale.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. I have been playing with a clockwork astrolabe of your making. Exquisite.
- Ah, dwarf. Before you ask: no, nothing in this room is an illusion.
- Speak, friend. Your gold is real and our words are true, so we should do very well together.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your merchants accuse our mages of trickery again. What is it this time?
- You fear magic and despise mages, and yet here you stand. Go on.
- If you have come to complain about illusions, kindly note that I am not one.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Weighed, counted and solid, just as dwarves prefer.
- Done. You may bite the coins if you must.
- Fair. Even a dwarf can see it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Generosity from the vaults of the Khazad? Let me check my purse is still there. Thank you.
- Our thanks. Generosity from the Underhome is rare indeed.
- Thank you. We will treat it better than the old kingdoms treated your smiths.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You have priced our spellwork as if it were worthless, and it is not.
- We decline. Even the Khazad must pay for what they cannot make.
- Too little. Your gold is good, but not that good.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to your forges, then, and we to our books.
- We accept. Our siege-mages have heard quite enough of your cannons.
- Very well. Stone and spell can live side by side, if they keep to their own valleys.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your vaults are not yet empty enough to make you reasonable.
- Not yet. You would only use the time to cast more guns.
- We refuse. A dwarf can wait out any siege, so we will bring a longer one.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a dwarf? Your vaults are fuller than ours.
- No. Be content with your own gold.
- Even the cleverest clockwork will not wind us into paying.

### Amurites → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates. You welcome every people, and we welcome every magic. Let us see if that makes us friends.
- We hear your lamia command great respect among your magi. Our archmages are most eager to meet them.
- Centaurs, giants and men all under one crown. A remarkable binding, if it is a spell at all.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements sprawl over lands our surveyors mapped first. We are coming to survey them again.
- You claim far more than you can hold. We will find out how hard the shell is.
- Your sphere of influence is too wide for comfort. We will narrow it.

#### Refuses to talk
- Retreat into your shell, and we will talk when you come out of it.
- No envoys. Not even centaurs.
- The confederacy may wait. We are busy winning.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. How fare your lamia? Our archmages ask after them constantly.
- Ah, the Kuriotates. You offer asylum to everyone; have you room for a few scholars?
- Your great cities are as learned as they are large. Sit, and tell me what they need.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlements lure away our students with promises of citizenship. Explain.
- Your centaurs trampled our survey stakes. Speak.
- You claim the wilderness as royal land, and we claim the mana in it. Go on.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your royal administration is so efficient that I almost envy it.
- Done. A bargain fit for a great city.
- May it travel quickly through your settlements. Well struck.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Your crown is generous indeed.
- A gift! The faculty sends its thanks, and possibly a lecturer or two.
- Our gratitude. Your confederacy remembers its friends, and so do we.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That would cost us more than it brings your settlements.
- We decline. A clever offer, but far too royal for our purse.
- Not enough, friend. Our schools cost more than a centaur's saddle.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Retreat into your shell, and we will retreat into our libraries.
- We accept. Your peoples and ours are too clever to waste on this.
- The frontier may grow quiet again. Very well.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your shell is cracking, and we will finish it.
- Not yet. Your core cities still stand too close to ours.
- We refuse. Your crown regrows what it loses unless enough is taken.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Ask your client states for tribute.
- Tribute to the confederacy? We are not one of your settlements.
- The answer is no, with all courtesy to your crown.

### Amurites → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun. Your ancestors ferried Patria's fleeing mages and then sold ships to the priests hunting them. We still have the receipts.
- Pirates and traders. We are scholars; you can only rob us of things we have not written down twice.
- Greetings, captains. A ship of yours once set sail for our shores under a captain named Malus and never arrived. Do you know what it carried?

#### Declares war
- You helped both sides in Patria. This time you will help only one, as prisoners.
- Your ships are fast, but water burns too, given a good enough mage.
- The sea no longer answers your priests. It will answer ours.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with privateers.
- Go and sail somewhere far away.
- The word of a Lanun lasts as long as a tide. No talks.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Have you brought any curiosities from distant shores?
- Ah, the Lanun. Tell me, have your priests heard from Danalin yet? We are professionally curious.
- Speak, captain. We always pay well for strange things dredged from the deep.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your ships smuggled a condemned necromancer away from our justice. Explain.
- You sell to both sides, I hear. Which side are you selling me today?
- The last captain who came here left with one of our tomes. Speak quickly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. We will count the cargo when it lands, of course.
- Done. A bargain is a bargain, even with a pirate.
- Very well. Fair winds, and do not sell the same goods to my rival.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the sea? We are touched, and curious where you got it.
- Our thanks, captain. Sometimes the tide does bring good things.
- Thank you. That is more honest than the histories ever were about your ancestors.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That cargo will be worth half as much by the time it reaches port.
- We decline. Our father's empire learned what Lanun bargains cost.
- Not enough. Even pirates must pay for spells.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to your islands and your plunder.
- We accept. Keep your sails on the horizon, and we will keep our fire on the shore.
- Very well. Open your harbours, and we will open our markets.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your ships have aided our enemies once too often.
- Not yet. Your fleets still rule waters we mean to study.
- We refuse. A pirate's peace lasts until the next fat merchantman.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a pirate? Come and take it, if you can swim through fire.
- No. Go and plunder someone without wards.
- The Amurites pay for knowledge, not for threats.

### Amurites → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The elves of the Summer Court. We hear Evermore trains archmages as fine as ours. We should like to test that.
- You crept back from your hidden groves; we came out of the ice. Survivors both, it seems.
- Your archmages once confiscated a Calabim grimoire of necromancy. We would pay handsomely to read it, through proper channels.

#### Declares war
- Your groves sit on mana you barely use. We will use it.
- Evermore's magic against our schools. The faculty is very curious which will prevail.
- Your ancient forests burn like any other, given a patient enough adept.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not listen to the leaves.
- You hid in your groves for a whole age. Hide from us a little longer.
- Your envoy spoke in songs, and we are in no mood for music.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. How fares Evermore? Our archmages send their regards, and their envy.
- Ah, the Ljosalfar. Your druids and our adepts could teach each other a great deal.
- Speak, friend of the forest. Your new god has been kind to you of late.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Priests of Leaves called our woodcutters defilers. What do you want?
- You treat every axe as an act of war. Ours was for firewood. Speak.
- The Summer Court frowns on us again. Go on.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Elves bargain slowly, but they bargain fairly.
- Done. Let it grow, like your oaks.
- The grove and the school both profit. Well bargained.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Elven gifts are rare, and rarely simple.
- Our thanks. We shall plant it or study it, whichever it seems to prefer.
- Generous. The groves remember their friends, and so do we.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That would cost us more than an elf's patience.
- We decline. Your terms grow as slowly as your trees.
- Too little. We know what the lore of Evermore is worth.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Mend your forest; we have classes to resume.
- We accept. The seasons turn, and so do wars.
- So be it. Leaves and scrolls may both rest a while.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your ancient forests hide too much mana to leave alone.
- Not yet. Your Fellowship still hangs our woodcutters.
- We refuse. Elves remember slights for centuries; the least we can do is finish a war.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. The oak is not the only thing that does not bend.
- Tribute? Ask your treants for it.
- The Amurites give nothing to those who merely ask.

### Amurites → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp. You give clockwork a kind of life, which we find wonderfully improper. Let us talk.
- Greetings, heirs of the Open-Skiers. Your golems are the only magic a dwarf ever trusted.
- We admire your enchanters. Your golems, we would very much like to take apart.

#### Declares war
- Your golems are marvels. We shall see how they fare against a dispelling.
- Runes and gears against the schools of Kylorin. A fascinating experiment, and you are the subject.
- The long winter broke your golems once. We have since worked out how.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not argue with gears.
- Return to your workbench.
- Your envoy was a golem. It did not understand our refusal, so please pass it on.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. How go your enchantments? Our faculty would love a demonstration.
- Ah, the Luchuirp. Clockwork that walks and obeys. I never tire of it.
- Speak. Your enchanters and our adepts have more in common than either will admit.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems marched over our survey lines again. Speak.
- You call our magic careless. Speak, but carefully.
- Clockwork soldiers stand staring at our border. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your craftsmanship is worth the price.
- Done. Your work is as honest as your gears.
- Fair dealing, gnome. May your clockwork never rust.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Is it a golem? Please tell me it is a golem.
- Our thanks. Luchuirp gifts always seem to tick a little.
- Generous. We shall take it apart lovingly.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your enchanters ask too much.
- We decline. We could build this ourselves, given a century.
- Not enough. We know exactly what a mana node is worth to a golem-maker.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to the workbench with you.
- We accept. Your golems deserve better work than dying in our ditches.
- Very well. Under Kilmorph's mountains and above them, there is room for us both.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems keep coming, so we keep breaking them.
- Not yet. The faculty has not finished studying your wrecks.
- We refuse. The Age of Ice could not finish the Luchuirp; we are more thorough.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Build it yourself; you are good at that.
- Tribute for the workshop? We pay for golems, not for threats.
- Ask again, and we will dispel your messenger.

### Amurites → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim. A desert people who took their faith from an elf found freezing in the snow. Our own founding is stranger, if you can believe it.
- Your Empyrean judges each case on its merits rather than by a codex. Our tribunals do the same; we should get along.
- Greetings, children of the sun. You prize wisdom, and we prize learning. Let us not split hairs over the difference.

#### Declares war
- Your sun has blinded you to what lies beneath your sands. We are coming to dig it up.
- Your Radiant Guard shines very brightly. Light is the easiest thing in the world for a mage to bend.
- The Empyrean gives a voice to small nations, you say. Hear ours, then.

#### Refuses to talk
- We need no more of your light shone on our affairs.
- You preach impartial judgement and then send armies. Go home.
- No talks. Your Vicars have said quite enough.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your Vicars ask better questions than most priests. Sit down.
- Ah, the Malakim. Lugus values wisdom and we value learning; between us, we may even arrive at the truth.
- Speak. Your deserts hide ruins from the Age of Magic, and our scholars dream of them nightly.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You call our mages shadow-workers. We call your priests short-sighted. Speak.
- Your Vicars stir our students against the schools. What is it?
- The sun is hot today, and so is my temper. Be quick.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Fair and reasoned, as Lugus would wish.
- Done. We trust the judgement of the Empyrean in this, at least.
- A fair bargain, under any sun.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. The desert gives rarely, so we value it all the more.
- Our thanks. Generosity is the best light your faith has shown us.
- A gift! The faculty will drink to the Malakim tonight, and argue about you until dawn.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Consult on the merits of this case, and you will find none.
- We decline. Weigh it again, by daylight.
- Too little. Wisdom costs more than that, as your own priests should know.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let the sun shine on both our lands, and the lamps burn late in our schools.
- We accept. Wisdom prefers peace, and for once we agree with it.
- Very well. You have your prayers and we have our studies; both need quiet.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your Radiant Guard still stands at our gates.
- Not yet. The Empyrean has judged us without hearing us; we will be heard.
- We refuse. This war ends at dusk, and we choose when dusk comes.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. You say small nations have a voice; here is ours.
- Tribute for the sun? It shines for free.
- We give nothing to those who come bearing demands instead of wisdom.

### Amurites → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels who broke the Compact. We find you fascinating. You will find our summoners less so, I suspect.
- Greetings, soldiers of the war in hell. Our adepts study demons, and you merely kill them. Perhaps we can share notes.
- The Mercurians. We were warned you care nothing for mortals. We, in turn, care little for warnings.

#### Declares war
- You kill summoners for summoning. We train them for it. One of us must give way.
- Your host broke the gods' own treaty. Ours is a smaller rule: stay off our mana nodes.
- Wings and war hammers against the schools of Kylorin. Let us see whose discipline is stricter.

#### Refuses to talk
- You would only call us demonologists and leave. Leave now and save us both the time.
- We will not be judged by an angel who abandoned Arawn.
- No talks with the host. Go and fight your demons.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our adepts can sanctify a tainted land; perhaps that is of use to your war.
- Ah, the Mercurians. What news from the hells?
- Speak. Our firebows face the Infernal too, you know.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your soldiers smashed a summoning circle in one of our schools, and the students in it. Explain.
- You look at our mages as though they smell of sulphur. They do not. What is it?
- You call us dabblers in darkness. Speak, angel, and quickly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Now go back to your war.
- Done, and briefly, as you like it.
- Very well. Even angels need supplies.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The host stoops to give? Remarkable. Thank you.
- Our thanks. We had heard you thought mortals beneath your notice.
- Thank you. We shall not summon anything to celebrate.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your war is not ours to pay for.
- We decline. Fund your crusade in hell yourselves.
- Too little. Spells cost dearly, even when aimed at demons.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. The hells need you more than our border does.
- We accept. Fight the demons, not the schools.
- Very well. Our wards and your wings point at the same enemy, after all.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You came for our summoners, and we will finish this.
- Not yet. The host has yet to learn what a school of mages can do.
- We refuse. You broke the gods' compact; why would you keep ours?

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Your crusade is not our tithe.
- Tribute for the war in hell? Our schools fight their own wars.
- We give nothing to angels who hold mortals in contempt.

### Amurites → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. Some of your people learned their first runes in our schools, I suspect. We would like our books back.
- Greetings, gate-openers. We study power for its own sake. You study it for the end of everything.
- Your Armageddon rites are a fascinating field of study. We regulate fascinating fields.

#### Declares war
- Our law on forbidden magic is merciless and spectacular, and you have broken every clause.
- Your gates open onto the hells. Ours are trained to close them.
- The end of the world would interrupt our research. We will not permit it.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not negotiate with the end of the world.
- Your envoys came through a gate. Send them back the same way.
- We have read your doctrines; we know how they end. No talks.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- I will speak with you, [CT_NAME], though I do not care for the smell of your gates.
- Ah, the Sheaim. Your runes are elegant; your aims are less so.
- Speak. I am curious, if not trusting.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Every rite you perform drags the world closer to its end, and every visit you make tries my patience. Speak.
- The land sickens wherever your gates open. Be quick.
- You want us to help you end the world. No. What else?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Hardly the end of the world, is it?
- Done. Enjoy it while creation lasts.
- Very well, though we read it twice for hidden runes.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Into a sealed vault it goes, to be studied at leisure. Thank you, I think.
- Our thanks, gate-opener. I trust it does not open.
- Thank you. Generosity is strange from those who want the world to end.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Nothing you give lasts long enough to be worth it.
- We decline. Every one of your bargains ends with everything ending.
- Too little, and far too apocalyptic.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Close your gates and go home.
- We accept. Creation survives another season.
- Very well. Our wards will be watching your gates.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every gate you open shortens the life of the world.
- Not until your planar gates are rubble.
- We refuse. Some magic is forbidden for a reason, and you are that reason.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the end of the world? It can collect it itself.
- No. Why would you want gold, when everything is about to end?
- The answer is no. Add it to your apocalypse.

### Amurites → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. You traded your souls for time to study. We admire the scholarship and question the method.
- Our tribunals once condemned a man for sustaining a life past its natural span. Your whole nation would fill our prisons.
- We saw you only because our wards did. You walk very quietly, for neighbours.

#### Declares war
- You traded your souls for knowledge. We will take the knowledge, without the trade.
- Our law on prolonging life past nature is clear, and every one of you is in breach.
- Shades are very hard to kill, they say. Our adepts adore a difficult problem.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not speak to fog.
- Back to your hidden cities with you.
- Your envoys flicker. We do not trust anything that flickers.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Endless years to study. I confess I envy it, some days.
- Ah, the Sidar. What have you read this century?
- Sit, if shades sit. Your libraries must be older than our nation.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades drift through our schools uninvited. Explain.
- You think us children, and we think you unlicensed. Speak.
- I have little time, Grey one, unlike you. Be brief.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. You will outlive the deal, and we will profit from it.
- Done. Time is on your side, and gold is on ours.
- Very well. A bargain for an age.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Something from the Grey? Thank you, and do tell us what it is.
- Our thanks. You remember the living, sometimes.
- Thank you. We shall study it, as you would.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You can wait a century for a better offer, and so can we.
- We decline. Too little, even for immortals.
- Not enough. Knowledge costs more than you seem to remember.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your mists.
- We accept. You have eternity for your studies; we have rather less, and would like it back.
- Very well. War bores the immortal and exhausts the mortal; let us both be spared.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your hidden cities hold libraries we mean to read.
- Not yet. You are hard to kill, but not impossible.
- We refuse. We will finish this before you have time to forget it started.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. You have all the time in the world to earn it.
- Tribute to ghosts? Collect it in your next life, if you kept one.
- No, and the answer will not change in a century.

### Amurites → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Unseelie court. You were always the more arcane of the elves. We look forward to learning your secrets, one way or another.
- Greetings, Svartalfar. We are told you betray your allies. We are warded against it.
- Dark elves of the Winter Court. Your magic is older than ours, but ours is better organised.

#### Declares war
- Your assassins came to our academy. Now our academy comes to you.
- The Winter Court practises magic with no licence and no limit. We bring both.
- You traded Sucellus for Esus. Let us see what that bargain has bought you.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not believe a single word you have spoken, so why hear more?
- Return to your winter.
- No talks. We know all about your academies of persuasion.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Please keep your knives where I can see them.
- Ah, the Svartalfar. Your sorcerers are sharp. So are mine.
- Speak. Our wards are listening as well.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- I found one of your assassins under my lectern. Explain.
- You smile like a contract with hidden clauses. Speak.
- The Winter Court comes calling. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. And yes, I counted my spoons.
- Done. We will test the goods for poison later.
- Very well. A fair deal from the Unseelie, for once.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Unseelie generosity. We shall ward it very carefully.
- Our thanks. I shall not taste anything that came with it.
- Thank you. We will not ask whom you robbed to send it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offers always come with a dagger folded inside.
- We decline. Too clever, and not nearly honest enough.
- Too little, and far too dark.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your shadows and your Esus.
- We accept. Keep your assassins home this winter.
- Very well. A truce, until the seasons turn and your court remembers its knives.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your peace is a poisoned cup.
- Not yet. Your sorcerers have a great deal to teach us, in chains.
- We refuse. You betray your own kin; you would betray a treaty before the ink dried.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Steal it, as you usually do.
- Tribute to the Winter Court? The court is closed for the season.
- We give nothing to those who would put a knife in us afterwards.

## Balseraphs

### Balseraphs → Amurites

#### First contact
- Kylorin's other children! Old Kylorin built a tower of eyes to keep Jubilee in, you know. We got out. Did he never mention it?
- Schoolmasters and spellbooks and committees, oh my. Is there anyone in your country who knows how to laugh?
- The Laughing Court greets the Children of Kylorin. Shall we see which of the old man's families learned the better tricks?

#### Declares war
- Your father locked us in a tower in a swamp. We have been planning a little party for his children ever since.
- Off with the robes and on with the dance! Our Harlequins want to see if mages juggle when they burn.
- Every faculty needs a few new lessons. Today's lesson is the Puppet, and the strings are tied to your archmages.

#### Refuses to talk
- Shh, the schoolmasters are knocking. Pretend we are not home.
- Talk, talk, talk, that is all your people ever do. We would rather watch.
- Oh, it is you. I was hoping it was someone with a sense of humour.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Do you have time for a game of Somnium, [CT_NAME]? I promise not to read your cards. Much.
- Cousins of a sort! The old man taught us both, and see how differently we turned out.
- Come in, come in, mind the trapdoor. Have your archmages finished their quarrel yet?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our Puppets came home with their strings cut. That was rude of your adepts.
- You frown just like your father did when he locked the door. What do you want?
- Sit, schoolmaster. No, not that chair; that one bites.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done! Write it in triplicate, so your committees have something to argue about.
- Agreed, agreed. I won't vote for you at your next faculty meeting, though.
- A bargain! The old man would have been proud of us both. Or horrified. Same face, really.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present! Is it a spell? Is it a book? Oh, I do hope it explodes.
- How generous of the schoolhouse! We shall hang it in the hall of mirrors.
- You're the best! Your father never gave us anything but a cell.

#### Turns down a deal
- That deal is dull as a lecture and twice as long. No.
- We would sign it, but the voices in our head voted against it.
- A bargain fit for a bursar. Bring me something with more colour in it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Run along to your lessons, and we shall find a new game.
- Let's put the toys away. You're my new best friend; I broke my last one.
- Very well, the curtain falls. Do come to the next performance, as audience this time.

#### Refuses peace
- Stop now? But your archmages make such marvellous screams.
- The old man never let us finish anything. We intend to finish this.
- Not yet, not yet! A tower of eyes for a tower of eyes; then we'll talk.

#### Rejects a demand
- Not sharing makes you a bad playmate, but demanding makes you a worse one.
- Your schools want our toys? Make your own, clever children.
- No! The court has voted, and every one of us laughed.

### Balseraphs → Bannor

#### First contact
- Oh, the Bannor! You swore to fight chaos forever, and here we are. Isn't that lucky?
- Such straight lines, such shiny helmets, such grim faces. Does anyone in your country ever smile?
- Greetings, soldiers of Junil. We are the reason your priests tell children to say their prayers.

#### Declares war
- Toy soldiers are no fun without battles to fight with them, and yours are the tidiest toys in Erebus.
- Your Law against our Laughter! Let us see which one the crowd cheers for.
- Every farm a castle, they say? Then every farm shall be a stage, and our Harlequins have rehearsed.

#### Refuses to talk
- I'm busy. Come back when you've learned a joke.
- Your heralds only quote scripture. I've heard all the verses.
- No talks with the Bannor! The court has decided to sulk.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME], what a surprise! I promise, nothing chaotic has happened all week.
- Come in, soldier. Shall we play at cards? You can be the side with all the rules.
- The Bannor, visiting Jubilee! Your confessors must be fainting.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your confessors have been preaching in my circus tents again. They frighten the Freaks.
- Back again with your codex? Which of our crimes is it this week?
- You glare like a wall with a helmet on. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! A just and equitable deal, as you would say. How very boring of us both.
- Done. See? Even chaos keeps its word, when it feels like it.
- A bargain! I'll put it in the scrapbook next to the wanted posters you nailed up about us.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present from the Bannor! Are you sure Junil allows this?
- Oh, splendid! I shall wear it at the next masquerade, dressed as a Bannor general.
- How sweet. We shall keep it in the room with the other relics we didn't steal.

#### Turns down a deal
- That deal has too many rules in it. No.
- Every one of your clauses begins with thou shalt not. We much prefer thou might. No.
- Fair, even, honest, orderly. I yawned four times reading it. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Your crusaders may go home and polish something.
- Very well, let's play another game instead. Something with fewer hymns.
- The curtain falls. Do tell your priests we were terribly sorry, and keep a straight face.

#### Refuses peace
- But we are having so much fun!
- Your Crusade only just started. Leaving now would ruin the second act.
- Not yet. I want to see how far a Bannor march can go before it trips.

#### Rejects a demand
- A demand from the Law-givers? Isn't asking for free things a little bit like stealing?
- No, no, and no. One for each of your Orders.
- That hardly seems fair. And you, of all people, care about fair.

### Balseraphs → Calabim

#### First contact
- The Calabim! We keep slaves for the masque; you keep cattle for supper. We shall have so much to talk about.
- Greetings, cousins of the night. We do adore a court with a few corpses in it.
- How charming, a kingdom run by its appetites. Ours is run by its whims; they're very similar.

#### Declares war
- You fed on one of our dancers, and nobody eats the performers. The show must go on, so you must go.
- Let's see whose courtiers last longer: yours, who cannot die, or ours, who cannot stop laughing.
- Our Taskmasters want your herds. Your herds will thank us; we at least make them dance before they die.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now, darling, the blood has gone to your head.
- You only come to talk when you're hungry. Go and eat someone else.
- I've drawn the curtains. Vampires hate that, don't they?

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Can I offer you a drink, [CT_NAME]? I'm afraid we only have wine. Unless...
- Darlings! The masque begins at midnight. Do come as yourselves; no one will believe it.
- Come in, come in. Do the Grand Broods still argue over who gets the prettiest villages?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- One of your nobles bit my best juggler. He can't juggle any more.
- You smile like we're supper. We are not supper.
- Oh, the leeches. What now?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Sealed in ink, not blood. I know, I know, terribly dull.
- Done. One monster to another, it's a lovely trade.
- A bargain! Send it before sunrise, or it won't arrive at all.

#### Thanks for a gift
- How thoughtful! Is it still warm?
- How thoughtful of the Broods! I'll keep it in the cellar, where you'd feel at home.
- Oh, a present from the Broods. Is anyone missing from your cattle towns?

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That would leave us looking pale.
- A deal with a vampire is like a kiss with a vampire. Somebody leaves drained.
- We would, but you'd only bleed us dry later. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Off to your herds, then. Ours need a rest too; they've been screaming all week.
- Peace, then, and a masked ball to seal it. Do come as a bat.
- Very well. A truce of the night, until one of us gets peckish again.

#### Refuses peace
- But your castles are so lovely when they burn.
- I'd like to see a vampire at noon first. Not yet.
- Peace? You'd only grow fat on another village. No.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want our slaves? Breed your own cattle.
- Demanding things of us! How rude. Do vampires have no manners?
- No. Suck it out of somebody else.

### Balseraphs → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs! Big ones! Have you ever considered a career in the circus?
- The Clan of Embers. We hear you throw people into fires. So do we, but we sell tickets.
- How delightful. You carry a burning girl's head about, I hear. We have a whole court of voices in ours; we're practically family.

#### Declares war
- Our Taskmasters need strong backs, and nobody's backs are stronger than yours.
- Your Ember Banner will look lovely as a tent.
- Fire-eaters and fire-breathers! The arena is ready, and the audience is hungry for orc.

#### Refuses to talk
- Grunting is not talking, dear.
- Go and set something else on fire.
- I'm afraid I don't speak axe.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Come, sit, but don't sit on the jester again.
- Ah, my favourite brutes. What shall we smash together today?
- Welcome, welcome! The Freaks have been asking about your goblins all week.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders stole our dancing bear. It was a man in a costume, you know. He's very upset.
- You smell of smoke and spite. What do you want?
- Have you come to burn something? Not the tents, please.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Look at you, trading like a civilised orc.
- Done. That will buy a lot of axes, won't it?
- A bargain! Bhall would be proud. Or on fire. Hard to tell with her.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present from the orcs! Did you only burn it a little?
- Lovely! It goes in the Freaks' tent; they'll fight over it.
- How generous. Your fallen goddess must be smiling, somewhere very hot.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even I can count well enough to see that's a bad deal.
- That's not a trade, that's a raid with paperwork.
- I would, but it's not shiny enough. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Go home and bang on your drums.
- Then we'll stage the rest of the war with actors. You can play the monsters; you won't need costumes.
- Very well. Our arena could do with a rest.

#### Refuses peace
- But the arena crowds love watching orcs!
- Not yet. Our Taskmasters haven't caught nearly enough of you.
- Peace? You'd only burn something of ours tomorrow.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want our things? Come and take them, if you can find them in the hall of mirrors.
- No, and if you sulk, I'll send a Harlequin to cheer you up.
- Orcs never ask nicely, and we never answer nicely. No.

### Balseraphs → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello! You ran free in the winter while we hid from the White Hand. How rude of you to enjoy it.
- Your people learned their manners from a wolf pack. Ours learned theirs in a madhouse. We shall get along famously.
- Charmed. You cull your weaklings; we put ours in costumes and sell tickets.

#### Declares war
- Your pack would make a lovely act: the Wolves of Winter, in three scenes and a feeding.
- You cull the weak and we cull the boring. Let us find out which of the two you are.
- Here, wolfie, wolfie. Our Taskmasters have collars in every size.

#### Refuses to talk
- Sit. Stay. Go away.
- Your envoy chewed the treaty. I assume that is the answer.
- Old Kylorin taught your pack to heel once. Heel.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Wipe your paws, and mind the dancing bear; he gets jealous.
- Ah, the pack is here. Whom shall we hunt together this season?
- Welcome! You howl and we laugh, and between us we keep the neighbours up all night.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your wolves ate a performing goat. It sang. It was our best act.
- You come growling into a court of laughter. What do you want?
- Did Camulos send you to spoil my afternoon?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Good dog.
- Done. You could have done it the hard way, I know, but the easy way is funnier.
- A bargain! The pack shares its kill, for once.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present! It isn't half-eaten, is it?
- How kind. I shall scratch behind your ears next time.
- The Doviello, giving? Somewhere a wolf is weeping.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That's a weakling's deal, and you of all people hate weaklings.
- Too small a bone, wolf. Dig up a bigger one.
- I would take it, but then I'd have to count my fingers afterwards.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Go and howl at the warm weather somewhere else.
- Very well, the arena can wait a while for its wolves.
- Off you trot. Find something slower to chase.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The masquerade needs a wolf-skin cloak or two.
- The pack only wants peace when it is losing. That is my favourite part.
- Stop now? Your War Machine hasn't even fallen over yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- Wolves don't get to want things; they get to beg.
- No. Bark louder.
- The pack asks the jester for tribute? The jester says no, with bells on.

### Balseraphs → Elohim

#### First contact
- Pilgrims and monks and holy places! You'll be pleased to hear we have a shrine as well. It's to us.
- The Elohim. Sirona's sisters once kept one of our court in an asylum, you know. It ended very badly for the sisters.
- Monks who fight without weapons! Can they juggle without hands, too?

#### Declares war
- You guard all those sacred sites and never let anyone play in them. We're coming to play.
- Your monks are so very pure. Let's see how pure they look in motley.
- Peace, purity and prayer. It's all so dreadfully dull that we've decided to liven it up.

#### Refuses to talk
- Shh. If we keep very quiet, the monks will start meditating and forget we're here.
- I'm afraid I don't speak homily.
- No talks. You'd only try to heal me.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Come in, [CT_NAME], and don't mind the cages; they're decorative.
- The Elohim! Have you come to tend the sick? Our court is full of them, and we like them that way.
- Welcome, keeper. Tell me the story of the Compact again, the part with the Godslayer. It's my favourite.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your pilgrims keep freeing our slaves and calling it charity. I call it theft.
- You look at me as if I were a ruin that needed tending. What do you want?
- Oh, the saints are here. Mind your halo on the doorframe.

#### Accepts a deal
- We most humbly accept your generous proposal. There, you see, I can talk like you too.
- Done. Don't tell your monks; they'll fret about where our gold came from.
- A bargain! Even saints have to shop.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Elohim! Is it blessed? Will it burn when I touch it?
- How kind. It shall go in our chapel, between the juggling skulls.
- Charity, for us! I am almost moved. Almost.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your deal is far too fair for us to trust.
- That offer is as plain as a monk's robe. Add some colour and try again.
- Our court took a vote: one yes, and a thousand voices laughing.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Go and tend your shrines, and leave us to our revels.
- Very well, holy ones, we'll stop, if you stop praying for us. It itches.
- The play is over. Take your bows, monks.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. I've always wanted to see where Finner is buried, and you keep the map.
- Peace? You'd only spend it converting my jugglers.
- Stop now? Your warrior monks were just starting to get interesting.

#### Rejects a demand
- Alms for the shrines? We spent it all on bells.
- You're asking us for charity? Isn't that backwards, holy one?
- No. Pray for it.

### Balseraphs → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori! A whole nation that thinks for itself. How exhausting. Our people let us do it for them.
- You turned your backs on the gods, and we turned our backs on sanity. Shall we compare notes?
- Greetings, free folk. Your Adventurers look like they would make wonderful acts.

#### Declares war
- Free will is such a fragile toy. Let's see if it breaks.
- Your Adventurers want glory. We have a stage for them, with sharp things on it.
- No god will help you; you made very sure of that. Neither will we.

#### Refuses to talk
- Think for yourself and go away.
- Your envoy kept asking me to be reasonable. Reasonable! The cheek.
- Not today. I'm busy being worshipped, which is more than your people ever do.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Come in, [CT_NAME]. Every thought you have in here will be your own. Probably.
- The godless ones! My favourite heretics. What brings you to Jubilee?
- Welcome! You serve no god and we serve no one at all. We're practically twins.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Adventurers rescued a whole troupe of our slaves in the middle of a performance.
- You preach freedom along my borders, and now my subjects are getting ideas.
- Oh, it's the people who think too much. What?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! And nobody had to read anybody's mind at all.
- Done. Freely given, freely taken; your founder would approve.
- A bargain! Two free spirits and one terrible idea.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present, given of your own free will? How novel. Ours are usually compelled.
- Thank you! I'll give it to my favourite Puppet.
- No god made you do it, did they? How charming.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. A free people ought to understand that word.
- That deal smells of good sense. Take it away.
- Hmm, let me think for myself. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Run along to your free cities; they're dull, but they're yours.
- Very well. Freedom wins this round. Don't get used to it.
- Enough, enough. Your Adventurers are learning far too much from my Harlequins.

#### Refuses peace
- No. A few more of your heroes would round out my collection.
- Not yet. Free will has to be tested before it can be proven.
- Stop? But you're thinking so very hard about how to win.

#### Rejects a demand
- You don't answer prayers, and neither do we.
- No. Help yourself; isn't that your whole creed?
- Tribute, from people who bow to no one? Bow to us first, and then we'll discuss it.

### Balseraphs → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus! Your raiders once took our coin to fetch us some dwarves and came back with none. We still laugh about it. Mostly.
- Horse lords! Do your horses dance? Ours did, before they were eaten.
- Greetings, sellswords. We pay well, we pay strangely, and we always need riders for the parade.

#### Declares war
- You took our gold and delivered no dwarves. We've come for the refund.
- Our Taskmasters have been dreaming of horses. And riders. Mostly riders.
- Every circus needs a horse act, and yours is about to join ours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No haggling today; your horses are frightening the Freaks.
- Come back when you've finished the last job we paid you for.
- Ride away, ride away, as fast as you can.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Bring your riders in; the stables are full of monsters, but friendly ones.
- Ah, the Hippus. We have another job for you, and this time the dwarves are smaller.
- Welcome! How's business? Ours is booming; everyone is terrified.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your companies rode for our enemies last season. Whose coin are you carrying now?
- You still owe us a cart of dwarves. Speak.
- The horse-thieves are back. Mind the jewellery.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Gold for gallops, a fine trade.
- Done. And this time, deliver the goods.
- A bargain! You're a shrewd negotiator; I very nearly noticed.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A mercenary giving something away? Is someone paying you to do it?
- Thank you! We shall name a pony after you.
- How lovely. Most of your people only ever send us bills.

#### Turns down a deal
- That price gallops away faster than your riders.
- No. Last time we paid you in advance, we got an empty cage.
- Too dear for a horse and too cheap for a hero. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Go and find someone richer to rob.
- Very well. A contract is a contract, even when it's a peace.
- Let's stop. Your horses are tired and my jugglers are dizzy.

#### Refuses peace
- No, no. I promised the court a cavalry charge, with real cavalry.
- No. You owe us dwarves, and we'll take it out in Hippus instead.
- Stop? Your riders haven't even fallen off yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a hired sword? Go and get hired.
- No. Mercenaries are paid for work, and asking isn't work.
- Your threats would frighten us more if you had ever delivered those dwarves.

### Balseraphs → Illians

#### First contact
- The White Hand! We spent the whole Age of Ice hiding from your priests. Shall we play hide-and-seek again?
- When the Illians wake, the world sleeps, they say. We never sleep at all. How awkward for you.
- Brr. Who let the winter in?

#### Declares war
- We hid from your White Hand for an age. Now it's our turn to seek.
- You want a god of your own? How sweet. Every god needs a jester, and every jester needs a joke at the god's expense.
- Let's melt something. You, perhaps.

#### Refuses to talk
- Too cold to talk.
- Your envoy froze to the doorstep, so we've left him there as a statue.
- No. Go and wait for your god in the snow.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Shut the door, you're letting the cold in.
- Ah, the Illians. Do you still talk to that dead god of yours? We talk to all sorts of dead people.
- Welcome! We lit every fire in the palace for you. You'll hate it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your blizzards ruined our summer carnival.
- The White Hand at our door again? Go away; we're not hiding any more.
- Brr. You again. What?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Cold hands, warm deal.
- Done. It will keep, I suppose; everything does in your country.
- A bargain! Even the winter likes a party.

#### Thanks for a gift
- From the frozen north! Should I keep it on ice?
- Thank you! It goes in the summer palace, where it can melt in peace.
- How kind, for a glacier.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Too cold, too grim, too godly.
- That bargain will freeze solid before it pays out.
- I'd say yes, but my teeth are chattering too hard.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Go back to your caverns and dream of snow.
- Very well, but promise not to end the world before the next carnival.
- Let the thaw begin. Again.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. We still owe you for an age of hiding in holes.
- Stop? I've only just started to warm up.
- No. A god in the making makes such a lovely target.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Your new god can conjure it.
- Tribute for the winter? We paid that for a whole age, shivering in the dark.
- You want our toys? Make snowmen.

### Balseraphs → Infernal

#### First contact
- A demon lord! Our nursery was full of your little cousins. The imps send their love.
- Hell has come to visit. We'll set an extra place and hide the silver.
- You torment souls for eternity? We do it for an afternoon, and we sell tickets.

#### Declares war
- Our conjurers have bound Balors before. Let's see how a whole hell takes to a leash.
- You crawled up here for mortal toys to torment. So did we. Only one of us gets to keep them.
- Hell is all fire and screaming and no jokes. We're coming to fix that.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now, the imps are napping.
- I don't bargain with hell. Hell cheats, and cheating is my job.
- Go back down the hole you came up.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Do sit; the chair is fireproof.
- Ah, the demons. Our summoners say hello; they've borrowed a few of your servants.
- Welcome! Down there you only have screaming. Up here we have screaming and music.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your hellhounds ate my favourite Freak. He had three heads, so that's a lot of dinner.
- You stink of sulphur and self-importance. What is it?
- The pit sends an envoy. How very unsurprising.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Now, whose soul did that cost? Not mine, I hope.
- Done. Ink, not blood; we're not that kind of court. Most days.
- A bargain with a demon! My court will talk of nothing else.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from hell! Does it bite, burn or whisper? I love all three.
- It will go in the nursery with the imps. Thank you!
- How sweet. I'll pretend I don't know what it cost.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Every demon's bargain has a trapdoor, and I built all of mine myself.
- Too much hell in that deal, and not enough fun.
- If I said yes I'd belong to you, and I'm already spoken for. Several times over.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Back to your fires, and we to ours.
- Very well. You may teach my jugglers to breathe fire, as a token of friendship.
- The show's over. Mind the stage on your way down.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. I want a Pit Beast for the menagerie.
- No. Our summoners haven't finished collecting your servants.
- Peace with hell? Hell would win the fine print.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand? Imps demand. Lords ask nicely.
- No. Take a soul out of someone duller.
- Our souls are ours to waste, thank you very much.

### Balseraphs → Khazad

#### First contact
- Dwarves! Your grandfathers traded their finest work to tricksters for baubles and illusions. We are the grandchildren of those tricksters. Hello!
- The Khazad. You hate illusions, I'm told. Then you'll adore our court, where nothing is what it seems and everyone admits it.
- Greetings, little gold-counters. We once hired riders to bring us a few of your people. They came back rather singed.

#### Declares war
