- We have always wanted dwarves for the mines under Jubilee. Soon we shall have hundreds.
- Your vaults are full, your walls are thick, and your sense of humour is empty. We are here to fix all three.
- Black powder and stubbornness won't help you against a Puppet wearing your own general's face.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talks. You'll only poke me to see whether I'm real.
- Go back to your hole, little miser.
- Your envoy kept tapping the walls for secret doors. He found three. That's quite enough.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Do bite the gold; it's real this time.
- Ah, the Khazad. Shall I make a coin vanish and come back? No? You never did like that trick.
- Welcome, welcome! Our court hasn't cheated a dwarf in weeks. I swear it on somebody's beard.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You've been telling the neighbours our gold turns into leaves. That only happened once.
- Your merchants called my ambassador a swindler. Accurately, but still.
- Frowning won't make you any taller. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Count it twice; I know you will.
- Done. And look, the coins will still be there in the morning!
- A bargain! Even a dwarf can see this one is real.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The vaults have opened! Is someone ill? Has a dwarf ever done this before?
- Thank you! I shall have it appraised by a dwarf, to be safe.
- How kind. It goes in the treasury, which is real. Mostly.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You've weighed it too carefully for my taste.
- That deal has fewer laughs in it than a dwarven funeral.
- We'd sign, but you'd only test our signature for illusions, and it would fail.

#### Agrees to peace
- Down you go under your mountain, and count something.
- Very well. The circus will leave your mountain passes alone, for now.
- Your cannons are giving my jesters headaches. Peace, peace!

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The mines under Jubilee still need diggers.
- No. Our Taskmasters have learned to say please in dwarvish, and they're dying to practise.
- Stop now? Your vaults aren't even half empty.

#### Rejects a demand
- Gold, from us? You must have us confused with someone honest.
- No. Your vaults are deeper than our pockets.
- Tribute? Our conjurers will make you a chest of it. It vanishes at sunrise, mind.

### Balseraphs → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- Centaurs and giants and lamia! The Freaks of Jubilee are dying to meet your citizens.
- A king who never grows up! We never grow up either. We shall be the best of playmates.
- Greetings. You take in every odd creature in Erebus, and so do we. Ours just end up in cages.

#### Declares war
- Your menagerie is far too fine to waste on a kingdom. It belongs under the big tent.
- Pull your head into your shell, turtle; our Harlequins are going to knock on it.
- We have always wanted a centaur act.

#### Refuses to talk
- Hide in your shell. We'll wait.
- No talks. Your giants make the tent poles shake.
- Your envoy was half horse. I only speak to whole people.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Bring your lamia; the court has so many questions about scales.
- Welcome, dear confederacy. Any new species to show us this season?
- Come in! We both rule a crowd of oddities, so let us compare.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlements gave asylum to our runaway slaves. Very kind, and very annoying.
- Your centaurs keep sneering at my Freaks. They're sensitive.
- You gather every misfit in Erebus and then look down on mine?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Let it draw our peoples closer, or at least into the same tent.
- Done. Send it by centaur; they're so quick.
- A bargain! Your royal bureaucrats will adore the paperwork.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Is it alive? Please say it's alive!
- Thank you! Your settlements are so generous with other people's things.
- How thoughtful. We'll give it a cage of its own.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That's too sensible to be any fun.
- A royal offer, and a royally dull one.
- Even our two-headed councillor disagrees with itself less than it disagrees with this. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Back into your shell with you.
- Very well. Keep your centaurs, for now.
- Truce! Your settlements are so far apart that burning them is exhausting.

#### Refuses peace
- Not until I have a giant for the tent-pole act.
- No. Your shell has only just started to crack.
- Stop? But you've only just retreated, and that's the best part.

#### Rejects a demand
- You take in everyone else's runaways; take your tribute from them.
- No. Grow up first.
- This isn't the way we do things around here. Ha! I've always wanted to say that to you.

### Balseraphs → Lanun

#### First contact
- Sailors! Your captains come all the way to our waters for the wine, you know. We put things in it.
- The Lanun. You keep Dreamers with needles in them for your Overlords. We keep madmen too, but ours sing.
- Pirates! We love pirates. They're jesters with boats.

#### Declares war
- Your galleys would make lovely floats for the parade.
- You plunder our coasts and we plunder your crews. It's fair, which is very unlike us.
- Every pirate dreams of treasure. We dream of pirates in chains, dancing the hornpipe.

#### Refuses to talk
- Go and drown somewhere.
- No talks. Your sailors kept stealing the spoons.
- Sail away, and take the smell of fish with you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Have some wine; it's the vintage your captains keep stealing.
- Ahoy! See, I can talk like you too. What have you brought me?
- Welcome, sea-thief! Any new songs from the far islands?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your privateers stole our whole wine harvest. Again.
- You came by ship, so I assume you came to rob us. Go on.
- Your Dreamers have been dreaming about us. I don't like being dreamt about.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Shake on it, and count your rings afterwards.
- Done. A pirate's word and a madman's oath; what could possibly go wrong?
- A bargain! Toast it with our wine, which you'll steal later anyway.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present from the sea! Did it belong to someone who's now at the bottom of it?
- Thank you! It shall hang in the hall beside the figureheads we kept.
- Pirates giving things away? The tides must be turning.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That deal leaks.
- I've seen better offers floating face down in the harbour.
- We'd accept, but you'd sail off with it before it was paid for.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Plunder someone without a sense of humour next time.
- Very well. The wine harbours are open again, and the poison is optional.
- Let's stop. Your sailors sing better when they're not drowning.

#### Refuses peace
- A ship of my own first, and yours is right there.
- No. Your captains still owe me for a vintage.
- Stop? The sharks have only just arrived.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Raid for it, like a proper pirate.
- No. Try charm; I hear some of your captains have it.
- Sharing is for crews, and we are not your crew.

### Balseraphs → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- Elves! The pretty ones! Your Summer Court must throw such wonderful parties.
- The Ljosalfar. You dance only at Beltane; we dance all year round. We shall teach you.
- Greetings, children of the leaves. Our Freaks have never seen a treant. Have you one to spare?

#### Declares war
- Your forest would make the most wonderful stage, once the trees are out of the way.
- Elves in cages sing so beautifully. We'd like a choir.
- The Summer Court is over. Welcome to the Carnival Court.

#### Refuses to talk
- Go and hug a tree.
- No talks. Your envoy kept trying to plant things in the throne room.
- Rustle off.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Come and dance; the musicians have been waiting all night.
- Ah, the elves. Did you bring your fawns? The Freaks adore them.
- Welcome! Our gardens are poisonous, but very pretty; you'll feel right at home.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your rangers shot my jugglers out of the trees. Very rude, and very accurate.
- You look at us as if we were a blight on your forest. What?
- Has the Summer Court come to scold the Carnival?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Elves are lovely to trade with; they never notice the trick until spring.
- Done. Seal it with a song.
- A bargain! Plant it and see what grows.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Something from the forest! Does it bloom, or bite?
- Thank you! I'll wear it in my hair at the next masque.
- How kind. We'll keep it well away from the bonfires.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That deal would take a century to ripen.
- Too slow, too green, and far too sensible.
- We'd say yes, but your trees are listening, and I don't trust trees.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, and a dance to seal it! Then off to your groves.
- Very well. The forest may keep its elves, for now.
- My Harlequins keep getting splinters, so yes, peace.

#### Refuses peace
- Not until I have an elf for every season of the masque.
- No. Your ancient forests would make such a lovely bonfire.
- Stop? Your treants have only just started walking.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. The oak doesn't bend, and neither does the jester.
- You want gifts? Go and ask your Fellowship.
- Tribute to the Summer Court? It's always winter in our pockets.

### Balseraphs → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp! One of your lords once danced for our court, diving into the mud for a coin. We still sing the song.
- Come, people, come, behold, the gnomes who make their men of gold! Oh, they're iron? Never mind.
- Clockwork toys that walk! Will you sell us one? Will you sell us two?

#### Declares war
- Our mud pits are empty and our vipers are bored. Send us some more of your diggers.
- Your golems are the finest toys in Erebus, and we never could keep our hands off other children's toys.
- Clockwork and courage against Harlequins and madness. Place your bets!

#### Refuses to talk
- No talks. You'll only bring up that business with the mud.
- Go back to your workshop and wind something.
- Your golem envoy didn't laugh at a single joke. Out.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Did you bring a golem? Please say you brought a golem.
- Welcome, little craftsman. We let all your people go in the end. Well, most of them.
- Ah, the Luchuirp, Kilmorph's darlings. What shall we build, or break, today?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems trampled our travelling show. The bearded lady is furious.
- You've told everyone about the mud and the viper. It was a game, and your people won! Why sulk?
- Glaring isn't becoming on such a small face.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Fair, square, and wound up tight.
- Done! A brilliant light in darkness shines, a piece of gold from muddy mines.
- A bargain! And no vipers hidden in it, I promise.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Does it tick? Oh, please say it ticks.
- It shall sit in the gallery beside our old mud pit. How fitting!
- How lovely. Kilmorph must be very forgiving.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Not nearly enough gold in it to dive for.
- Too fair, too square, too dwarvish.
- We'd sign it, but you'd only build a golem to read it back to us.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! The game is won, and both sides applaud.
- Very well, little ones. Run home, as one of you did before.
- Let's stop. Our Mimics can't steal anything worth having from a golem.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The pit is dug, and the viper is hungry.
- No. I want a golem of my very own.
- Stop? Your golems have barely been dented.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want gold? Dive for it, like old times.
- No. Wind up a golem and send it to fetch some.
- Tribute? We know how your people like to earn their gold: head first, in the mud.

### Balseraphs → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim! People who worship the truth. Oh dear. We shall have to be very careful what we say.
- Children of the sun! We prefer torchlight; it's kinder to masks.
- Greetings from Jubilee. We ride Sand Lions too, you know. Ours wear little hats.

#### Declares war
- Your Lugus loves the truth, and the truth is that we're bored. War!
- The sun shows everything. Let's see how bright it is with the shutters closed.
- Your Radiant Guard glows so prettily. We'd like to snuff them out one by one.

#### Refuses to talk
- Too bright to talk. My eyes hurt.
- No. You'd only ask me what I really meant.
- Go and shine somewhere else.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Take off that honest face and put on a mask; it's a party.
- Welcome, sun-folk! We lit a thousand candles for you. One of them is a trick.
- Ah, the Malakim. Tell me a truth and I'll tell you a lie, and we'll see which one you believe.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars keep telling our slaves the truth. It upsets them terribly.
- You stare as though you can see right through our masks. Rude. What is it?
- The sun has come to judge us again. What now?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! And I promise that's the truth. This time.
- Done. Lugus would approve; I barely lied at all.
- A bargain, struck in broad daylight! How novel.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Is it sand? I love sand. Thank you, sun-folk!
- Thank you! We'll hang it where the sun can see it.
- How kind. Your god must be smiling. Ours is laughing.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your deal is so honest I can't find the joke in it.
- That offer burns like noon. Come back at midnight.
- Too much daylight in it. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Go back to your sun, and leave us our shadows.
- Very well. Truth wins. Don't tell anyone.
- Let's stop; my masks are melting.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your Radiant Guard would make lovely lanterns for the carnival.
- No. I want to see the sun set on your empire.
- Stop? But there are still so many lies left to tell your people.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Let the sun pay you.
- No. And that's the honest truth, which you love so much.
- The light reveals all, you say. Then it reveals that our purse is empty.

### Balseraphs → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels! Real ones! You carve prayers into your own skin, I hear. How wonderfully theatrical.
- You broke the Compact to fight demons, and we keep demons as nursemaids. This should be fun.
- Greetings, grim ones. You look so much like demons that I nearly offered you a treat.

#### Declares war
- You hate demons and we keep them as pets. One of us has to go, and the pets have voted.
- Let's see whether angels' wings can be clipped to fit a costume.
- Your host forsook its own gods to fight. Let's see how it fares against a madhouse.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talks. You'd only smash something of ours.
- You frightened the imps. Go away.
- Angels never laugh, and I never talk to people who never laugh.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Don't mind the Balor in the corner; it's on a leash.
- Ah, the winged ones. Any good stories from hell?
- Welcome! You fight demons and we tease them. We're on the same side, sort of.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your soldiers killed our summoners and smashed the circle. Do you know how hard it is to find a good Balor?
- You glower as if I smelled of brimstone. It's perfume. Mostly.
- Speak quickly, angel. You're scaring the jugglers.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Now back to your war; don't trip on your wings.
- Done. Even angels have to go shopping, it seems.
- A bargain! I shall carve it on an arm, the way you do. Somebody's arm.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from heaven! Or from wherever it is you live now.
- Thank you! Is it a feather? I collect feathers.
- How kind. I'll keep it away from the imps; they get jealous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Not enough fun in it, and far too much righteousness.
- That deal is as grim as a sermon in hell.
- Sign it? You'd only smite us for the handwriting.

#### Agrees to peace
- The hells are more your sort of party anyway. Peace!
- Very well. You may keep your wings.
- Put the hammers down; you're ruining the scenery.

#### Refuses peace
- Only once I have an angel for the top of the tent.
- No. You killed my summoners, and I keep score.
- Stop? But you're so much fun when you're angry.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for your holy war? Ask Arawn. Oh, wait, you left.
- No. You'd only spend it on hammers.
- Smite me if you like. You'll still be poorer than we are.

### Balseraphs → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim! You once sent a very pretty spy to our court. We kept the mirror she whispered into. Would you like it back?
- Gate-openers! You want to end the world? But the party has barely started!
- Greetings, doom-mongers. Your last guest at court stayed a very long time, and left us quite a souvenir.

#### Declares war
- You want the world to end. We want it to go on forever, so we can keep laughing at it.
- Your spy whispered our secrets into a mirror. Now we'll whisper yours into a grave.
- Nobody ends the world before the finale. We're coming to close your gates.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now; the world is ending, didn't you hear?
- No talks. The last Sheaim we let into the palace was a spy, and look how that turned out.
- Go and stare into your gates.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Is the world ending today? No? Then let's have tea.
- Ah, the Sheaim. Keep your mirrors covered while you're here; we know how you use them.
- Welcome, fellow monsters! Do the gates still sing at night?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- We found another of your spies at the masquerade. That's the third this season.
- Your gates keep spitting demons onto our roads. They're stealing the act.
- You want the end of everything, and I want you out of my throne room. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Enjoy it while the world lasts.
- Done. No mirrors, no gates, no spies. Promise?
- A bargain! I shall laugh about it at the end of the world.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Is it a bomb? I love bombs. Thank you, doom-cult!
- That goes on the shelf beside the mirror we confiscated.
- How sweet. A present, just before the apocalypse.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Why buy anything when the world is ending?
- That deal ends badly, like everything you touch.
- Your ink smells of Armageddon. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Now go and sulk in your gates about the world still being here.
- Very well. The end of the world can wait; the carnival can't.
- We'd like the world to last at least until the next masque, so yes.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. We're closing your gates one by one, and it's such fun.
- No. We remember your spy, and we always repay a courtesy.
- Stop? You wanted an ending, and we're giving you yours.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Everything's ending anyway; what would you do with it?
- No. Take it out of the apocalypse fund.
- Ask your spies to steal it. They're good at that.

### Balseraphs → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar! You traded away laughter and music for a few extra centuries? The worst bargain ever struck.
- Shades! You walk through walls. Can you walk through our hall of mirrors? We'd love to watch you try.
- Greetings, grey ones. Our court is full of ghosts too, but ours live inside our heads.

#### Declares war
- You gave up feeling for knowledge. Let's see if you've kept the ability to feel afraid.
- Hard to kill, are you? Our Harlequins love a challenge.
- A people without laughter is a crime, and Jubilee is the court that judges it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talks. You never smile, and I can't bear it.
- Go and fade somewhere else.
- Your envoy was half fog. I spoke to the half that was there, and it said nothing.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Do try the food. Oh, you can't taste it. Pity.
- Welcome, grey one. Have you remembered how to laugh yet? We can help.
- Ah, the Sidar. Come and watch the masque; it might remind you of something.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades crept into the masquerade and stood there, not laughing. It ruined the evening.
- You look at us like naughty children. We are naughty children, with armies. What?
- Oh, the gloom has arrived.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! Try not to get too excited.
- Done. You'll outlive it, but we'll enjoy it more.
- A bargain! Smile. No? Fine.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Did you feel anything when you gave it? Anything at all?
- Thank you! We'll throw a party in your honour; you needn't come.
- How kind. Grey, but kind.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Too grey, too careful, too dead.
- That deal has all the joy of a shade's wedding.
- We'd sign it, but you'd still be around to collect in a thousand years.

#### Agrees to peace
- Fade back into your mists and your books. Peace.
- Very well. Fade away now.
- Fighting you is like stabbing fog, and twice as dull. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- First I want to know whether shades can scream.
- No. You have a thousand years to wait for peace; wait a little longer.
- Stop? We've only just made you feel something.

#### Rejects a demand
- You don't even enjoy things. Why would you want ours?
- No. Buy it with your soul. Oh, wait.
- Tribute to ghosts? We burn paper money for those.

### Balseraphs → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Unseelie! Masks, poison and betrayal; we'll get along beautifully until one of us wins.
- Greetings, Winter Court. You run academies of persuasion, I hear. We skip the lessons and simply take the mind.
- Dark elves! You betray your allies and we forget ours. Neither of us has any friends, so let's be friends.

#### Declares war
- Your assassins are so very graceful. We'd like them as acrobats.
- You call yourselves masters of intrigue. A mind-mage needs no intrigue; it is enough to reach in.
- The Winter Court against the Carnival Court! Only one of us can rule the night.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talks. Every word you say has a knife in it.
- Go and scheme somewhere else.
- I already know what you're thinking. I'd rather not hear you say it as well.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]! Leave the daggers at the door. All of them. Yes, that one too.
- Ah, the Svartalfar. Shall we plot something together, purely for sport?
- Welcome, sister court! Whose ruin shall we arrange tonight?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Twelve of your assassins in my palace? I counted fourteen. Two of them are mine now.
- Your persuaders tried to turn my Puppets. Puppets have no minds to turn, darling.
- You smile like a knife. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed! I'll check it for poison later, and you can check it for madness.
- Done. Two liars shaking hands. How sweet.
- A bargain! Faster than stealing, and nearly as much fun.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Winter Court! Which part of it is poisoned?
- Thank you! My taster will try it first. And then my taster's taster.
- How generous. I'll be suspicious for days; it's lovely.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offers always have a second lining.
- I can read the clause you didn't write. No.
- Too clever, darling, and not nearly clever enough.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Until one of us gets bored.
- Very well. You spin your webs, and we'll pull our strings.
- Let's stop. The game is more fun when we're both pretending to be friends.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your whole court would look lovely in motley.
- No. You'd only use the peace to sharpen something.
- Stop? But the betrayal hasn't even happened yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Steal it; isn't that your art?
- Persuade me. Go on. Your academies must have taught you something.
- Tribute from Jubilee? The jester bows, and gives you nothing.

## Bannor

### Bannor → Amurites

#### First contact
- The Children of Kylorin. Our priests have read of your schools, where necromancy is licensed instead of forbidden. We will be watching your scholars closely.
- Greetings, mages. Our cities are gracious and our friendship unwavering, so long as your arts stay within the bounds of Law.
- You worship magic for its own sake, we are told. The Bannor worship Junil, and we have seen what power without a master becomes.

#### Declares war
- You regulate the dark arts when you should root them out. The priesthood has judged, and the Orders march.
- Your schools have bred one necromancer too many. We come to close them.
- Kylorin's own pupils once drowned Patria in wickedness. We will not wait for his children to repeat it.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your envoy argued doctrine like a lawyer and lied like a conjurer. We have heard enough.
- There is nothing to discuss until your necromancers are in chains.
- Send your clever words elsewhere. The Bannor answer with steel.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your adepts have stood with us against the Veil, and the Halls remember it.
- Come, make your case, but be quick. Evil's reach grows by the year, and even scholars must prepare for the end.
- Speak freely, mage. Your people keep their own laws strictly, and the Bannor respect any people with laws.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- There could have been nobility in your schools. Instead you license the very arts that feed the hells.
- Our confessors report Amurite necromancers at work again, permitted by your own tribunals. Explain this.
- You stand above good and evil, you say. No one stands above them; they only fall between.

#### Accepts a deal
- A just and equitable deal for us both, I think.
- Agreed. Let our scribes and your scholars record it with equal care.
- Done. The Bannor keep their word, and we expect the same of those who study the arcane.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our thanks. Generosity is a virtue even Junil's sternest priest must honour.
- A gift freely given. Perhaps your schools teach more than spells after all.
- We thank you. This will go to arming the Orders against the dark you claim to study and we mean to end.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Our gold will not be spent on your laboratories.
- We cannot accept this. It asks the Bannor to trust magic, and magic has never earned our trust.
- Unbalanced and unjust. Bring us a fair offer or none.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Turn your arts against the Veil, and you will find the Bannor beside you.
- We accept. Remember that the Law spared you, and keep your necromancers in their cells.
- Enough. I am tired of old men dreaming up wars for young men to die in.

#### Refuses peace
- The Crusade has been called. It does not turn back for a scholar's apology.
- No. Your schools still teach what should never be taught.
- Peace will come when your tribunals hang necromancers instead of licensing them.

#### Rejects a demand
- A just ruler provides for the needs of their people, but not like this. Look to your own treasuries.
- The Bannor tithe to Junil and to no academy. No.
- You ask for gold to fund your studies? Study humility first.

### Bannor → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- So this is the mad court. Our fathers swore in the fires of hell to war against chaos forever. You are what they meant.
- Greetings, Balseraphs. Our priests have sermons about your Harlequins, and none of them end well for you.
- A kingdom of slaves, masks and madness. Know that the Bannor see what lies behind every mask.

#### Declares war
- Our forefathers bound themselves and every child of theirs to battle chaos. Today we keep that oath on your borders.
- Your Taskmasters drag free men into chains for the amusement of a madhouse. The Orders march to break those chains.
- The jest is over. The Law has come to Jubilee.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not treat with chaos. It cannot keep its word, and you would only laugh at ours.
- Your heralds speak in riddles. Ours speak in drums.
- Civilized men know talk is better than war, but your court is not civilized.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. We will listen, though the Orders keep their hands on their hilts in your presence.
- You have kept your word to us so far, which surprises our priests more than anyone.
- Welcome. Leave your jesters at the border, and we may yet do honest business.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our scouts found Bannor captives performing in your circus. You will explain this, and then you will release them.
- You laugh as though nothing matters. Everything matters, and Junil keeps the account.
- Your Puppets have been seen in our free lands. Be very careful what you say next.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even a mad court can make a fair bargain, it seems.
- Done. We will hold you to every letter of it, whatever game you think you are playing.
- Signed. The terms are plain; mind that they stay plain.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Jubilee. We will have our priests bless it before we touch it, but we thank you.
- Our thanks. Perhaps there is something in your court besides madness.
- Generosity from the Balseraphs? We will note it, with some astonishment.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offers twist like your jesters.
- We will not trade with a court that keeps men in cages for sport.
- That deal hides a trick, as your deals always do. Refused.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Free the captives you hold, and keep your Harlequins far from our villages.
- We accept, though our priests will pray against your madness every day of it.
- Very well. The Law rests for a season. It does not forget.

#### Refuses peace
- Every Order is in the field. There will be no peace while a single Bannor wears your chains.
- You offer peace with a painted smile. We will see your true face first.
- No. Chaos must be broken, not bargained with.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a madman's court? The Orders would sooner die in the field.
- No. Slink back to your circus, thief.
- You demand like a child and threaten like one. The answer is no.

### Bannor → Calabim

#### First contact
- The Calabim. Your nobles drink the blood of their own people. Know that the Bannor are the natural enemy of everything you are.
- So the vampire lords have a kingdom now. Our priests had hoped the Age of Ice finished your kind.
- We greet you because Law requires courtesy. It does not require us to forget what feeds in your castles.

#### Declares war
- Your cities are farms and your people are cattle. The Orders come to set the herds free.
- Junil commands us to bring Law to the dark places of the world. There is no place darker than your Grand Broods' cellars.
- War does not determine who is right, only who is left. When this is done, there will be no vampires left.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not sit at a table with those who drink from the living.
- Your envoys smile with too many teeth. No more talk.
- There is nothing to say to the Calabim that a crusader's blade cannot say better.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME], and keep your hunger far from Bannor lands.
- We have kept the peace with you because Law demands it. Do not mistake that for friendship.
- You may speak. Our confessors are present, and they are not afraid of you.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Bannor villages along your border are emptying by night. We know what hunts there. Speak, if you dare.
- There is no nobility in you, only appetite. What do you want?
- Every word you say tastes of the grave. Be brief.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Let it be paid in gold, and nothing else.
- Done. We trade with you as we would handle a blade: carefully, and by the hilt.
- The terms are just. That is more than can be said of your rule.

#### Thanks for a gift
- We accept this with thanks, and our priests will see that it is clean.
- We will not ask whose blood paid for this, but we thank you.
- Our thanks. It changes nothing of what we think of your cellars.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Nothing that passes through your hands comes away clean.
- We will not barter with the masters of the herds.
- Refused. The Bannor do not grow fat on trade with the undead.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Feed on no Bannor, and the Orders will stay on their side of the river.
- We accept, for now. Your herds will be waiting when the Law returns.
- Very well. Let there be no more disappearances in the night.

#### Refuses peace
- No peace until every Grand Brood is ash.
- No. Your people are still in their pens.
- Peace with the vampire lords would only mean a slower slaughter. We refuse.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want tribute from the Bannor? You have drunk enough from mankind.
- No. Find your nourishment somewhere other than our treasury.
- We give nothing to the Calabim but steel and prayers for your victims.

### Bannor → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs of Braduk. We remember the fire, the pit, and the hell your goddess dragged our fathers into. We remember Orthus.
- The Ember Banner. The Bannor have been at war with your kind since the day we stepped out of your sacred flame.
- You burned our soldiers alive to honour Bhall. Know that every Bannor child is taught the names of the ones you burned.

#### Declares war
- The Bannor were forged for one purpose: to break the Clan. The war of the Age of Rebirth resumes today.
- We walked out of hell through your fires once. Now we walk back in, and Braduk will burn for its own sins.
- The priesthood has spoken the old judgement against the Clan. No orc camp will stand between our walls and the sea.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with the people who threw our sons into Bhall's fire.
- Get back to your burning pits. There is no word between us but the sword.
- The Bannor speak to orcs only across a shield wall.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. Our priests do not believe orcs can keep a treaty. Prove them wrong.
- You have kept the peace, which is more than any orc has done before you. Say what you came to say.
- One of your own was raised among us once, and the Bannor learned that orcs can learn. Speak.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your warbands raided another of our fortress farms. Every one of them will be repaid in kind.
- I smell the smoke of Braduk on you. What do you want?
- Orthus once laughed at Bannor women too, until one of them gutted him. Choose your words.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. We will see whether an orc keeps a bargain.
- Done. Hold to it, and the Orders will hold back.
- The terms are fair. Mark them well; the Bannor do not forgive a broken word.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The Clan gives instead of taking? We accept, and wonder what it means.
- There is more in you than fire and hunger, it seems. Thank you.
- Generous. Our priests will not believe it, so we shall keep it as proof.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not arm the hands that raid our villages.
- No. Everything the Clan owns was taken from someone.
- That is a raid with a seal on it. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. It will not last, for it never has, but we will honour it while it does.
- We accept. Keep your warbands home, and our garrisons will stay in their forts.
- Enough, then. Our soldiers are weary of digging orc graves.

#### Refuses peace
- The Crusade has been launched. Every man has taken his sword, and the legions march on Braduk.
- No. Our fathers' screams still echo in your fire-pits.
- Peace with the Clan has always been a breath before the next raid. Not this time.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Clan? Come and take it, and meet every Bannor man and woman with a blade.
- No. We paid you in blood for an age; the account is closed.
- The orc asks the Bannor for gold. The Bannor answer with iron.

### Bannor → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. You let the weak die and called it strength. The Bannor call it damnation.
- We are told you hunted alongside Mulcarn's winter, preying on those the White Hand cast out. The Law has a long memory.
- Greetings, northmen. Our villages are forts and our farmers are soldiers. Your wolves will find no easy prey here.

#### Declares war
- You abandon your own wounded to the wolves. We have come to teach you what Law is.
- The pack has raided our free lands for the last time. The Orders hunt now.
- Your people kneel to nothing but strength. Then kneel.

#### Refuses to talk
- Diplomacy is not a trick of the weak, whatever your people believe. But it is wasted on you.
- We do not bargain with wolves. We build walls against them.
- Go back to your frozen wastes. There is nothing to say.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. You have kept the peace with us; perhaps the pack can learn order after all.
- Come, sit. Even a Doviello is welcome in our halls if Law is kept.
- Your hunters are strong and fearless. If you ever turn them against true evil, the Bannor will fight beside you.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders left one of our farm-castles burning and its children in the snow. Speak, before I lose my patience.
- You chose the wolf's way over the ways of men. What now?
- You smell of blood and woodsmoke. Be quick.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair deal, kept fairly, may yet teach the pack something.
- Done. Keep your word as we keep ours.
- We will trade with the wolf so long as its teeth stay sheathed.

#### Thanks for a gift
- From the pack, a gift? We thank you, and hope it is the first of many better habits.
- So the pack can share after all. Our thanks.
- We accept this with gratitude, and with some surprise.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would only spend it on your raiders.
- The pack takes, it does not trade. No.
- That bargain profits wolves, not men.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and hunt the beasts of the wild, not the people of the Law.
- We accept, and may the pack learn that a treaty is stronger than a fang.
- Very well. May you use this peace to become something better than a wolf.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The pack only begs for peace when it is starving. We remember what it does when fed.
- The Orders ride on. Your raids will end with your strongholds.
- There will be no peace while Bannor children are buried in the snow you left them in.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the pack? The Bannor feed their own weak, and that is all.
- No. You are not strong enough to take it, and we will not give it.
- Howl if you must. The answer remains no.

### Bannor → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim, who tended the broken through every age of the world. The Bannor honour your monks, though we think a sword would serve them better.
- Keepers of the holy places, the soldiers of Junil greet you. Where your shrines are threatened, call on us.
- You witnessed the Compact itself. Then you know as we do how much evil still waits to be loosed upon Erebus.

#### Declares war
- You have made peace with demons and called it wisdom. The priesthood names that complicity.
- Mercy without Law is weakness, and weakness opens the door to the pit. We will guard your shrines ourselves.
- It grieves us to march on gentle people. But you shelter what should be judged, and Junil does not leave judgement undone.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not be lectured on gentleness by those who let evil walk free.
- Your monks may pray for us. We will not hear them now.
- No talks. Words were your choice; the sword was forced on ours.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. The noble halls of the Bannor will ever be open to the Elohim.
- Come, friend. Between your monks and our Orders, the shrines of Erebus will want for no protector.
- Speak freely. There are few in this world the Bannor trust, and you are among them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You signed a peace with the Infernal. Our priests cannot understand it, and neither can I.
- Gentleness is a virtue until evil takes advantage of it. What do you want?
- Your pilgrims preach against our Crusade in our own markets. Explain yourselves.

#### Accepts a deal
- Honest terms from honest people. We expected nothing less of the Elohim.
- Agreed, with gladness. May the shrines prosper by it.
- Done. Your word is as sacred as your sites, and ours is no less.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, friend. The Elohim give as they have always given, without counting.
- Our gratitude. This will help keep the Veil from the shrines you tend.
- Generous, as the stories say. The Bannor will not forget it.

#### Turns down a deal
- We cannot, friend. It would leave our garrisons short when the darkness comes.
- Not this, though we wish we could. The Crusade's needs come first.
- No. Even between friends, the terms must be just.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. We should never have stood against each other while the hells rise.
- We accept. Return to your shrines, and let the Orders guard their gates.
- So be it. May the years of peace between us outlast this foolish war many times over.

#### Refuses peace
- Not until you renounce your treaty with the demons.
- No. Your gentleness has armed our enemies once too often.
- We cannot stop. The judgement has been given, however much it grieves us.

#### Rejects a demand
- Alms for the poor are a holy thing, but our soldiers must eat too. No.
- We will defend your shrines with our lives. We will not empty our treasury for them.
- It was not for our own sake that we refuse. The Crusade needs every coin.

### Bannor → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori. You follow an angel who turned from the gods. The Bannor keep faith with Junil, who has never turned from us.
- We are told your cities shelter any man who wishes to live without the gods. Some of our own deserters, perhaps.
- You call our faith servitude. We call it the only wall between mankind and the pit.

#### Declares war
- A people who answer to no god answer to no Law. The priesthood has declared you damned.
- Your cities harbour apostates who fled the Bannor. We come to bring them home, and you to judgement.
- You would leave men alone in the dark to fend for themselves. We bring them the light, whether you like it or not.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not hear the gospel of godlessness.
- Your heralds asked us to think for ourselves. We have, and we choose Junil.
- Your people abandoned heaven; we will not abandon it to talk with you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. You are godless, but you are not lawless, and the Bannor respect that much.
- Welcome. Your Adventurers fight the Veil as fiercely as any crusader; on that we can agree.
- Come, make your case. Even heretics are owed a fair hearing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- One of our merchants took a new name in your capital and spat on the faith of his fathers. Why are you here?
- You preach freedom from the gods while the hells grow stronger. Speak quickly.
- There could have been nobility in your people, but you chose pride over faith.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Honest dealing, even from those without faith.
- Done. Our word binds us to believers and heretics alike.
- A fair exchange. Let it be recorded so.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our thanks. The godless can be generous, it seems.
- A gift, freely given. Junil sees it, even if you will not look up.
- We accept, and pray you will one day accept something from us in return.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not fund the cities that steal our faithful.
- Your terms favour those who need no one, and the Bannor need allies. No.
- That is not a just offer, and you know it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Keep your apostates, and we will keep our faithful.
- We accept. The true war is with the hells; let us both remember it.
- Let it end. Even a heretic's blood is precious when the end approaches.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your creed is a door left open to the darkness.
- The Crusade marches until your people bend the knee to something higher than themselves.
- Not yet. Your Adventurers have slain too many crusaders to be forgiven so quickly.

#### Rejects a demand
- You preach that men should provide for themselves. Then provide.
- No. The Bannor tithe to Junil, and you scorn Junil.
- Tribute from the faithful to the faithless? Never.

### Bannor → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus. Our Orders take good fighters from every nation; your riders would be welcome among them.
- Horse lords who sell their lances. We will see whether you sell them to Law or to chaos.
- Greetings, riders. Your clans spent an age raiding each other. The Bannor would teach you discipline, if you would learn.

#### Declares war
- You took the gold of our enemies and rode against our villages. Mercenaries share the judgement of their masters.
- Honour that is for sale is no honour. The Orders will teach your companies what a vow is.
- Your raiders have burned their last Bannor farm. The cavalry of the Law rides now.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not haggle with sellswords in the middle of a war.
- Ride back to your masters, whoever they are this month.
- Your contract is with our enemy. Talk to them.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your companies fought well beside our Orders; the Halls remember it.
- Speak, horse lord. The Crusade always needs swift riders.
- Come in. A Hippus who keeps a contract is worth ten who do not, and you have kept yours.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your riders were seen in the service of the Calabim. Explain why I should hear you.
- You sell your swords to anyone. Even the damned.
- Mercenary, your company burned a Bannor estate last month. Speak quickly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Paid in full, as a contract should be.
- Done. A fair price for fair service.
- Keep to the terms, and your riders will always find work with the Bannor.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Hippus? That is rarer than a free lance. Thank you.
- Our thanks. Perhaps there is more than gold in your hearts.
- Generous. The Orders will toast your clans tonight.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your price is a raid by other means.
- Too dear. The Crusade cannot spend its treasury on one company.
- Refused. We will not pay for lances that may turn on us next season.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Find an honest employer, and ride for the Law next time.
- We accept. The Bannor and the Hippus should be allies, not enemies.
- Very well. Take your companies home; the war is over.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You chose your side when you took their gold.
- The Crusade does not stop for a renegotiated contract.
- Not until your companies have paid in blood for the villages they burned.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to mercenaries? The Bannor pay for service, not for threats.
- No. Earn it, as soldiers should.
- Ride around our walls as long as you like. Every farm here is a fortress.

### Bannor → Illians

#### First contact
- The men of Letum Frigus. Your god broke the Compact and buried the world in ice. Junil remembers, and so do we.
- The White Hand. Those who served the winter have no friends among the Bannor.
- You follow a ruler who would be a god. The Bannor already have one, and Junil does not share a throne.

#### Declares war
- Mulcarn broke the Compact. His servants have no claim on its protection.
- Your ruler reaches for godhood. The priesthood calls that the oldest blasphemy, and the Orders will answer it.
- The long winter is over. We will not let your new lord bring it back.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not speak with the priests of the winter.
- Your envoy's words are as cold as his breath. Go.
- Those who long for the Age of Ice may long for it in silence.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME], but leave the cold outside.
- You have kept your treaty with us. That is more than your god ever did.
- Welcome. We pray you have put the winter behind you, as the world has.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Snow fell on our fields in high summer. We know whose hand that was. Speak.
- Your priests whisper that a new god walks in the north. Our priests call that blasphemy. Choose your next words with care.
- Your people chose the ice once. Have you come to choose it again?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even the cold may trade with the hearth.
- Done. Hold to it; the Bannor will.
- Just terms. Let them stay so.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Warmth from the north at last. We thank you.
- Perhaps the thaw has reached your hearts as well.
- We accept, with gratitude, and with our eyes open.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not feed the priests of the winter.
- That would only arm a would-be god.
- That offer is as barren as the ice. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your caverns and leave our fields green.
- Let the snows stay in the north, and we accept.
- Then go. Junil is patient, and the spring will outlast you.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your god broke the Compact, and his heir would break the world.
- Not until the last temple of the White Hand is cold ash.
- Not while frost still creeps across Bannor fields.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the winter? We have paid it in our dead.
- No. Let your would-be god make gold out of snow.
- The Bannor bow to Junil, not to Letum Frigus.

### Bannor → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demon. Our fathers were prisoners in your hell, and we know your stench. The Bannor have waited for this day since the gate of light closed behind us.
- So the pit has climbed into Erebus. The Bannor were made for this hour.
- One of ours stayed behind in your hell to hold the gate shut, swearing to come back through every demon in it. Have you met Donal Lugh?

#### Declares war
- We marched out of your hell once with the dead behind us. Now we march into your cities.
- Junil's oath binds every Bannor alive: no truce with the pit. The Crusade begins.
- You tear the Order from every city you take. We will tear you from every city you hold.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not bargain with the jailers of our fathers.
- Every word of a demon is a hook. We will hear none of them.
- Go back down. There is nothing a Bannor will say to you but a prayer over your corpse.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. The Law requires that we hear you. It does not require that we believe you.
- We keep this peace because the priests command it. Say what you want, quickly.
- You may speak. Every crusader in this hall has a hand on a blessed blade.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our confessors have been burned in your cities and our temples defiled. Speak, if you dare.
- I can smell the plains of ash on you. What do you want?
- You are hunger and spite wearing a crown. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, in ink and nothing else. Our priests read every clause.
- Done. We keep our word, even to demons, and we keep our oaths against you too.
- The terms are just. That will be a new experience for you.

#### Thanks for a gift
- We take this with blessed gloves, and give it straight to the priests.
- A gift from hell. Our thanks, and our confessors' suspicion.
- We acknowledge your gift. It buys you nothing.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Nothing from the pit is ever paid in full.
- Refused. We know your bargains; we lived inside them.
- We will not trade with those who trade in souls.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. The Bannor do not forget, and neither does Junil.
- We accept, because the Law demands it. The Crusade waits at the border.
- Then keep your hounds in their kennels, and we will keep our swords sharp.

#### Refuses peace
- Every man and woman of the Bannor has taken up the sword. There will be no peace until you are back in the pit.
- Never. We have seen your hell from the inside.
- No. A truce with a demon is a knife held in the other hand.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand from the Bannor? We were your prisoners once. Never again.
- No. Not a coin, not a soul, not a single grain.
- Take your demands back to the fire. That is all we will give you.

### Bannor → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad. A people of order, oaths and stone. The Bannor respect all three.
- Greetings, dwarves. Our capital's markets welcome honest merchants, and we are told you count honestly, if slowly.
- You slept through the Age of Ice under your mountains while our fathers burned in hell. Welcome to the war that came after.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults bulge while the Crusade goes hungry. Kilmorph's children will learn that gold cannot hold a wall.
- You turned away from the war against evil to count your coins. The priesthood has judged that as well.
- Your guns are good and your walls are thick. Bannor discipline is better than both.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not bargain while our men lie dead below your walls.
- Go back under your mountain. We will talk when we have reached your gates.
- Your envoy weighs every word like a coin. We have none to spare.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. A dwarf's word and a Bannor oath; few things in Erebus are as solid.
- Come, friend. Your hammers and our swords stand well together.
- Speak. The Halls have always valued Khazad steel.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your merchants sell powder to the Clan of Embers. Explain that to a Bannor widow.
- You hide in your halls while the world is threatened. What do you want now?
- Your vaults are full and your hearts are shut. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Weighed, counted and just. Agreed.
- Agreed. The Bannor pay in full, as dwarves prefer.
- Done. May both our forges prosper by it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Khazad gold, freely given! Our thanks, friend.
- We are grateful. This will arm many a free-land conscript.
- Generous, and solid. Like your walls.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your price is fair for a merchant, but not for an ally.
- We cannot spend the Crusade's treasury on a single bargain.
- Even a dwarf must see this offer is too heavy on one side.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your forges, and send us your steel instead of your soldiers.
- We accept. Let Bannor and dwarf stand together against the darkness again.
- Agreed. Our quarrel was never worth this much blood.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your guns killed too many of our crusaders.
- Open your gates, and then we will speak of peace.
- Not yet. Your vaults will pay for what your armies did.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a dwarf? Your vaults are fuller than our granaries.
- Our gold is pledged to the war against evil.
- You ask for gold for nothing. Even Kilmorph does not ask that.

### Bannor → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates. You welcome every race to your banner; so do our Orders. We may have much in common.
- Greetings. Your realm is ruled firmly from the throne, and every province answers to it. The Bannor understand such a realm.
- Centaurs and men and giants under one law. That is no small achievement.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements shelter the fugitives of our justice. That shelter ends.
- You have refused to stand against the darkness. The priesthood has spoken.
- Retreat into your core if you like. The Orders are patient besiegers.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not hear your envoys while our crusaders lie in your fields.
- Not now. Your shell can wait for our answer.
- Withdraw your armies, and then we will talk.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your realm is orderly and your word is good. The Bannor value both.
- Come, friend. Your centaurs would make fine knights of the Orders.
- Speak. We remember those who stood with the Law, and you have.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlements give asylum to deserters from our Orders. Explain that.
- Your lamia wield magics our confessors would burn at the stake. Speak.
- Your borders sprawl into lands the Crusade has claimed. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- A bargain worthy of two orderly realms.
- Agreed. Let it draw our peoples closer, as your envoys like to say.
- Done, and every term will be honoured.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The confederacy is generous, as always. Thank you.
- A gift freely given. The Halls will remember it.
- We are grateful. When the vampire lords next devour one of your envoys, the Bannor will remember this kindness.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. It would leave our garrisons short.
- Regretfully, no. The terms favour your settlements too much.
- We cannot. Your royal clerks drafted this to profit the throne alone.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. The Calabim, who ate your ambassador, are a far better target for us both.
- We accept. May our realms be friends again.
- The Law and the throne need not be at war. Peace.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your shell will crack before we stop.
- Our columns march on. Your settlements will learn the Law one by one.
- Not until the fugitives you shelter are returned to us.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? We are not one of your client states.
- No. Your crown commands its own provinces; it does not command ours.
- This is not the way we do things in the Halls. Take your demand elsewhere.

### Bannor → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun. Your ancestors obeyed only the laws they liked and smuggled every fugitive in Patria to freedom. The Bannor are not Patria.
- Greetings, captains. Our harbours are open to honest traders. Our gallows are open to the other kind.
- Sea-rovers with a flexible sense of honour. Know that the Bannor sense of honour does not bend.

#### Declares war
- Your privateers have plundered Bannor ships for the last time. The Law has a navy now.
- You worship the Overlords beneath the waves and drown men to make your Stygian slaves. The priesthood has judged you.
- A captain answers to no one, you say. You will answer to us.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with pirates.
- Your word lasts as long as a tide. We will not waste ink on it.
- Sail away. We will talk when your fleet is at the bottom of the sea.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your ships have carried our crusaders faithfully, [CT_NAME]. The Halls remember.
- Speak, captain. An honest trader is always welcome in Bannor ports.
- Come in. You have kept your word to us, and that is rarer on the sea than pearls.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your ships carried escaped criminals from our harbours again. Explain.
- There is a smell of the Overlords' asylums about you. What do you want?
- Pirate, your crews robbed a Bannor pilgrim ship. Speak quickly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Put it in writing, and keep it written.
- Done. A fair bargain, even with a sea-captain.
- Sealed. May your word prove steadier than the tide.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the sea-rovers! Our thanks; we will not ask where it was found.
- Generous. Perhaps there is an honest captain on the sea after all.
- We accept with thanks. Not every Lanun takes before giving.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That cargo was stolen from someone, and the Law knows it.
- We do not buy what pirates sell.
- Your terms shift like the sea. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your raiders far from Bannor waters.
- We accept. Let the trade ships sail again, and only trade ships.
- The sea is wide enough for both our fleets. Let it be peace.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every pirate in your fleet will hang first.
- The Crusade does not stop at the waterline.
- Not while your raiders still plunder our coasts.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to pirates? Come and take it, if you dare beach your ships here.
- No. Plunder is theft, whatever you call it.
- A just ruler provides for their people. A pirate steals for them. Slink away, thief.

### Bannor → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The Ljosalfar. Our confessors once followed the Ashen Veil into your forest to burn it out. Your rangers shot them from the trees. The Bannor have not forgotten.
- Greetings, elves. You returned from your hidden groves as we returned from hell. Survivors understand each other, or should.
- Children of the forest, the Order greets you. We ask only that you do not shelter the Veil among your trees.

#### Declares war
- Your forests hid the Ashen Veil, and your rangers killed the confessors who came to root it out. Now the Orders come.
- You care for your trees more than for the world. The end comes for both, unless we act.
- The priesthood has judged your Fellowship. Your ancient trees will not shelter you.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not hear the elves who murdered our confessors.
- Go back to your groves. There is nothing to discuss.
- Your words are leaves in the wind. We want deeds.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your forests are clean of the Veil, and the Bannor are grateful.
- Come, friend. Elven archers and Bannor shields would make a fine wall against the dark.
- Speak. The Summer Court has been a good neighbour to the Law.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your druids called our foresters defilers and hanged them from your oaks. Explain.
- You would let the world burn rather than lose a single tree. What do you want?
- Your court would watch the world burn and ask only after its trees. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, and in the old courtly manner.
- Agreed. Let it grow as slowly and as strongly as your oaks.
- Done. You will find no Bannor slow to keep it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The Summer Court is generous; the Halls will remember it.
- This came from your forest, and we will treat it with respect.
- We are grateful, friend. May your forests stay clean of the Veil.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms profit the groves and nothing else.
- The Crusade needs more than leaves.
- We cannot. It is not a just offer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep the Veil out of your forests, and the Orders will stay out of them too.
- We accept, and the trees may grow again.
- So be it. Our quarrel was never with your trees, only with what hid under them.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Our confessors' blood is still on your roots.
- We march until the Veil is gone from your forests.
- Not yet. The elves must learn that the world is bigger than their groves.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Summer Court? You have your forests; be content.
- Those who stand aside in the war against evil get nothing from us.
- Ask your trees for gold. We have none for you.

### Bannor → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp. Kilmorph sheltered your clan beneath the ice while our fathers fought their way out of the fire. Survivors should stand together.
- Greetings, heirs of the Open-Skiers. Your golems never tire and never desert; our drill sergeants envy you.
- Small folk with mighty works. The Bannor respect craft and discipline, and you have both in abundance.

#### Declares war
- Your golems guard your mines while the Crusade bleeds alone. The priesthood has judged that neutrality.
- You build soldiers of clay and iron that can neither pray nor repent. The Orders will show you what faith does to clockwork.
- The winter broke your forefathers' golems. The Bannor will break yours.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not talk while your golems stand on Bannor soil.
- Your envoy was a machine. The Law does not parley with machines.
- Go back to your workshops and mend what we have broken.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our crusaders still speak of your golems holding the line beside them.
- Come, friend. We both have reason to hate the mad court of the Balseraphs; shall we discuss it?
- Speak. The Bannor are always glad to see the children of Kilmorph walking under the open sky again.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems trampled a Bannor village and did not even stop. Explain.
- You sell your golems to anyone with gold, even to the damned. What now?
- Your enchanters dig up cursed relics and then wonder why demons follow. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Well made, like your clockwork. We accept.
- Agreed. Luchuirp work has always been worth its price.
- Done. May Kilmorph and Junil both look kindly on it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our thanks. Luchuirp craftsmanship is a gift in itself.
- A golem for the Orders? It will never tire of guarding a gate. We are grateful.
- We accept with gratitude. Your folk give the way they build: solidly.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your enchanters ask more than the Crusade can spare.
- Refused, with regret. The free lands need that gold for their conscripts.
- We cannot. Not even a golem is worth that much.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. Kilmorph's children and Junil's should never have fought.
- We accept. Send your golems back to the mines, and we will send our men home.
- So be it. There are worse things in the dark than either of us.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems still stand on our fields.
- The Crusade marches until your workshops fall silent.
- Not yet. Our dead are owed more than an apology from a forge.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the workshops? Build your own fortune, as you always have.
- No. The Bannor need their gold for soldiers of flesh.
- You ask too much, friend. Even a golem would know better.

### Bannor → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim. Where the Order keeps the Law, your Empyrean weighs each case on its merits. We shall see which serves the world better.
- Greetings, children of the sun. Your faith is bright and your hearts are honest; the Bannor ask no more of a neighbour.
- You were led into the light out of the snow, as we were led out of the fire. Both our peoples owe their lives to a faith.

#### Declares war
- Your Vicars judge every case on its merits and let the guilty walk free on clever arguments. Junil's Law does not haggle.
- The Empyrean has crept into Bannor towns and taught our people to question their priests. That ends now.
- The sun shines on all alike, they say. So does a crusader's blade.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not debate law with those who have only opinions.
- Your Vicars may consult among themselves. We will not consult with you.
- No talks until your Radiant Guard has left our lands.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. The Order and the Empyrean disagree on much, but never on the darkness.
- Come, friend of the sun. Your Radiant Guard beside our crusaders would be a sight to make the hells tremble.
- Speak. The Halls are always open to the honest folk of the desert.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars preach in our markets that Law without wisdom is tyranny. Is that your message too?
- You shine your light on our Crusade and call what you see cruelty. Speak.
- Your judges set free a man our confessors had condemned. Explain.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair bargain, judged on its merits, as your priests would say.
- Agreed. The sun and the sword may trade honestly.
- Done. Lugus values truth, and the Law values a kept word.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our thanks. The Malakim give as freely as the sun shines.
- From the desert, with friendship. The Bannor are grateful.
- Generous. Your Vicars teach charity well, whatever else they teach.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Weigh it on any scale you like; it still comes out unjust.
- We cannot spare it. Every coin we have is pledged to the Crusade.
- Not even your own judges would call this fair.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Two holy peoples should not spill each other's blood while the hells rise.
- We accept. Let the Order and the Empyrean argue in temples, not on battlefields.
- Very well. May the sun shine on both our lands, and the Law keep them.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your doctrine has spread too far into our cities to be left alone.
- The Crusade goes on until the Empyrean bows to the Law.
- Not yet. Wisdom is no defence against judgement.

#### Rejects a demand
- The Empyrean gives an equal voice to small and great, you say. Then hear the Bannor's: no.
- Ask the sun. It gives freely; we cannot.
- Tribute to the desert? Our granaries feed soldiers, not sermons.

### Bannor → Mercurians

#### First contact
- The Mercurians. You broke the Compact to fight hell with your own hands. The Bannor kept it, and fought with ours.
- Greetings, rebel host. Our fathers were carried out of hell by an angel who kept faith. We know what angels can do.
- You fight the demons and care nothing for the men they butcher. The Bannor fight for both.

#### Declares war
- You broke the Compact that holds the gods back from Erebus. Whatever your cause, the Law cannot permit it.
- You have grown as merciless as the demons you hunt, and the priesthood has seen it.
- An angel who disobeys is a rebel, and the Bannor were made to fight rebels.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not hear oath-breakers, however bright their wings.
- Go back to your war in hell.
- No talks. You trample our dead to reach your enemy and call it holy.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. The war against the pit has no better soldiers than yours and ours.
- Come, warrior of heaven. The Crusade and the host march against the same enemy, whatever we think of each other's oaths.
- Speak. Any news from the hells is welcome in the Halls.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your soldiers trampled a Bannor village chasing a single demon. Our dead are not your concern, I suppose?
- You broke the gods' own treaty, and you dare lecture us on duty?
- Your contempt for mortals is carved on your faces as plainly as your prayers. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Go back to your war; we will go back to ours.
- Done, and quickly, as you prefer.
- Fair enough. Spend what you gain on demons.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the host. We will spend it against the pit, and thank you.
- Our thanks. We had not thought mortals worth your notice.
- Generous. The Crusade is grateful, and so are its widows.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not fund oath-breakers, even against the hells.
- Our treasury arms our own crusaders first.
- We cannot. Your war is not ours to pay for.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. The demons laugh while angels and crusaders fight.
- Accepted. Let us both turn our blades on hell.
- Very well. There is only one war that truly matters, and neither of us is winning it like this.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You have shed Bannor blood in your hunt, and you will answer for it.
- We fight on until the rebel host kneels to the Law.
- Not yet. Even angels must learn that the Law binds them too.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for your war in hell? We fight it ourselves, and pay for it ourselves.
- No. Rebels receive nothing from the Bannor.
- You have not proven your devotion to the Law. Not a coin.

### Bannor → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. Our faith teaches that unequalled evil will one day be loosed upon Erebus. We did not expect it to introduce itself.
- You would end creation itself. The Bannor were bound in hell to stand against exactly that.
- Greetings, gate-openers. Some of your cultists were born Bannor, they tell me. They will be judged twice.

#### Declares war
- You long for the end of the world. The Bannor were forged to prevent it. The Crusade begins.
- Every gate you open is a wound in creation. We will close them all, and you with them.
- You would hand the world to the pit. We walked out of the pit once; we will not let it walk in.

#### Refuses to talk
- There is nothing to discuss with those who want everything to end.
- Your envoys smell of the void. Go.
- We do not negotiate with Armageddon.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. We are at peace, and the Law requires that we hear you. Nothing requires us to trust you.
- We keep this peace with our hands on our swords. Say what you want.
- Speak quickly. Every hour of your rites brings the end nearer.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your gates spew horrors onto Bannor roads. Speak, if you dare.
- Your cultists stand in our squares preaching the end of all things. What do you want?
- You sold your souls to hasten the apocalypse. Mine is not for sale.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. The Law keeps its bargains, even with the damned.
- Done. Know that our priests read every rune in it.
- The terms are just. May creation outlast them.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our priests will purify this before it enters the Halls.
- We acknowledge your gift. It does not buy you the world.
- Our thanks. We shall wait to see what doom it hides.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Everything you touch is meant to end.
- We will not trade with the apocalypse.
- That gold would only build another gate. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. Close your gates, and the Orders will stay home.
- We accept, because the Law demands it. The Crusade will be waiting.
- Very well. Creation survives another season, and the Bannor still stand guard over it.

#### Refuses peace
- The Crusade has been launched. There will be no peace until your gates are rubble.
- Never. Every day you live, the world dies a little more.
- No. You want an ending; we will give you yours.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the end of the world? It will have no need of gold.
- The Bannor give nothing to those who would destroy everything.
- Take your demands into your gates, and follow them.

### Bannor → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. You traded pieces of your souls for long life. Our priests call that a bargain struck in the wrong market.
- Greetings, Grey ones. You walk through other lands unseen, they say. The Bannor watch more closely than most.
- You hunt the undead, which the Bannor applaud. You hide from every other war, which we do not.

#### Declares war
- You have watched the world bleed from your hidden cities for ages. Watching is a sin as well.
- A soul is not a coin to be spent. The priesthood has judged your trade.
- You sit out every war against the darkness. You will not sit out this one.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not speak to shadows.
- Go back to your fog.
- No talks. You have said nothing new in a thousand years.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your hunters of the undead have done good work along our borders, [CT_NAME]. Speak.
- Come, friend. Even a shade may stand with the Law against the dark.
- Speak. The Halls will hear the Sidar, however faintly you speak.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades walk our cities unseen. By any law, that is spying.
- You care nothing for the war against evil. What do you want?
- You gave away love and anger with your souls. Then you will not mind that we are angry. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair deal, even with the Grey.
- Done. The Bannor keep their word for as long as you live, which may be some while.
- Fair terms. Let them stand.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our thanks. The Sidar remember the living, sometimes.
- We are grateful to the Grey, and a little surprised.
- Generous. Perhaps you kept more of your souls than we thought.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You can wait a century for a better offer; you have the time.
- We cannot spare it while the Crusade is in the field.
- Not this. Come back with terms a living people can accept.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your hidden cities.
- We accept. Hunt the undead, not the Bannor.
- Very well. Our quarrel was never worth your eternity or our blood.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You will learn that even shades can be judged.
- We will march until your hidden cities are found.
- Not yet. You have hidden from too many wars to be allowed to hide from this one.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to ghosts? The Bannor tithe to the living.
- You have all the time in the world to earn it. Earn it.
- No. The dead need nothing from us but prayers.

### Bannor → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Svartalfar. Your court slaughtered its own kin for keeping faith with their god. The Bannor do not forget such things.
- Greetings, Winter Court. We have heard what you do to your allies; we shall sleep in armour.
- Dark elves who traded their god for Esus. The Law has a name for such people.

#### Declares war
- You murdered elves for praying to their own god. The priesthood has judged you.
- Your assassins have killed their last Bannor. The Orders come for the Winter Court.
- Treachery is your art. War is ours.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not trust a single word from your court.
- Go back to your shadows.
- No talks. Your envoys carry daggers in their sleeves.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Speak, [CT_NAME]. We are at peace; for now, that is enough.
- You have kept your word to us, which is more than your Seelie kin can say of you. Speak.
- Welcome, though our guards will be watching your hands.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your assassins were found inside the Halls. Explain, if you can.
- Your court smiles while it sharpens its knives. What do you want?
- Twelve assassins in our palace, you boast? We hanged nine of them last winter. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. And our priests will read it twice.
- Done. Our word is good; we expect you at least to try.
- Just, for once. Keep it so.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our tasters will see to this first. Then, perhaps, our thanks.
- Our thanks, and our suspicion.
- Generous. We will wait to see what it costs us.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offers always hide a knife.
- We do not trade with assassins.
- That deal is a trap with a seal on it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your assassins at home.
- We accept, with our guards doubled.
- Very well. The Law rests, but it does not sleep.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your treachery must be answered in full.
- Not until the Winter Court is broken.
- Not yet. Your peace is a poisoned cup.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Winter Court? Steal it, as you usually do.
- No. Not to traitors, not ever.
- Your academies of persuasion failed you here. No.

## Calabim

### Calabim → Amurites

#### First contact
- The Children of Kylorin, at last. They say your blood hums with his magic; forgive us if we listen closely.
- Welcome, scholars. Our Broods rule their cities as estates and keep their herds content. Your archmages might learn something of governance from us.
- You keep necromancy under lock and law, we are told. How quaint. We keep it under our own roofs, and it keeps us young.

#### Declares war
- Your schools have grown fat with gifted students. The Broods have never tasted a mage, and they are curious.
- Kylorin left you his blood and walked off into the ice. Now we will take that blood back, a cup at a time.
- Ready your siege-mages, Amurite. Spells run dry by midnight; our hunger never does.

#### Refuses to talk
- Send your envoy back to the lecture hall. We are not finished with your borders.
- Petitions, committees, careful arguments... save them for your archmages. We have nothing to discuss.
- No. Your mages are bleeding beautifully, and we will not cut the evening short.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. Come in from the cold; our halls are warm, and tonight the wine is merely wine.
- The Children of Kylorin are always welcome at our table. Such interesting conversation, such interesting veins.
- You leave us to our nights, and we leave you to your studies. A fine arrangement. What brings you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your archmages have been saying things about the Broods. Choose your next words with more care than they did.
- We have outlived wiser mages than you, Amurite. Speak quickly; patience is not infinite, even for us.
- Another lecture? Your people mistake us for a regulated branch of magic. We are not regulated.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even scholars can strike a fair bargain when they stop quarrelling amongst themselves.
- Very well, Amurite. Write it in your ledgers; we will remember it in ours.
- A sensible exchange. Your archmages may keep their secrets, and we our appetites.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Children of Kylorin? We are touched. Few mages part with anything freely.
- How generous. We will raise a glass to your schools tonight, and the glass will be full.
- Most gracious. The Broods will speak kindly of the Amurites, for a season or two.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer is as thin as the blood of an old professor.
- You dress a poor bargain in learned words. We have lived too long to be impressed by vocabulary.
- We decline, scholar. Come back when your committees have agreed on something worth our while.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough, then. Your mages may return to their schools; the herds will be fatter for the rest, and so will we.
- Peace, Amurite. Let your students grow and multiply. We are patient, and we can count.
- We will sheathe our fangs. The fire of your adepts has made the hunt more tiresome than tasty.

#### Refuses peace
