- Peace? Our nobles have only just acquired a taste for arcane blood. Ask again when they are sated.
- We outlasted the Age of Ice, Amurite. We will outlast your grandmasters' indignation.
- No. Your universities still stand, and we have not yet dined with the faculty.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand tribute of the Calabim? Study your history: we are what remains after the kings who made demands are gone.
- An interesting experiment, Amurite. Its result is no.
- Spellcraft does not frighten those who have watched ages pass. You will have nothing from us.

### Calabim → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- Masks, puppets and a laughing throne. At last, a court very nearly as decadent as ours.
- Greetings from the Calabim to the masquerade of Jubilee. We, too, keep slaves, though ours rarely notice the strings.
- You grow strong on the blood of captives, we hear. How flattering; we had thought ourselves the only ones.

#### Declares war
- Your harlequins amused us, but the jest is over. The Broods will see what lies beneath the masks, and drink it.
- Puppets do not bleed. Fortunately, the hands that hold their strings do.
- We have come to collect your court, Balseraph: every dancer, every freak, every slave you thought was yours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No more riddles and rhymes. When we wish to hear a jester, we will send for one.
- Your envoy wears a painted smile. Ours are real, and we are not smiling now.
- Talk is a game in Jubilee. Here it is a courtesy, and you have spent yours.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, the masquerade comes calling. Do sit; our servants are trained not to scream at guests.
- Welcome, Balseraph. Two courts that understand the pleasures of ownership ought to be friends.
- [CT_NAME]! Tell us the latest from Jubilee; nothing half so amusing happens in our quiet halls.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Keep your mind out of our servants' heads, Balseraph. They belong to us, body and blood.
- We are not one of your caged curiosities. Speak plainly, or do not speak.
- Your mimics have been sniffing at our borders. Whatever you want, want it quickly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, and without a single rhyme. We are impressed.
- So be it. A bargain between owners of people is a bargain we understand.
- Done. Have your Taskmasters bring it round; ours will take it from there.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A present from the laughing court, and no trap inside? We will check twice, but thank you.
- How delightful. The Broods will toast Jubilee tonight, and perhaps a slave or two of yours.
- Charming. Generosity from a mad court is rarer than an honest face at its masquerade.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We know sleight of hand when we see it, Balseraph.
- That offer is a costume with nothing inside it. Take it back to your wardrobe.
- Regrettably, no. Your court may find this sort of thing funny; we find it cheap.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well, let the masquerade resume. We were growing tired of the taste of greasepaint.
- Peace. Keep your harlequins on your side of the line, and we will keep our appetites on ours.
- Enough. Two courts of masters gain nothing by emptying each other's pens.

#### Refuses peace
- The show is not over, Balseraph. We are only now reaching the interesting act.
- No. Your slaves are plump and frightened, and we will not leave the cellar half full.
- Peace with a madman lasts until the next whim. We prefer to finish this while we can.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want tribute? Write the demand as a song; perhaps we will laugh instead of feeding.
- We are not one of your puppets. The strings will not take.
- No, Balseraph. The Calabim pay nothing to clowns, mad or otherwise.

### Calabim → Bannor

#### First contact
- The Bannor. Soldiers of Junil, drilled from the cradle. We have always admired a well-kept herd.
- You climbed out of Hell, we are told, to bring Law to the dark corners. Ours is a very dark corner. Mind your step.
- Greetings, crusaders. You will hear dreadful stories about us; most of them are understated.

#### Declares war
- Your priests have long named us damned. Very well: the damned are coming to collect.
- Every farm a castle, every man a soldier, every soldier a full cup. The Broods march on the Bannor.
- The Order taught your children to fear the dark. Tonight we teach them why.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your Confessors have nothing to say that we wish to hear. Go back to your barracks.
- We do not parley with a people who burn their dead so nothing can rise in them. You know what we are.
- No. The Order wants obedience and we want blood. Neither of us is in the mood to bargain.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- A crusader at our table. How novel. Do not be alarmed; you are a guest tonight.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Even the Order needs neighbours who keep their own people in good order.
- The Bannor and the Calabim both prize discipline. Our herds, too, never question us.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Confessors preach against us in every market. Silence them, or we shall.
- We know you call us the natural enemy of every holy nation. Enemies may still talk, briefly.
- Why have you come, crusader? To repent? It is a little late for that, on both sides.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A just and equitable bargain, as your priests would say. They need not know with whom.
- Very well, Bannor. You keep order and so do we; in this, at least, we understand each other.
- Done. Your quartermasters are as precise as your drill sergeants.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Halls of Sabathiel? Your priests would faint. We are most grateful.
- How kind. Do the Families know you are so generous to the damned?
- Thank you, crusader. We will remember this, should your people ever need a merciful end.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your Order demands unquestioning obedience; we give none, least of all to bad bargains.
- That is the sort of offer one makes to a conscript. We are not conscripts.
- We think not. Bring something worth the trouble of dealing with Junil's own.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Your free lands will breed new soldiers, and we will be here, waiting.
- Lay down your spears, Bannor. Holy war is so tiring, even for those who never tire.
- As you wish. Let the crusade rest a while; your people will grow healthier for it, and so will their blood.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace with the Order? You would sooner forgive us than we would leave a full garrison untouched.
- Your crusaders came to cleanse us. Let them learn what the damned do with the righteous.
- No. Every Bannor fortress is a larder, and we have only begun to open the doors.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Bannor? Junil asks obedience of his own. We are not his own.
- You demand like a priest in the confessional. We have nothing to confess and nothing to give.
- No. Bring your Crusaders if you must; they always arrive so well fed.

### Calabim → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs who keep a banner and a priesthood. How civilized. The blood, we are told, still tastes of smoke.
- So you are the children of Braduk the Burning. Bhall's fall made you; Mulcarn's winter nearly unmade us. We have that much in common.
- Greetings, Clan. We, too, survived the Age of Ice by keeping close to our food.

#### Declares war
- Your warriors are many and cheap, and we are very hungry. A pleasing arithmetic.
- Raise the Ember Banner if you like. It will make a fine tablecloth.
- The Broods have tired of thin human blood. Orc blood runs hot, and we mean to drink it.

#### Refuses to talk
- Grunt at someone else, orc. We are busy.
- Your envoy smelled of ash and fear. Send no more; we have eaten the last.
- No. We do not haggle with beasts who feed their captives to a fallen goddess's fire.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, the Clan. You have washed for the occasion. We are touched.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your raiders keep the wild places thin, and our herds stay close to home. We approve.
- Come in and sit by the hearth. We know your people like to be near a fire.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders have been taking our cattle. Ours, orc. Make your excuses quickly.
- Smoke, sweat and insolence. Say your piece and get out of our hall.
- The Broods are short-tempered with orcs today. Choose your words as you would choose your last meal.

#### Accepts a deal
- Then it is settled. A fair bargain, even if it came wrapped in fur.
- Agreed. You count better than your reputation suggests.
- Done. Take it back to Braduk and tell them the Calabim pay their debts.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, from orcs? Bhall must be stirring in her pit.
- How thoughtful. We will not eat your messenger, this once.
- Most gracious of the Clan. The Broods will remember that not every orc is a brute.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We are not some starving tribe to be cheated beside a campfire.
- You trade like a raider: take much, give little. Not with us.
- We decline. Bring something better than whatever fell off your last plunder cart.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your fires, orc; we will go back to our cellars.
- Peace. Your blood is hot but coarse, and we have finer herds to tend.
- Very well. Two peoples who outlived the winter by their wits need not bleed each other dry.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? Your camps are still full of warm bodies. We have not finished counting them.
- No. The Clan has always lived by the axe. Let it die by the fang.
- You would run home to Braduk now? Run, then. We hunt better in the dark than you do.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute, from us to you? Orcs are many things, but rarely funny. Well done.
- You may take what you can carry, orc. Try it, and we will carry you off.
- No. The Calabim do not feed the Clan; it is rather the other way round.

### Calabim → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. We knew vampires like you once: they ran wild in the Age of Ice and ate what they could catch. Most of them died.
- You run with wolves, we hear. We keep shepherds. You may find our way more comfortable.
- Greetings, northmen. You smell of the hunt. We prefer our meals delivered.

#### Declares war
- A pack hunts what is weak. So do we, and we have marked yours.
- Your strongest warriors would make magnificent bloodpets. We have come to choose them.
- You call yourselves wolves. Let us see how wolves fare against what has hunted men since the first villages.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not bargain with beasts. Bark at the moon, if you need to be heard.
- No. You told us diplomacy is a trick of the weak. Let us not be weak together.
- Your envoy came in snarling. We sent the snarl back without the envoy.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, the pack leader. Do sit; we had the meat served raw, as we know you like it.
- Welcome, northman. You cull your weak and we harvest ours. We are not so different.
- [CT_NAME]. You look well fed. The hunting must be good in the wastes.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your warbands have been taking from our herds. Raiding the Calabim is a short career.
- You smell of wet fur and bad intentions. Speak.
- Wolves that snap at the shepherd tend to end as rugs. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even a wolf knows a fair share when it sees one.
- Very well, Doviello. Take your share and go back to the cold.
- Done. You bargain better than you dress.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the pack? You must be expecting a hard winter.
- How unexpected. We will not ask what you killed for it.
- Thank you, northman. Generosity is so rare in the wastes, it must have hurt.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You offer scraps as if we were one of your hounds.
- Regrettably, no. The strong take, you say; the clever simply refuse.
- That is a poor trade even by the standards of the tundra.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and harry someone weaker; there are many, and we will gladly watch.
- So be it. A pack that bleeds itself dry is easy prey for others. Even wolves know that.
- Enough. There is nothing to gain fighting a people whose blood is mostly sinew.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your pack is thinning, and the stragglers are ours.
- You cull the weak, northman. We are merely helping.
- Peace, after you came howling at our gates? Lie down and bleed a while longer.

#### Rejects a demand
- A wolf demands, and a vampire laughs. Run along.
- No. The Calabim have outlasted packs fiercer than yours.
- You think we fear teeth? We were biting before your pack learned to howl.

### Calabim → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim. Keepers of shrines, menders of the broken. We, too, take a great interest in the sick and the dying.
- You witnessed the Compact, we hear, and the Godslayer handed to Finner. Our eldest remember that age too, from the shadows.
- Greetings, monks. Your order is the most trusted in Erebus, we are told. How very useful that must be.

#### Declares war
- You shelter the weak at your sacred sites. We have come for the sheltered.
- Your warrior monks carry no weapons. A charming custom. We shall see how long it lasts.
- The holy nations call us their natural enemy. Let us be natural, then.

#### Refuses to talk
- No sermons, monk. Your purity is no ward against an appetite as old as ours.
- Go and tend your shrines while you still have them. We will not talk.
- The Elohim seek peace with everyone. That is precisely why we refuse it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Pilgrims at our gate. Come in; our hospitality is as old as yours, we promise.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. We do not share your faith, but we admire your devotion to the frail.
- The Elohim and the Calabim, at peace. The world is stranger than either of us thought.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You have been sending monks to preach to our herds. Our herds do not need saving.
- Your purity does not impress us, monk. What do you want?
- Why do you come, Elohim? To pray over us? Save it for the ones we leave behind.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. You bargain honestly; it is almost disarming.
- As you wish. Take it to your shrines with our compliments.
- Done. Even a monk may profit from dealing with the Calabim, once.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Elohim, given freely. You truly do believe in charity.
- How kind. We will try to deserve it, though neither of us expects we will.
- Thank you. Such generosity would make a lesser creature feel guilty.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Mercy is your trade, monk, not ours.
- We think not. You offer what any pilgrim might; we expect more from a nation.
- That bargain is as thin as temple gruel.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and bind your wounds; you are good at it, after all.
- Then it is settled. Your monks may return to their shrines. We have other cattle to tend.
- Enough. Even we tire of blood that tastes of prayer.

#### Refuses peace
- No. A nation of healers has a great many patients, and we are not done visiting them.
- You sheltered the weak through the Age of Dragons and the Age of Ice. Shelter them from us, if you can.
- Peace with the Elohim? We would sooner drink holy water.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Monks who carry no weapons should not make demands.
- No. Your shrines may live on alms; the Calabim do not give them.
- We give to no one, Elohim, least of all to those who preach against us.

### Calabim → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori, who serve no god. No god will come for you, then, when something comes for you in the night.
- Greetings to the people of the angel who walked away from heaven. We, too, gave up whatever slowed us down.
- You offer haven to anyone who would lead their own life. How generous. We have always liked an open door.

#### Declares war
- Your adventurers are famous across Erebus. Heroes are the richest blood of all.
- You turned from the gods to stand alone. Stand alone, then, when the Broods arrive.
- No temple will ring its bells for you, Grigori. We are coming, and no one above is listening.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your angel offers counsel and nothing more. We need neither.
- No. Lead yourselves, as your creed teaches. Lead yourselves out of our sight.
- We have nothing to say to a people who believe in nothing.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Free people are so rare; we enjoy watching them.
- The Grigori owe no god and no master. Refreshing company, for an evening.
- Come in. There are no priests here to frown at you either.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your adventurers keep wandering into our lands looking for monsters to slay. They found us. What do you want?
- You preach freedom to our herds. That is a dangerous gospel, Grigori.
- Speak, and be brief. You have no god to intercede for you here.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A sensible bargain between peoples who answer to no heaven.
- Very well. The godless know how to count, at least.
- Done. No priest blessed it, and it will hold all the better.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, freely given by a free people. We are touched.
- How unexpected. No god told you to do this, and that makes it sweeter.
- Thank you, Grigori. We will remember you fondly when the gods' wars reach your door.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. A hero's courage does not make a bad bargain good.
- We decline. Your adventurers may take risks; we do not.
- That offer is not worth our time, and we have a great deal of it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your haven and let your heroes heal. We will be patient.
- So be it. You wanted the world left to mortals. We are content to leave it to them, for now.
- Enough. Your adventurers have proved costly to hunt.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Without a god's protection, your cities are the easiest pickings in Erebus.
- Your heroes keep coming, and we keep drinking. Why stop?
- Peace? You have nothing above you to swear it by.

#### Rejects a demand
- No god backs your demand, Grigori, and neither does your army.
- You ask for tribute as if we were one of your refugees. We are not.
- No. The gods themselves could not make us kneel; those who left them certainly cannot.

### Calabim → Hippus

#### First contact
- Horse lords. Your mercenaries are spoken of in every court. We do so like people who can be bought.
- Greetings, Hippus. Your blood smells of horse, they say. We shall try not to hold it against you.
- You sell your swords for foreign gold. The Calabim pay well, and in coin, if you prefer.

#### Declares war
- Ride as fast as you like, Hippus. The night is faster.
- Your companies have bled for every paymaster in Erebus. Now they bleed for us, without the pay.
- The Broods have a craving for the steppe. Saddle up; it will not help.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You would sell us a peace and our enemies a war in the same breath.
- Ride away, horseman. We are not hiring today.
- Your clans cannot agree among themselves. Why would we listen to any of you?

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, the riders. Come in; we have had the stables cleared for your mounts.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Should you ever need a paymaster, the Calabim are generous and punctual.
- The Hippus at our door. Have you come to sell, or to buy?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your companies took our gold and turned up on the other side. We remember such things for centuries.
- We have no use for horse-thieves in our halls. Say it quickly.
- The Hippus raid everyone, even each other. What makes you think we will be gentler?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair price, fairly paid. Mercenaries understand that.
- As you wish. You haggle like a horse-trader, but the bargain is sound.
- Done. Ride home with it before we change our minds.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Hippus, and no contract attached? Remarkable.
- How generous. We will put it to better use than horse feed.
- Thank you, rider. Do mention it to your clans; it may start a fashion.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That price would insult a sell-sword.
- Regrettably, no. Even your raiders ask for more than that.
- You offer us the lame mare and keep the stallion. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Gallop off, Hippus, and sell your lances somewhere else.
- Then it is settled. Your riders are hard to catch, and harder still to drink from in the saddle.
- Enough. A hired war ends when the gold runs out; consider ours spent.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You can outride our armies, but your cities cannot.
- Your herds are scattered and your companies far away. Why would we stop now?
- Peace? Ride back to your plains, if you can still find them.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute is what you take from villages, Hippus. We are not a village.
- No. Your mercenaries are for hire; our treasury is not.
- You want gold for nothing? Even a sell-sword must earn his pay.

### Calabim → Illians

#### First contact
- The men of Letum Frigus. Your winter nearly starved our kind out of the world. We have not forgotten.
- Greetings to the Illians. They say that when you awake, the world sleeps. We, too, prefer the world asleep.
- A ruler who would become a god. How ambitious. We were content to become something better than mortal.

#### Declares war
- Mulcarn's ice emptied our hunting grounds once. This time we will empty yours.
- Your lord would be a god. Gods bleed too, if one bites deep enough.
- The Age of Ice is over, Illian. We will make certain it never returns.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. The White Hand once let whole villages freeze. We will not bargain with the cold.
- The winter does not negotiate, they say. Neither do we.
- Go back to your broken mountain. We have nothing for you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Illian. Come in from the snow; our halls are warm, unlike yours.
- [CT_NAME]. We keep our people fat and warm; perhaps your frozen folk could learn from us.
- The Illians, at peace with the Calabim. The winter must be mellowing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You bring the cold into our halls, Illian. Say what you want before the wine freezes.
- We survived Mulcarn once. We will not be bullied by his leftovers.
- Your would-be god's eyes have wandered to our lands. Let them wander back.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even cold blood can be warmed by a fair bargain.
- Very well, Illian. Take it back to Letum Frigus.
- Done. Let it thaw the air between us a little.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the frozen north? We are surprised it did not shatter on the way.
- Thank you, Illian. The Calabim remember warmth, even when it comes from the cold.
- How generous. Perhaps a god-in-waiting has a heart after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. The winter took enough from us without a bad bargain on top.
- We think not. Your offer is as barren as the ice fields.
- That is a frozen pittance, Illian.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go and dream of your new god; we will keep our nights.
- Very well. A world without men is a world without food for us; your winter and our thirst should not meet.
- Enough. Fighting in the snow reminds us of times we would rather forget.

#### Refuses peace
- No. While the Illians stand, the ice might come back. We will not have it.
- Your cities are full of warm bodies for once. We intend to keep them that way, in our cellars.
- Peace with the winter's heirs? The Calabim nearly died of your kind of peace.

#### Rejects a demand
- Mulcarn took everything once, and our kind paid. Never again.
- No. Make your demands of the snow; it may listen.
- You would have us pay tribute to the cold? We have paid enough.

### Calabim → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons of Agares' hell, walking in Erebus. You want mortal souls for your fires; we want them for our veins. We will have to share.
- Greetings, Infernal. We have tasted souls before. We wonder what yours taste like.
- So Hell has come to Erebus. We had hoped it would be more elegant.

#### Declares war
- Every soul you drag to the pit is one less for our tables. We will not let you poach our herds.
- Your demons carved their cities with their claws. We will see how they fare against teeth.
- The Calabim do not share their cattle, not with the living and not with Hell.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A demon's bargain is a cell whose door opens only inward.
- Go back to your Obsidian Gate. We have nothing to discuss with Hell's tax collectors.
- Even we draw a line, demon. You are on the wrong side of it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Infernal. Do not burn the tapestries; they are older than your gate.
- [CT_NAME]. We are both monsters to the holy nations. It makes for a certain fellowship.
- Ah, our neighbours from below. Do sit; the chairs are fireproof.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your demons have been dragging our servants into the pit. They were ours. Explain.
- You reek of sulphur and greed. Speak quickly.
- We are not one of your tormented souls, demon. Mind your tone.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. We read every word, of course. One learns to, with Hell.
- So be it. A bargain between predators, fairly struck.
- Done. Keep your side of it, or we will keep your envoy.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Hell? We will have it checked for curses, but thank you.
- How generous. We had heard demons give nothing without a price; we will wait for it.
- Thank you, Infernal. Even brimstone can be sweet, it seems.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We know how demons write contracts.
- We decline. You would take our blood and leave us the ash.
- That is a devil's bargain, and we are not devils.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Erebus is wide enough for two kinds of hunger, for now.
- As you wish. Go and torment the righteous; we will not stand in your way.
- Enough. War with Hell only feeds Hell. Let us both eat elsewhere.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every city you hold is a herd you will drag below. We will not allow it.
- Demons do not die easily, we know. We have time.
- Peace with Agares' dogs? Not while you hold what is ours.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to Hell? The Calabim cheated death; we will not pay its landlord.
- No. We gave no soul to Agares, and we give nothing to you.
- Demand all you like, demon. Our veins are cold, and so is our answer.

### Calabim → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad, come up from under the hills. You count your gold; we count our servants. Both make us rich.
- Greetings, dwarves. We hear you distrust illusions. Good: we are entirely real.
- Men cheated you in the Age of Magic, we are told. We would never cheat you. We would simply eat you.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are full of gold, and your halls are full of dwarves. We want only one of those.
- Stout walls and stout hammers. We will come through the cellars.
- The Broods have never tasted dwarf. They are told it is like very old wine.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back underground and count your coins.
- A dwarf who wants to talk is a dwarf who is losing. We are enjoying ourselves.
- Your merchants may haggle with everyone else. Not with us, not now.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Khazad. Bring your ledgers; we have centuries of patience for accounts.
- [CT_NAME]. You are the only guest who ever looked at our silver before our throats.
- The dwarves come to call. How delightful. Do mind your beards near the candles.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your miners have been digging under our hills. They found more than ore.
- You eye our treasury like a thief. Say what you came to say.
- A dwarf in a temper. We have met mountains that were more polite.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Dwarven terms, dwarven precision. We approve.
- Then it is settled. You drive a hard bargain, dwarf; we drive a long one.
- Done. Weigh it twice if you like; it will all be there.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Khazad? Who counted it out? We must thank them personally.
- Gold given freely by a dwarf. We will have it framed.
- Thank you, dwarf. We know what it cost you to let go.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You will not trade us trinkets for silver, as men once traded you.
- Regrettably, no. Your appraisers must have been drinking.
- That price is lighter than a beggar's purse, and you know it, dwarf.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your halls and seal the doors, if it comforts you.
- Very well. Your walls are thick and our patience is long, but not that long.
- Enough. Dwarf blood is not worth chipping our fangs on all that iron.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your halls are deep, but every door opens eventually.
- Peace? You would only spend it fortifying. We prefer you unfortified.
- The Khazad hid from the world for three generations. We can wait longer.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a dwarf? You must have confused us with one of your clients.
- No. Gold flows to the Calabim, never from them.
- Something for nothing? That is not the dwarven way, we were told.

### Calabim → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- Centaurs, lamia, giants and men, all under one crown. So many kinds of blood in a single nation. We are fascinated.
- Greetings, Kuriotates. You grant asylum to anyone, we hear. How very... open.
- A kingdom of a few great cities, crowded and rich. You keep your table well laid.

#### Declares war
- Your ambassadors once offered us peace. We sent our answer home in the shape of an empty chair.
- Your cities are few and full to bursting. We prefer to dine where the table is crowded.
- Retreat into your shell, Kuriotate, as you always do. We have all the time in the world to crack it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your envoys have a way of not returning from our court. Spare this one.
- We do not bargain with a nation that shelters every stray in Erebus.
- Send no more envoys. They smell of horse, and the cooks complain.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Kuriotate. Your centaurs may wait outside; the floors are freshly polished.
- [CT_NAME]. A crown that keeps every faction in balance. We admire such control.
- Come in. We promise this audience ends with you leaving.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlements creep ever closer to our estates. Explain yourself.
- Your lamia have been meddling with our servants' minds. That is our privilege.
- We have eaten Kuriotate envoys before. Say what you came to say.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A sensible bargain, as befits a sensible kingdom.
- So be it. Your merchants may carry it home, and this time they will arrive.
- Done. Your confederation is a pleasure to deal with, when it stays on its side.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Kuriotates. How fitting, from a nation that welcomes everyone.
- Thank you. We will drink to your great cities, and leave them standing.
- How generous. Your settlements must be very rich indeed.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You may impress your client tribes with that sort of offer. Not us.
- We think not. Your settlements are not the only ones who can refuse a poor trade.
- That bargain has more legs than a centaur, and still it does not stand.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Retreat into your heartland, and we will retreat into the night.
- As you wish. Your giants are tiresome to bleed; there is so very much of them.
- Enough. Keep your borders open to all the world, but not to us.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? Your last envoy offered that too. We kept him.
- No. Your cities are the richest table in Erebus, and we are not done eating.
- Your shell is cracked, Kuriotate. We will not stop now.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute from the Calabim? Your settlements must have mistaken us for one of their protectorates.
- No. We do not pay those we might yet devour.
- You ask the way a child asks for sweets. The answer is the one a child gets.

### Calabim → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun, kings of the waves. We prefer our blood warm and on dry land, but sailors are sometimes worth the trouble.
- Greetings, captain. We hear a Lanun keeps a promise about as long as the tide does.
- Pirates and sea-traders. We have much in common: we both take what we need, and smile while we do it.

#### Declares war
- Your ports are crowded with drunken sailors. A feast that comes to us on every tide.
- The sea will not save you, Lanun. Your sailors must come ashore to sleep.
- Danalin no longer answers you, we hear. Then no one will answer you tonight.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A Lanun's word drifts with the current; we will not waste ours on it.
- Row back to your ship, captain. We are not buying.
- We do not parley with pirates while they still hold our silver.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, captain. Tell us of the sea; we have never been fond of water.
- [CT_NAME]! Which of your many promises are you keeping today?
- Come in, Lanun. The wine here is better than anything you have stolen from Balseraph waters.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders took one of our ships, and a cargo of servants with it. We want them back.
- You come with salt on your boots and lies on your lips. Speak.
- A pirate in our hall. Do not touch the silver.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Sign it, captain, and remember that you signed it.
- Then it is settled. A fair trade, which is rare from a Lanun.
- Done. Sail home with it before the weather turns.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from a pirate. Whose was it before?
- Thank you, captain. We will not ask where it was found.
- How generous. The sea must have been kind to you lately.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You will not fleece us like some fat merchant galley.
- We decline. That offer is as leaky as an old trireme.
- No. Offer it to the drowned; they might take it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to the sea with you; we will keep to the land.
- Very well. Hunting sailors is wet, cold work, and we are tired of it.
- Enough. You have your waves, and we our nights.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your harbours are full, and we are not done.
- Peace with a pirate is a pause between raids. We prefer to finish.
- Sail away if you like. Your cities cannot.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You may plunder others, captain. Not us.
- No. Come and take it, if you can climb a cliff in the dark.
- We do not pay pirates. We sometimes eat them.

### Calabim → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The elves of the forest, back from your hidden groves. We believe you still have a book of ours.
- Greetings, Ljosalfar. You nearly died in the Age of Ice, as we did. Survivors should recognize each other.
- Elves. Long-lived, graceful, and full of the blood of ages. You will understand why we stare.

#### Declares war
- You stole a grimoire from the Calabim once. We have come for the interest.
- Your trees cannot hide you from creatures who see in the dark.
- The Summer Court is fair and gentle. We are neither.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Let your druids talk to the trees; we have nothing to say to you.
- We do not bargain with thieves of necromancy. Return what you took, and then we may talk.
- Your forest is burning, elf. Go and see to it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Ljosalfar. Your kind lives long; perhaps you understand us better than the mayflies do.
- [CT_NAME]. You bring the smell of green things with you. How refreshing.
- The forest folk at our table. Do try the wine; it is older than most of your trees.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your rangers shoot our scouts from the treetops. We will not forget it.
- You look at us as if we were a blight on your forest. Speak, then leave.
- We know what is written in the grimoire your archmages kept. Mind your tongue, elf.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Elves bargain slowly, but fairly.
- So be it. A pact between long lives.
- Done. We will remember it as long as you do, which is saying something.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Ljosalfar? We expected arrows.
- Thank you, elf. You are kinder than your cousins of the Winter Court.
- How generous. We will raise a glass to your new god of the forest.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We have more time than you, and more patience.
- Regrettably, no. That bargain would wither faster than a leaf in autumn.
- No. Offer us something worth an elf's lifetime.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your groves and heal them.
- As you wish. Your forests are dense and your archers keen; this hunt is not worth the thorns.
- Enough. Two old peoples can afford to be patient with each other.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Elven blood is the rarest vintage in Erebus. We will not stop at one glass.
- Your groves are burning, and we are warming our hands.
- Peace? Your ancestors survived the Age of Ice by hiding. Hide again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Ljosalfar? We would sooner forgive you the grimoire.
- No, elf. The forest may obey you; we do not.
- You want gifts from us? Return what you stole first.

### Calabim → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp, makers of golems. Your servants have no blood at all. How dreadfully dull.
- Greetings, little folk. You lost your empire to the ice, and we nearly lost our kind. We understand each other.
- Clockwork and clay serve you; living men serve us. We will see which lasts.

#### Declares war
- Your golems will not bleed. Fortunately, the hands that build them do.
- Hide behind your clay soldiers, Luchuirp. We will wait until you come out to mend them.
- The Broods want something smaller and sweeter tonight.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go and tinker with your golems.
- We do not negotiate with puppeteers of clay.
- Your envoy might as well be a golem. Send one with a pulse, or send none.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Luchuirp. Do leave your golems at the gate; they frighten the servants.
- [CT_NAME]. The heirs of the Open-Skiers, at our table. You build such lovely things.
- Come in. We have no use for golems, but we admire good craftsmanship.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems trample our fields. Say what you came to say.
- You look at us with all of Kilmorph's disapproval. Spare us.
- A three-foot-tall temper. Amusing, briefly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Precise, like your clockwork.
- Then it is settled. Luchuirp craftsmanship is worth the price.
- Done. Your artificers may keep their secrets.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Luchuirp? Is it wound up, or does it bite?
- Thank you. It is beautifully made, as everything of yours is.
- How kind. We will place it where the servants can admire it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You are better at building golems than bargains.
- We think not. Your offer is all gears and no weight.
- No. We have no need of anything that runs on clockwork.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Wind down your golems, and we will rein in our hunters.
- Very well. Fighting clay is tedious work, with nothing to drink at the end of it.
- Enough. Go and rebuild your workshops.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems fall, and your people are still behind them.
- Peace? You are still building, and we are still hungry.
- Your clay will not save you, Luchuirp. Neither will your goddess beneath.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Build it yourselves; you are clever enough.
- No. We pay nothing to those who will not even bleed for their own wars.
- Make your demands of your golems. They might obey.

### Calabim → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim, children of the sun. The first of our kind was born from the blood of an acolyte of Lugus. We owe your god a great deal.
- Greetings, desert people. We prefer the night, but we can be patient through a long day.
- Your hunters once took in a stranger dying in the snow, and gained a god for it. How trusting. We like trusting people.

#### Declares war
- Lugus gave us our first taste. We have come back for more.
- Your sun sets every evening, Malakim. We will be waiting when it does.
- The light of Lugus makes your cities shine. It also shows us where to go.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your priests would judge us on the merits of the case. We know their verdict.
- Go back to your sun. We have nothing to say.
- We do not bargain with the Empyrean. Its light is tiresome.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Malakim. Come in from the glare; our halls are cool.
- [CT_NAME]. A people of the sun, polite to a people of the night. How rare.
- Sit, desert traveller. We keep water for guests, and wine for friends.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars preach against us. Tell them we do not burn so easily.
- You bring too much light into our hall. Speak quickly.
- The children of Lugus look at us with such contempt. Speak, then go.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even the sun and the night share the dusk.
- So be it. A just bargain, as your Empyrean would demand.
- Done. Take it back across the sands.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the children of Lugus? How ironic, and how welcome.
- Thank you, Malakim. The desert breeds generous people.
- How kind. We will think of you at sundown.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer is as barren as your desert.
- We decline. Weigh it again in your Empyrean scales.
- No. We know a dry well when we see one.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let the sun rise and set on our border undisturbed.
- As you wish. Your light has made the hunt uncomfortable.
- Enough. Take your radiance home.

#### Refuses peace
- No. A priest of Lugus made us what we are. We will thank your god in the old way.
- Your sun cannot protect you every hour of the day.
- Peace? The night has only just begun.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the sun? We have spent ages avoiding it.
- No. The Calabim do not kneel in the light of Lugus.
- You demand impartially, we are sure. We refuse impartially.

### Calabim → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels who broke the Compact to fight the demons. We are not demons, and we hope you can tell the difference.
- Greetings, Mercurian. You care little for mortals, we hear. Neither do we, but for different reasons.
- Rebel angels, in Erebus. What does an angel's blood taste like? We have always wondered.

#### Declares war
- You defied Arawn for your war. We will take you out of it.
- Angels bleed, Mercurian. We intend to find out how much.
- You think only demons are worth fighting. Let us show you otherwise.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You only came to tell us we are next after the demons.
- We do not bargain with zealots who carve prayers into their own skin.
- Go back to your war in Hell. We have nothing to say.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Mercurian. There are no demons here; you may lower your hammer.
- [CT_NAME]. Our enemies and yours are the same: those who would drag our people below.
- Come in. You look as though you have been fighting for ages; so have we, in our way.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your angels look at our cities as if they were Hell. They are not; they are merely ours.
- You are often mistaken for demons, we hear. We know the feeling. Speak.
- Your righteousness is tiring. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even angels can be practical.
- Then it is settled. A clean bargain, and no sermon attached.
- Done. Return to your demon-hunting.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Mercurians? We are honoured, and a little suspicious.
- Thank you, angel. We had heard you cared nothing for the living, or the undying.
- How generous. We promise not to spend it on demons.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your war is not our war, and your price is not ours.
- Regrettably, no. Take it back to your host.
- No. Not even an angel could sanctify that offer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and find your demons; we will keep out of your way.
- Very well. You have greater enemies than us, and so do we.
- Enough. Neither of us gains by this while Hell walks the world.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your host is thin, and every angel that falls is one less judge for us.
- Peace? You came to burn us as if we were hell-spawn. Let us be thorough in return.
- You broke one Compact. You will not get another from us.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to rebel angels? You serve no god any longer; why should we serve you?
- No. Find a demon to bully.
- Demand all you like. We are not yours to judge.

### Calabim → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim, who want the world to end. A world without men is a world without food. You will understand our concern.
- Greetings, gate-openers. Os-Gabella keeps company with you, we hear. Do give her our regards.
- So you are the ones calling for Armageddon. How tiresome. Some of us intend to be here for a very long time.

#### Declares war
- You would end creation. We would rather keep it, and its herds. One of us must go.
- Your Armageddon will have to wait. The Broods are hungry now.
- You long for the end of the world, Sheaim. We can arrange the end of yours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Talk to your gods of ruin.
- We do not bargain with those who would burn the larder.
- There is nothing to discuss with people who want nothing to remain.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Sheaim. Do not open any gates in here, if you please.
- [CT_NAME]. Ceridwen's runes made the first of our blood; you serve her too. We are almost family.
- Come in. We are always curious about people who hate the world as much as we enjoy it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your planar gates are opening near our estates. Close them, or we will close you.
- You want the end of all things. We want the end of this conversation. Speak.
- Your cultists preach the end to our herds. They need no help despairing.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Enjoy it while the world lasts.
- So be it. We trade for the long run; we trust you will at least be here for the short one.
- Done. Our dealings may outlast creation yet, if we have our way.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim? You may as well; you will not need it after the end.
- Thank you. We will use it to make the world a little more worth keeping.
- How generous. Is it cursed? We ask only out of habit.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Why trade with a people who plan to abolish tomorrow?
- We think not. Your offer is as empty as the world you dream of.
- No. We prefer bargains that do not end with the sky falling.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your gates; we will keep the herds safe from your apocalypse.
- As you wish. Two old grudges against the gods need not destroy each other.
- Enough. The world will last a little longer, and we are glad of it.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every Sheaim city that stands brings the end a little closer.
- Peace with Armageddon? We think not.
- You want the world to end. We are starting with you.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for the end of the world? Spend your own.
- No. We have outlived every doom ever foretold, and we will outlive yours.
- You want something from us; we want you to fail. Neither of us will be satisfied today.

### Calabim → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar, who traded their souls for long life. We took ours from others. A more efficient method.
- Greetings, shades. You hunt the undead, we hear. We are not undead; we are merely very well preserved.
- Pale skin, dull eyes, endless years. You could almost be one of us, Sidar.

#### Declares war
- You would hunt our kind as aberrations. Come out of your hidden cities and try.
- Shades are very hard to kill, we know. So are we. Let us discover who is harder.
- The Broods wonder whether a shade has anything left to drink. We will find out.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Fade back into your fog.
- We do not bargain with ghosts.
- You hold yourselves above the world, Sidar. Stay above this talk as well.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, shade. Two immortals at one table; let us not waste the evening.
- [CT_NAME]. You understand the long view, as few others do.
- Come in. There is little in our wine for you, but the conversation should suit.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You call us aberrations, shade, while half your soul is missing. Speak quickly.
- Your hidden cities keep their eyes on our lands. Close them.
- You came all this way to look at us with those dull eyes. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Patience recognizes patience.
- Very well, shade. An agreement for the ages.
- Done. We will both remember it long after the mortals have forgotten.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sidar? We thought you had given up generosity along with your soul.
- Thank you. It is good to be remembered by those who forget so much.
- How unexpected. Perhaps some warmth survived the ritual.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We can wait for a better offer. So can you, Sidar.
- We decline. Your offer is as thin as your shadow.
- No. That is a mortal's bargain, and we are not mortal.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your hidden cities; we will return to our feast.
- Then it is settled. Two immortals can afford to wait for each other's mistakes.
- Enough. Your shades are tiresome to catch, and there is nothing in them to drink.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You hunt what you call aberrations. Now be hunted.
- Peace? You are fading anyway. We are merely helping.
- Shades or not, your cities are full of the living.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to ghosts? Haunt someone else.
- No. You gave your soul away; do not expect us to give anything.
- We do not pay those who are barely there.

### Calabim → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Winter Court. Elegant, cruel, patient. We will get along or we will not, but either way it will be stylish.
- Greetings, Svartalfar. You chose Esus when your god fell silent. We chose blood. Both have served us well.
- Dark elves. We had heard you were the only court in Erebus to rival ours in malice.

#### Declares war
- Your Council of Esus pays for its miracles, we hear. Pay for one now.
- You hunted your own kin through the Age of Ice for praying to the wrong god. Now be hunted for less.
- Elven blood, chilled by winter. The Broods have been looking forward to this.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We know Unseelie courtesy; it ends with a knife.
- Your envoy smiled too sweetly. We sent the smile back.
- Go and plot with your shadows. We will not hear you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Svartalfar. Your courtesies are as poisonous as ours; we will enjoy this.
- [CT_NAME]. The Winter Court at our table. Do not mind the chill; you brought it.
- Come in. We admire a court that can nurse a grudge for an age.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Shadowriders slip through our lands. Call them back.
- We know an Unseelie smile. Drop it, and speak.
- You think yourselves the cruellest court in Erebus. You have not dined with us.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A bargain between two courts that will both try to cheat it.
- Very well. Even Esus would approve; there was a price.
- Done. We will watch your side of it closely.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Svartalfar? What did it cost, and whom?
- Thank you. We will keep it, and wonder why you gave it.
- How generous. It must be part of a longer plan.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We know an Unseelie trap when we see one.
- Regrettably, no. Your offer is cold, even for the Winter Court.
- No. Esus may sell miracles; we do not buy forgeries.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your war with the Ljosalfar; it is more entertaining to watch.
- So be it. Two courts of shadows have better things to do than bleed each other.
- Enough. Our quarrel can wait until winter.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your court is cruel, but we are hungrier.
- Peace with the Unseelie? We prefer our enemies dead rather than plotting.
- No. You drove your own cousins into the snow. We see no reason to be kinder.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Winter Court? The Calabim give nothing to anyone, in any season.
- No. Esus may take payment; we do not make it.
- Demand away, dark elf. We were old before your civil war began.

## Clan of Embers

### Clan of Embers → Amurites

#### First contact
- Children of Kylorin. Your archmage burned Patria clean with fire Bhall gave her faithful. We remember whose flame that was.
- Mages. A whole nation of soft hands and loud spells. We have met your kind before, on the end of a spear.
- Do not mistake us for the wild tribes, Amurite. We have a banner, a goddess and a long memory.

#### Declares war
- Your schools are full of children who can throw fire. Bhall's children throw more of it, and they do not need to study.
- Your mages need time to chant. My warriors do not. We march.
- You worship magic, Amurite. We worship the goddess who fell burning. Let us see whose fire is hotter.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talking. Your words are spells, and I will not stand still for them.
- Get out, before I find out how well an archmage burns.
- Go back to your school and argue with each other. We are busy winning.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Amurite. Your fire-mages would be good company around a war camp. What do you want?
- [CT_NAME]. You leave us alone, we leave you alone. Good. Talk.
- Scholars at Braduk's fire. Sit, but keep your hands where I can see them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your mages look at us like something to cut open and study. Careful, or we do the cutting.
- Speak fast, wizard. My patience burns quicker than your candles.
- You think orcs are stupid because we do not read your books. Say what you want and go.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A fair bargain, even from a wizard.
- Good. No spell hidden in it? Then it is done.
- Agreed. Tell your archmages the Clan can bargain too.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the mages. Hm. You are smarter than you look.
- Good. The Clan will remember the Amurites kindly. For now.
- Thank you, wizard. Bhall's fire burns warmer for it tonight.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your words are clever; your offer is not.
- You think orcs cannot count? Count this: no.
- No. Even a goblin would walk away from that, and goblins take anything.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your fire hurts, and so does ours. Let us both lick our burns.
- Peace, Amurite. Go back to your schools. We will find softer meat.
- Fine. Your spells cost us too many spears. This time.

#### Refuses peace
- No! Your schools are still standing. When they are ash, ask again.
- Peace? Your mages are tired and my warriors are not. We keep going.
- The fire is spreading, wizard. You do not stop a fire by asking it nicely.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want tribute from the Clan? Come and take it, wizard. Bring your best spells.
- No. Magic does not frighten orcs. A falling goddess made us; your tricks are nothing.
- We pay nothing. Your archmages can squabble over that.

### Clan of Embers → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- Clowns. A whole nation of clowns. By Bhall's fire, what a world.
- You hid from the White Hand all through the Ice, behind masks. We hid behind a fire. Both of us lived.
- Do not try your mind tricks on orcs, Balseraph. Our heads are thick and our tempers are hot.

#### Declares war
- Your court laughs at everything. Laugh at this: we are coming.
- Masks burn. So do jesters. Bhall will enjoy the show.
- You keep slaves and puppets. We will take them, and your heads with them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No rhymes, no riddles, no talk. Go away.
- Your envoy danced in front of me. I broke the dancing legs. Send someone who walks.
- Not now, clown. We are winning.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- The clowns are here! Good. Make me laugh, and then talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You are mad, but you are not soft. I can deal with that.
- Balseraph. Your harlequins fight well, for dancers. What do you want?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Stop smiling. That painted face makes my warriors want to hit something.
- Your mind-mages poked at my chieftains' heads. Do it again and I burn Jubilee.
- Say it plain, Balseraph, or say nothing.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. No jokes in the small print? Then done.
- Agreed. Even a madman can make a fair trade.
- Good. Take it, and stop grinning.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift with no trick in it? Now that is a good joke.
- Hm. Thank you, Balseraph. I will check it for snakes.
- Good. Your court is strange, but generous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I know when I am being played, clown.
- Funny offer. Not funny enough. No.
- Take it back to your puppets. They might want it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your freaks bleed, my warriors bleed, and nobody is laughing.
- Peace. Go and put on your show somewhere else.
- Fine. The masquerade can go on, far away from Braduk.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The show ends when the stage burns.
- You want peace now? Your court has stopped laughing. Good. We keep going.
- No, clown. I am enjoying this too much.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Ha! That is your best joke yet.
- No. Dance for it, if you want it so much.
- Send your Taskmasters to take it. They will not come back with chains, or with anything.

### Clan of Embers → Bannor

#### First contact
- Bannor. You walked out of our Sacred Fire and called it salvation. We call it the night you came to kill us.
- So. The humans who came out of Braduk's flames. We remember your faces. We remember everything.
- Junil's soldiers. You have hunted us since the Ice. Now we have a banner too.

#### Declares war
- You crawled out of Hell through our fire and have hunted us ever since. Now we hunt you.
- Your Order says we must repent. Here is our answer: the Ember Banner, over your walls.
- Bring your Crusaders, Bannor. The fires of Braduk have waited a long time for you.

#### Refuses to talk
- I do not talk to Bannor. I burn them.
- No. Your priests talk of law while your soldiers burn our camps.
- Go away, human. The last Bannor who came to talk went into the fire.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Bannor, at peace with the Clan. Bhall must be laughing in her pit.
- [CT_NAME]. I do not trust you. But I am listening.
- You talk, I listen, nobody draws steel. A strange day. Go on.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Every orc here has lost kin to your crusades. Speak carefully.
- Your Confessors call us vermin. Say what you want before I decide the same about you.
- You look at us like something to stamp out. Careful, human. We bite.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Do not think this makes us friends.
- Fine. A fair bargain, even from the Order.
- Done. Your priests will hate it. Good.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Bannor? What is wrong with you, human?
- Hm. Thank you. My warriors will not believe it.
- Strange. Your people have only ever given us steel. This is better.

#### Turns down a deal
- You Bannor always want the bigger half. No.
- No. You expect us to take the scraps, like always. Not any more.
- You think orcs cannot count? We have been counting dead Bannor since the Ice.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your crusade and our raids can rest. Not end. Rest.
- Peace, for now. The fires of Braduk will still be burning when you come back.
- Fine. Go home and pray. We will sharpen our axes.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You came out of our fire. You will go back into it.
- Peace with the Bannor? Not while one of your fortress-farms still stands.
- You had a whole age to make peace with us. You chose the sword. So do we.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You have taken enough from us, human. Not one more coin.
- No. Junil's law is not our law, and it never will be.
- Your Crusaders can come and collect it. Bring plenty; the fire is hungry.

### Clan of Embers → Calabim

#### First contact
- Bloodsuckers. You drink men; we burn them. At least ours go to a goddess.
- Calabim. You lived through the Ice feeding on a tribe of humans. We lived through it around a fire. Both of us are still here.
- Night-drinkers. Keep your teeth off my warriors and we will get along.

#### Declares war
- Your nobles grow fat on blood. Bhall's fire will cook them in it.
- Your human herds would make good slaves for the Clan. We are taking them.
- Vampires live long, they say. Let us see how long, once Braduk's fire touches you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your tongue is too smooth. Go away.
- I do not talk to leeches.
- Your envoy wanted to taste my warriors. Now my warriors have tasted your envoy.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Calabim. You are cold, but you pay well. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your wine is too red for my taste. What do you want?
- Vampires and orcs, talking. The humans would faint.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Broods are sniffing around my camps. Keep them home.
- I see you looking at my throat. Do not.
- Speak, bloodsucker, before I light a torch.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Bloodless, but fair.
- Agreed. Nobody drinks from my envoys, and it is done.
- Good. You count like a merchant, for a corpse.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Calabim. I did not know you could give anything but bite marks.
- Thank you. You are not as cold as they say.
- Good. The Clan remembers who helps it, even leeches.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You want to drain this bargain dry, like everything else.
- You take the blood and leave us the bones. No.
- No. Find another fool, vampire. Your herds are full of them.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your vampires bleed slower than men, but they bleed. Peace.
- Fine. Go back to your cattle. We will go back to burning things.
- Peace. There are warmer enemies to fight.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your castles are full of fat nobles. We burn every one.
- Peace? You suck your own people dry. We are setting them free, with fire.
- No. A vampire never tires, they say. Neither does the Clan.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Go and drink it from someone else.
- A test of wills, leech? Orcs never back down either.
- We give nothing to things that should be dead.

### Clan of Embers → Doviello

#### First contact
- Doviello. Wolves of the north. You ran free in Mulcarn's winter while we huddled by Bhall's fire.
- Savages from the snow. Do not confuse us with you. We are more civilized, and more deadly.
- Beastmen. You hunt like a pack; we fight like a horde. Good to know each other.

#### Declares war
- You lived fat while the winter starved everyone else. Bhall's children will thaw you out.
- Your pack is strong. Our horde is bigger. We are coming.
- The Ice is over, wolf. Your time is over with it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talking, wolf. Fight.
- You say diplomacy is for the weak. Good. We agree. Go away.
- Howl all you like. Nobody here is listening.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Doviello! Good raiders, good fighters. What do you want?
- [CT_NAME]. You and I both know the strong take. So let us take from others.
- Wolf. Sit by the fire. Your people never had a good one, I hear.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders hit my camps. Bad idea, wolf.
- You stink of cold and wet dog. Talk fast.
- You think we are prey, Doviello? Look closer.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A good trade, wolf.
- Agreed. Even savages can share a kill.
- Done. Take your share and go back to the snow.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the pack? You must want something. Still, thank you.
- Good. We remember who shares the kill.
- Hm. The Doviello giving gifts. The winter must be over for good.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I know the wolf's trick: you take the big piece.
- No. Hunt somewhere else.
- No. That carcass is already picked clean.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. We are both hungry, and there is weaker prey around.
- Peace, wolf. Go back to your snow.
- Fine. Two packs fighting only feed the crows.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your pack is breaking. We finish it.
- Peace? You started this, wolf. We end it.
- No. A whole age of ice could not kill us. You will not either.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Wolves do not get to beg at Braduk's fire.
- No. If you want it, bite for it.
- Take it in single combat, if you are brave enough. You are not.

### Clan of Embers → Elohim

#### First contact
- Monks without weapons. Strange. Braduk would eat you alive.
- Elohim, keepers of holy places. Bhall once had holy places too. Now she has us.
- You tend the broken, monk? We were broken once, the day our goddess fell, and nobody came.

#### Declares war
- Your shrines are full of treasure and empty of warriors. We are coming for them.
- You keep the holy places of the gods. Bhall wants hers back.
- Monks who fight with bare hands. Let us see you fight fire.

#### Refuses to talk
- No sermons. Go away.
- Your peace is a coward's peace. We will not hear it.
- No. Your envoy prayed for me. I did not ask.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Elohim. You are soft, but you are honest. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You do not preach at us like the Bannor do. That is something.
- Monk. Sit. Nobody here will hit you today.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your monks look at us like a sickness to be nursed. Careful.
- Speak, Elohim, but no prayers.
- You guard every shrine in Erebus except Bhall's. Why should I listen to you?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. You bargain honest. Good.
- Fine. Take it to your shrines.
- Done. Even a monk can make a fair deal.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, for nothing? You Elohim are strange. Thank you.
- Hm. You give the way you heal, without asking. Good.
- Thank you, monk. Your shrines will not burn for this. This year.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Charity is your trade, not ours.
- No. You think we are fools because we are orcs.
- No. Try again, and put more in it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. You fight better than a monk should. Peace.
- Peace. Go and tend your wounded. You have many.
- Fine. Your shrines can stand, for now.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your shrines are still standing.
- Peace? You hide behind your purity. We will burn through it.
- No. You sheltered the weak through two ages. Not through this one.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Monks do not demand. Go and pray.
- No. Your gods gave us nothing. Neither will we.
- You want something from us? Come and take it, with no weapons, as your monks do.

### Clan of Embers → Grigori

#### First contact
- Grigori. You turned away from the gods. Our goddess turned away from us. Maybe we understand each other.
- People with no god. Bhall would make an example of you, if she still looked our way.
- Adventurers. Heroes. We have killed a lot of those.

#### Declares war
- Your heroes are strong. My warriors are many. Many wins.
- You have no god to save you, Grigori, and Bhall does not forgive.
- Your adventurers have killed too many of my raiders. Now we come for all of you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go away, godless.
- Your angel gives advice and nothing else. I do not want advice.
- Talk later. Fight now.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Grigori. You lead yourselves. So do we, mostly. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. No god, no priest, no sermon. I like that.
- Your cities take in anyone who wants a life of their own. Even an orc?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your adventurers go hunting in my lands. Tell them to stop.
- You look down on us for worshipping fire. Careful.
- Speak, Grigori. Your angel will not help you here.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A good trade, and no priest needed to bless it.
- Agreed. You bargain like free people: hard, but fair.
- Done. Your heroes can carry it home.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, Grigori. No god told you to do it. That makes it better.
- A gift from the godless. Hm. Good.
- We will remember this. Bhall may not, but we will.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Not worth the trouble.
- No. Your heroes take risks. I do not take bad deals.
- No. Make it better, or make it nothing.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your heroes are too much trouble. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to your free cities.
- Fine. There are god-fearing enemies to burn first.

#### Refuses peace
- No. No god protects you. Nothing stops us.
- Peace? Your heroes killed my warriors. I want their heads.
- No. You stand alone, Grigori. Fall alone.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You do not even pay your own gods.
- No. If you want something, send your heroes for it.
- We give nothing, Grigori. Not to gods, not to you.

### Clan of Embers → Hippus

#### First contact
- Hippus. You raid your own cousins for fun. We like you already.
- Horse lords. Your lances are for sale, I hear. The Clan pays in plunder.
- You held back the frostling hordes all through the Ice. Not bad, for people who never get off their horses.

#### Declares war
- Your herds are big and fat. My warriors are hungry. Simple.
- Ride fast, Hippus. Fire runs faster across dry grass.
- No more contracts. This time we take your gold, and your horses.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You sell your word to whoever pays most.
- Ride away, horseman, before I eat your horse.
- Talk to my spears.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hippus! Good fighters, for hire. Are you selling?
- [CT_NAME]. Your riders and my warriors could take half the world between them.
- Horse lords. Sit. Leave the horse outside.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your riders took our plunder from under our noses. Explain fast.
- You fought for my enemies last season. Why should I listen now?
- Speak, horse-thief.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A fair price. You are good at prices.
- Agreed. Gold for steel. Mercenaries understand.
- Done. Gallop home.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Hippus, with no contract? Hm. Thank you.
- Good. We will remember the riders.
- Thank you, horseman. Next raid, we ride together.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You price like a thief.
- Your mercenaries ask more than that for one day's fighting. No.
- No. Even a goblin knows a lame horse when he sees one.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your riders are hard to catch. Peace.
- Peace. Go and sell your lances somewhere else.
- Fine. We both have easier prey.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your herds are not all ours yet.
- Peace? You can run, Hippus. Your cities cannot.
- No. Ride faster.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You are mercenaries. Earn it.
- No. Raid someone else.
- No coin for horse-thieves.

### Clan of Embers → Illians

#### First contact
- Illians. Mulcarn's men. Our goddess fought your god. Our goddess is still burning; your god is gone.
- Men of the frozen mountain. We spent the whole Ice around Braduk's fire, cursing your master.
- So the winter has a new lord. Bhall remembers the old one.

#### Declares war
- Mulcarn was Bhall's enemy. You are Mulcarn's heirs. That is enough.
- Your winter starved us for an age. Now we bring the fire to you.
- You want to be a god, Illian? Bhall was a goddess. Ask her how gods fall.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Ice and fire do not talk.
- Go back to your cold mountain.
- Your words are frost. I do not want them.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Illian. Strange to talk to the winter without hating it. Speak.
- [CT_NAME]. Stand close to the fire. Your people need it.
- The winter's men at Braduk, and no war. Bhall must be sleeping.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You bring the cold into my camp. Say it fast, before I throw you on the fire.
- Mulcarn's priests froze our people for an age. Why should I listen to you?
- Speak, Illian. The fire is listening too.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Even ice can trade fair.
- Agreed. Take it back to the snow.
- Done. Strange, a bargain with the winter.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the cold north? Thank you. I will warm it up.
- Hm. The winter gives something back, for once.
- Thank you, Illian. Bhall may forgive you a little.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. The winter has taken enough from us.
- No. Your offer is as cold as your god.
- No. Try again when it thaws.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Fire and ice can stand apart for a while.
- Peace. But the fires of Braduk will not go out.
- Fine. Keep your snow on your side.

#### Refuses peace
- No. As long as one Illian stands, the winter can come back.
- Peace with Mulcarn's heirs? Bhall would spit me out of the fire.
- No. We melt you first, then we talk.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the winter? We paid that for an age. Never again.
- No. Ask your snow for gifts.
- You want something? Come and take it out of the fire.

### Clan of Embers → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons. Agares whispered until our goddess fell. We have not decided whether to thank you or kill you.
- Hell walks in Erebus. Bhall is down there somewhere. Tell her the Clan still burns for her.
- So, demons. We were made the day a goddess fell into your pit. Maybe we are cousins.

#### Declares war
- Agares tricked Bhall into falling. Today the Clan starts paying that debt back.
- Your demons want our souls for Hell. Our souls belong to Bhall.
- Fire against fire, demon. We were born when a goddess fell burning. Your flames do not scare us.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Demons lie, every word.
- Go back to your pit.
- No talk. Your words have hooks in them.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Demon. You smell like Braduk. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Hell and the Clan, at peace. The humans should be very afraid.
- Infernal. Sit close to the fire; you will like it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your demons dragged my warriors' souls below. Explain, or burn.
- Speak, Infernal. And no tricks.
- You want orcs for your pit? Careful. We bite on the way down.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. I read it twice. It is fair.
- Agreed. Even a demon can deal straight, once.
- Done. Keep your side, or I come down to Hell to collect.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Hell? Hm. And the price?
- Thank you, demon. I will check it for curses.
- Good. Bhall's children thank you, even if your master whispered her into the pit.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Demon bargains always cost more than they say.
- You hid my soul somewhere in the small words. No.
- No. Not even for Hell.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. We both want the humans burning. Peace.
- Peace. There are softer souls to take.
- Fine. Go and torment the Bannor. We will watch.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Agares' servants pay for what was done to Bhall.
- Peace? Your demons still hold my cities.
- No. Burn, demon. Burn hotter.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to Hell? Hell already took our goddess. That is enough.
- No. Go and bargain with someone stupid.
- You want our souls? They are already promised to the fire.

### Clan of Embers → Khazad

#### First contact
- Dwarves. Your stone halls kept you through the Ice; our fire kept us. Different shelters, same winter.
- Khazad. Gold-counters. You will not cheat the Clan the way men once cheated you. We cannot be cheated; we just take.
- So the dwarves come up into the light. Bad timing. We are already here.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are full of gold. My warriors want it.
- Your walls are thick, dwarf. Fire gets into everything.
- The goblins have been asking to visit your mines. Today they do.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back under your mountain.
- No talking, dwarf. Your gold speaks louder than you do.
- Shut your gates and wait. We are coming in anyway.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Dwarf. You trade fair and you fight hard. I respect that.
- [CT_NAME]. Bring your gold, we bring our plunder. Everybody is happy.
- Khazad. Sit down. I will find you something to stand on.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your miners dig too close to my camps. Stop.
- You look at orcs like thieves. Fair enough. Speak.
- Talk fast, dwarf, or count your teeth.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A dwarf bargain: fair, boring, good.
- Agreed. You weigh everything twice. So do we, now.
- Done. Count it if you want.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A dwarf giving gold away? By Bhall's fire, it is the end of the world.
- Thank you, Khazad. We will not raid your caravans. This season.
- Good. The Clan remembers.

#### Turns down a deal
- You think I'm dumb, dwarf? Even I can count well enough to see that is bad.
- No. Keep your coins.
- No. Your appraisers are cheating, and they know it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your hammers hit hard. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to your halls.
- Fine. Your walls are too thick, for now.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your vaults are still full.
- Peace? When the gold is ours.
- No. Your halls will burn from the inside.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a dwarf? You have more gold than anyone in Erebus.
- No. Go and dig some more.
- We give nothing. You would not even notice it missing.

### Clan of Embers → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- Kuriotates. Centaurs, giants, lamia and men, all crammed into a few big cities. Easy to find.
- Your nation takes in every outcast in Erebus, they say. Do you take orcs?
- Centaurs. Fast, strong, and they would feed a whole warband. Hm.

#### Declares war
- You keep all your treasure in a few great cities. Thank you. Easier to burn.
- Your settlements are thin and far apart. We start there.
- Crawl into your shell, Kuriotate. We bring the fire inside it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your settlements are burning. Go and look.
- I do not talk to horse-men.
- No talk. You hid in your shell; stay in it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Kuriotate. You let everyone in. Maybe even us. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your centaurs fight well. What do you want?
- You treat outcasts as equals. Orcs know about being outcasts.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlements creep onto our hunting grounds. Stop.
- Your lamia were poking around in my warriors' heads. Get them out.
- Speak, Kuriotate. Then go.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A fair trade.
- Agreed. Good for both of us.
- Done. Send it with a centaur; they are fast.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Kuriotates? Thank you. You are good neighbours.
- Hm. Generous even to orcs. Strange people.
- Good. We remember who is generous, and whose giants we did not fight.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your merchants are greedy, all of them, whatever kind they are.
- No. Offer that to your client tribes.
- No. Not good enough.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your giants hit hard. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to your great cities.
- Fine. Keep your settlements; we keep our plunder.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your great cities are not burned yet.
- Peace? Your shell is cracked. We are going in.
- No. My warriors want centaur hides for their cloaks.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Go and ask one of your protectorates.
- No. Orcs pay nothing to anyone, outcasts least of all.
- We give nothing, Kuriotate. You have enough strays to feed.

### Clan of Embers → Lanun

#### First contact
- Lanun. Your grandfathers sold ships to the fire priests of Patria. Bhall's priests. We remember good customers.
- Pirates. Good. We understand pirates. You take, we take.
- You sail the seas your god forgot. We serve a goddess who forgot us. Not so different.

#### Declares war
- Your ports are full of ships. Ships burn.
- The sea protects your ships, captain. Not your harbours.
- Your captains flee to sea when things go bad. Let them. Your cities stay, and burn.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A pirate's word is worth nothing.
- Row away, captain.
- No talk. Your promises sink faster than your ships.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Captain! You bring good loot. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You raid, we raid. Let us raid other people.
- Lanun. Sit, drink. Not the sea water.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders stole my plunder off my own coast. Talk fast.
- Pirate. I do not trust you. Speak anyway.
- You smell of salt and lies. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Good bargain, captain.
- Agreed. Sign it in front of your crew, so you remember.
- Done. Sail it home.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from a pirate? Who did you steal it from?
- Thank you, captain. We will not burn your ships. Today.
- Good. The sea was generous to you, and you to us.

#### Turns down a deal
- You will not cheat the Clan like some fat merchant. No.
- No. That bargain leaks.
- No. Go and sell it to the fish.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your ships are hard to catch. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to the sea.
- Fine. You keep the water, we keep the land.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your harbours still have ships in them.
- Peace with a pirate? It lasts until the next tide.
- No. Sail away if you like. Your cities cannot.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Plunder someone else, captain.
- No. Come ashore and take it, if you dare.
- We pay pirates nothing. We burn them.

### Clan of Embers → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- Elves. Your trees, our fire. You know how that story ends.
