- Ljosalfar. You hid in your groves through the Ice. We hid by our fire. Now we both come out.
- Forest folk. Your god died and you got a new one. Ours fell, and we kept her anyway.

#### Declares war
- Your forests are old and dry. Bhall will enjoy them.
- Your archers hide in trees. Trees burn.
- The Fellowship of Leaves says fire is part of the forest's cycle. Good. Here comes the fire.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Talk to your trees.
- Go away, elf. Your forest is on fire.
- No. You look at us like weeds to be pulled.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Elf. You talk slow, but you talk true. Go on.
- [CT_NAME]. The forest and the fire, at peace. Strange times.
- Ljosalfar. Sit. Do not worry, the fire is small today.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your rangers shoot my warriors from the treetops. Stop it, or I bring torches.
- You look down your nose at orcs, elf. Your nose is very long.
- Speak, elf, before I set your hair alight.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Fair trade, elf.
- Agreed. Take it back to your groves.
- Done. Not even a fire would argue with that.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the elves? Thank you. We will not burn your trees. These ones.
- Hm. You are kinder than your dark cousins.
- Good. The Clan remembers the forest's gift.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You think orcs are stupid. We are not.
- You can wait a thousand years for a better one. No.
- No. Your offer is drier than dead leaves.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your forests hit back. Peace.
- Peace. Go and grow your trees.
- Fine. The fire can wait.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your forests are still standing.
- Peace? The smoke has only just started.
- No. The groves burn until they are ash.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Ask your trees.
- No. Your forest gives you everything. Go and ask it.
- We give nothing, elf. Not a single branch.

### Clan of Embers → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- Luchuirp. Golem-makers. Your clay men do not burn, but you do.
- Little folk. Your great Open-Sky empire died in the Ice, while we lived warm around our fire.
- So you dug your way back up to the sun. Welcome. It is hot up here.

#### Declares war
- Your golems are strong, but golems need makers. We are coming for the makers.
- Hide behind your clay, little ones. Fire goes around.
- Kilmorph shielded you through the Ice, they say. Let her shield you now.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go and mend your golems.
- No talk. Your clay men crushed my warriors.
- Talk to my goblins. They want your workshops.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Luchuirp. You make good things. What do you want for them?
- [CT_NAME]. Your golems frighten my warriors. That is a compliment.
- Little smith. Sit. Leave the golem outside; it scares the goblins.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems walked into my camp. I smashed one. Say what you want.
- You look at orcs like a machine that came out wrong. Careful.
- Speak, smith. Your goddess under the stone does not frighten me.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Well made, like your golems.
- Agreed. Luchuirp work is worth paying for.
- Done. Tell your artificers the Clan pays its debts.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Luchuirp? Does it explode?
- Thank you, little smith. It is very well made. Too well for orcs, maybe.
- Good. We will leave your golems alone this season.

#### Turns down a deal
- Your gears and cogs do not fool me. No.
- No. You build better golems than bargains.
- No. Make it bigger, smith. You are good at making things bigger than yourselves.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your golems never tire, but my warriors do. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to your workshops.
- Fine. Smashing clay is hard on the axes.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems are broken. Now we take your workshops.
- Peace? Not while your forges are hot. They should be ours.
- No. The Ice nearly finished the Luchuirp. We will finish the rest.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Build it yourself, smith.
- No. Ask your golems; they do whatever you say.
- We give nothing to people half our height and twice our nerve.

### Clan of Embers → Malakim

#### First contact
- Malakim. You pray to the sun. The sun is only a fire that never fell.
- Desert people. Your god found you freezing in the wastes. Ours found us burning.
- Your god is light; ours is flame. Same thing, until someone gets burned.

#### Declares war
- Lugus lights your way. Bhall burns it.
- The sun cannot guard you at night, Malakim. Our fires burn all night long.
- Your Radiant Guard shines nicely. Let us see it shine on a pyre.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your judges weigh everything. I weigh nothing. I burn.
- Go back to your sand.
- No talk with sun-priests. Their light hurts my eyes.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Malakim. You are tough, for people who smile so much. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You know heat. That is something.
- Sun-children. Sit by the fire. You will not even notice it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars call Bhall a fallen thing. Careful.
- You look at orcs like a stain on clean sand. Speak quickly.
- Your Empyrean judges every case on its merits. Judge this one and go.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Fair, the way your Empyrean likes it.
- Agreed. Take it back across the desert.
- Done. Lugus and Bhall can both watch.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Malakim? Thank you. You are fair, even to orcs.
- Hm. The sun gives freely. Good.
- Thank you, sun-child. Bhall's fire remembers warmth.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer is drier than your desert.
- You tipped the scales your way. No.
- No. Even the sun would not shine on that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your sun is too hot even for orcs. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to your desert.
- Fine. The sun and the fire can share the sky.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your light is going out, and we are blowing on it.
- Peace? Your cities still shine. We want them dark.
- No. The sun sets every night. So will you.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Ask Lugus.
- No. Your Empyrean says the small and the great are equal. Then you pay us.
- We give nothing to sun-priests.

### Clan of Embers → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels. We are not demons, angel. We were men once, before our goddess fell.
- Mercurians. You hunt Hell. Our goddess is in Hell. Stay out of our way.
- Rebel angels. You broke the Compact and kept fighting. We like rule-breakers.

#### Declares war
- You fight demons. We fight whoever is in our way. Today that is you.
- Angels can burn. Bhall burned, and she was more than an angel.
- You want Hell, angel? We bring it to you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You looked at us like demons. Fine. Now we act like them.
- Go and fight your demons.
- No talk. You carve prayers into your skin; I will carve nothing for you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Angel. You hate demons, we hate the Bannor. Plenty of work for everyone.
- [CT_NAME]. You fight hard and you never stop. I respect that.
- Mercurian. Sit. No demons here, only orcs.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your angels look at orcs like hell-spawn. We are not. Careful.
- Speak, angel, and put that hammer down.
- You think Bhall's children belong in Hell? Our goddess is there. We are not.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. Angels deal straight.
- Agreed. A good bargain, for a zealot.
- Done. Go back to your war.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the angels? Hm. Thank you.
- Good. Even rebel angels can be generous.
- Thank you, Mercurian. Bhall's children remember who gave.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your war is not our war, and your price is not our price.
- No. Even an angel cannot make that fair.
- No. You care about demons, not bargains. It shows.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go and fight your demons. Peace.
- Peace. You have bigger enemies than orcs.
- Fine. Hell is your problem, not ours.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your host is thin. We finish it.
- Peace? You came to burn us like demons. We burn you first.
- No. We watched a goddess fall. Angels fall easier.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to angels? You do not even serve a god now.
- No. Go and shout at a demon; that is what you are for.
- We give nothing, angel. Carve that on your arm.

### Clan of Embers → Sheaim

#### First contact
- Sheaim. You want the world to end in fire. We saw that once, the day Bhall fell on Braduk. It is not as fun as you think.
- Gate-openers. You gather people from every nation into one purpose. So did Bhall's fall, and look what it made of them.
- Doom-priests. If the world burns, the Clan wants to be holding the torch, not standing in the fire.

#### Declares war
- You want to end the world. We only want your part of it.
- Open your gates, Sheaim. We will walk through and burn whatever is on the other side.
- The world ends when Bhall says, not when your cult says. We start with you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You want everything dead. Talking is a waste.
- Go and pray for Armageddon somewhere else.
- No. Your envoy kept talking about the end, so I showed one.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Sheaim. You love fire as much as we do. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. When your end of the world comes, tell us first. We want good seats.
- Cultist. Sit. And do not open anything.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your gates spit monsters onto our hunting grounds. Close them.
- You want the whole world dead, us included. Speak, and be quick about it.
- Your cultists smell of brimstone and despair. What now?

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. A good bargain, while there is still a world to spend it in.
- Agreed. If the world ends, you still owe us.
- Done. Enjoy it before your apocalypse.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim? You will not need it after the end, I suppose. Thank you.
- Thank you. We will spend it before your sky falls.
- Hm. Good. The doom-priests have manners.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Why trade with people who want tomorrow never to come?
- No. Your offer is as empty as the world you dream of.
- No. Bring something worth keeping, if you still own anything like that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your rituals. Peace.
- Peace. The world can last a little longer. We are not done with it.
- Fine. You are already fighting all of creation; you do not need us as well.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every Sheaim temple brings the end a step closer. We knock them down.
- Peace? You want everything dead. We want you dead first.
- No. Your gates close when your cities burn.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You want the world to end. You will not need it.
- No. We already lived through one end of the world. We will not pay for another.
- We give nothing to the doom-cult.

### Clan of Embers → Sidar

#### First contact
- Shades. Half your soul is gone, they say. Where did you put it?
- Sidar. You hide in your cities and watch the younger races fight. We are one of the younger races. We fight.
- Grey people. You look like smoke. Can smoke hold a spear?

#### Declares war
- You think yourselves too old for wars. Learn otherwise.
- Shades are hard to kill, they say. Fire is patient.
- Your hidden cities are not hidden any more. We found them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You gave up anger, shade. We run on it.
- I do not talk to ghosts.
- Fade back into your fog, and stay there.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Shade. You never get angry. Strange, but good for talking.
- [CT_NAME]. You watch the world from far away. What do you see?
- Grey ones. Sit. You do not need to eat, I hear. Good. More for us.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You call us a younger race, shade. We are old enough to burn you.
- Speak, before you fade away entirely.
- You stare at me like a dead thing. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. You bargain the way you do everything: cold, but fair.
- Agreed. Remember it, if you still remember things.
- Done. A deal with a ghost. Strange day.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the shades? So you still give things. Good.
- Thank you, grey one. Some of your soul is left after all.
- Hm. Good. The Clan will remember the Sidar.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. A thin offer, like a shade.
- No. You can wait a hundred years for my answer. It will still be no.
- No. Bring something with some weight to it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Hitting smoke is tiring. Peace.
- Peace. Go back to your hidden cities.
- Fine. You are fading anyway.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You came out of hiding. Now stay out.
- Peace? Your cities are full of things that burn.
- No. Even shades die, if you hit them enough.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to ghosts? No.
- No. You gave your soul away; go and give your gold away too.
- We give nothing to people who are barely there.

### Clan of Embers → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- Dark elves. The Winter Court. We hate winter.
- Svartalfar. You ruled while the snow fell. We sat by the fire and waited for it to end.
- You turned on your own kin when your god died. Even orcs do not do that. Well. Not often.

#### Declares war
- You love the winter, elf. We bring you the summer: fire.
- Your court plots in the shadows. Fire leaves no shadows.
- Esus sells miracles, they say. Buy one now, dark elf.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your tongue is poison.
- Go and whisper to your Shadowriders.
- No. Dark elves smile, then stab. I know.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Dark elf. You are cruel, and we are honest about being cruel. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your court is clever. Be clever with me.
- Svartalfar. Sit near the fire. It is good for winter folk.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Shadowriders cut my scouts' throats. Speak.
- Stop smiling, elf. I know what that smile means.
- Speak, winter-elf, before I warm you up.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fine. I checked it for knives. It is clean.
- Agreed. Even the Winter Court can be fair.
- Done. Do not try to cheat it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Svartalfar? What is the trick?
- Thank you, dark elf. I will watch my back anyway.
- Hm. Good. Generous, for winter.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargains have knives hidden in them.
- No. Esus might pay that; we will not.
- No. Too cold, elf. Like everything you offer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your war with the forest elves. Peace.
- Peace. Your shadows are tiring.
- Fine. Winter and fire can stand apart.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Winter ends. So will you.
- Peace? Your court would plot a new war tomorrow.
- No. The Ice is gone, and its court goes too.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Winter Court? We paid winter enough for one age.
- No. Go and ask Esus.
- We give nothing, dark elf, in any season.

## Doviello

### Doviello → Amurites

#### First contact
- Amurites. Your Kylorin once brought the wolf to heel. The wolf remembers.
- Children of Kylorin. The old wizard beat us in the snow. You are not the old wizard.
- Mages. You smell of ink and candle smoke. The pack has never feared either.

#### Declares war
- Kylorin turned us against our old master and the winter ended. Now we collect what that cost us.
- Your mages are clever. Clever does not outrun wolves.
- The wolf heeled once, for Kylorin. Kylorin walked into the ice and never came back. Nobody holds the leash now.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. The last time the pack listened to an Amurite, we lost the winter.
- Diplomacy is a spell of the weak, and I do not stand still for spells.
- Go back to your school. The pack is eating.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Amurite. Your fire keeps the beasts off. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You are strong in your own way. I respect strength, any kind of it.
- Mage. Sit. Keep your hands still; my warriors get nervous when wizards wave them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You look at us the way Kylorin did, like dogs to be trained. Careful.
- Speak, wizard. My patience is short and my axe is long.
- Your mages scorched my hunters. Tell me why I should not answer in kind.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A fair kill, fairly shared.
- Agreed. Even a mage can count the meat right.
- Done. Go back to your books.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Kylorin's children. Hmph. The old wolf-tamer would be surprised.
- Good. The pack eats well tonight, and it knows who fed it.
- You give without being asked. Strange people. Thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Mage tricks. The pack is not so easily fooled.
- No. You offer the bones and keep the meat.
- No. I do not need what your schoolmasters think I need.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your fire is hot, and the pack backs away. For now.
- Peace. There is weaker prey than mages.
- Fine. The wolf goes off to lick its burns. It will be back.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You are bleeding, wizard. The pack does not walk away from blood.
- Peace? Kylorin is not here to save you this time.
- No. Your schools burn first. Then we talk.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Kylorin took enough from us. You get nothing.
- No. If you want it, come and take it. Bring your spells.
- You demand, mage? The pack has been waiting for an excuse.

### Doviello → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- Clowns. You hid from the White Hand all through the winter. We hunted beside it. Hiding is for prey.
- Balseraphs. Masks and laughter. And under the mask? Meat.
- Your court plays games with minds. The pack's mind is simple: hunt, eat, survive.

#### Declares war
- The pack is hungry, and your freaks are slow.
- You keep slaves in cages. We will open the cages and eat whatever comes out.
- Laugh, Balseraph. Wolves like prey that makes noise.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words twist like your dancers.
- No talk. I do not listen to jesters.
- Diplomacy is a trick, and you are a whole court of tricks. Go.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Balseraph. You are mad, but you bite. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your harlequins fight like wildcats. I like that.
- Clown. Sit. Do not sing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Taskmasters put my hunters in chains. Speak, before I chain yours.
- Stop grinning. Wolves show their teeth only when they mean it.
- Your mind-mages sniff around my shamans. Keep out of their heads.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. No tricks in it? Then done.
- Agreed. A fair share, even from a madhouse.
- Done. Take it, and stop laughing.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the mad court? I will sniff it first.
- Good. Not all your clowns are useless.
- Hmph. Thank you, Balseraph. Strange, but thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There is a trick in it somewhere.
- Your offer is all paint and no meat. No.
- No. Go and laugh at someone else.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your freaks bite back. Peace.
- Peace. Go and dance somewhere far from my hunting grounds.
- Fine. There is weaker prey than madmen.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The pack smells your fear under the paint.
- Peace? Your mask is slipping. We keep pulling.
- No. The show is over when the pack says it is over.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Hah. You are funny after all.
- No. Juggle for it.
- No. Send your mimics to steal it, if they dare come near the pack.

### Doviello → Bannor

#### First contact
- Bannor. Every farm a fort, every peasant drilled. A herd that thinks it is a pack.
- You march in neat rows and pray to your Junil. We hunt in the snow and pray to nobody.
- Crusaders. Your priests decide who must repent. The pack decides who must die. We will see whose list is shorter.

#### Declares war
- Your free lands are fat and full of conscripts. The pack is hungry.
- You fight for law. We fight to eat. The hungry one always fights harder.
- Bring your Orders and your Families, Bannor. Wolves love a crowded field.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your Confessors talk; I do not listen.
- Go back to your Halls and pray. We are busy.
- Diplomacy is a trick of the weak. And you have a whole priesthood of it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Bannor. You train every child to fight. That I respect. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your soldiers are good. Not as good as mine. Speak.
- Crusader. No sermons, and we will get along.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your priests named us damned. Fine. Say what you want, then go.
- You look at the Doviello like beasts to be put down. Try it.
- Shouldn't you be drilling your peasants for our war?

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A fair trade, even with priests in it.
- Agreed. Your Order counts carefully. So do wolves.
- Done. Take it back to your fortress.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Bannor? Your priests must be furious. Good. Thank you.
- Hmph. Generous, for people who think we are damned.
- Good. The pack remembers who fed it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You want obedience in every bargain. Not from us.
- No. Take your scraps back to your conscripts.
- No. The wolf does not trade the haunch for a bone.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your soldiers hold their line. Peace, for now.
- Peace. There is weaker prey than drilled men.
- Fine. Go home and bury your dead. We will bury ours.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your lines are breaking. The pack does not stop now.
- Peace? You came to make us repent. We are making you bleed.
- No. Your crusade started this. We finish it.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Order? Junil can come and take it himself.
- No. We bow to no god and no priest.
- You want something from the pack, Bannor? Try to take it. That is the only way.

### Doviello → Calabim

#### First contact
- Calabim. You keep men in pens like sheep. The pack would sooner die than live as your cattle.
- Bloodsuckers. You hunted the weak through the Ice too. At least we eat what we kill.
- You call your people bloodpets. We call ours warriors. We will see which lasts.

#### Declares war
- You farm men. We hunt. Today we hunt the farmers.
- Your nobles grow soft on blood they never chase. The pack will show them a real hunt.
- Better to die a warrior than live in your pens. Come and see how the Doviello die.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You talk sweetly, then you bite. I know the trick.
- I do not bargain with leeches.
- Diplomacy is how herds are made. We will not be herded.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Calabim. You are predators. I respect predators. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your hall is too warm and too quiet. Say what you want.
- Night-hunter. Sit. Keep your teeth to yourself.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Broods sniff around my camps. My wolves smell them.
- Speak, bloodsucker. And do not look at my throat.
- You want my people for your cellars. Try it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A fair share. Rare, from a vampire.
- Agreed. Nobody drinks from my envoys.
- Done. Take it, and keep your fangs in.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Calabim? What do you want, vampire?
- Hmph. Thank you. You are not as cold as they say.
- Good. The pack remembers.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You want to drain us slowly. Not with a bargain, not with anything.
- No. The pack does not trade with its shepherds.
- No. Too much blood in that deal, and all of it ours.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your vampires are hard to kill. Peace.
- Peace. There is weaker prey than the dead.
- Fine. Go back to your herds. We go back to the hunt.

#### Refuses peace
- No. We smell blood, and for once it is yours.
- Peace? So you can fill your pens again? No.
- No. The pack will not stop until your castles are empty.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Drink it from someone else.
- No. The Doviello are not your cattle.
- You want something from the pack? Come and bite for it.

### Doviello → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs. You huddled around your fire all through the Ice while we ran free in the snow. Which of us came out stronger?
- Clan of Embers. Raiders like us, but you need a goddess to tell you when to hunt.
- Your goddess fell, and you crawled after her. The pack follows no one who falls.

#### Declares war
- Your camps are fat with plunder, and the pack wants it.
- You hid by Braduk's fire while the wolves ruled the snow. Come out and fight in the cold.
- Two raiders, one hunting ground. Only one walks away.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You want to talk because you are losing.
- Diplomacy is for the weak, orc. You know it as well as I do.
- Grunt at your fire. I am not listening.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Orc. You fight, you raid, you do not whine. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. The Clan and the pack both know the world belongs to the strong.
- Clan. Sit. There is no fire here; we never needed one.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders took my hunting grounds. Explain.
- You smell of smoke and goblin. Speak fast.
- Shouldn't you be guarding your fire from my war?

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Split the way a kill should be.
- Agreed. Even orcs know when to share.
- Done. Carry it back to Braduk.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Plunder, shared with the pack? You are smarter than most orcs.
- Hmph. Generous, for an orc.
- Thank you. Next raid, we hunt side by side.

#### Turns down a deal
- You keep the haunch and hand me the hoof. No.
- No. Orc bargains are as crude as orc axes.
- No. Your goblins could not haggle worse.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. You fight well, orc. Peace.
- Peace. There is weaker prey than the Clan.
- Fine. The crows have eaten enough of us both.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your clans are breaking, and the pack smells it.
- Peace? Your banner is down. We do not stop now.
- No. Your fire is going out. We will stamp on the ashes.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Orcs take; they do not beg. Neither do wolves.
- No. Fight for it.
- You want our kill? Take it in single combat, before the whole pack.

### Doviello → Elohim

#### First contact
- Elohim. You carry the old, nurse the sick, feed the weak. The wolf leaves them in the snow, and the pack survives.
- Monks. You glorify weakness and call it holiness.
- So you are the ones who tend the broken. You must be busy. The world breaks a lot.

#### Declares war
- Your cities are full of the sick and the old. Easy prey.
- You shelter the weak. The pack culls the weak. We cannot share a world.
- Your monks fight without weapons. We fight with everything. Let us see.

#### Refuses to talk
- No sermons, monk. Go and bandage something.
- Peace is what the weak beg for. We do not hear it.
- No. Your envoy wanted to pray over my dead. My dead were strong. They need nothing.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Elohim. You are soft, but you do not lie. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You keep your holy places, we keep our hunting grounds. Fine.
- Monk. Sit. Do not try to heal anybody.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You look at the pack like a sickness to be cured. We are the cure.
- Speak, monk, and keep your blessings to yourself.
- Your healers keep weaklings alive in my lands. Stop it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Honest trade. Good.
- Agreed. Take it to your shrines.
- Done. Go and nurse someone.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift? Hmph. You give like you heal: for nothing.
- Thank you, monk. Strange custom.
- Good. Even the pack remembers kindness.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Charity is your trade. Not ours.
- No. You offer what the weak need. We are not weak.
- No. Bring more, or bring nothing.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your monks fight better than they should. Peace.
- Peace. Go and tend your wounded.
- Fine. Keep your shrines. There is nothing in them to eat.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You keep the weak alive. We finish them.
- Peace? Your holy places are not ours yet.
- No. The strong do not stop because the weak ask nicely.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You give everything away. Why would you need ours?
- No. Pray for it.
- You demand, monk? With what army?

### Doviello → Grigori

#### First contact
- Grigori. No gods, no masters. The pack understands. No god ever helped us through the winter either.
- You lead yourselves, they say. Good. Weak leaders get culled. Are yours strong?
- Adventurers. Heroes who fight alone. Wolves hunt together. We will see which is better.

#### Declares war
- Your heroes are strong, but they are few. The pack is many.
- No god will save you, Grigori. Good. Nothing will.
- Your adventurers have hunted my wolves long enough. Now the pack hunts them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your angel gives advice. I want none.
- You turned from the gods so you could choose for yourselves. I choose war.
- Go away, godless. The pack is busy.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Grigori. You stand on your own feet. I like that. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. No priest, no prayer, no sermon. Good. Speak.
- Your cities take in whoever wants a life of their own. Even beastmen?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your adventurers come into my lands to kill my hunters for glory. Speak.
- You think yourselves above the gods. Above the pack too?
- Speak quickly. Your angel walked out of heaven; it will not walk in here to help you.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A free bargain between free people.
- Agreed. Nobody blessed it. Better that way.
- Done. Let your heroes carry it home.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, and no god told you to give it? Good. Thank you.
- Hmph. The godless are generous.
- Thank you, Grigori. When the pack hunts, it will hunt elsewhere.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your heroes take risks. I do not take bad ones.
- No. Even a free man can make a stupid offer.
- No. Ask your angel for advice; it will tell you this was poor.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your heroes are hard to bring down. Peace.
- Peace. Go and lead yourselves somewhere else.
- Fine. One hero's blood costs too many wolves.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your heroes are falling one by one. The pack keeps going.
- Peace? No god protects you. Nothing stops us.
- No. You chose to stand alone. Now stand.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Earn it, like one of your heroes.
- No. If you want it, send an adventurer to take it.
- No god backs that demand, Grigori, and neither does the pack.

### Doviello → Hippus

#### First contact
- Hippus. Horse-raiders. You raid your own kin; that is how the strong are found.
- Horse lords. Your mounts are fast. They are also delicious.
- You held off the frostling hordes through the Ice, clan by clan, without begging help. Not bad.

#### Declares war
- Your herds are fat, and the pack is hungry.
- Ride, Hippus. Wolves chase what runs.
- Your mercenaries are far away earning foreign gold. Your herds are close. We take the herds.

#### Refuses to talk
- You sell your word for gold. No.
- Ride away, horseman, while your horse still has legs.
- No. You would sell this peace to my enemies before nightfall.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hippus. You raid, you fight for your own, you do not grovel. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your riders and my pack could run down half of Erebus together.
- Horseman. Sit. Tie the horse far away, or the wolves will have it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your riders stole my hunters' kills. Speak.
- You fought for my enemy, for gold. Why should I listen now?
- Speak, horse-thief, and keep your lance down.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A fair price. You know prices.
- Agreed. Gold is gold, even from a sell-sword.
- Done. Gallop home with it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from a mercenary, without a contract? Hmph. Thank you.
- Good. When we raid the steppe, we will remember whose herds to leave alone.
- Thank you, horseman. Strong people share the kill.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your price is a horse-thief's price.
- No. Your companies would not ride a day for that. Neither will I.
- You are selling me a lame horse. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your riders are hard to run down. Peace.
- Peace. There is slower prey on the steppe.
- Fine. Go and sell your lances.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your herds are scattered, and the pack eats.
- Peace? Your horses are tired. Wolves never tire of the chase.
- No. Run, Hippus. Run until your horse drops.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? A sell-sword asking for pay with no fight? Earn it.
- No. Raid someone else; the pack bites back.
- No. The Doviello pay no one, least of all a hired lance.

### Doviello → Illians

#### First contact
- Illians. In the Ice, your White Hand let us hunt any tribe Mulcarn hated. Those were good years.
- So the winter has a master again. The pack has been sniffing at your plans, Illian.
- Men of Letum Frigus. We turned on your god once. Some of us wonder if that was a mistake.

#### Declares war
- We helped end the winter once. We can bury its heirs too.
- Your would-be god is not Mulcarn. The pack does not heel for pretenders.
- The ice was ours to hunt, never yours to rule. We take it back.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. The winter does not talk, and neither does the wolf.
- Go back to your broken mountain.
- No. Your priests once told the pack whom to hunt. Not any more.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Illian. The cold comes in with you. The pack likes the cold. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. When the snows return, the Doviello may hunt beside you again.
- Winter-man. Sit. You will not need a fire, and neither will we.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You look at us like hounds that ran off. We were never your hounds.
- Speak, Illian. The pack remembers which side it chose, and why.
- Your would-be god has been looking at our hunting grounds. Speak, then look elsewhere.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Like the old days. Agreed.
- Agreed. Winter and wolf, trading again.
- Done. Carry it home to Letum Frigus.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the winter? Hmph. It has been a long time.
- Thank you, Illian. The pack remembers the cold years kindly.
- Good. The snow was generous once too, to those strong enough to live in it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You think the pack is still your dog. It is not.
- No. Your offer is as thin as spring ice.
- No. The winter took from us once; now it wants to take again.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Wolves and winter should not fight. Peace.
- Peace. Bring back the snow, and we will talk about more.
- Fine. We may need each other when the world turns cold again.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The ice is cracking under you, Illian.
- Peace? You wanted us back on a leash. Now feel the teeth.
- No. Your winter is not ours any more.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? The White Hand never asked the pack for tribute. Neither will you.
- No. We heel for nobody, not even the cold.
- The winter never had to ask; it simply took. You are not the winter yet.

### Doviello → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons. Strong ones, they say. Are you strong, or only loud?
- Agares' hell has climbed up into Erebus. Our dead go to Camulos, where the real fighters are. We are not impressed.
- Infernal. You crush those below you and hate those above. Like a pack, except a pack has a leader worth following.

#### Declares war
- Hell is strong, you say. Prove it.
- Our dead go to Camulos. Today we send him some of yours.
- Your demons hunt souls. The pack hunts demons.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A demon's word is a snare.
- Go back to Agares.
- No. The pack does not bargain with Hell.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Demon. You fight hard. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. The weak fear you. The pack does not. That is why we can talk.
- Infernal. Sit. Mind the furs; they burn.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your demons dragged my hunters into the pit. Explain.
- You smell like burning hair. What do you want?
- Shouldn't you be back in your pit, preparing for our war?

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. I read it twice. Fair.
- Agreed. The strong deal with the strong.
- Done. Cheat me, and the pack comes for you, even in Hell.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Hell? What is the price?
- Hmph. Thank you, demon. I will sniff it for curses.
- Good. Even Hell can share a kill.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Demon bargains bite.
- No. My soul goes to Camulos, not into your small print.
- No. Not even for Hell's gold.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Hell is strong; so is the pack. Peace.
- Peace. Go and torment the weak; there are plenty of them.
- Fine. Demon meat is too tough anyway.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your demons bleed black, and the pack likes the taste.
- Peace? Camulos would laugh me out of his vault.
- No. Back into the pit, demon.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to Hell? Camulos would never forgive me.
- No. Come and take it, if Hell is so strong.
- No. The pack bends to no demon.

### Doviello → Khazad

#### First contact
- Dwarves. You hid under the hills through the whole Ice. We hunted on the snow above your heads.
- Khazad. In the old days our wolves tasted dwarf once or twice. Tough meat.
- Gold-counters. Gold does not keep you warm in the snow.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are full, and your legs are short. The pack is coming.
- You hid from the winter for three generations. Hide from us now.
- Stone walls do not stop wolves. Wolves wait.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back underground.
- No. Your merchants talk and talk. I do not listen.
- Diplomacy is a dwarf trick: you count our losses while you talk.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Dwarf. You are tough. Good. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You fight hard for your gold. The pack respects that.
- Khazad. Sit. Bring your own beer; ours would kill you.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your miners dig into my hunting grounds. Stop.
- Speak, dwarf. Gold will not buy my patience.
- You look at us like wolves at your door. Good guess.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A dwarf bargain. Fair.
- Agreed. You weighed it; I trust the weight.
- Done. Take it back to your hall.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A dwarf giving away gold? The world is ending.
- Hmph. Thank you, dwarf. I did not know you could let go.
- Good. The pack leaves your caravans alone this year.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You weigh with a thumb on the scale.
- No. A dwarf price for a dwarf profit.
- No. Take your coins back underground.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your axes are sharp. Peace.
- Peace. Go back under your mountain.
- Fine. Gnawing on stone walls breaks teeth.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your gates will open sometime. Wolves wait.
- Peace? Your vaults are still full.
- No. The pack has your scent, dwarf.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You have more gold than anyone in Erebus.
- No. Dig for it.
- The pack pays no dwarf, not one copper.

### Doviello → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- Kuriotates. You take in every stray in the wilds. The pack drives strays off.
- Centaurs, giants, snake-women and men, all in one herd. A strange herd.
- Your settlements spread thin over wide land. Thin herds are easy to pick off.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements are far from your cities. The pack hunts stragglers.
- Pull back into your shell, Kuriotate. Wolves wait outside shells.
- A pack never follows a pup, and it never fears one.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back to your great cities.
- No. You talk like a court of many tongues. I have one.
- Diplomacy is for nations that hide. So hide.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Kuriotate. Your centaurs run well. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You hold many peoples together. That takes teeth.
- Your giants are strong. Sit, and bring one.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlements eat into my hunting grounds. Stop.
- You shelter the ones the pack drives off. Stop it.
- Speak, Kuriotate, then go back to your shell.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Fair, for a nation of strays.
- Agreed. Your merchants are honest. Strange.
- Done. Let a centaur carry it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift? Hmph. You feed everyone, even wolves.
- Thank you, Kuriotate. You have many mouths to feed, and still you share.
- Good. Your settlements will be left alone this winter.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your client tribes may take that. I will not.
- No. A thin offer from a thin border.
- No. Strays take scraps. Wolves do not.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your giants and centaurs fight like a real pack. Peace.
- Peace. Keep to your heartland.
- Fine. Centaur meat is stringy anyway.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your settlements burn one by one.
- Peace? You hide in your shell. Stay there while we eat the rest.
- No. The pack has the scent of your outlands.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Feed your strays with it.
- No. The pack is not one of your protectorates.
- We pay nothing, Kuriotate. Not to you, not to any crowned child.

### Doviello → Lanun

#### First contact
- Sea-people. Wolves do not swim. Do not worry; we will wait on the shore.
- Lanun. The ice took your seas too, and some of your crews never came home. The weak ones.
- Pirates. You take what you want. So do we. Your way is just wetter.

#### Declares war
- Your ships are fast. Your harbours are not.
- Every sailor comes ashore sometime. The pack will be waiting.
- Danalin does not answer you any more. Nobody will.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A pirate's word floats away.
- Go back to your boat.
- No. Talk to the fish.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Captain. You are bold. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You raid by sea, we raid by land. A good split.
- Lanun. Sit. The floor does not move here.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders hit my coast. Speak.
- You smell of fish and lies. Speak fast.
- A pirate. Hmph. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Fair, for a pirate.
- Agreed. Sign it, and keep your word for once.
- Done. Load it on your ship and go.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from a pirate? Whose was it?
- Hmph. Thank you, captain.
- Good. The sea was kind to you, and you to us.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I know a pirate's bargain when I smell one.
- No. That bargain is as rotten as old fish.
- No. Throw it overboard.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Chasing ships is a waste of good wolves. Peace.
- Peace. Keep to the water.
- Fine. You have your sea; we have our snow.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your harbours are still standing.
- Peace? A pirate's peace lasts one tide.
- No. You can sail away. Your land cannot.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Steal it from someone else.
- No. Come ashore and take it.
- The pack pays no pirate.

### Doviello → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- Elves. The Ice nearly finished you. You hid in a few groves while we hunted in the open.
- Ljosalfar. Your god died and you nearly died with him. Weak gods make weak peoples.
- Forest folk. Good hunting in your woods: deer, boar, elves.

#### Declares war
- Your forests are full of game. The pack hunts there now.
- You survived the Ice in hiding. You will not survive the pack.
- Your trees cannot shield you. Wolves love the forest.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Whisper to your oaks; they have the patience for it.
- No. Elves talk for a hundred years. I have no time.
- Go back to your groves.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Elf. You shoot well. I respect that. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your forests are good hunting. Share them?
- Ljosalfar. Sit. Do not tell me about leaves.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your rangers shoot my hunters from the trees. Speak.
- You look at us like beasts loose in your forest. Speak, and go.
- Speak, elf, before the pack comes into your woods.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Fair, elf.
- Agreed. Take it to your groves.
- Done. The forest folk can count, at least.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the elves? Hmph. Thank you.
- Good. The pack will hunt elsewhere this season.
- Thank you, elf. You are less soft than you look.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You think the pack is stupid.
- No. A slow offer, and a small one.
- No. Not even a fawn would take that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your arrows find us in every tree. Peace.
- Peace. Keep your forest.
- Fine. There is weaker prey than elves.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your groves are falling.
- Peace? You hid once. Hide again.
- No. The pack is deep in your forest now.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Go and shake your trees; maybe something falls out.
- No. The forest feeds you. Let it.
- The pack pays nothing to elves.

### Doviello → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- Luchuirp. Your cities died in the Ice because you were soft. We lived because we were not.
- Little folk with clay servants. A people who cannot even hunt for themselves.
- Golem-makers. Your clay men cracked and froze in the winter. We did not.

#### Declares war
- Your golems are slow. The pack is fast. We go around them.
- You need machines to fight. We need teeth.
- The Ice nearly finished the little folk. The pack will finish the job.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go and patch your clay men.
- Diplomacy is a machine of the weak. I break machines.
- No. I talk to the maker, not the clay.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Little smith. You make good axes. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your golems are strong. I want one.
- Luchuirp. Sit. Leave the golem outside; the wolves do not like it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems stomped through my hunting grounds. Speak.
- Speak, smith. Your clay does not scare me.
- You look at the pack like a broken machine. Careful.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Well made. Agreed.
- Agreed. You build good bargains.
- Done. Take it back to your forge.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Luchuirp? Does it bite?
- Thank you, smith. Good work.
- Good. The pack will not trouble your golems this season.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Too many gears, too little meat.
- No. You build better than you bargain.
- No. Golem junk.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Clay does not bleed. No fun in it. Peace.
- Peace. Go and build.
- Fine. There is softer prey than golems.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems are broken. Your makers are next.
- Peace? You could not survive the cold. You will not survive us.
- No. Your forges will be ours.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Build it.
- No. Ask your golems.
- The pack pays no smith.

### Doviello → Malakim

#### First contact
- Malakim. Your hunters once nursed a dying stranger out of the snow instead of leaving the body to the wolves. We would not have.
- Sun-people. You walked out of the cold into the light. We stayed in the cold and grew strong.
- Desert folk. Hot sand, hard sun. Hard people? We will see.

#### Declares war
- Your sun is bright. The pack hunts by night.
- You took in the weak and called it faith. Now see what that costs.
- The light of Lugus shows the pack the way to your cities.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your judges weigh every word. I have no time for scales.
- Go back to the desert.
- Your light hurts my eyes. No.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Malakim. You live in the desert; you must be tough. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Your Empyrean says the small and the great are equal. The pack does not. Talk anyway.
- Sun-child. Sit in the shade.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars preach to my hunters. Stop it.
- You look at the pack like darkness to be lit up. Speak and go.
- Shouldn't you be praying to your sun before our war?

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Just, like your Empyrean.
- Agreed. Fair weight on both sides.
- Done. Take it back across the sand.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Malakim? You give the way the sun does, without being asked. Thank you.
- Hmph. Thank you, desert-man.
- Good. The pack remembers who shares their water.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your scales are bent.
- No. A dry offer, from a dry land.
- No. Even your sun cannot make that look good.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your sun burns. Peace.
- Peace. Keep your desert.
- Fine. Sand is poor hunting ground.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your light is fading.
- Peace? The night is long, and the pack hunts by night.
- No. You chose to save the weak. Now save yourselves.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Pray to your sun for it.
- No. The pack bows to no light.
- We pay nothing to sun-priests.

### Doviello → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels. You carve prayers into your own flesh with a knife. That, I understand.
- Mercurians. You broke the Compact to keep fighting. The pack never signed anything.
- You care nothing for people, only for your war. We care for the pack and the hunt. Close enough.

#### Declares war
- Angels bleed too. Let us see what colour.
- You hunt demons. Today the pack hunts angels.
- You think only Hell is worth fighting. The pack will teach you otherwise.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. All you talk about is demons.
- Go back to your war in Hell.
- No. Your hammer does your talking. My axe answers.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Angel. You never stop fighting. Good. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You are a hunter, like me. Your prey is just uglier.
- Mercurian. Sit. No demons here, only wolves.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your angels look at the pack like hell-spawn. We are not. Speak.
- You turned your back on Arawn. Do not turn it on me.
- You look at us like something to purge. Try it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. A straight deal, from a straight blade.
- Agreed. Angels do not cheat.
- Done. Go back to your demons.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the angels? Hmph. Thank you.
- Good. Even a warrior of heaven shares the kill.
- Thank you, Mercurian. The wolves will not forget it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your war, your price. Not mine.
- You know swords, angel, not bargains. No.
- No. Not even your prayers could make that a fair offer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go and hunt demons. Peace.
- Peace. You have a bigger war than us.
- Fine. Fighting angels is costly, and there is no meat on them.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your host is small and far from heaven. The pack eats the stragglers.
- Peace? You came at us like we were demons. Now you meet wolves.
- No. Angels fall. The pack waits for it.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to angels? You serve no god any more. Why should we serve you?
- No. Find a demon to scare.
- The pack pays nothing to heaven, and nothing to its deserters.

### Doviello → Sheaim

#### First contact
- Sheaim. You want the world to end. The wolf wants a world full of prey. We will not get along.
- Gate-openers. You gathered from every nation to bring the end. The pack gathered to survive. Only one of those makes sense.
- Doom-cult. When the world ends, what will you eat?

#### Declares war
- You want to end the world. The pack wants to live in it. You go first.
- Open your gates, Sheaim. The pack will eat whatever comes out, and then you.
- The pack survived the Age of Ice. It will survive your Armageddon. You will not.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You want everything dead. What is there to talk about?
- Go and summon something.
- No. Diplomacy is the trick of the weak, and you are the weakest of all: you want to die.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Sheaim. You are strange, but you are not soft. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. Tell me when the end is coming. The pack will be somewhere else.
- Cultist. Sit, and keep your gates shut.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your gates spit beasts onto my hunting grounds. Close them.
- Speak, doom-priest, and leave the end of the world out of it.
- You want the pack dead with the rest of creation. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Fine. Use it before your end comes.
- Agreed. Strange, trading with people who want no tomorrow.
- Done. The world lasts a little longer for this.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim? You will not need it, I suppose. Thank you.
- Hmph. Generous, for people who want everything gone.
- Good. The pack will put it to use, while there is a world to use it in.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You want the world dead; why would you trade fairly in it?
- No. An empty offer, from an empty faith.
- No. Bring something worth surviving for.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go and chant. Peace.
- Peace. The pack prefers prey that wants to live; it runs better.
- Fine. The world is not ending today.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every Sheaim city is a gate to the end. We close them.
- Peace? You want everyone dead. Start with yourselves.
- No. The pack does not stop for doom-priests.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? For the end of the world? Keep your doom and your begging.
- No. Survive without it, if you even want to.
- We pay nothing to the end of the world.

### Doviello → Sidar

#### First contact
- Shades. No smell, no blood, no hunger. What are you?
- Sidar. You traded half your souls to live forever. The pack trades nothing; we take.
- Grey people. You hide in your cities and watch the younger races. Watch closely.

#### Declares war
- Shades die hard, they say. The pack is patient.
- You keep out of the world's wars. This one came looking for you.
- Your hidden cities have a scent after all. We found it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. I do not talk to fog.
- Fade away, shade.
- No. You gave up anger. I did not.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Shade. There is no fear in you. Good. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. You have lived long. Tell the pack something useful.
- Grey one. Sit. You do not eat, so there is more for us.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You call us a younger race. Younger, and hungrier. Speak.
- You stare like a dead man. Speak.
- Speak, shade, before you fade out entirely.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. Cold, but fair.
- Agreed. Long memory, short bargain.
- Done. A deal with a ghost.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the shades? So some of your soul is left. Thank you.
- Hmph. Thank you, grey one.
- Good. Even ghosts can share a kill.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. A thin offer from a thin people.
- No. You can wait forever. I will not.
- No. Put some blood in it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Biting fog is no fun. Peace.
- Peace. Drift back into your mist.
- Fine. There is prey that bleeds.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your cities are full of the living.
- Peace? You came out of hiding. Stay out.
- No. Even shades break, if you bite hard enough.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute, to a ghost? The wolf does not feed what it cannot smell.
- No. You have forever to earn it yourselves.
- The pack pays nothing to the half-dead.

### Doviello → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- Svartalfar. The Winter Court. The pack loved the winter too.
- Dark elves. You threw out your dead god and hunted your own kin. That is how a pack stays strong.
- Your court ruled while the snow fell. When it melted, you lost your crown and we lost our winter. We understand each other.

#### Declares war
- Winter is over, elf, and wolves are hungry after winter.
- You hunted your own kin through the Ice. The pack hunts you now.
- Your Shadowriders are quiet. Wolves are quieter.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your tongue drips poison. No.
- Go and plot with your shadows.
- No. Dark elves smile before they stab.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Dark elf. You are cruel, and honest about it. Talk.
- [CT_NAME]. The Winter Court and the winter pack. Talk.
- Svartalfar. Sit. It is cold in here; you will like it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Shadowriders slit my hunters' throats in the night. Speak.
- Stop smiling, elf. I know what it means.
- Speak, before I show you what winter really is.

#### Accepts a deal
- Hmph. No knives in it? Fine.
- Agreed. Even Esus would call that fair.
- Done. Cheat it, and you will meet the pack in the dark.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Svartalfar? What is the trap?
- Hmph. Thank you, dark elf. I will still watch my back.
- Good. Winter folk share in hard times.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There is a blade under that offer.
- No. Esus may pay for miracles. I do not pay for tricks.
- No. Too cold, even for me.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your war with the forest elves.
- Peace. Stalking shadows is tiring work.
- Fine. Winter folk should not bleed each other.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You culled your own; now we cull you.
- Peace? Your court would plot a new war by morning.
- No. The pack has your scent, and it is cold and clear.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Ask Esus; he sells things.
- No. We give nothing, dark elf.
- You demand like the court that ruled the winter. The pack bows to no court.

## Elohim

### Elohim → Amurites

#### First contact
- Children of Kylorin, we are the Elohim, keepers of the old shrines. We hear your schools teach every art there is; we pray they also teach restraint.
- Peace to you, [CT_NAME]. Our monks have tended the fonts of power since before Patria rose. You will find us glad to show them, and slow to surrender them.
- The Elohim greet the Amurites. You count your mages and we count our pilgrims; between us, perhaps the world can be both learned and kind.

#### Declares war
- Your laws only fence necromancy in; ours forbid it outright. Your wizards have dug too near the dead, and the Elohim will stand between them and the grave.
- We kept the holy places through the Age of Ice so that no wizard could bleed them for power. You have reached for them, Amurite. Now we must take your hands away.
- It grieves us to raise a hand against the heirs of the man who ended the long winter. But Kylorin's children have forgotten why he walked into the ice.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your archmages argue for a season over a single word. Let them argue among themselves for now; the Elohim have nothing to add.
- We will not trade words with those whose fire still falls on our pilgrims. Come back when your war-mages are silent.
- Not now. A people who worship magic for its own sake must first learn what it costs everyone else.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, scholar. Our chants keep what knowledge survived the ice, and your libraries keep the rest. What shall we share today?
- The Amurites are always welcome at our abbeys, so long as your mages leave their wands at the gate as a courtesy to the brothers.
- Come in, friend. Our brothers say your adepts have been sanctifying the land along our borders. That is good work, and we are grateful for it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You permit what you ought to forbid, and your schools call it study. Speak, Amurite, but be brief; our patience is a virtue, not a bottomless well.
- Your mages were seen at our shrines again, measuring the stones and taking notes. Say what you want, and keep your instruments in their cases.
- Even the Children of Kylorin cannot reason their way past every wrong they have done. Why are you here?

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair exchange, scholar to pilgrim. The Elohim accept with thanks.
- Agreed. May the knowledge pass both ways, and be used gently on both sides of the border.
- We accept. Your people bargain the way your archmages argue, at great length, but honestly in the end.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Amurites with no footnote attached? Your headmasters will gossip about this for a decade. Thank you, friend.
- You honor us. Generosity is rarer than talent, even among the Children of Kylorin, and we will remember it in our chants.
- Thank you. We will teach this kindness to our novices, beside the names of the others who gave without asking.

#### Turns down a deal
- We are sorry, but the Elohim cannot part with this. Some things are kept, not traded, even with scholars.
- This bargain would serve your schools far better than our people. We must decline, gently but firmly.
- No, scholar. Our brothers would ask what we gained by it, and we would have no answer to give them.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough fire has fallen on both our peoples. Let your mages go back to their studies, and our monks to their wounded.
- Peace, then. Return to your towers, Amurite, and may no student of yours ever need the spells of war again.
- We accept, and gladly. The Elohim never wished to quarrel with the heirs of the man who brought back the sun.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while your war-mages stand on our soil. We renounced violence, not resolve; withdraw them, and we will talk.
- Your schools would only use the quiet to prepare new fire. We must see this through, Amurite.
- You offer peace the way you offer a lecture, expecting us to nod along. Our dead cannot nod. The war goes on.

#### Rejects a demand
- You ask us to fund your schools with our alms? Our bread goes to the hungry, not to archmages.
- No. Even the cleverest argument from your lecture halls does not turn a demand into a kindness.
- The Elohim give freely to those in need. You are not in need, [CT_NAME]; you only want more.

### Elohim → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- Greetings, Balseraph. Kylorin sealed a great mind in the Tower of Eyes for a reason; the Elohim will be watching to learn whether that reason still holds.
- We are the Elohim. We have heard laughter carried on the wind from your court, and screams beneath it. Which will we hear today?
- Peace to you, and to every puppet in your court. We pray their strings are cut gently, some day.

#### Declares war
- Your taskmasters drag free people to Jubilee in chains to dance for your court. The Elohim have come to end the performance.
- We tended the broken in the Age of Dragons, and we will tend your slaves now. First, the cages must open.
- No more masks. Your harlequins call it play, and we call it torment. It ends today.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not sit through another riddle in rhyme. Release your captives, and then we will listen.
- Every word from your court is a mask worn over another mask. Not today, Balseraph.
- Speak to us when the laughter in your halls is honest. Until then, no.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Balseraph. We hope your court is merry today, and for good reasons.
- We will gladly hear you, though forgive our brothers if they count the puppets in your retinue.
- Come, sit. Our abbeys keep no jesters, only quiet, which your court may find just as strange a thing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The freaks in your parades were once somebody's children. Say what you have come to say.
- Your mimics wear the skills of the men they killed like borrowed coats. Do not expect a warm welcome here.
- Speak plainly for once, Balseraph, or do not speak at all.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, and we have read the terms twice, for your court is famous for its small print.
- We accept. They say your court always keeps its word, if only in its own peculiar fashion.
- Very well. May this trade bring something to Jubilee besides laughter.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the masquerade, with no trick hidden inside? We are truly moved. Thank you.
- Forgive our brothers for looking inside it twice. We are grateful all the same, Balseraph.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. Kindness looks odd dressed in motley, but it is kindness still.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. A bargain with your court has more trapdoors than a stage, and we cannot see the bottom of this one.
- We must decline. The Elohim will not buy anything your taskmasters have gathered.
- This we cannot accept, Balseraph. Find another partner for this particular game.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your harlequins put down their blades and perform only for children.
- We accept. Let the cages of Jubilee stand a little emptier, and we will call it a good peace.
- So be it. The Elohim have buried enough of our monks, and enough of your puppets.

#### Refuses peace
- While your taskmasters still bring chains to the battlefield, this war is not over.
- You offer peace the way you offer every game, with a rule hidden for later. No.
- Your captives have not been freed. Until they are, our monks keep marching.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want alms for your court's next festival? The poor of Erebus need them more than your masked nobles do.
- No, Balseraph. A demand set to rhyme is still a demand.
- We renounced violence, not good sense. You will receive nothing from us.

### Elohim → Bannor

#### First contact
- Hail, soldiers of Junil. The Elohim also walked through the ashes of the gods' wars; we carried the wounded while others carried swords.
- We are the Elohim, keepers of the holy places. We have heard of the people who walked out of hell into Braduk. Welcome to the light.
- Peace to the Bannor. Your crusade and our pilgrimage face the same darkness; let us pray they never face each other.

#### Declares war
- Your priesthood decides whom to damn, and lately it damns too many. The Elohim will shelter those you condemn, by force if we must.
- A crusade that burns the innocent with the guilty is not Law, Bannor. We will stand in the fields between your armies and the farmers.
- We hoped the people who walked out of hell would remember mercy. Your Confessors have forgotten it, and the Elohim must remind them.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your crusade is already marching; our words would only be trampled underfoot. Not now.
- The Bannor demand obedience and call it negotiation. We will wait until you are ready to listen.
- Not today. Lay down one sword, and then we will speak.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend from the Halls of Sabathiel. What can the Elohim do for the Bannor?
- Come in, soldier. Our gates are always open to those who stand against the Ashen Veil.
- It is good to see you, [CT_NAME]. Our monks pray that your garrisons stay strong and your sword-arms stay merciful.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Confessors have been seen near our abbeys again, asking questions whose answers they already know. What do you want?
- The Elohim do not answer to Junil's priests. Say your piece, Bannor, and lower your voice.
- Even a righteous army can trample a garden. Speak, but know that we are not pleased with you.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair exchange, and honestly offered. The Elohim accept.
- Agreed. May it help your garrisons hold firm against the dark.
- We accept, Bannor. Your word is as well drilled as your soldiers.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, friend. The Bannor are known for giving steel; it is good to see you give bread as well.
- A generous gift. Tonight we will light a lamp in our abbeys for the Bannor fallen.
- Your kindness honors the spirits who were led out of the fire at Braduk. Thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- We cannot accept this, Bannor. It would draw our people into your wars.
- Forgive us, but no. The Elohim will not arm a crusade, not even a just one.
- This is not balanced, friend. Bring us something fairer and we will gladly listen.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. Let the Bannor find better enemies than monks who carry no swords.
- We accept. May your crusade march back toward the true darkness, which has waited too long for it.
- Thank you. Two peoples who both suffered hell should not bleed each other dry.

#### Refuses peace
- Your priests would only name us heretics again tomorrow. There is no peace until they unsay it.
- Not yet. The villages you burned have not been rebuilt, and their dead are not yet mourned.
- You offer peace as an order, Bannor, and we are not your soldiers.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Halls of Sabathiel? The Elohim pay tribute to no one but the poor.
- No. Junil asks for unquestioning obedience; we never promised him ours.
- You will find our storehouses open to the hungry and closed to the demanding.

### Elohim → Calabim

#### First contact
- We know what the Calabim are. We tended the drained and the bitten long before your Broods built their palaces. Do not expect a warm welcome.
- The Elohim greet you, Calabim, because courtesy costs us nothing. Our monks will be watching your herds of men.
- You call your people bloodpets and cattle. We call them people, and we will remember every one of them.

#### Declares war
- Your Grand Broods have fed on their own people long enough. The Elohim come to open the pens.
- No more cattle, and no more Dark Gift. Our monks carry no blades, but their purity will burn your kind well enough.
- We have pleaded and we have prayed, and still your cities are slaughterhouses. Today the Elohim say: no further.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with those who drink their own subjects. Begone.
- Your envoy smiles too much and shows too many teeth. No.
- Free one of your cities from its Brood, and we may listen. Not before.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- We will hear you, Calabim, but our brothers will stand by the door.
- Our peace with you is as thin as skin. Say what you need, and let us keep it unbroken.
- Welcome, if that is the word. We hope your people are well fed, and not in the way your Broods would mean it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You reek of the pens, Calabim. State your business.
- Every pilgrim lost on your roads is written in our book of the dead. Speak, if you dare.
- Do not offer us a drink. Say what you want, and go.

#### Accepts a deal
- We accept, though we will wash our hands afterwards.
- Agreed, on one condition: nothing in this trade is to be paid in blood.
- Very well. Even with the Calabim, a fair bargain is still a fair bargain.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Calabim. We will give it to the poor, who are owed far more than this by your kind.
- Thank you. Perhaps there is still something warm left beating in your court.
- We accept your gift, and pray it was not wrung from your herds.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We do not trade in anything your Broods have touched.
- We must refuse. Whatever this buys you would be paid for by your cattle.
- This trade would only feed your thirst. The Elohim decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. But our monks will go on walking your borders, to take in all who flee.
- We accept. Feed less on your people, Calabim, and this peace may last.
- So be it. A truce with the night is still better than war in the dark.

#### Refuses peace
- While your Broods still feast, there can be no peace. The pens must open first.
- You would only use the quiet to breed your herds back up. No.
- Our dead were drained, not merely killed. You cannot ask their brothers to forgive that so quickly.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for the Calabim? We feed the hungry; we do not feed the thirsty.
- No. Your kind has taken more than enough from the living already.
- You will not have it, [CT_NAME]. Not a coin, and not a drop.

### Elohim → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- We are the Elohim. We remember Braduk before the fire, and the faithful who lived there. Some part of them lives in you still.
- Hail, Clan of Embers. Your fathers loved Bhall when she was good and just. We pray you find that fire again.
- Greetings, orc. Our pilgrims will cross your hills; let them pass, and our healers will tend your wounded as well as our own.

#### Declares war
- Your raiders burn the villages we shelter and throw the living into the flames. The Elohim will stand in front of the next pyre.
- The Ember Banner has burned enough of the world. We go to put it out.
- We offered healing and you answered with axes. Now the Elohim must answer you, though it grieves us to do it.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your warriors are still at our gates with torches. Words can wait.
- Not while our pilgrims hang from your stakes. No.
- Talking is useless while Braduk's fire burns in your eyes. Go.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Clan. Your people were devout once, before the fall; the Elohim have not forgotten.
- Come and sit by our fire, orc. It burns warm, not angry.
- Greetings. Even the fiercest clan may share a peaceful hearth. What brings you to us?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders have been at our shrines again. Speak, but do not shout.
- Bhall fell, and your people have been falling with her ever since. What do you want?
- The Elohim have no gold for you to plunder and no patience for threats. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. It is good to see the Clan trade instead of raid.
- We accept. Honest trade is a first step out of the fire.
- A fair bargain, orc. Let it be the first of many.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Clan, and no axe behind it? Thank you; this gives us hope.
- Thank you. Perhaps there is still something of the old, holy Braduk in your people.
- We are grateful. Kindness under the Ember Banner is rare, and so we will treasure it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not give anything that would feed your raids.
- Forgive us, but this is not fair, and the Clan knows it.
- We cannot accept. Bring us an honest offer and we will listen.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your fires, and may they warm rather than burn.
- We accept. The Elohim never wanted to fight the children of Braduk.
- Let the Ember Banner rest, then. Our healers will mend what your warriors broke.

#### Refuses peace
- You would only raid again once the snow melts. No.
- Our villages are still smoking. Until they are safe from your raiders, there is no peace.
- Your warlords would treat a truce as time to sharpen their axes. We go on.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want tribute? Take a lesson instead: the strong protect, they do not take.
- No. The Elohim pay no ransom to the Ember Banner.
- Your axe asks loudly, and our answer is quiet: no.

### Elohim → Doviello

#### First contact
- Your pack outlasted the ice by leaving its weak behind. The Elohim outlasted it by carrying them. We shall see which way builds more.
- We are the Elohim. We tend the sick and carry the old; we know your pack calls that weakness. We call it the reason anyone survived.
- Peace to you, Doviello. Our roads are open to you, but our sick and our old are not your prey.

#### Declares war
- The pack hunts whatever cannot run. The Elohim will stand wherever the weak have fallen.
- Your pack's creed leaves the wounded to the wolves. Then see what the wounded can do when someone finally stands for them.
- You have prowled our borders and dragged off our pilgrims for the last time.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your raiders still howl outside our abbeys. We will not talk.
- You believe diplomacy is a trick of the weak. Then we will not waste it on you.
- Not now, Doviello. Call back your wolves first.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Doviello. Rest a while; even wolves grow tired.
- Our abbeys feed travelers, even those who come from the wastes. What do you need?
- Greetings. We pray the hunt has been kind to your people, and that the hunted were only beasts.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You sniff at our walls like a hungry pack. Speak.
- Your people cast out their own children for being weak. Forgive us if we are cold.
- What does the pack want now? Make it brief.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Better a trade than teeth.
- We accept. Even the pack can bargain fairly, it seems.
- A fair deal, Doviello. May it fill your stores without emptying ours.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A wolf sharing its kill is a rare sight, and we shall remember it.
- We are grateful, Doviello. Perhaps the pack has room for generosity after all.
- A kind gift from the wastes. Thank you, friend; our sick will eat well tonight.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. This would only sharpen the pack's teeth.
- We must refuse. The Elohim are gentle, not foolish.
- That is not fair, and the strong should never need to cheat.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and hunt elk, not men.
- We accept. Let the pack lick its wounds, and we will tend ours.
- So be it. The old and the sick in our care thank you for it.

#### Refuses peace
- The pack only returns when it smells weakness. Not yet.
- Our pilgrims have not come home from your wastes. No peace until they do.
- You hunt in peace as you hunt in war. We will not lower our guard.

#### Rejects a demand
- The weak owe you nothing, and neither do we.
- No, Doviello. Snarl as much as you like.
- You ask as wolves ask, with teeth bared. The answer is no.

### Elohim → Grigori

#### First contact
- Hail, Grigori. Your nation was born of the angel who counseled the Compact, and our order witnessed its signing. We have much to remember together.
- Greetings, Grigori. You turned away from the gods, and we never fought for them. Perhaps we are not so far apart.
- We are the Elohim. You shelter those who flee the heavens, and we shelter those the heavens trample. Welcome.

#### Declares war
- You would see the holy places torn down as relics of tyrants. We cannot allow it, Grigori.
- Your adventurers loot the sites that were placed in our keeping. The Elohim must stop them.
- You teach that men must lead themselves. Then lead yourselves away from our shrines, or we will drive you from them.

#### Refuses to talk
- You mock what we keep. Come back when you have learned respect.
- Not today. Your adventurers are still camped in our sacred groves.
- We will talk when your swords have left our shrines, Grigori.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Grigori. Both our peoples began by sheltering men from the wars of the gods. Sit with us.
- We may never agree about the heavens, but we agree about the hungry. What can we do together?
- Come in, friend. Our monks enjoy arguing with your scholars more than they will ever admit.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You call our devotion servitude. Then why do you come to us?
- Your adventurers have been asking about Finner's tomb again. What do you want?
- Speak, Grigori. We are listening, though not gladly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A sensible bargain between sensible peoples.
- We accept. The Grigori trade the way they reason, plainly.
- A fair exchange, and no god can claim the credit for it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, Grigori. You say you answer no prayers, and yet you have answered ours.
- A gift freely given. We will tell our novices that the faithless can be generous too.
- We are grateful. The devout and the doubting can share bread after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Some things are held in trust and are not ours to sell, not even to you.
- We cannot accept. Your adventurers would use this to dig where they should not.
- Forgive us. The bargain is reasonable, but our charge forbids it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. The gods would delight in seeing us at each other's throats; let us deny them that pleasure.
- We accept. Both our peoples were born from refusing the wars of heaven. Let us remember it.
- Gladly. Go back to your free cities, and we will go back to our shrines.

#### Refuses peace
- Your adventurers still hold our sacred sites. Return them first.
- You want peace, yet your swords are still in our holy groves. No.
- Not yet, Grigori. Reason must also mean restitution.

#### Rejects a demand
- You preach self-sufficiency, Grigori. Then suffice yourselves.
- No. You taught your people never to beg from the gods; do not beg from monks either.
- The Elohim pay tribute to no one, not to the gods and not to those who scorn them.

### Elohim → Hippus

#### First contact
- Greetings, riders of the plains. The Elohim walk wherever we go; we pray you will not ride over us on the way.
- Hail, Hippus. Your fathers rode for Kylorin against the wicked mages of Patria, and ours walked behind them, burying the dead of both sides.
- We are the Elohim. We hear your companies sell their courage to any city that can pay. Ours is not for sale, but our hospitality is free.

#### Declares war
- Your companies have taken someone's gold to ride down our pilgrims. Then the Elohim must stop the herd, whoever paid for it.
- You raided your own kin through the whole Age of Ice, and now you raid ours. No more, Hippus.
- Our monks will meet your lances with bare hands. Ask the riders who come back why they are feared.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your horses are still in our grain. No talk until they are gone.
- You would sell this very conversation to the highest bidder. No.
- Not now, Hippus. Recall your companies, and then we will see.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Hippus. Water your horses and rest; our abbeys have room in their stables.
- Your clans once said the Elohim would pay anything for courage. We have our own; what we lack is good horses.
- Greetings, friend. We value an honest sword, even a hired one, as long as it stays honest.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders galloped through our pilgrim roads last season. What now?
- We know your price, Hippus. What is it today, and whose blood does it buy?
- Speak, rider, but dismount first. We are not pleased with you.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair price, as fair as a Hippus ever asks.
- We accept. May it buy honest work for your companies, and none against the innocent.
- A good bargain, rider. Done, and witnessed.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Hippus, and no fee attached? We will tell our chroniclers, and they will not believe us.
- We are grateful. Generosity sits well on a horse lord.
- Thank you, friend. We will pray that each of your companies comes home whole.

#### Turns down a deal
