- Snow fell in summer near your border. Explain it, or say nothing at all.
- They say you mean to become a god. Gods need not bring petitions to our court.

#### Accepts a deal
- Let honest trade keep both our peoples warm. Agreed.
- Done. Even the White Hand could find no fault in these terms.
- A fair bargain, Illian. May it thaw a little of the ice between us.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the north. We thank you, and wish you a mild season.
- Thank you. We did not expect warmth out of Letum Frigus.
- Perhaps the Illians have learned what the thaw can bring. Generous of you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not provision a people preparing the next Age of Ice.
- Your terms are as cold as your mountain.
- Not on these terms. Our granaries remember the long winter, even if you have forgotten it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your mountain, and let the world stay green.
- We accept, but our watchmen will keep their eyes on the northern sky.
- Let both our peoples live to see a spring. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- You would freeze our cities the moment we sheathed our swords. No.
- Not until your priests stop calling down the frost.
- When the Illians wake, the world sleeps, they say. We are wide awake.

#### Rejects a demand
- Hasten the winter's return with our gold? Never.
- No. The confederation does not pay homage to the cold.
- Ask again in high summer, [CT_NAME]. The answer will be just as frozen.

### Kuriotates → Infernal

#### First contact
- So hell has a city in Erebus now. The confederation opens its borders to every people; we find the rule has limits after all.
- Speak, demon. We judge all who come to us by their deeds, and yours arrived before you did.
- Our centaurs refused to stand in the same hall as your envoy. We have stationed them outside, within earshot.

#### Declares war
- You came to drag mortals down to the pit. Not ours. Never ours.
- Our gates are open to many peoples, never to the legions of Agares. We march to close the door you crawled through.
- Every soul you have stolen from our borderlands will be avenged. War, demon.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not bargain with hell.
- No. Your words are a fire we will not invite into our halls.
- The court has nothing to say to the servants of the pit, [CT_NAME].

#### Greeting (friendly)
- We speak because we must. Keep your fires on your own side of the border, and we will manage.
- Greetings. Our scribes are recording every word you say. You understand why.
- You are polite, for a demon. We will be polite in return, for as long as that lasts.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The ash blowing from your lands is choking our fields. What do you want?
- Our people flee at the sight of your envoy. Make this quick.
- You reek of sulfur and of lies. Speak, and go.

#### Accepts a deal
- We will count every coin twice, in daylight. But we agree.
- Done. Let it keep your armies hungry for something other than us.
- A bargain, then. Do not imagine it makes us friends.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the pit? We will have it blessed before it enters our treasury.
- Our priests insist on cleansing it first, nothing personal. Still, thank you.
- Generous. We find ourselves wondering what it will really cost us.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Every bargain with your kind has a soul hidden somewhere in the price.
- We will not trade our people's safety for hell's trinkets.
- Not these terms, nor any terms that smell of brimstone.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. Keep your demons behind your Obsidian Gates.
- Our people have endured enough of your company. We accept.
- Agreed. But our borders remain closed to your kind.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace with hell? When hell stands empty.
- Not while a single demon walks our lands.
- No. You would only use the time to tear open another gate.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to hell? The confederation would sooner burn.
- No. Go back to the pit and make your demands there.
- Our coin buys bread for the living, not favors from the damned.

### Kuriotates → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad, come up from under the hills. Welcome to the sunlight; it has improved since your last visit.
- Well met, dwarves. We hear you remember every swindle ever done to your people. We intend to give you no new ones.
- A people of vaults and hammers. Our cities will always have use for good stone and honest gold.

#### Declares war
- Your miners have tunneled beneath our border. We will fill the shafts with your army.
- You count gold while our people go hungry for your tariffs. Count your dead instead.
- The Khazad hoard what the world needs. We have come to open the vaults.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Not even your finest appraiser can put a price on this war.
- Go back beneath the mountain, dwarf. We are not talking.
- The court does not haggle in wartime, and certainly not with the Khazad.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend! Our masons speak of your stonework with something close to reverence.
- Your merchants and ours have been doing good business, [CT_NAME].
- The Khazad envoy is welcome. Our scales are honest here; check them yourself, as we know you will.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your merchants have been weighing our goods with a thumb on the scale.
- You trust no one, Khazad, and it shows. What now?
- Speak, but do not expect us to stand in awe of your coffers.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Sound coin and sound stone make a fine bargain.
- Even a dwarven appraiser would call that fair, and they call nothing fair. Done.
- A deal. We will put it in writing, carved in stone if you prefer.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Khazad! Our treasurers will not believe it until they have weighed it.
- Thank you. The dwarves are generous when they choose to be, and we are honored you chose us.
- Your gold is every bit as heavy as they say. We thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You bargain like a dwarf, and we are not dwarves.
- These terms would empty our coffers into yours. No.
- You of all peoples know the worth of what you are asking.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let our merchants meet in the markets again.
- Your siege engines have made their point. We accept.
- Agreed. Go home to your halls and your hammers.

#### Refuses peace
- Your engines still batter our walls. There will be no peace.
- Not yet. The Khazad must learn that the confederation cannot be bought.
- No. You would only use the quiet to dig in deeper.

#### Rejects a demand
- The richest people in Erebus, asking us for tribute? You jest.
- No. You have gold enough beneath your mountains.
- Ask your vaults, dwarf, not ours.

### Kuriotates → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun, lords of the waves. Our harbors are open, but our customs officers are very thorough.
- We hear every one of your captains rules a ship as a kingdom. To which of them are we speaking?
- Welcome. Our coasts are long and our patience longer, but please do not test either.

#### Declares war
- Your captains have plundered our coasts once too often. We will burn your harbors to the waterline.
- A pirate's word is wind, and we are done waiting for it to blow our way.
- You raid where you please and sail off laughing. Not this time; our army marches on your ports.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We know how a Lanun bargain ends.
- Sail away, captain. There is nothing here for you but war.
- The court will not hear sea-wolves while our coast still burns.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, captain! Our merchants have been watching the horizon for your sails.
- You bring the smell of the sea, [CT_NAME], and, we hope, a full hold.
- The Lanun are always welcome in our ports, so long as they pay the harbor fees.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our merchant ships keep vanishing near your islands. Curious, is it not?
- Your sailors are drunk and brawling in our ports again. Take them home.
- Speak, captain, and keep your hands where we can see them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Let the cargo reach port only once this time, and we will be friends.
- A fair trade, and not a single ship boarded; how novel. Done.
- A bargain. Our harbors will be glad of your sails.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Lanun, and nobody had to be boarded for it. Thank you.
- Thank you, captain. We will drink your health in rum, as your custom demands.
- Our harbor masters will never believe it. Generous, captain.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms are as slippery as a deck in a squall.
- We decline. Pirates make poor creditors.
- Not on those terms. Even your own crews would mutiny if they were offered that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your ships carry cargo into our ports, not boarding parties.
- The sea is wide enough for both our peoples. We accept.
- Agreed. Only try to keep your word longer than a Lanun usually does.

#### Refuses peace
- Your fleets would use a truce to reload their cannon. No.
- Not until our coastal cities are free of your crews.
- Peace with pirates? When the tide forgets to turn.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for pirates? We would sooner sink it in the harbor.
- No. You will have to steal it, and you will find that harder than you think.
- Our coin is for honest ships, captain.

### Kuriotates → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The elves of the Summer Court! Our confederation has long hoped to meet the Ljosalfar.
- Greetings. Your groves were few when the ice withdrew; we are glad to see them spreading again.
- Welcome. Centaurs and lamia are citizens among us. Perhaps one day elves will join them.

#### Declares war
- Your forests creep over our settlements and your archers shoot our woodcutters. Enough.
- Our people need timber and land, and you would rather they froze. We will take both by force.
- Elves live long and forget nothing. Remember this, then: you forced our hand.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now, elf. The forest can wait; our war cannot.
- Your rangers killed our people from the treetops. We will not talk.
- The court is closed to the Ljosalfar until this is settled.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your people's patience is a model for our own young nation, friend.
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. The Fellowship of Leaves is well respected in our cities.
- An elven envoy! Our court is honored. Tell us of the hidden groves that outlasted the winter.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your rangers stalk our woodcutters like deer. Call them off.
- You speak to us as to children. Our nation is young, not foolish.
- Elves have centuries to spare; we do not. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Let our peoples grow together, like roots beneath the same soil. Agreed.
- Done. A fair bargain, and an elegant one.
- A deal. The Summer Court bargains as gracefully as it dances.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the elves. We are honored, [CT_NAME].
- Thank you. The Ljosalfar give rarely, so we treasure it all the more.
- Generous and graceful. Our court thanks you, and so do our centaurs.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your patience is long, and so, this time, is our refusal.
- We decline. The terms are elegant, but they are not fair.
- You live long enough to make us a better offer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your forests grow and our cities stand, side by side.
- Your sacred groves will not be touched. You have our word, and our peace.
- Agreed. Return to your woods; we will return to our building.

#### Refuses peace
- Your archers still hold the hills above our settlements. Peace can wait until they come down.
- No. You would melt back into your forests and strike again next spring.
- The Ljosalfar remember every slight. We will make sure they remember this lesson too.

#### Rejects a demand
- You have no need of our gold, elf, and we have no wish to give it.
- No. Our people are not your servants, however old your court may be.
- The oak does not bend, your people say. Neither does the confederation.

### Kuriotates → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp, heirs of the Open-Skiers! Your golems are the stuff of legend in our cities.
- You waited out the ice beneath the mountains and came back to the sun, as you swore you would. We salute such patience.
- Welcome, friends of Kilmorph. Our engineers would give a great deal for an hour with your artificers.

#### Declares war
- Your golems trample our fields without a care. Then neither will we care for your workshops.
- The ice broke your golems once. Our centaurs mean to do it again.
- You build tireless armies of clay and iron. We will see how they fare against a people who never tire of freedom.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Golems do not negotiate, and neither will we, today.
- The court will not speak with the Luchuirp while their machines march on our cities.
- Your golems do not talk, and today neither do we.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend. Our engineers are hoping you brought a golem to show them.
- How do your people find life under the open sky again, [CT_NAME]?
- The Luchuirp are always welcome among us. Graoin the Delver's heirs could ask for nothing less.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems wrecked our roads again. Who pays for that?
- Your artificers' arrogance is as finely made as their machines.
- Speak, Luchuirp, but do not expect us to marvel at every gear today.

#### Accepts a deal
- Your craftsmanship is worth every coin. Agreed.
- Done. Kilmorph smiles on fair dealing, we are told, and so do we.
- A bargain. Our engineers will be delighted.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Luchuirp! Our engineers will take it apart at once, with your permission.
- Your generosity is as fine as your craft, friend.
- We will put it on display in the capital, where every guild can admire it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even one of your golems could tell this is unbalanced.
- We decline. Your terms are as rigid as your machines.
- Not good enough. The old Open-Skiers would have offered more.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your golems go back to tilling fields.
- Neither of us can afford more broken machines. We accept.
- Agreed. Go home and build; that is what both our peoples do best.

#### Refuses peace
- Your golems are still standing in our wheat. When they walk home, we will talk.
- No. Your clockwork armies do not tire, and neither will we.
- The war continues until your machines go home.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Build it yourself; you are good at that.
- No. Your workshops are rich enough without our coin.
- We pay nothing to the Luchuirp but our respect, and today you have less of that.

### Kuriotates → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim, people of the sun. We hear you once took in a dying stranger from the wastes. So do we, every day.
- Greetings. Your Empyrean gives small nations the same voice as great ones, we are told. Our confederation likes the sound of that.
- Welcome, travelers from the desert. Our centaurs wonder how anyone crosses that much sand without four legs.

#### Declares war
- Even the light of Lugus casts shadows, and yours has fallen across our lands. We march.
- Your zealots burn our shrines and call it illumination. We call it war.
- The sun does not rule here, Malakim. Our army will show you where its warmth ends.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your preachers can carry their light elsewhere. The court will not listen.
- No. You have nothing to say that the desert wind could not say better.
- Not while your soldiers stand in our settlements, [CT_NAME].

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your Empyrean's courts are fair, friend, and fairness is the rarest coin in Erebus.
- Greetings. Our merchants are eager for your caravans and the spices they carry.
- The children of the sun are welcome in our halls. Let us open the shutters for you.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars keep telling our people what Lugus thinks of them. We did not ask.
- You preach that small empires deserve an equal voice. Then listen to ours, for once.
- You blaze into our court like noon, Malakim. Dim yourself a little, and speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair judgment, as the Empyrean would want.
- May your caravans and our settlements prosper together. Done.
- A good bargain. The sun shines on both of us today.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A generous gift. We thank you, [CT_NAME], and so do our merchants.
- Thank you. The light of Lugus is kinder than we were told.
- Your people give as freely as the sun. We are grateful.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Weigh it again, on the scales your own judges use.
- We decline. Sunlight is free, Malakim; these terms are not.
- The desert has made you a hard bargainer, Malakim.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your caravans cross our lands again in safety.
- We accept. Lugus would hardly want this war to go on, and neither do we.
- Let your oases bloom and our cities grow; there is room under the sun for both.

#### Refuses peace
- Your zealots would not stop for a treaty. Neither will we.
- Not yet. Our settlements are still in your hands.
- No. Even the sun sets, Malakim; we will wait for yours.

#### Rejects a demand
- Your own Empyrean says small nations are not to be bullied. Remember that.
- No. Find your gold in the desert sand.
- Our treasury owes nothing to the light of Lugus.

### Kuriotates → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels, walking among men. We have heard you care little for mortals. Our people are mortals; we hope that will not matter.
- Warriors of the heavens! You defied the Compact to keep fighting. That takes a stubbornness we can respect.
- Welcome. Our people took you for demons at first sight. We apologize; you do look the part.

#### Declares war
- You march wherever demons are, and you trample whatever stands between. Today that was us.
- Heaven sent you to fight hell, not our settlers. We will remind you of the difference.
- Even angels may be driven out of a land that does not want them.

#### Refuses to talk
- You care nothing for mortals, so why should mortals care for your words?
- No. Go and hunt your demons; we have nothing to say.
- The court does not hear those who see our people only as obstacles.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, angel. Our scholars have a thousand questions; I promise to ask only a few.
- Your war against hell makes our nights safer, [CT_NAME]. We thank you.
- The Mercurians honor us. Rest your wings in our halls a while.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your soldiers marched through our fields as if they were not there. They were.
- You fight the hells, and that is admirable. Then go and fight them.
- Speak, angel, but do not look past us while you do it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Let it help your crusade and our people alike. Agreed.
- Done. A bargain fit for heaven and for earth.
- A fair deal. We are glad to arm a war we cannot fight ourselves.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the angels. Our priests will speak of it for years.
- We did not think you noticed us at all. Thank you.
- Generous, Mercurian. Perhaps mortals matter to you after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your war is holy, but our coin is still our own.
- We decline. Even angels must offer a fair price.
- Not on these terms. Our people cannot carry heaven's war on their backs.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and fight the demons; that is your war, not this.
- Neither of us should spend our strength on the other while hell stands.
- Agreed. Let your hammers fall on the damned, not on our gates.

#### Refuses peace
- You trampled our settlements without a thought. We will make you think about it.
- Not yet. Angels should learn that mortals bleed back.
- No. Your war against hell can wait; ours cannot.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to angels? Heaven has no need of our coin.
- No. Fight your crusade with your own wealth.
- We give to those who ask with humility, [CT_NAME]. That was not humble.

### Kuriotates → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. You gather people from every nation, as we do. We gather them to build. You gather them to end the world.
- We are building an edifice to last the ages, Sheaim. We understand you hope to have no ages left.
- Our lamia felt your gates open long before your envoy arrived. They are not pleased.

#### Declares war
- You would end the world. We happen to live in it. War.
- The confederation was built to outlast every danger of this age. You are the first we mean to remove.
- Every gate you open is a wound in Erebus. We march to close them, and you with them.

#### Refuses to talk
- What could a cult of the apocalypse possibly offer us? Nothing. Go.
- No. We do not negotiate with the end of the world.
- The court will not listen to those who long for its ruin.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- We speak, Sheaim, but our lamia watch every gesture you make.
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. While the world still stands, let us at least be courteous.
- You are welcome, for today. Tomorrow, we shall see if there is a tomorrow.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our harvests wither near your borders. We know whose rituals do that.
- You long for the end. Must you rehearse it on our lands?
- Speak quickly; you would hate to waste the little time you think is left.

#### Accepts a deal
- We will build with it, even if you will not. Agreed.
- Done. A curious bargain to make with those who want nothing left to trade.
- A fair exchange. Spend it on something that lasts, for once.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim? Our lamia will check it for curses, but thank you.
- Thank you. Perhaps you are not wholly eager for the end.
- We will build something with it, which may annoy you. Generous, all the same.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not feed the rituals that would unmake us.
- We decline. Why trade for the future with those who want no future?
- No terms that hasten your apocalypse will ever please us.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your gates, and may they stay shut.
- We accept, but our magi will watch the sky for your work.
- Let the world turn a little longer, for both our sakes. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- You would use the peace to finish your rituals. No.
- Not while your gates still stand open on our borders.
- The world cannot afford your peace. The war continues.

#### Rejects a demand
- Pay to hasten the end? We will not buy our own ruin.
- No. Our coin builds things; yours would only unmake them.
- Ask the void for it, [CT_NAME]. You seem to know it well.

### Kuriotates → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar, the Grey. Our confederation has taken in many of the rarer peoples of Erebus, but never shades. You would be welcome.
- Greetings. We had heard your people were fading from the world. We are glad to have met you before you did.
- Our centaurs could not tell where the fog ended and your envoy began. Welcome, all the same.

#### Declares war
- Your hidden cities sit on land our people need. We regret it, but you will have to fade somewhere else.
- You trade pieces of your souls for endless years. Let us see what you will trade to keep your cities.
- You keep out of the wars of the younger races, you say. You should have kept out of ours.

#### Refuses to talk
- You never cared for our affairs before. We will not care for your words now.
- No. Go back into your fog, and take your envoy with you, if you can tell where it ends.
- A people with half a soul gets half a hearing, and today not even that.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Sidar. Our scholars marvel at your learning; you have had a long time to gather it.
- It is good to see you still with us, [CT_NAME], more or less.
- The Grey honor us. Sit by the fire; we know you cannot feel it, but it is our custom.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades have been drifting through our settlements at night. Our people cannot sleep.
- You care for nothing, your own scholars boast. Then why meddle in our lands?
- Speak, Sidar, before you blur away entirely.

#### Accepts a deal
- A bargain with the patient is a good bargain. Agreed.
- Done. Our archives will gain much from your long memory.
- A fair trade, and a calm one. We would expect nothing less from the Grey.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Grey. We are touched, and a little startled.
- We did not think the Sidar noticed the younger races enough to give them anything. Thank you.
- Generous. A token of feeling, or only of old habit? Either way, we thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You have centuries to wait for a better offer, so make one.
- We decline. Detachment is no excuse for poor terms.
- Not this. Our people live short lives and cannot spend them on bad bargains.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your hidden cities; we will not follow you into the mist.
- The world is hard enough without fighting shadows. We accept.
- Agreed. Let us leave each other to our very different lives.

#### Refuses peace
- Our people still wake to find your shades at their bedsides. No.
- No. You would only vanish into the fog and return when it suits you.
- The war continues, Sidar, until you are either a friend or a memory.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to shades? What would you even do with it?
- No. Our coin is for the living, every one of them.
- You gave up appetite along with your souls, they say. Then you will not miss our gold.

### Kuriotates → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The dark elves of the Winter Court. We know of your war with your Summer kin, and we would rather stay out of it.
- You turned to Esus when your god fell silent. We judge a people by its deeds, not by its gods.
- Welcome. Our lamia say your envoy carries more knives than courtesies.

#### Declares war
- Your assassins have killed our officials in their beds. We answer in daylight, with an army.
- Your court ruled through one long winter and thinks it may rule ours. We march to remind you that winter ends.
- The shadows of Esus have crept into our cities. We are coming to drive them back to their source.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Every word you speak has a knife beneath it.
- The court will not listen to the Unseelie while their blades are still wet.
- Go back to the dark, elf. We have no words for you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Svartalfar. Our court is curious about the Unseelie ways; tell us something true, if you can.
- You are courteous, [CT_NAME], which is more than your reputation promised.
- The Winter Court honors us. Please keep your daggers sheathed through dinner.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your spies were caught in our capital. Did you think a confederation of many peoples has no eyes?
- You smile, elf, but your eyes are counting our guards.
- Speak, Svartalfar, and spare us the riddles of Esus.

#### Accepts a deal
- Even the Winter Court can strike an honest bargain, it seems. Agreed.
- Done. Let it ease a few of the shadows between us.
- A fair exchange. We will still look for the catch, but we accept.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Unseelie? We are surprised, and grateful, and having it tasted for poison.
- We will remember that the dark elves were generous with us.
- Your trickster god must be in a giving mood.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There is a trap in this somewhere, and we will not step into it.
- We decline. Your terms are cut as finely as an assassin's blade, and aimed as carefully.
- Not this. The Council of Esus may pay for miracles; we do not pay for tricks.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your shadows, and we will return to our lamplit streets.
- Let the Winter Court turn its gaze back to its old Summer quarrel, and away from us.
- Agreed. A long war profits neither of us, and we are not elves, to wait forever.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while your assassins still hide in our cities.
- No. You would only strike again from the dark.
- The war continues until your court learns that the confederation cannot be cowed.

#### Rejects a demand
- The Unseelie will have no tribute from us in any season.
- No. Our coin will not buy your daggers.
- You may wear the crown of winter, elf, but you will not take ours.

## Lanun

### Lanun → Amurites

#### First contact
- Children of Kylorin! Our grandsires ferried his runaway mages across the sea, then sold ships to the fire priests chasing them. Good business, both ways.
- Ahoy, Amurites. They say your mages can walk on water. The trick is not looking down, but ye'll find a deck more comfortable.
- A nation of wizards, eh? Every wizard needs rare things from far shores, and every far shore is ours.

#### Declares war
- Your spells can boil a bay, they say. Let's see ye boil the whole ocean before my fleets reach your harbors.
- Fire and lightning are fine tricks on land. At sea, a wizard is just a passenger who can't swim.
- I've been lifting your schools' cargo for years and ye never noticed. Now ye will.

#### Refuses to talk
- Parley with a mage? I'd sooner parley with a squall; at least it's honest about drowning me.
- No talk. Your envoy can try walking home across the water.
- I've heard what your archmages do with a promise once the ink's dry. Not today.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Need exotic reagents, [CT_NAME]? My captains found a chest of them... somewhere.
- Welcome aboard, mage. Mind the rigging; it bites the clumsy.
- Ah, the scholars come calling. A rum for the archmage, and a smaller one for the clerk.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your apprentices set one of my ships alight to test a spell. Who's paying for my mast?
- Wizards. Always looking at a captain as if I were a toad they hadn't made yet.
- Speak up, Amurite, and keep your hands out of your sleeves while ye do.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done, and done well. Never let it be said a Lanun can't bargain with a wizard.
- Your crates will arrive before the ink dries, and hardly opened at all.
- A fair trade. Your schools will want for nothing that floats.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the wizards! I'll name a cannon after you.
- The lads will drink to the Amurite schools tonight. Thank ye kindly.
- Generous! The next adept of yours who needs passage rides free, and gets the good hammock.

#### Turns down a deal
- That deal's lighter than a wizard's purse after a night in port. No.
- Ye'd have to enchant me to make me take that, and I'm wearing my wards.
- No, Amurite. Even your own bureaucrats would blush at those terms.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go back to your books, and I'll go back to the sea.
- My crews are sick of lightning on the masts. Aye, done.
- Your mages study, my captains sail, and there's coin in both. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? Your harbor's still burning, and I'd hate to waste a good fire.
- Not yet, wizard. My crews have a taste for your treasure now.
- Ye'll have to beg louder than that before I haul down my colors.

#### Rejects a demand
- Conjure it yourself, wizard. My hold's not open to you.
- Ha! Ye want my gold, ye come and take it. Bring your best spells.
- No, [CT_NAME]. A captain doesn't pay; a captain collects.

### Lanun → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- The mad court! Your vintages are famous in every port from here to the ice; I've a hold standing empty for them.
- You've freaks and puppets, Balseraphs, and I've pirates. We'll understand each other fine.
- A circus that grew into a kingdom. I've seen stranger things at sea, but not many.

#### Declares war
- Your Taskmasters took Lanun sailors for slaves. Now my fleets come for every barrel in your cellars.
- I've laughed at your jests long enough. Here's mine: a thousand sails on your horizon.
- Ye love a spectacle, jester? Then watch your harbor burn from the palace windows.

#### Refuses to talk
- No parley with a court that rhymes its lies.
- I don't bargain with puppets. Send the hand that works the strings.
- Go juggle somewhere else, Balseraph. The sea isn't laughing.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Did ye bring any of that vintage? No? Well, come aboard anyway; I'll forgive you by the second cup.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your harlequins entertained my crew for a week, and most of the crew came back.
- Ah, the masked court! Take off the mask, have some rum, and let's do business.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- One of your mimics stole my bosun's swagger. I want it back.
- Ye slipped a puppet aboard my flagship. It's at the bottom of the harbor now, still smiling.
- Speak your riddle, Balseraph, and tell me when I'm meant to laugh.

#### Accepts a deal
- A mad bargain, but I've struck madder. Done!
- Agreed, and I'll count the casks myself, jester.
- A fine trade. Always a pleasure doing business with lunatics.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift! Is it a trick? It's always a trick with you lot. Thank ye anyway.
- I'll drink this vintage slowly, Balseraph, and think kindly of your madness.
- I'd kiss your mask for this, if I trusted what was behind it.

#### Turns down a deal
- That deal's madder than your court. No.
- Nice try, jester. I know a thimblerig when I see one.
- No. Those terms have more strings than your puppets.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace! Send the wine, and we'll call it square.
- Your harlequins dance, my crews drink, and everybody's happy. Peace.
- Let's both pretend this never happened. You've a talent for pretending.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace now, with half your vintage still in the cellars? Not yet.
- Peace with a madhouse? You'd forget it by supper.
- No. My crews are enjoying plundering a circus far too much.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the jester? Make me laugh first.
- Ha! The answer's no, and that's no joke.
- Your Taskmasters can't whip coin out of a Lanun, [CT_NAME].

### Lanun → Bannor

#### First contact
- The Bannor. All law and order, I hear. Well, the sea keeps its own law, and out here I'm the one who keeps it.
- Ahoy, crusaders. You keep fugitives in chains; we sign them on as crew. Let's not quarrel over it.
- Soldiers of Junil! I've sold swords to worse folk. Might sell a few to you.

#### Declares war
- Your priests declared me damned. Fine, then: the damned are coming for your coast.
- Law is a fine thing in a city. At sea it drowns, and so will your fleet.
- Your Crusade marches beautifully. Let's see how well it swims.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talk. Your priests would only add it to my list of sins.
- Go preach to the fish, crusader.
- I'll talk when your Confessors stop hanging my sailors in your ports.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Leave your sermons on the dock, [CT_NAME], and come aboard.
- Welcome. I've a few runaway Bannor conscripts in my crew; they send their regards, from below decks.
- Order and discipline, the Bannor way! I keep a little of each in the hold, for emergencies.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your priests hanged one of my captains in port. Talk fast.
- Ye want order? Then keep your patrol boats out of my waters.
- Speak, crusader, but say the word repent and ye go over the side.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. A lawful bargain, even. Don't tell my crew.
- Sealed properly, the way your priests like it. You've a deal.
- Not even Junil could find a sin in that one. Struck.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank ye, crusader! My crew will drink to Sabathiel tonight, or near enough.
- Did your priests approve this gift? Never mind; I'll take it, with thanks.
- My cannon will point the other way for a good long while after this.

#### Turns down a deal
- That deal's lawful, I'll grant ye, but it isn't profitable.
- No. Your terms march in close order, and my purse prefers to run loose.
- Too rigid. Slacken your terms like a sail and maybe we'll catch some wind.

#### Agrees to peace
- Your navy's a disgrace anyway; there's no sport in sinking it. Peace.
- Agreed. March your Crusade off somewhere dry, where my ships can't trouble it.
- Let the Halls of Sabathiel sleep easy tonight. Aye, peace.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? You'd only hang my sailors for piracy the moment it was signed.
- The Halls of Sabathiel can wait for their peace. My crews are still busy on your shore.
- No. Your Crusade wanted a war, and now it has one with the whole sea.

#### Rejects a demand
- The Order wants a tithe? The sea pays no tithes.
- No. Junil can pray for my gold, if he wants it so badly.
- Demand away, [CT_NAME]. The Lanun don't kneel to anyone's god.

### Lanun → Calabim

#### First contact
- Vampires! Ye'll find nothing worth drinking aboard my ships but rum and seawater.
- The Calabim. Your nobles go about by night; so do my smugglers. We'll get on.
- Fair warning, noble: Lanun blood is mostly salt and grog. You'd not enjoy it.

#### Declares war
- Your Broods rule from fine castles. Castles on a coast fall to cannon.
- You bled my sailors dry in your ports. Now my crews come to bleed your treasury.
- Sharpen your fangs, noble. My cutlasses are already sharp.

#### Refuses to talk
- No talk with leeches.
- I've heard what happens to envoys who dine in your halls. Mine won't.
- Go back to your silk sheets and your bloodpets, vampire.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome. Your Grand Broods buy silk and silver from my captains; we're old friends by now.
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Night trading suits us both, doesn't it?
- Come aboard, Calabim, though the crew sleeps in shifts, with cutlasses. No offense meant.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Broods snatched sailors off my docks. Explain it, before I explain things with cannon.
- You look at my crew the way a butcher looks at a herd. Stop it.
- Speak, vampire, and keep your teeth behind your lips.

#### Accepts a deal
- A cold-blooded bargain, but a good one. Struck.
- Agreed. Pleasure doing business with the nobility.
- I'll deliver by night, as your kind prefers. We've a bargain.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Broods! Thank ye, and I'll not ask whose it was before.
- I'll toast your health for this, though not in your house wine.
- My crew will sleep sounder knowing you're pleased with us. Thank ye.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You're draining my purse like it was one of your bloodpets.
- Too thin, Calabim. Bring something with a little more blood in it.
- That deal's as dead as you are.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep to your castles by night, and my ships will keep to the open water by day.
- Let's stop bleeding each other; that's your trade, not mine.
- My crews will be glad to stand night watch without flinching. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? So your herds can be bled the faster? No.
- Your coastal castles still have silver in them. The war goes on.
- No. My crews fear nothing that can't follow them out to sea.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a leech? I'd sooner open my own veins.
- No, noble. You'll not drink my gold.
- Demand it of your cattle, [CT_NAME], not of the Lanun.

### Lanun → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs of Braduk! Ever seen the sea? Fire doesn't take on water, ye'll find.
- My forebears sold ships to Patria's fire priests, back when Bhall still answered them. Care to buy one, Clan?
- The Ember Banner. You raid on land, I raid at sea. Let's keep it that way and stay out of each other's pockets.

#### Declares war
- Your warbands torched my harbor towns. Now I'll show ye how a sea fire burns.
- Orcs and ships don't mix. I'll prove it on every coast ye own.
- You raid like wolves. I raid like a storm. Let's see which leaves more behind.

#### Refuses to talk
- No parley with orcs. You'd eat the envoy.
- Go back to your sacred flame and warm your hands. We're done talking.
- Talk? With the ash of my towns still on your boots? No.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- My crews love orc grog, [CT_NAME]; it strips the tar off a hull.
- Welcome, Clan. You're the first orcs to come aboard without trying to burn the ship.
- I've axes, spears and goblin boots in the hold, all lightly used. Interested, orc?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your goblins stole my anchors. What would orcs even do with anchors?
- You burned a fishing village of mine. Explain, before I burn one of yours.
- Speak, orc, and stand downwind.

#### Accepts a deal
- You're a straighter dealer than most humans I know. Done!
- Orc gold spends as well as any other. Shake on it.
- A fair trade, Clan. Let's both keep raiding other folk.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Orcs bearing gifts? The sea's full of surprises. Thank ye.
- Thank ye, Clan. My crew will drink to your fires tonight.
- Next time your warbands need a ferry, the first trip's free. Generous of you, orc.

#### Turns down a deal
- That's a raider's offer, orc, and I'm a raider too. No.
- Even a goblin haggles harder than that, and goblins are terrible at it.
- No. I don't trade good timber for rusty axes.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your sacred flame in Braduk; the sea would only put it out.
- There are softer coasts than yours to plunder. Aye, peace.
- Let's both burn other people's villages instead.

#### Refuses peace
- Ask Bhall to put out the fires on my waterfront first. Then we'll talk of peace.
- No. Ye burned mine, so I'll burn yours a while longer.
- Peace with orcs lasts till supper. Not worth the ink.

#### Rejects a demand
- A raider asking a raider for tribute? Bring a boat first, orc.
- No. The Lanun don't pay raiders; we are raiders.
- Ye'd need a fleet to threaten me, [CT_NAME], and orcs make poor oarsmen.

### Lanun → Doviello

#### First contact
- The wolves of the north. Ye survived the ice; so did we, dodging bergs that could tear a galley in half. Respect, of a sort.
- Can wolves swim, Doviello? Asking for the sake of my harbors.
- Northmen! I've furs to sell back to you at twice the price, and rum to keep out the cold you love so much.

#### Declares war
- Your pack raided my harbor towns. Wolves don't do well in deep water; let's prove it.
- You cull the weak, they say. Out at sea, the storm does the culling, and it's coming for you.
- I'm hungry too, wolf, and I've a thousand sails to feed.

#### Refuses to talk
- I don't parley with a pack. Go howl at the tide.
- No. Ye'd only bite the hand that held out the treaty.
- Talk is for folk who keep their word. Wolves keep only what they kill.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Come aboard, [CT_NAME], and shake the snow off; my deck has seen worse than wet wolf.
- Your hunters bring the best pelts in Erebus, Doviello, and my merchants pay well for them.
- Sit, pack leader, drink, and tell me which of your rivals is fattest for plunder.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your raiders killed my fishermen for sport. Explain, or I'll raid ye for sport.
- You snarl at my crew like they're lame sheep. They're not.
- Speak, wolf, and mind your teeth near my officers.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done! You bargain like you hunt: straight to the throat.
- Fur for rum, the oldest trade in the north. Agreed.
- Your pack won't starve this winter, wolf. It's a deal.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The pack, giving? Ye didn't even make me fight for it.
- Thank ye, Doviello. My crew will wear your furs with pride, and sweat.
- I'll remember the wolf who shared. Thank ye.

#### Turns down a deal
- That's a scrap thrown to a dog. I'm no dog.
- No. You take the carcass and offer me the bones.
- Hunt harder, wolf, and bring back a fatter offer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to your snow, and leave my harbors be.
- My crews are tired of fishing wolves out of the surf. Peace it is.
- There's richer prey than either of us out there. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Ye bit first; I'll bite last.
- No. A wolf let off the hook comes back with the whole pack.
- Your coast is weak and I'm strong. You of all people know what that means.

#### Rejects a demand
- The strong take, wolf, and at sea I'm the strong one.
- No. Your creed says the weak pay. I'm not weak.
- Come and take it, [CT_NAME]. Swim if ye must.

### Lanun → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim! Your pilgrims are forever asking passage to the Aegean Isles, then never finding the time to sail. The offer stands.
- Ahoy, monks. You tend the old holy places; my captains have found a few on islands nobody else remembers.
- Keepers of the holy sites, eh? We keep the sea. Between us, we've most of the world covered.

#### Declares war
- Your warrior monks boarded one of my ships barehanded and sent the crew swimming. Now my whole fleet comes calling.
- Holy men make poor sailors. My fleets will prove it on every shore you hold.
- I'll not plunder your shrines, but everything around them is fair game.

#### Refuses to talk
- No, monk. I know how your envoys work: they talk until the enemy surrenders.
- I'll not sit across from an Elohim. I'd come away having agreed to something.
- Go and tend your shrines, monk. My guns don't need tending.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ahoy, [CT_NAME]! Come aboard, but no sermons; my crew blushes.
- Your healers patched up half my crew last winter, Elohim. I owe you.
- Need passage somewhere holy, pilgrim? My rates are... reasonable.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your monks keep converting my sailors. I lose good men to your monasteries.
- You say ships should be for trade, not war. Tell that to your neighbors.
- Speak, holy one, and make it short; my crew doesn't like your stare.

#### Accepts a deal
- An honest bargain from honest folk. Strange feeling, but I'll take it.
- Agreed. Your word's good; I'll try to keep mine as long.
- Even my crew can't find a way to cheat it. Sold.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Elohim? I'll not even ask what it costs; you'd tell me the truth.
- Your monks sail safe on any ship of mine from now on. Thank ye.
- You make it very hard to be a pirate, Elohim.

#### Turns down a deal
- Too charitable to yourselves, monk. Try again.
- No. Your kindness is free; your terms aren't.
- I'd love to help, but the sea doesn't run on kindness.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your monks tend the sick, and my ships carry them.
- Aye. Your ships of trade and exploration, mine of... trade, mostly.
- I never enjoyed fighting folk who fight back with prayers. Peace.

#### Refuses peace
- Your coastal towns still have cargo worth carrying off. Peace can wait.
- No. You'll only talk my crews into deserting.
- The sea doesn't hurry, monk, and neither does a Lanun's mercy.

#### Rejects a demand
- Monks making demands? Your founder would weep to hear it.
- No. Charity's your trade, not mine.
- Ask Finner's tomb for gold, [CT_NAME]; your order are the ones who know where it lies.

### Lanun → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori! A Lanun captain named Malus once carried an artifact from your lands toward the Amurites. The blizzards took ship and cargo both. Our condolences, a little late.
- No gods, no masters, every soul its own captain? Ye'd make fine sailors, Grigori.
- A haven for runaways, eh? We've ferried runaways since before Patria fell. Let's talk about shipping.

#### Declares war
- Your adventurers raided my ports and called it a quest. Here's mine: your whole coastline.
- No god will lift a finger for you, by your own choosing. My fleets thank you for the courtesy.
- You lead yourselves, ye say. Then lead yourselves out of the path of my broadsides.

#### Refuses to talk
- Parley with folk who answer to no one? Who would I hold to the bargain?
- No. Your heroes have talked enough; let them fight.
- Tell your adventurers to swim out and ask. I'll listen to whichever one makes it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Any adventurers looking for a berth, [CT_NAME]? A good ship always needs hands who think for themselves.
- Welcome, Grigori. No priests at your back scowling at my crew; that makes you the best company in Erebus.
- Ah, the free folk! Sit, drink, and tell me what your heroes have dug up lately. I may know a buyer.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- One of your adventurers walked off my flagship with my best chart. I want it back, and the thief with it.
- You scorn the gods. Fine. Must you scorn my harbor fees as well?
- Spare me the lecture on freedom, Grigori. My people learned it on the open water, long before yours.

#### Accepts a deal
- Free folk trading freely; that's how the sea likes it. Done.
- Agreed, and no god consulted on either side. Refreshing.
- A fair trade. Now your heroes can buy a ship of their own and stop borrowing mine.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Grigori! Thank ye, and not a prayer owed for it.
- Your adventurers sail free on any Lanun ship this year. My thanks.
- I'll tell my crews the godless make better friends than the godly.

#### Turns down a deal
- Too little, free folk. Ye taught yourselves everything else; teach yourselves to bargain.
- No. Even a haven has to pay its way in the world.
- That deal has no wind in its sails. Try again.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your adventurers go hunting monsters instead of my treasure.
- There were no gods in this war to blame, so let's agree it was the rum.
- Back to the sea for me, and back to your freedom for you.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your heroes still owe me a ship and a chart.
- No. You've no gods to pray to for rescue, and I'm in no mood to play one.
- Your coast's too tempting and your heroes too few. The war sails on.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You won't even pay the gods their due. Why would I pay you?
- No. Your adventurers can earn their gold the honest way, like pirates.
- Go and lead yourself somewhere else, [CT_NAME].

### Lanun → Hippus

#### First contact
- The horse lords! A Lanun captain once gave one of your queens passage. Paid in contracts, cursed the sea all the way, and still looked back from the dock.
- No one outruns the Hippus on land, they say. Out here, no one outruns us.
- Mercenaries and pirates; we both sell what others won't. Let's talk.

#### Declares war
- Your raiders hit my harbor towns at a gallop. My fleets hit back under full sail.
- No one outruns the Hippus on land. Pity for you, this war's coming in from the water.
- Your companies took gold to raid my coast. Let's see what they charge to drown.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your riders talk as fast as they ride, and I'll not be carried off by it.
- Go and ride in circles somewhere else, horse lord.
- I'll talk when your horses learn to swim.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Bring a horse, [CT_NAME]? My crew wants to watch one try a gangplank.
- Your companies and my crews drink in the same taverns. Never a dull night, never an unbroken chair.
- Sit, drink, and tell me which war your companies are hiring out to next. I might sell it some ships.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your companies took my enemies' coin. A contract's a contract, ye say. So is a grudge.
- You sneer at sailors who can't sit a horse. Try sneering at a broadside.
- Speak, horse lord, and keep your spurs off my deck.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. A contract's a contract, and you of all folk honor one.
- Hippus gold rings true, and there's more of it every year. Agreed.
- Your companies will march well provisioned. You've a bargain, horse lord.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the horse lords! Foreign gold, flowing the wrong way for once. Thank ye.
- I'll drink to your herds tonight, and to the fastest of your mares.
- The next time one of your companies needs ferrying, the passage is on my purse. Generous of you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even a sell-sword can see this is a bad contract.
- That offer's worth less than a saddle with no horse under it.
- Too thin, Hippus. Saddle up a better offer and ride it back here.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Ride home over your plains; the waves were never your road.
- The sea's no place for horses, and the steppe's no place for ships. Let's each keep our own.
- Let's go back to brawling in the same taverns instead. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Ye've raided your own cousins' herds for generations. You know better than to stop a raid halfway.
- No. Your companies would hire themselves to my enemies before the ink dried.
- Your raiders struck and ran. Let them see how far they can run from a fleet.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You're the mercenaries; I'm the one who pays you, remember?
- No. Ride off and find a richer client.
- Charge your employers, [CT_NAME], not the Lanun.

### Lanun → Illians

#### First contact
- The Illians. Your winter froze our seas, cut off our islands and swallowed a generation of good crews. We have not forgotten.
- Ahoy, men of Letum Frigus. Back from the ice, are ye? The sea's warm again. Keep it that way.
- Mulcarn's own. In his winter our priests lost Danalin's voice, and what answers now is stranger. Some of us blame you.

#### Declares war
- Your winter took our islands once. My fleets will take your coast in payment.
- You would bring the ice back. Not while there's one Lanun hull afloat.
- Every berg that split a galley of ours was a debt. Today I come to collect.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Cold words from a cold people, and I'm sick of shivering.
- Talk to the icebergs, Illian. They used to listen to you.
- My crews remember the frozen years. They'd mutiny if I so much as sat down with you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ahoy, [CT_NAME]! Come stand by the galley stove; ye look chilly.
- Welcome, Illian. My crews don't trust you, but my merchants trust your silver.
- Ah, Letum Frigus sends an envoy! A rum to warm the bones, if yours still need warming.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Ice in my harbor at midsummer. Explain that, if you can.
- Your White Hand chants to a vanished god of winter along my coast. My sailors can't sleep for it.
- Speak, Illian, before the sea freezes under my keel.

#### Accepts a deal
- Cold coin is still coin. Done.
- Agreed. Let's keep the sea open and the bergs away, for both our sakes.
- No frostbite and a fair price. I'll take it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the north? Thank ye. Warmer than I expected.
- I'll drink to a mild winter for this, and a short one.
- Maybe the ice between us is finally thawing. Generous of you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That deal's as cold as the bottom of the sea.
- Thaw your purse a little, Illian, and we'll see.
- I'll not pay a copper toward bringing back the winter.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your ice off my seas, and we'll get along.
- My crews hate fighting with frost in the rigging. Aye, peace.
- Let the sea run free and the islands stay green.

#### Refuses peace
- Your winter cost us too many ships to forgive in one season.
- No. The ice took its due from us; now we take ours.
- Peace when the last berg has melted, and not a day before.

#### Rejects a demand
- I'd sooner sink my treasure in the deep than send it north to the cold.
- No. My gold stays somewhere warm.
- Ask Mulcarn for it, [CT_NAME]. Oh, that's right; he's gone.

### Lanun → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons with a city of their own, in Erebus. Well, the Lanun trade with anyone, they say. Today we find out if that's true.
- Ahoy, envoy of the pit. Ye smell of sulfur; stand well away from the powder kegs, there's a good devil.
- Every soul aboard my ships is already promised to the sea. Ye'll find nothing to collect here.

#### Declares war
- Ye burned a Lanun port to the waterline. Hellfire doesn't burn underwater, demon, and that's where I'm sending you.
- I'll bargain with anyone, but not with folk who take souls as interest. War.
- The sea drowns everything in the end. We'll start with your legions.

#### Refuses to talk
- There's no good deal to be made with demons. Every sailor's grandmother knows that.
- No. Ye'd have my soul in the fine print before I'd finished reading.
- Go back through your Obsidian Gate and knock on it. Maybe someone will answer.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- I'll talk, [CT_NAME], but my chaplain stands right behind me, and he's armed.
- Your gold's good, I'll grant, even if it's warm to the touch.
- Keep your claws on the table where I can see them, demon, and we'll do fine.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your imps set fire to my sails. Again.
- My crew won't come up on deck while you're aboard. Speak, and be quick.
- The ash blowing off your lands fouls every harbor I own. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- I've read every word of it twice, by lamplight, with a priest. Done.
- Agreed. My soul stays mine, mind; that's not part of the cargo.
- A fair trade. Strange words to say to a demon, but there they are.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from hell? I'll have the priests look at it before anyone drinks it.
- I'll do my best to forget where it came from. Thank ye, I suppose.
- Somewhere, a damned soul paid for this, didn't it? Still, generous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Every bargain with your kind has a hook in it, and I'm no fish.
- That deal smells of brimstone. No.
- Not even a Lanun is greedy enough to take that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your fires off my water.
- My crews have had their fill of hellhounds on the docks. Peace.
- Go and torment someone who can't sail away from you. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace with hell? When the sea boils dry.
- No. Every quiet day gives your Ashen Veil friends time to dig another door.
- Not while one demon still walks on my shores.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to hell? Come and take it, if you can swim in all that armor.
- No. The damned can pay their own way.
- Ask your friends in the Ashen Veil, [CT_NAME]. They seem to enjoy giving you things.

### Lanun → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad! Our grandsires traded with yours in the Age of Magic. I hear your people are still sore about it.
- Up from under the hills at last, dwarves! The sea's like a mountain, only wetter, and it moves.
- A people with gold and no ships. My favorite kind of neighbor.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are full and your coast is bare. No pirate born could leave that alone.
- In the old days the dwarves had no army to win redress. Let's see if you've raised one since.
- You distrust every foreigner, they say. Good instincts, dwarf. Too late.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Ye'd want it all carved in stone, and I'm not waiting that long.
- Go back down under your mountain, dwarf. My cannon will do the talking.
- Your black powder blew a hole in my flagship. I'm done listening.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- No illusions in my cargo this time, [CT_NAME]. I swear it on the sea.
- Welcome, Khazad. My merchants love your gold, and my crews love your ale even more.
- Ah, the dwarves! Come aboard, and mind the swell; it isn't stone underfoot.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your merchants called my captains swindlers. Fair, but rude.
- You weigh every coin I hand you, twice, in front of me.
- Speak, dwarf, and stop counting my cannon.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Real goods for real gold, and no tricks. Your ancestors would be stunned.
- Weigh it all you like, dwarf; it's honest, this time.
- I'll not even resell it at a profit. Much. You've a deal.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Khazad? Has anyone told your treasurers?
- I'll keep it somewhere a dwarf would approve of: a locked chest, under guard. Thank ye.
- Dwarven gold, freely given! Now the sea has seen everything.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Ye drive a hard bargain, dwarf, and I drive a harder one.
- You've mountains of gold; spare me a hill.
- That deal sits lower on your side of the scale than a dwarven anchor.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go home and polish your axes; I'll go and count what's left of my harbor.
- Your siege engines are too good for my harbor walls, I'll admit. Peace.
- Let's trade again honestly, or as honestly as I get.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. I've not seen the bottom of your vaults.
- No. You'd only dig in deeper and wait me out.
- Not until I've been paid, dwarf, and not one coin short.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? From me, to a dwarf? The fish would laugh.
- No. Your vaults are deep enough without mine.
- Go and dig it up, [CT_NAME]. You're good at that.

### Lanun → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates! Centaurs, lamia and men under one crown. A ship's crew is much the same, only wetter.
- Your settlements trade with everyone, and so do my ships. We'll be good friends or great rivals, confederation.
- Your borders are open to all, they say. My captains will take that as a warm invitation.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements are rich and your coast is lightly watched. That's all the reason a pirate needs.
- Pull back into your core lands like a turtle, if ye like. My fleets will take everything outside the shell.
- You take in everyone. Make room in your harbors, then; my crews are coming.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Ye'd talk me in circles with your courtly manners and I'd sail off owing you.
- Go back inside your shell, turtle.
- I'll not sit across from a centaur in this mood. They kick.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ahoy, [CT_NAME]! Your settlements are the friendliest ports in Erebus.
- Your lamia frighten my crew, Kuriotate, in the pleasant way.
- Do any of your centaurs fancy a sea voyage? We've never had one aboard, and the crew is placing bets.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your customs officers searched my ship three times. Three!
- One of your centaurs kicked my bosun clean into the harbor.
- Speak plainly, and save the court manners for someone who's impressed by them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Your settlements and my ships; a fine match. Done.
- Agreed. Let's hope this draws our peoples closer, as your court likes to say.
- Even your customs officers will be pleased with that one. Struck.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Gifts from the confederation, and I didn't even have to dock. Thank ye kindly.
- I'll fly your banner from my mainmast for a week.
- Generous. You make plundering your coast a touch awkward.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Polite, beautifully worded, and still no.
- That deal's got four legs and not one of them standing.
- Too courtly and too cheap. Try again.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Open your harbors again; I'll come as a customer this time.
- Your shell is too hard to crack anyway. Aye.
- Trade's better than war, and your harbor wine is better than both.

#### Refuses peace
- Your outer settlements are thinly guarded and richly stocked. I'll stop when one of those changes.
- No. You'd pull into your shell, muster, and come back for everything.
- Your crown can have its peace once I've finished touring its coast.

#### Rejects a demand
- You're the empire with the treasury, not me. Pay yourselves.
- No. Build your great edifice with your own gold.
- Take your bullying elsewhere, [CT_NAME]. I believe that's how your court puts it.

### Lanun → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The Ljosalfar. Fine forests ye have there. I'm only looking, I swear it.
- Ahoy, elves. Your groves outlasted the ice, and so did our islands. Tough folk, both of us.
- The Summer Court, is it? The sea keeps only two seasons, calm and storm. Which are you?

#### Declares war
- I need masts, and you've the tallest trees in Erebus. I asked nicely, elf.
- Your archers shot my woodcutters out of the trees. Now my cannon will shoot back.
- The forest can't follow a ship out to sea. Every elf on the coast is mine.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Elves talk for a century before they reach the point.
- I've nothing to say to people who shoot sailors for cutting firewood.
- Go and sulk in your groves, elf. I've a war to run.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your wine's the finest in Erebus, [CT_NAME]. Did ye bring any?
- Welcome, Ljosalfar. My crew sings your songs badly, but with real feeling.
- Ah, the elves! I've a cargo of rare seeds from the far isles; I thought of you at once.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your rangers cut my lumber camp to pieces.
- You look at my ships as if they were coffins for trees.
- Speak, elf, and stop staring at my mainmast like that.

#### Accepts a deal
- No trees were harmed, I promise. Done.
- Agreed. Your goods are as fine as your manners, and nearly as old.
- Even your Fellowship of Leaves couldn't fault that. A bargain.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the elves? Thank ye. I'll plant something, in your honor.
- My crew will toast the Summer Court tonight. Thank ye kindly.
- I'll steer my woodcutters well clear of your forests for a while. Generous of you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even an elf won't live long enough to make me take that.
- That deal's greener than a spring sapling.
- Too little, Ljosalfar. You've had centuries to save; spend some.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Your forests are safe from my axes, for now.
- My crews are sick of arrows coming out of the leaves. Peace it is.
- Let the leaves grow back over the stumps, and we'll speak no more of masts. For a while.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. I still need masts.
- No. Ye'd melt into the woods and wait for me to forget. I won't.
- Ye'll have peace when my shipyards have their timber, elf.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to elves? Ha! What would ye spend it on, acorns?
- No. Your treasure grows on trees; mine has to be stolen.
- The oak doesn't bend, your people say. Neither does a Lanun's purse, [CT_NAME].

### Lanun → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp! I've wanted a golem to turn my capstan for years. Name your price.
- Heirs of the Open-Skiers, back under the open sky! Try the open sea next; it's even bigger.
- Ye build servants that never tire. I've a crew that never stops drinking. We should talk.

#### Declares war
- Golems sink, gnome. Every last one of them.
- The ice crushed your golems once. The deep will do it again, and quicker.
- Your workshops are stuffed with treasure and your coast is lightly held. A pirate's dream, and I'm wide awake.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Talk to my anchors; they understand iron.
- I'll not parley with folk who send clockwork to do their bleeding for them.
- Go back to your workbench and build yourself a better argument.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Bring any clever contraptions, [CT_NAME]? My bosun's been praying for a pump that bails by itself.
- My shipwrights have been begging to meet your artificers. Bring one next time.
- Come aboard, gnome, and tell me what you think of my rigging. Honestly, now; I can take it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- One of your golems walked off a pier and took my best crane down with it.
- You look at my ships as if they were badly made. They're not; they're well stolen.
- Out with it, gnome, and call that iron man away from my docks before it sinks them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Luchuirp craftsmanship is worth every coin, and I've paid in real coin, too.
- Your goods are worth their weight in gold, and they're heavy. Agreed.
- Kilmorph smiles on honest dealing, I'm told, so mark this one down in my favor.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Luchuirp! I'll bolt it to the bow and polish it every morning.
- My shipwrights will take it apart, with your blessing, and maybe even put it back together.
- You've a friend at sea now, gnome, and a fast one.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I can see the gears in this one turning your way.
- Your workshops are full to the rafters; empty one a bit and ask again.
- That deal's as stiff as a rusted gear. Oil it and try again.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Your golems can go back to the fields where they belong.
- I'm tired of fishing iron men out of my harbors. Aye, peace.
- Your machines fetch better prices whole than in pieces. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Your artificers' workshops are still full of wonders, and my holds are still empty.
- No. I've a harbor full of drowned iron to avenge.
- Call your machines home first. Then ask me again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Ye've golems to fetch and carry gold for you. Send one.
- No. A Luchuirp crying poor is a sight I'll not pay to see.
- Ask again with a golem at your back, [CT_NAME]. I'll still say no, but I'll say it politely.

### Lanun → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim! Desert folk. Ever seen the sea? It's like your sand, only it fights back.
- Ahoy, children of the sun. Lugus loves the truth, they say. I'll try to keep my lies small while you're aboard.
- Your caravans carry spice across the dunes, my ships carry it across the waves. Let's not undercut each other.

#### Declares war
- Your Empyrean judges named my captains pirates. Accurate, but now they'll learn what pirates do.
- The sun beats down on your sand. My fleets will beat down on your coast.
- Your zealots burned a Lanun ship for carrying an idol of the Overlords. I'll burn ten of yours for it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Folk who worship truth make poor company for a pirate in wartime.
- I'll not argue with folk who think the sun itself is on their side.
- Go back to your oases and wait for the tide. It's coming.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Did ye bring any of that desert spice, [CT_NAME]? My cook has been weeping for it.
- Welcome, Malakim. Your judges listen to small folk and great alike, I hear. Even a pirate can respect that.
- Ah, the sun people! Come aboard; the sea breeze will cool you after all that sand.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your priests preached honesty to my crew. Half of them jumped ship, and the other half are confused.
- You squint at me as if I were a shadow that needs burning away.
- Speak, Malakim, and turn down that glare.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair trade under a fair sun. Done.
- Agreed. Your Empyrean would approve, though I'm not sure my crew will.
- A good bargain. Your caravans, my ships; between us, the whole world's covered.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the desert! Thank ye; I'll not even ask what it's worth. Well, maybe later.
- I'll drink to Lugus tonight, and nobody tell the Overlords.
- So the sun shines on pirates too. Generous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There's too much sand in that deal and not enough gold.
- Even the desert gives up more water than that, Malakim.
- That deal's as dry as your dunes. Wet it a little.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your caravans and my galleys meet at the coast as traders again.
- My crews were never made for this heat. Peace.
- Even the sun has to set some time.

#### Refuses peace
- Your coast still smells of spice and silver. I'm not done.
- No. Your zealots would only light another fire on my decks.
- Peace? The tide's still coming in, sun-child. Wait for it to turn.

#### Rejects a demand
- Your god of truth ought to have told you how I'd answer that.
- No. Go and sift your sand for gold.
- Ask the sun for it, [CT_NAME]. It gives everything away for free, I'm told.

### Lanun → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels! Rebel angels, at that. Ye broke the Compact; I break a law every morning before breakfast. We'll get on.
- My crew took you for demons at first sight, Mercurians. You do look the part, ye know.
- Warriors of heaven, eh? The deep has its own horrors these days, older than any demon. Fancy hunting a few?

#### Declares war
- You care nothing for mortals, they say. Then you'll not mind when mortals care nothing for you.
- You trampled my harbor flat chasing one devil. Now my fleets come chasing you.
- Heaven's soldiers are big, slow and bright. Perfect for cannon.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Ye never listen to mortals anyway; why should I bother?
- Go back to hell and hunt your demons. I'll be here when you're done.
- I don't parley with folk who carve their prayers into their own skin. It's off-putting.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Any demons need killing, [CT_NAME]? I know where a few have been hiding.
- Your soldiers keep my harbors clear of devils, Mercurian, and I owe you for that.
- Have some rum, angel. Does heaven allow rum? Ye've left heaven, so I'd say it does.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your angels flattened my docks chasing an imp. One imp.
- You look straight through me as if I weren't here. I am, and I'm armed.
- Speak, angel, and stop scowling at my crew; they've done nothing worth a holy war.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Arm your crusade; I'll take the gold and wish you luck.
- I never thought I'd take heaven's silver, but here we are. Agreed.
- Kill a demon for me with it. We've a deal.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from heaven itself? Well, I'll be keelhauled.
- I'll pray to somebody tonight, for the first time in years. Thank ye.
- My crew will swear for years that an angel bought them a drink.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Holy war's expensive; ye pay for it, not me.
- Heaven can afford better than that, angel.
- That deal would be a sin, and I'm saving my sins for better occasions.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go and kill demons; it's what you're good at.
- Fighting angels is bad luck, every sailor knows it. Aye.
- Your war's with hell, not with the Lanun, and we both know it.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your hammers wrecked my harbors; you'll pay for the timber.
- No. Let heaven's soldiers learn what it's like to be outnumbered at sea.
- You never asked for peace with the demons. Why should I give it to you?

#### Rejects a demand
- Heaven's paid you nothing since you broke the Compact, angel, and neither will I.
- No. Your crusade can fund itself, or ask Arawn.
- Heaven doesn't need my gold, [CT_NAME], and neither do you.

### Lanun → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. You want the world to end? Then nobody pays their debts, and I'm owed plenty. I'm against it.
- Ahoy, gate-openers. Ye open doors to other planes; I open casks of rum. Mine's the better hobby.
- A people gathered out of every nation for one purpose, they say. So is a pirate crew, but ours is a merrier purpose.

#### Declares war
- You'd drown the world in fire. I'd rather it drowned in seawater, and only the bits I don't need.
- Every gate you open fouls my seas with things that shouldn't swim. I'm closing yours, with cannon.
- No world, no sea; no sea, no plunder. Your Armageddon would put me out of business, so I'm putting you out of yours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. What bargain can I strike with folk who want everything gone, the bargain included?
- Go and stare into your gates. I've nothing to say.
- I don't parley with people who pray for the last day. It's bad luck aboard ship.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ahoy, [CT_NAME]! Still here? The world, I mean. Good, good.
- Welcome, Sheaim. While the world lasts, let's make some coin out of it.
- Ah, the doom-sayers! Come aboard and watch a sunset; I'll show you something worth keeping.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Things have been crawling out of the sea off your coast, all eyes and teeth. Yours?
- Your rituals are rotting my fishing grounds. The fish come up wrong.
- Speak, Sheaim, and stop looking at my ships as if they were already wrecks.

#### Accepts a deal
- Spend it before the world ends, eh? Done.
- Agreed. An odd bargain with odder folk, but gold is gold.
- A fair trade. Let's both enjoy it while there's still a sky to drink under.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim? Thank ye; I'll spend it fast, just in case.
- Maybe ye're in less of a hurry for the end than you let on. Thank ye.
- Generous. Odd, coming from folk who want it all gone, but generous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Why should I trade for tomorrow with folk who don't want one?
- Too little, Sheaim. If the world's ending anyway, ye might as well be generous.
- That deal stinks of a ritual, and I'll not be part of the offering.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your gates shut and my seas calm.
- Let the world spin a while longer; I've ports I haven't visited yet.
- Back to your rituals, and I'll back to my rum. I know who's having the better evening.

#### Refuses peace
- Your gates are still open on my coast. Shut them, then ask.
- No. Ye'd use the quiet to finish your spells.
- Peace with the end of the world? Not while the world's still worth plundering.

#### Rejects a demand
- Ye'll not need gold when the world ends, so why ask for mine?
- No. My treasure is for spending, not for feeding your apocalypse.
- Ask the void for it, [CT_NAME]. It's never given me anything either.

### Lanun → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. My lookouts swore they saw ghosts walking in the fog. It turns out it was you.
- Grey folk! Ye traded pieces of your souls for long life. I'd have haggled harder.
- Shades, eh? The sea's full of the dead. Ye'll feel right at home on it.

#### Declares war
- Your hidden cities are hidden no longer. My fleets found them through the fog.
- Ye hunt the walking dead, and my Drown pull my oars. We were never going to be friends.
- Ye can float through walls, they say. Let's see ye float through a broadside.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. I can't even tell where you end and the fog begins.
- Ye gave up your feelings with your souls. Ye'll not miss a conversation.
- Go back to your mist, shade. This war's not finished.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ye look paler than last time, [CT_NAME], and that's saying something.
- My crew is terrified of you, Sidar, but my merchants love your silver.
- Come aboard, shade, and hold on to something; I'd hate for you to drift off in the breeze.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades unmade my Drown at the harbor. Those were good rowers, and they were paid for.
- You look at my crew as if they were already dead. They're not, and they'd like to keep it that way.
- Speak, shade, before you fade out halfway through a sentence.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. A bargain with ghosts; the crew won't believe a word of it.
- Gold is gold, even when a shade hands it over. Agreed.
- Ye've had centuries to learn bargaining, and it shows. Struck.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Grey? Thank ye. My crew will light a candle for you, if that means anything to you.
- I'll spend it before you change your mind; ye've time to spare, and I haven't.
- I didn't think shades bothered with the living. Generous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Ye've centuries to make a better offer; spend a few minutes of them.
- Too thin, shade. Like everything else about you.
- That deal's as grey and cold as your cities.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back into your fog, and I'll keep my ships out of it.
- Cannon do poorly against things made of mist. Peace.
- Ye leave my Drown alone, and I'll leave your cities alone. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while your shades keep unmaking my Drown.
- No. Ye'd just fade away and come drifting back when my guard was down.
- You've eternity to wait for peace, shade. Wait a little longer.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to ghosts? Ye can't even hold a coin, can ye?
- No. The dead don't need gold, and you're most of the way there.
- Fade away, [CT_NAME], and take the demand with you.

### Lanun → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Svartalfar! Knives in the dark and smiles by daylight. Ye'd make fine pirates.
- Ahoy, Winter Court. Ye pray to Esus; I pray to luck. Might be the same god under different sails.
- Dark elves, eh? Your cousins in the summer woods can't stand you. That makes us half friends already.

#### Declares war
- Your assassins knifed one of my captains in port. Now the whole fleet comes for you.
- Esus may hide you in shadows, but shadows don't stop cannon.
- Ye play your games in the dark. I play mine on the open sea, with more players.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. I've seen how the Unseelie seal a bargain: with a blade, after dark.
- I'll not parley with assassins. I like my throat the way it is.
- Go back to your shadows, elf, and stay in them.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Brought any secrets to sell, [CT_NAME]? I pay well for good ones.
- Welcome, Svartalfar. Two peoples who love a good trick; we'll have plenty to talk about.
- Ah, the Unseelie! Come aboard, and keep your daggers sheathed at my table; I'll do the same.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your spies were caught in my harbor, counting my ships. Count this: one fewer spy.
- You smile like a shark circling a raft, elf. Out with it.
- Out with it, elf, and keep both hands on the table; my bosun's counting your fingers.

#### Accepts a deal
- A deal with no tricks in it; we're both surprised, I think.
- Agreed. The Council of Esus pays for its miracles, and so do you. I like that.
- Let's both pretend neither of us tried to cheat, elf. Agreed.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Unseelie? Thank ye. I'll check it for poison, purely out of respect.
- I'll remember that the Winter Court was good to me.
