- Is this the part where ye ask a favor? No? Then I'm doubly grateful.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There's a trick in this somewhere, and I'm the one who usually plays them.
- Your court's rich, elf; pay like it.
- Nice try. I've cut purses finer than that one.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Melt back into your winter shadows, and I'll keep to the sunlit water.
- Let's save our knives for other folk. Aye.
- Your summer kin will be disappointed we stopped. Agreed.

#### Refuses peace
- Your assassins are still breathing, and so is my grudge.
- No. Ye'd sign it with one hand and sharpen a knife with the other.
- Peace with the Unseelie? I'll take it when your winter ends, and not before.

#### Rejects a demand
- I'd sooner pay the fishes than the Winter Court.
- No. Esus charges for miracles; I charge for everything.
- Steal it if ye can, [CT_NAME]. I'd almost admire you for it.

## Ljosalfar

### Ljosalfar → Amurites

#### First contact
- The Amurites. When Patria burned, your people were a single clan shivering in the snow. You have grown quickly, children of Kylorin.
- We know something of magic ourselves; our mages kept the last groves alive through the long winter. Use your gift as carefully.
- Welcome, scholars. Walk softly in our woods. The trees remember every fire a wizard ever lit beneath them.

#### Declares war
- Your adepts have been stripping our groves for reagents. The season of patience is over.
- Magic for its own sake, you say. Then you will not mind if we test yours against the forest's own.
- Kylorin's children have forgotten what his age did to the world. We have not, and we will remind you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A wizard's words are spells by another name, and we will not be bound by them.
- Go back to your towers. We will speak again when your fires have gone out in our woods.
- The Summer Court has heard enough clever arguments from the Amurites for one age.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend. Our mages would gladly trade their lore of growing things for a little of yours.
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. Your schools are said to be the finest in Erebus. Ours were older, once; perhaps they will be again.
- It is pleasant to speak with a people who understand that magic is a living thing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your archmages squabble like jays and expect the rest of Erebus to fall silent while they do.
- One of your apprentices set a hillside of our oaks alight to prove a theorem. Explain yourself.
- Keep your hands still, Amurite. The forest does not like being gestured at.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair exchange. Our people will profit from your learning, as yours will from ours.
- We accept. Knowledge given freely grows like a seed, in both our lands.
- Even your most fastidious headmaster could find nothing amiss here.

#### Thanks for a gift
- An unexpected kindness from the Amurites. The Summer Court will remember it.
- Our mages will be delighted, [CT_NAME], and somewhat jealous.
- You give as one scholar to another. It is well received.

#### Turns down a deal
- This is not a balanced offer. Even an apprentice of yours could see it.
- No. You would trade us a little knowledge for a great deal of land.
- We decline. Our groves are not ingredients for your experiments.

#### Agrees to peace
- Let the fires die, then. Our forests need time to heal, and your schools need their students.
- Return to your studies, Amurite, and leave our woods to grow.
- We accept. Two peoples so devoted to magic should not waste it on each other.

#### Refuses peace
- Your fire still smolders in our forests. There will be no peace while it does.
- Not yet. You must first learn that some things do not belong in a laboratory.
- No. Your mages would use the respite to prepare a greater storm.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute from the forest? Write a treatise on why not; we will not read it.
- The oak does not bend for every blustering wizard.
- Our groves are not a library for your scholars to borrow from, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- The Balseraphs. We have heard of your court, where the masks laugh and the faces beneath them weep.
- A nation that wears other people's minds like costumes. You will find elven minds old, and very difficult to wear.
- Keep your puppets out of our forest, Balseraph; the trees do not care for things without souls.

#### Declares war
- Your Taskmasters took elves from our borders to perform in your court. We are coming to take them home.
- Every mind you have stolen cries out against you. The forest has heard them, and it is angry.
- Your carnival has wandered too close to our groves. We will end the performance.

#### Refuses to talk
- Every word from your court is a jest, and every jest has a blade in it. No.
- We will not dance to your tune, Balseraph. Not while this war lasts.
- Speak to your mirrors. We are not listening.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Balseraph. Our court is curious about yours, from a safe distance.
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. You are always entertaining; our only wish is that you remain only entertaining.
- Greetings. Your harlequins dance nearly as well as our own dancers at Beltane. Nearly.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your mimics have been prowling our woods, stealing the skills of our rangers. Call them back.
- We found one of your puppets in our grove, smiling at nothing. We buried it.
- Your court's laughter carries all the way to our borders. It is not a pleasant sound.

#### Accepts a deal
- We accept, though we read every word twice. One learns caution with your court.
- It is a fair trade, strangely enough. Let it stand.
- Agreed. Sanity is a strange thing to find in your court, but we will take it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Your court sends a gift and no jest. The forest finds that the strangest jest of all, and thanks you.
- Our thanks. We will look for the trick later, but for now, our thanks.
- You surprise us, Balseraph. The forest is grateful, if puzzled.

#### Turns down a deal
- There is a trap in this somewhere. We decline.
- Your terms are a masquerade. We would like to see the face beneath before we sign.
- No. We do not trade with those who keep slaves for their amusement.

#### Agrees to peace
- Let the laughter stop, then. Return our captives and keep your carnival away.
- May your court find other entertainments. Peace, Balseraph.
- We accept. Our forest needs quiet more than it needs vengeance.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while our people still perform in your court.
- Peace with a court that would forget it by morning? No.
- Your freaks still march in our woods. Not yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the jester? Not even for a good joke.
- No. The forest is not an audience for your threats; it does not applaud.
- Our forest is not your stage, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Bannor

#### First contact
- The Bannor. A confessor of the Order once brought fire into our forest to cleanse a cult. We sent him back to the Order in two pieces.

- You walked out of a hell of fire and became a people of order. We walked out of a winter and became a people of patience.

#### Declares war
- Your priests have named our groves heathen ground. Then come and take them, if the trees allow it.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not bargain with zealots who burn forests to save them.
- No. Your priests have already judged us; let them judge this silence too.
- Your Confessors' fire is still warm in our woods. The trees have nothing to say to you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Bannor. We respect a people who keep their word, even if they shout it.
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. Your discipline is admirable. Our rangers have been watching your drills from the trees.
- Greetings, soldier. There is room in this world for your order and our forests both.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your crusaders cut a road through our oldest grove. Explain that to the trees.
- Your priests preach that our faith is error. Our faith was old before Junil looked down at all.
- Speak, Bannor, but lower your voice. This is a grove, not a parade ground.

#### Accepts a deal
- A just and orderly bargain. We accept.
- Your priests and our druids can both bless this one.
- We accept. Let it stand, as your Order would say, without question.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Bannor, given without a sermon. You honor us.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. The forest will remember the Bannor kindly, for once.
- You give generously, as you fight. We are grateful.

#### Turns down a deal
- Your Order should know a fair offer from this one.
- No. Your terms march in lockstep toward your own advantage.
- We decline. Obedience is not a currency we accept.

#### Agrees to peace
- Let the swords rest. Our forests need tending, and your Crusade needs other enemies.
- Fight the demons, Bannor, and leave the trees alone.
- There is enough true evil in Erebus for both of us to fight. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while your Confessors still burn our groves.
- No. The Order would call it mercy, then return with more Confessors.
- You came into our forest with fire. You will leave it the same way.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Order? Junil is not our god.
- No. The forest pays no tithes.
- Command your own people, [CT_NAME]. Not ours.

### Ljosalfar → Calabim

#### First contact
- The Calabim. We keep a grimoire once taken from your libraries, locked away where such things belong.
- Vampires. The forest knows the cycle of death and rebirth. You stepped out of it long ago, and the trees can smell it on you.
- Nobles of the night. Our woods are dark too, but their darkness is full of life, not hunger.

- Your hunters have taken elves from our borders. Elven blood is older than your hunger, and it will cost you dearly.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We will not listen to a voice made for charming prey.
- Return to your estates and your cattle. The forest has nothing to say to you.
- We have centuries to wait, vampire, and so do you. Wait, then.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Calabim. Forgive our rangers their drawn bows; they mean nothing by it. Mostly.
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. You are gracious, for one who sees every mortal as a meal.
- Greetings. Your libraries are finer than your manners, we hear. We will gladly trade for books, never for blood.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your bloodpets were seen in our woods at night, marking trees. They will not be seen again.
- You look at our envoys as if wondering how elven blood tastes. Do not wonder aloud.
- Be quick, vampire. Our rangers dislike the smell of the grave.

#### Accepts a deal
- A sensible bargain, and our rangers will deliver it by daylight.
- We accept. Let coin pass between us, so that nothing else needs to.
- It is a fair trade. We had not expected one from the Broods.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Grand Broods. We will examine it carefully, but you have our thanks.
- Our thanks, though we would rather not know whose it was before it was yours.
- Unexpected. Perhaps your nobility runs deeper than appetite.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You bargain as you feed: a little at a time, until nothing is left.
- Our groves will not feed your herds, nor your hunger.
- This offer is as bloodless as the hand that wrote it. Improve it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your castles and your silk, and let the forest close behind you.
- The forest has buried enough of your victims. Let it end.
- We accept, for the sake of the living. You would not understand the reason.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while your hunters still prowl our borders by moonlight.
- No. Our rangers have only begun to learn the ways into your castles.
- Every life you took is remembered in the rings of our trees. Not yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- Not a coin, vampire, and not a drop.
- No. Your appetite gives you no rights over us.
- The forest feeds no parasites, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs of Braduk. Bhall's fire raged through every forest on the day she fell. Our oldest trees still carry the scars.
- The Ember Banner. You worship fire; we tend what fire devours. Mind where you carry your torches.
- Greetings, Clan. Once your people were men who loved justice. The forest remembers that, even if you do not.

#### Declares war
- Your warbands have set the borderwoods ablaze. Now our archers will make an example of you.
- Fire is part of the forest's cycle, but you burn without end. The cycle demands an answer.
- Every tree you fell for your war-fires will be paid for with an orc.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your torches are still lit in our woods.
- We do not parley with arsonists.
- Go back to Braduk and warm your hands at your fallen goddess. We are not talking.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- You have not set anything alight today, Clan. We count that as a beginning.
- Your people learn quickly, we are told, [CT_NAME]. Learn this, then: the forest can be a friend.
- Leave your torches at the edge of the wood, and you may sit with us.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Smoke rises from our border again. Your goblins, we presume?
- Your raiders cut our saplings for spear shafts. The forest has noticed.
- Say your piece, orc, and keep your breath off the leaves.

#### Accepts a deal
- So be it. A fair trade, and nothing burned to make it.
- We accept. Perhaps your clans are more than their axes.
- Let it keep your fires on your own side of the river.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, from the Ember Banner? The forest is surprised, and grateful.
- Our thanks. It is good to see something pass from your hands that is not aflame.
- You honor us, Clan. Perhaps a little of Bhall's old mercy lingers in you yet.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not trade timber to people who burn it.
- This offer is a raid wearing a treaty's clothes. We decline.
- You would take our green wood and give us ash. Not enough, orc.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Put out your fires, and let the ash become soil again.
- Green things will grow over the battlefield, as they always do.
- Return to your clans; the forest will mend itself without your help.

#### Refuses peace
- The embers you left in our woods still glow. Not yet.
- No. Every burned grove must be answered.
- You would use the respite to gather more torches. The war continues.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to those who burn our homes? Never.
- No. Take your threats back to your sacred flame.
- Burn every tree on the border if you can, [CT_NAME]; the roots will still say no.

### Ljosalfar → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. You were the winter's own wolves while our people froze in the last groves. We have not forgotten.
- You abandon your weak, northmen. The elves who survived the Age of Ice were the ones who never did.

#### Declares war
- You prospered in the winter that killed our god. Now it is spring, wolf, and the forest hunts.
- Your hunters killed our rangers and left them for the crows. That is the custom of your people; this is the custom of ours.
- The wolf culls the weak. Come into our woods and see who is weak.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Wolves do not keep bargains, and we will not offer one.
- The pack may howl at our borders. We do not answer.
- Go back to the snows that suited you so well.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- You came as a guest and not a hunter, Doviello; the forest notices such things.
- Your hunters move well among the trees, [CT_NAME]. Almost like elves.
- Even wolves have their place in the forest, so long as they keep to it. Sit.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your hunters have been killing our deer and leaving the carcasses to rot.
- Your envoy reeks of the kill. Speak, and then go and wash in the river.
- Bare your teeth in this grove again and our archers will answer them.

#### Accepts a deal
- We accept. A hungry pack is a dangerous neighbor; a fed one, less so.
- You bargain bluntly, and it saves us both a season.
- A fair exchange. Your pack will eat, and our forest will be left in peace.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the pack? The forest did not expect it, but welcomes it.
- You shared when you could have taken. That is not nothing, wolf.
- You honor us. Perhaps the thaw has softened something in the Doviello.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You offer the bones and keep the meat.
- We decline. Go and hunt for a better offer.
- Your own pack would not accept a share so uneven, wolf.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Hunt the elk of the north, and leave the deer of our forest to us.
- The forest needs time to bury its dead. Let it end.
- Even wolves must know where their range ends.

#### Refuses peace
- The forest has not finished hunting you. Not yet.
- You beg because you are wounded, wolf. Your own creed says the wounded are left behind.
- No. Your winter took too much from us to forgive so soon.

#### Rejects a demand
- Strength takes, in your creed. Come and see whether you are strong enough to take from the forest.
- No. The forest bows to no wolf.
- Howl all you like, [CT_NAME]. The answer will not change.

### Ljosalfar → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim! Before he fell silent, Sucellus entrusted his holy places to your order. His children thank you for keeping them.
- Greetings, pilgrims. Your order saw the seven firs born at the signing of the Compact. We would hear of it from your lips.
- Welcome. Your monks tended the dying through the winter that nearly ended our kind. We owe you more than words.

#### Declares war
- You have closed a holy place of Sucellus to his own children. We grieve to do this, but we will open it.
- Even the gentlest hands can wound a grove, and yours have. We march, with sorrow.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now, pilgrim. Our hearts are too heavy for your gentle words.
- No. We know how Elohim envoys work: they speak until their enemies lay down their arms.
- The Summer Court will not be talked out of this war, however wise the speaker.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- How fare the sacred places you tend, friend? The forest asks after them.
- Your monks and our druids pray in different tongues, [CT_NAME], but for the same things.
- It is always good to see the Elohim. Sit; the grove is glad of you.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your pilgrims tramp through our sacred groves as if they were their own.
- You preach peace to us while your monks lay claim to our holy places.
- Speak, Elohim. We are listening, but not as warmly as we once did.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair bargain, and an honest one. We expected nothing less.
- Agreed. May it serve both our peoples as the Compact served Erebus.
- Let it be so. Your word is good, and so is ours.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Your kindness is as old as the Compact. Our thanks.
- You give as your founder did, without counting. The forest is grateful.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. The Ljosalfar will not forget this.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even your generosity cannot make these terms fair.
- We cannot accept this, though we thank you for asking so gently.
- This is not a balanced offer, friend. Please improve upon it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. We never wished to fight the keepers of holy places.
- Your monks may tend the wounded of both sides.
- We accept. Let us now repair together the harm done to our lands.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The holy place is still closed to us.
- No. This war must run its course, however it pains us.
- We cannot stop, Elohim. Not until the grove is tended by elven hands again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Even pilgrims must carry their own bread. No.
- Tribute? Charity is your calling, not ours.
- You of all peoples should know that a gift demanded is no gift, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori. Our god died, and we prayed to an empty sky for an age. You chose that silence. We are curious why.
- You shelter those who would lead their own lives. In the long winter, the elves learned to do the same.

#### Declares war

- You turned away from the gods. Now the forest turns on you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. The forest has no patience for a people who scorn every power but their own.
- Your heroes came seeking adventure. They have found it; they will not find a parley.
- The Summer Court has nothing to say to Grigori raiders.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Our people know what it is to stand without a god, Grigori. We may have much to discuss.
- Your adventurers have been respectful in our woods, [CT_NAME]. We thank you.
- The Luonnotar you shelter speak of one greater god beyond the others. Our druids find that most interesting.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- One of your adventurers cut down a sacred tree to make a bow. Explain.
- The gods are no concern of yours, we know. Must the forest be none of your concern either?
- Be brief. Your heroes have worn out their welcome.

#### Accepts a deal
- Freely offered, freely taken. We accept.
- No priest blessed this bargain, and none needed to.
- Agreed. The forest bargains as freely as you live.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Our thanks. Kindness that no god commanded is kindness indeed.
- You honor us, [CT_NAME]. The forest will remember a free people's gift.
- Generous, and given without a prayer attached. The Ljosalfar are grateful.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms lean more on our goodwill than on your coin.
- Lead yourselves to a better offer.
- A people who rely on themselves should know how to make a fairer offer than this.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your adventurers seek other quests, far from our groves.
- No god demanded this war, so none need be appeased to stop it.
- Let both our peoples return to living as they choose. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Your adventurers still hold our sacred places. Peace can wait until they leave them.
- No. Your adventurers came for trophies; let them learn what the forest keeps.
- The war continues until your heroes understand that some places are not for plundering.

#### Rejects a demand
- You pay no tithe to the gods, Grigori, and we pay none to you.
- No. Rely on yourselves, as you are so fond of saying.

### Ljosalfar → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus. Your herds graze where forests once stood. We hope they do not graze further.
- Horse lords. You sell your swords, we hear. Elves are not for hire.

#### Declares war
- Your riders trample our saplings as they pass. We will plant arrows in their place.
- You sell your swords to anyone. Someone paid you to burn our borderwoods, and now you will pay for it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your riders are too quick with their words and their torches.
- Ride on, Hippus. We are not talking.
- We will speak when your horses are off our land.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your horses are beautiful, Hippus; we have none like them.
- Your companies keep their contracts, [CT_NAME], which is more than most can say.
- Our rangers and your riders could guard a long border together, if you wished it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your companies rode for our enemies last summer. Did they pay you well for elven lives?
- Your horses ate the young shoots in our groves. Keep them out.
- Speak, horse lord, and get down from the saddle; you are in a grove.

#### Accepts a deal
- Honest coin for honest goods. The forest accepts.
- Your companies know a good contract when they see one, and so do we.
- It is done. Your riders and our rangers have something to toast tonight.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the horse lords, and not a contract in sight. Our thanks.
- Our rangers will see your riders safely through the woods after this.
- The forest is grateful. Perhaps foreign gold is not the only measure of your clans.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your companies would not ride for so little, and we will not sell for it.
- Your herds are worth more than this offer, and so are our groves.
- We decline. You bargain as you ride: hard, and always in your own direction.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Ride home, and let the grass grow over the battlefield.
- Your mares are foaling and our trees are budding; both deserve a quiet spring.
- We accept. The plains are yours and the forest ours; let us both remember the line between.

#### Refuses peace
- Your riders are still raiding along the forest's edge. We are not finished with them.
- No. The forest does not forgive riders who burned it for hire.
- The war continues until no Hippus rider dares the forest's edge.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute is what you charge others. We do not pay it.
- No. We hire no mercenaries, least of all ones who threaten us.
- Ride on, [CT_NAME]. The forest has nothing for you.

### Ljosalfar → Illians

#### First contact
- The Illians. Your god's winter killed ours. The elves who survived it remember every frozen grove, and every name.
- Mulcarn's people, risen out of Letum Frigus. The forest shivers at your approach. So do we, but not from fear.
- Greetings, Illian. Spring never came to undo the winter decree, because of your master. We will be courteous, and no more.

#### Declares war
- Your winter killed Sucellus and split our people in two. We will not let it come again.
- The Age of Ice took nearly everything from us. Now we come to take everything from you.
- Frost has been found in our groves at midsummer. We know whose hand that is, and we will cut it off.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We have nothing to say to the servants of the long winter.
- Your words are frost on young leaves. Go.
- When the snow leaves our groves, perhaps. Not before.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- You come in peace, Illian, and we receive you in peace. But the forest remembers, and so do we.
- Sit by the fire, [CT_NAME], if you can bear the warmth.
- Our groves are green again. We would like them to stay that way, and we trust you agree.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your White Hand chants in the cold places near our border. We hear them at night.
- They say you would be a god. We have seen what gods of winter do to the world.
- Be quick. The dew on our leaves is turning to rime.

#### Accepts a deal
- We accept, though trading with the north still feels strange to us.
- It is a fair bargain. Let it warm the air between us, a little.
- May it bring both our peoples nearer to spring.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift out of Letum Frigus. We did not expect warmth from the north.
- Our thanks, Illian. Perhaps not everything that comes from the cold is cruel.
- The forest will think on this through many seasons.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We will not help the north prepare another winter.
- This offer would freeze the sap in our trees.
- Our grandmothers starved in your winter. We will not trade away what they died to keep.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let the seasons turn as they should, and keep your frost at home.
- The forest is weary of frost on its leaves. Let it end.
- May you find something better to worship than the cold. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while snow still falls on our groves out of season.
- No. Your master's winter took our god. We will take your army.
- The forest endured your cold for an age. It can endure a little more war.

#### Rejects a demand
- Never, not while one elf remembers the winter.
- No. We gave the winter everything once. Never again.
- Our god died in your master's winter, [CT_NAME]. You will have nothing from us.

### Ljosalfar → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons, walking in Erebus. Our priests teach that there is no rebirth for those exiled to your realm. Looking at you, we believe them.
- The Infernals. One of our rangers once brought down a Balor with plain arrows. We tell you so that you understand us.
- Greetings is not the word. Let us say: we see you, hellspawn.

- No. Our druids would have to burn the very air you spoke in.
- Your voice withers the leaves. Be silent.

- Our druids stand at our side, and the forest listens. Say what you came to say.
- You are courteous, [CT_NAME], for a demon. We will be courteous, for an elf.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The trees along your border are dying, one ring at a time. Explain.
- Your imps have been lighting fires in our groves.

#### Accepts a deal
- We accept, and our druids will cleanse every coin.
- It is a trade, not a truce of the heart. So be it.
- Let it turn your hunger elsewhere.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the pit. Our druids will purify it, but we thank you.
- Unexpected. We wonder what it truly cost, and who paid.
- The forest flinches at it, but thanks you all the same.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. A bargain with hell is a seed that grows only thorns.
- We would sooner trade with a forest fire.
- We decline. Even the shade of a tree would wither under these terms.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. Take your fires home, and let the rain do its work.
- Our soil needs time to heal from your touch.
- We accept, but our rangers will be watching every shadow along your border.

#### Refuses peace
- The soil you poisoned will take a century to heal. You will not have peace in less.
- Not while your ash still falls on our groves.
- No. The forest has begun to fight back, and it does not know how to stop.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to hell? We would bury our gold beneath an oak before we let you touch it.
- No. The pit may keep its threats; the forest has heard them before.
- Our groves owe nothing to the damned, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad, children of Kilmorph, up from under the hills. The sun has missed you; the forest, rather less.
- Dwarves, up from the deep. You did not even notice the winter that killed half our people. We try not to hold it against you.

#### Declares war
- Your miners have torn open the hills beneath our forest. The roots are dying, and so will your miners.
- You distrust magic and outsiders alike. Today you are right to.
- Your furnaces hunger for timber. Our forest is not fuel.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back beneath your mountain.
- We will not haggle with the Khazad while our trees burn in your forges.
- Your axes are still biting into our oaks. Let them fall silent, and perhaps we will speak.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your stonework is beautiful, Khazad. Our masons, such as they are, envy it.
- Your merchants deal honestly, [CT_NAME], and that is rarer than gold.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your woodcutters are in our forest again. Call them back.
- You weigh every word we say as if it were false coin.
- Speak, dwarf. We can see you appraising our trees for timber.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair trade, weighed and measured. We accept.
- Even your sternest appraiser would call it just.
- It is done. Carve it in stone, if that comforts you.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Khazad! The forest is honored, and a little astonished.
- Your generosity is as solid as your stone.
- You honor us, [CT_NAME]. The Ljosalfar remember such things for a very long time.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You weighed this on your scales, not ours.
- Our timber is worth more than your gold, dwarf.
- You of all peoples know this offer is unbalanced.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your halls, and we will tend our trees.
- Neither stone nor root wins this war. Let it end.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while your siege engines stand in our woods.
- No. Your miners have not yet left our hills.
- The roots you cut are still bleeding sap. Not yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- From the forest to the Khazad? You have more gold under one hill than we have in all our groves.
- No. Kilmorph gave you the riches of the earth; ask her for more.
- Dig deeper, [CT_NAME]. You will find nothing of ours down there.

### Ljosalfar → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates. Centaurs, lamia and men under one crown; the forest approves of such variety.
- Your crown sits on a head that never ages, we hear. Elves understand such things better than most.
- Welcome. Your nation is young, but its doors are open. That is a good beginning.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements creep over our forest's edge like ivy. We will pull them up by the root.
- Your confederation swallows everything around it. It will not swallow the forest.
- When threatened you retreat into your shell, they say. Let us see how hard that shell is.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your courtiers speak smoothly; we will not be smoothed.
- Go back to your great cities. We are not talking.
- The forest will not hear the confederation until its settlers leave.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your centaurs run well beneath the trees, Kuriotate. They are always welcome among us.
- Your nation is young, [CT_NAME], but it already knows how to listen.
- Your lamia and our mages could teach each other much, if you would allow it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your settlers have been felling our trees for their fences. That must stop.
- You address us as one empire to another. We are older than empires.
- Speak, Kuriotate, but spare us the courtier's flourishes; the trees find them tiresome.

#### Accepts a deal
- You are wise beyond your years, as ever. We accept.
- The confederation bargains with grace; we expected no less.
- A fair trade. It pleases us.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the confederation, given as freely as your asylum. You honor us.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. The forest remembers its friends, and now you are one.
- Your centaurs will always find an open path through our groves after this.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Beautifully argued, and still lopsided.
- We decline. A nation that builds for the ages should know how long we remember a bad bargain.
- Weigh it again, friend; the scale tips your way.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your settlements stand and our forests grow, each on its own side.
- Your court and ours both have better things to build.
- Your centaurs may run our paths again, as they once did. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Your settlers' fences still cut across our groves. Not yet.
- No. You would only withdraw into your core lands and come again with more.
- The forest is slow to start a war, and slower still to end one.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a nation not yet a century old? No.
- No. The forest was ancient before your crown was forged.
- Build your great edifice without our timber, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun. Your ships are built from our cousins, the trees. Forgive us if we look at them sadly.
- Greetings, sea-folk. You love freedom, they say. So does the wind in the canopy.
- Pirates and traders both. Keep to the coast, and our forest will keep to the hills.

#### Declares war
- Your shipwrights have felled our oldest trees for masts. The forest demands a reckoning.
- Your captains keep no word for long. Then we will keep no peace.
- The sea is yours. The forests along the coast are ours, and your fleets will learn where one ends.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A Lanun's word is as fleeting as sea foam.
- Sail away, captain. We are not listening.
- Not while your axes still ring in our coastal woods.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your sea songs are lovely, Lanun. Ours are of the trees; we should trade.
- Your ships bring wonders from far islands, [CT_NAME]. We are grateful for them.
- The seeds your captains brought from the far isles have taken root in our groves. Come and see.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your woodcutters have been in our coastal groves again.
- Your sailors drink and brawl in our harbor towns, and sing badly while they do it.
- Speak, captain. The trees are listening, and they remember every axe your crews have swung.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair trade. Your ships have brought us something worth having.
- Keep your word as long as this bargain lasts, captain, and we will be content.
- It is done. A hard bargain, captain, but an honest one this time.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the sea. The forest thanks the waves.
- Perhaps the Lanun are not all salt and steel, after all.
- Our thanks. Perhaps you will spare our forests an axe or two in return.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms shift like a tide.
- We decline. Not one more tree for your shipyards.
- You know as well as we do that the scale is tipped, Lanun.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Take your fleets back to the open sea.
- Our trees need their roots more than your ships need masts.
- We accept, captain. Try to keep this promise until the next tide, at least.

#### Refuses peace
- Your shipwrights are still at work in our forest. So are our archers.
- No. You would break your word before the tide turned.
- The forest wants its trees back, and it will have them.

#### Rejects a demand
- Steal it if you can, pirate.
- No. The sea gives you plenty; you need nothing of ours.
- The forest pays no harbor fees, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp, heirs of the Open-Skiers. The ice crushed your golems as it crushed our groves. We understand loss.
- Children of Kilmorph. Your golems are marvels. Please keep them on the roads.
- Welcome back to the sun. Our people also waited out the winter in hiding, and came back changed.

#### Declares war
- Your golems trample our groves and do not even notice. We will make them notice.
- Your forges have been fed with our timber for the last time.
- Clay and iron cannot hear the forest's anger. Their makers will.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Golems feel nothing, and it seems their masters have learned from them.
- Go back to your forges. The forest has nothing to say to them, or to you.
- Not while your machines still march through our woods.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your artificers are marvels, Luchuirp. Our mages would love to study their work.
- It is good to see you, [CT_NAME]. How fare your people under the open sky?
- A golem that tends a garden would be a beautiful thing. Have you ever thought of building one for us?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems flattened a stand of young oaks. They did not even slow down.
- You see the forest as lumber and fuel. We see it as family.
- Leave your clockwork outside the grove, gnome, and then speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Finely made, like everything from your workshops. We accept.
- Your work is worth every coin, and more.
- It is done. Kilmorph and the forest would both approve, we think.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift wrought by Luchuirp hands. The forest is honored.
- Your generosity matches your skill, [CT_NAME].
- You honor us. We will set it among our trees, where it will be admired for centuries.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. This bargain has all the warmth of a cold forge.
- You undervalue everything that grows.
- The balance is off, artificer. Recalibrate it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let your golems till fields instead of trampling forests.
- We both nearly perished in the ice; we should not finish its work for it.
- Return to your workshops, and we to our groves. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while a single golem stands among our trees.
- No. The forest grows back and your golems do not. We can afford this war longer than you.
- The roots your golems tore up are still dying. Not yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Your golems can dig you more gold than we will ever give you.
- No. Not even a golem could carry away what we will not give.
- Ask your golems, [CT_NAME]. They never refuse anything.

### Ljosalfar → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim. Your hunters once found an elf freezing in the wastes and chose to tend the wounds rather than kill. The forest remembers kindness.
- Greetings, people of the sun. Before that day, the only elves you had ever seen were our dark cousins. We are not them.
- Welcome. The light of Lugus is harsh on the desert, but our trees drink it gladly.

#### Declares war
- Your zealots would burn our groves to let in more light. The forest has its own light.
- The desert spreads wherever your herds walk. We will not let it reach our trees.
- Even the sun scorches what it touches too long. Your touch has lasted long enough.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your truth is a glare, and today we prefer the shade.
- Go back to your sands. The forest is not listening.
- Your soldiers still camp beneath our oaks. Remove them, and then we may talk.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Elven hands raised your first shrine to Lugus, we hear. We are prouder of that than you might think.
- Your Empyrean judges fairly, [CT_NAME]. We respect that.
- The sun you worship warms our groves. Be welcome beneath them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars preach in our groves as if the trees needed converting.
- The desert is creeping toward our forest, and your herds are to blame.
- Speak, Malakim, and step out of the sun; the shade will cool your temper.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair judgment, as your Empyrean would want. We accept.
- May the sun shine on both our peoples, then.
- It is done. Your caravans bring us much we cannot grow.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the desert. You honor us.
- The light of Lugus shines kindly on us today.
- The forest is grateful, [CT_NAME], and it does not forget.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even the noon sun does not take so much.
- We decline. You would take an oasis and give back a cup.
- Your own judges would call this unbalanced.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let the sun and the forest live side by side again.
- Your oases and our groves both need water more than blood.
- We accept. Lugus loves the truth, and the truth is that neither of us wanted this.

#### Refuses peace
- The smoke of our groves still drifts toward your temples. Not yet.
- No. The sun has scorched us long enough; now it is your turn to wilt.
- Every shrine you raised on our burned ground must come down first.

#### Rejects a demand
- Your Empyrean gives small peoples an equal voice, and ours says no.
- No. Lugus loves the truth, so here it is: you will get nothing.
- Shine as brightly as you like, [CT_NAME]. We have stood in harsher light.

### Ljosalfar → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels of Arawn who would not lay down their swords at the Compact. The seven firs were born to witness that peace, and you broke it.
- You hunt demons wherever they walk, Mercurians. Our forests have a few for you.
- Our scouts took you for demons. Then they watched you kill one, and changed their minds.

#### Declares war
- You care nothing for mortals, or for elves. You trample our groves to reach your enemies. No more.
- Your war against hell has spilled into our forest. We will push it back out, and you with it.
- Even angels must answer to the forest when they burn it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You hear only the screams of hell; you will not hear us.
- Return to your hunt, angel. The forest will not speak with a hammer.
- Not while your hammers still splinter our trees.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Your war against the pit makes our forests safer. We are grateful, Mercurian.
- Our druids watched your soldiers burn the taint from our soil, [CT_NAME]. It was a beautiful thing.
- Rest beneath our trees a while, angel. Even you must tire.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your soldiers cut through our sacred groves on their way to the pit, and never once looked down.
- You look past us, angel, as if we were in your way. We are not.
- Do not tower over us while you speak, angel.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair trade. Spend it well against the pit.
- Every demon you slay is one fewer fire in our woods. Take it, and welcome.
- It is done, angel, and done fairly.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from an angel's hand. The forest bows its branches.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. The forest will remember that heaven's rebels were kind to it.
- Perhaps there is more mercy carved into your skin than we knew.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your war is holy, but our groves are not yours to spend on it.
- Even heaven's soldiers must pay the forest's price.
- Your scales tilt toward your own war, angel.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to the hunt that called you down from heaven.
- The seven firs stood witness to one peace; let this one hold as well.
- Strike at hell, and leave our trees standing. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Your hammers are still loose in our forest, angel. Call them back, then ask.
- No. Even angels must learn that the forest bites back.
- You broke one Compact already. Why should we trust you with a peace?

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute from the forest to heaven's rebels? No.
- No. Your war with the pit does not entitle you to our gold.
- Carve your demand into your arm with the other prayers, [CT_NAME]. The answer is still no.

### Ljosalfar → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. A corruption once crept through our forest, withering everything it touched. We wonder now whose spell it was.
- Greetings, gate-openers. You want creation to end. The forest has endured every age so far, and intends to endure yours.
- You gathered from every nation to end them all. We gathered in the last groves to survive. We are not alike.

#### Declares war
- Our crops wither and our trees sicken near your borders. The Summer Court will burn out the rot, and you.
- You open gates the world should keep shut. We will close them, and you with them.
- You long for the end of all things. Then begin with your own.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. What could we say to those who want everything we love to die?
- Go and gaze into your gates; perhaps something there wants to hear you. We do not.
- Not while your rituals poison our soil.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- While the world lasts, let us at least be civil, Sheaim.
- Our druids are watching you closely, [CT_NAME]. Do not take offense.
- The forest is still green, despite everything. Come and see it, and perhaps reconsider.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our trees are sickening in rings around your border. We know your magic when we see it.
- You look at our groves as if imagining them in ashes.
- Speak, if you must, but keep that hungry look away from our trees.

#### Accepts a deal
- We accept. Spend it on something that grows.
- Agreed, though we wonder what you could want with a future.
- It is done. A strange trade with a stranger people.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim. We will bury it in the earth for a season to draw out any curse, then thank you properly.
- Our thanks. Perhaps you do not hate the world quite as much as you claim.
- You honor us, [CT_NAME]. Every gift is a seed; we will see what this one grows into.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Our harvests will not be fuel for your Armageddon.
- We decline. A people who plan no tomorrow cannot pay what they owe.
- This offer smells of the void between the planes.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Close your gates, and let the forest heal the wounds they made.
- The seasons should turn a while longer. Let it end.
- We accept, though our druids will keep watch on every star.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your gates are wounds in the world, and we do not stop until wounds are closed.
- No. Each day of truce is a day for your rites to ripen.
- The world is our home. We make no peace with those who would burn it down.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute, to hasten the end? We would sooner plant the coin and watch it grow.
- No. Everything we own is something living, and you want it dead.
- Your apocalypse can pay for itself, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. We live long by nature; you bought your long lives with pieces of your souls. The trees find the bargain sad.
- Grey ones. You fade from the world just as we return to it.
- Welcome, shade. Our oldest trees remember when your people still had warm hands.

#### Declares war
- Your hidden cities sit in lands our forest needs. Fade, or be driven out.
- You traded away your souls. We will not let you trade away our groves as well.
- The forest abhors stillness, and you are stillness given form.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You feel nothing; why would you listen?
- Drift back to your hidden cities. Whatever you meant to say can wait a century.
- A people who traded away their hearts have no claim on ours.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- You have watched the ages pass as we have, Sidar. Few understand that weight.
- Your scholars and our sages should speak, [CT_NAME]; we have both seen a great deal.
- Rest beneath our trees, Grey one. You may not feel the shade, but it is offered all the same.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades drift through our groves at night and frighten the deer.
- You look at life as a passing curiosity. We do not.
- Speak, Sidar, and try to remember what it was to care.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair trade between two patient peoples.
- Long-lived nations should deal with one another kindly. Let it be so.
- It is done. Our sages will treasure what you send them.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Grey, who give so rarely. The forest is moved.
- Perhaps something of your hearts remains after all.
- You honor us, [CT_NAME]. The forest has long memories, and this will be among the fond ones.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You have centuries to improve it, and so do we.
- You have forgotten what things are worth to those who still feel.
- This offer is as thin as mist, Sidar.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Fade back into your hidden places; we will not go looking for you.
- Two peoples so old should know better than to bleed each other.
- May you find a little warmth in the years you have bought. We accept.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The deer still flee from your shades at dusk.
- No. You feel no pain, so you will not miss the peace. We can wait a little longer for it.
- The forest is patient, Sidar, and it does not fade.

#### Rejects a demand
- Gold cannot buy back what you sold, Grey one.
- No. You gave up desire with your souls; give up this demand as well.
- The forest gives its gifts to living things, [CT_NAME].

### Ljosalfar → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- So the Unseelie court survives. You declared Sucellus dead and punished those who kept faith. We kept faith, cousins.
- Greetings, kin of the Winter Court. The rite of spring was never performed. Did you ever intend to perform it?
- The Svartalfar. We shared the Tan'elyn once, half a year each. You kept it through the longest winter in history.

#### Declares war
- The civil war never ended, cousin. It only froze. Spring has come.
- You traded Sucellus for Esus and turned your blades on the faithful. The Summer Court answers at last.
- Every elf you killed for keeping the old faith is remembered. Today we come to collect the debt.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We have heard Unseelie words before; they end with a knife.
- Take your whispers back to Esus. The Summer Court is deaf to them.
- Not while your assassins lurk in our groves.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Cousin. It is strange to speak without the war between us. Let us try.
- We remember when our courts dined together, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps they will again.
- The seasons turned once, and the crown passed in peace. Perhaps they may turn so again.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your assassins were found in our groves with poisoned blades.
- You smile as the Winter Court always smiled, cousin, while measuring us for a shroud.
- Speak, Svartalfar, and do not name Esus a god in our hearing.

#### Accepts a deal
- So be it. It is a fair trade, cousin, whatever lies between us.
- We accept. Perhaps the courts can trade, if they cannot yet trust.
- We read it twice, for old times' sake. It is done.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Winter Court. We did not expect one this side of spring.
- Our thanks, cousin. We will not ask what it is hiding.
- Perhaps the old courtesy between our courts is not quite dead.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There is a thorn hidden in this, as there always is.
- We decline. The Winter Court never offered a fair bargain in all the years we shared a crown.
- This is not a balanced offer, cousin, and it never was going to be.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, cousin. Let this be the rite of spring that never came.
- Too many elves have died already, on both sides. Let it end.
- We accept. The forest has buried enough of its children.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while the faithful you murdered remain unavenged.
- No. You declared our god dead; we will not declare this war over.
- The winter you ruled lasted an age. Our war can last a little longer.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Unseelie? The rite of autumn gave you the crown, not our treasury.
- No. The Summer Court bows to no winter crown.
- You took the crown for one winter and kept it for an age, [CT_NAME]. You will take nothing more.

## Luchuirp

### Luchuirp → Amurites

#### First contact
- Children of Kylorin, is it? Half of old Patria ran on golems our forefathers built. We should compare notes, mage to artificer.
- We hear your archmages bend the laws of nature with a wave of the hand. We prefer laws that stay bent once the rivets are in.
- A whole nation run like a school of magic! Do your professors still feud over footnotes? Ours feud over gear ratios, which at least turn.

#### Declares war
- Your siege-mages tire, bleed and shiver in their camps. Our golems do none of those things. Shall we measure the difference?
- A spell is gone the moment it lands, Amurite. What we build keeps walking. We are coming for your academies.
- Kylorin's children, meet the heirs of the Open-Skiers. Our children are made of iron, and they are already on the road.

#### Refuses to talk
- Write your plea up as a thesis, [CT_NAME], and submit it to a committee. We may read it after the war.
- No. Your envoys smell of ozone and scheming, and the workshop doors stay shut.
- Talk? Your mages talk for a living. We have heard quite enough of it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend, and mind the cogs on the floor. Have your enchanters found a better way to bind a spirit to stone yet?
- Ah, [CT_NAME]! Come in. I have a rune here that refuses to behave, and an Amurite eye might see why.
- Hello again. Your scholars and our tinkers get on famously, so long as nobody asks who invented what.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Another archmage come to explain our own craft to us?
- You again. Your mages keep prodding our golems' runes like children poking an anthill. Speak, and quickly.
- If this is about your wizards' little observations of our foundries, the answer is still no.

#### Accepts a deal
- Fair enough. Even a school of wizards needs honest goods. Done.
- Agreed. Kindly read the instructions before anyone tries to enchant it.
- Done. Your headmasters may squabble over who gets it; that is your trouble, not mine.

#### Thanks for a gift
- For us? A scholar giving something away with no lecture attached! Thank you.
- Well! Kylorin's folk can be generous after all. Our forges thank you.
- Most kind. It will end up in the workshop, I expect; everything does.

#### Turns down a deal
- No, no. You are pricing this the way an archmage prices a favour, and we are not apprentices begging for a seat.
- That trade has more holes in it than a first-year's warding circle. Try again.
- We build things to last. Your offer would not last the afternoon.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go back to your lecture halls; we have golems to mend.
- Agreed, and gladly. Your fire scorched some of our finest work, and I would rather not watch it happen again.
- Very well. Let the schools teach and the forges hammer, and neither come calling on the other with an army.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? Your war-mages have not run out of fire yet, and our golems have not run out of patience.
- Not while your academies stand. A little longer, and we will see whose works outlast whose.
- You started this with spells. We will finish it with iron.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a school of magic? Do we look like first-year apprentices paying for lessons?
- Hah! Conjure it yourself, if your archmages are so very clever.
- No. And tell your headmasters that threatening a golem-maker is a poorly designed experiment.

### Luchuirp → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- So this is the court of masks. We have heard how your merrymen carry dwarves off like sacks of potatoes, singing as they go.
- A whole people that laughs at everything. Let us see how hard you laugh at a clockwork golem.
- Keep your harlequins and their dancing on your side of the border, and our hammers will stay on ours.

#### Declares war
- Your court once made a Luchuirp lord dive into a mud pit for a coin while the nobles applauded. The show is over. The golems are coming.
- Mindless golems guarded the Tower of Eyes once, and your madness slipped past them. Ours have been built with more care.
- No more riddles and no more rhymes. We march on Jubilee, and iron does not laugh.

#### Refuses to talk
- Talk with a Balseraph? Every word you say has a puppet string tied to it.
- We are done being your entertainment, [CT_NAME]. Go and juggle somewhere else.
- No. Your envoys smile too much, and their masks smile more.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- You are behaving, for once. Speak plainly, and keep your hands where my guards can see them.
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Peace with your court is a strange thing. I keep checking my pockets.
- Welcome, I suppose. Leave the harlequins outside; the golems do not understand jokes.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Ah, the clown court. Is this a visit, or another one of your games?
- What do you want? And if you start rhyming at me, this meeting is over.
- We have not forgotten your cages, nor your mud pits, nor your vipers. Say your piece.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done, and we read every line twice. Your court is fond of tricks folded into the wording.
- Agreed. If it turns out to be an illusion at sunset, we know where to send the golems.
- Fine. For once the masquerade offers something real.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Balseraphs? We will check it for snakes first. Then, yes, thank you.
- Hm. Thank you. Forgive me if I wait for the punchline.
- Generous. Suspiciously generous. Thank you all the same.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We have seen what your court calls a fair game, and one of ours played it from inside a cage.
- That is a trick with a ribbon tied round it. No.
- Sell your baubles to someone who has never met your freaks.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then, and the gates stay barred. We trust your word about as far as a golem can throw a harlequin.
- Very well. Take your jesters home. Next time the golems will not stop at your walls.
- Agreed. May your court find some amusement other than dwarves.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? You would love a little intermission before the next act. No.
- Not until your palace of masks is rubble and the applause has stopped.
- Our golems are only now finding the rhythm. Listen to them dance.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You have mistaken us for one of your puppets, [CT_NAME].
- Hee. No. Put on a better show if you want our gold, and even then, no.
- We have danced for your court once. Never again.

### Luchuirp → Bannor

#### First contact
- So you are the Bannor, all drill and discipline. You would like golems; they never question an order either.
- Every farm a castle, we hear. Fine work. Our masons would love to see your walls, if your priests permit it.
- Greetings from the Luchuirp, children of Kilmorph. Your Junil asks only obedience, they say. We ask only fair trade.

#### Declares war
- Your priests have added us to their list, have they? Then they can explain it to our golems.
- Your Orders are the best-drilled men in Erebus. Ours are drilled in iron and never tire. March out and see.
- We will not kneel to Junil, not for your Confessors and not for your crusade. Come and take our halls, if you can.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your priesthood has damned us. Let it undamn us first, and then we will talk.
- No. Crusaders do not negotiate, and today, neither do we.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Go and consult your codex; we have repairs to make.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hail, Bannor. Your garrisons keep the orcs busy, and every Luchuirp sleeps better for it.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Are your armourers still asking about our riveting? The offer to teach them stands.
- Come in. A people that turns every farm into a fortress understands good craftsmanship.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Another sermon? We have heard the Order's views on us. State your business.
- If you have come to tell us that Kilmorph is not enough, save your breath.
- The Bannor again. Do your Confessors know you are visiting heathens?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your quartermasters drive a hard bargain, but an honest one.
- Done. May it arm your conscripts well against the Clan.
- Fair and square. Even your priests could find no sin in it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Generous, for a garrison nation; I thought every coin went to the Orders.
- Very kind. Kilmorph remembers those who give freely, whatever god they serve.
- A gift and no sermon! Thank you, truly.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Obedience may come free in your empire. Our work does not.
- Your offer reads like a conscription order. We decline.
- No. Fine steel costs fine coin, crusade or no crusade.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Turn your Orders back toward the Clan of Embers, where they belong.
- Agreed. You fight well, Bannor, but you were fighting the wrong people.
- Done. Have your priests strike us off their list, and the golems will stand down.

#### Refuses peace
- You marched under Junil's banner to damn us. Now you can march home under our hammers. Not yet.
- Not yet. Your crusade broke our walls, and our golems mean to break yours first.
- Peace? Your Confessors would call it a pause. So do we.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Order? Kilmorph's children tithe to Kilmorph.
- No. Your free lands owe you soldiers. We owe you nothing.
- Take it up with your priesthood, [CT_NAME]. Nothing leaves our halls to feed your crusade.

### Luchuirp → Calabim

#### First contact
- Vampires. Well, our golems have no blood, so you will find them poor company at dinner.
- The Calabim, shepherds of human herds. We prefer servants made of stone; they need no frightening into obedience.
- Greetings. We know exactly what you are, and our doors are very thick.

#### Declares war
- Your herds will thank us. We are coming to smash the pens, and iron does not bleed.
- Try your Dark Gift on a golem, my lords of the Broods. We will wait.
- Enough. Your nobles feed on men; our golems will grind their manors into gravel.

#### Refuses to talk
- No, [CT_NAME]. Silver words from a vampire court are still vampire words.
- We do not treat with the Grand Broods. Go and drink something.
- No talks. Our golems feel no charm, and today neither do I.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Peace with the Calabim; who would have thought it. Keep your nobles out of our mines, all the same.
- Welcome. Not too close, please; my guards have their orders, and they are very literal.
- Greetings. Your cities buy good tools, I will grant you, though I would rather not ask what for.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do the bloodsuckers want now?
- You smell of cellars and old blood. Speak, and then go.
- Your Broods have been sniffing at our borders. Explain yourselves.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Pay in coin, mind, and not in bloodpets.
- Agreed. A clean trade, which is more than your herds ever get.
- Fine. This bargain bleeds neither of us, for once.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Calabim? Thank you. I will count my apprentices tonight.
- Thank you. I shall not ask where it came from, or from whom.
- Kind of you. Golems do not drink, but I will find a use for it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your people have a habit of taking a few drops more than agreed.
- We are not one of your herds, to be bled a little at a time. No.
- That offer is pale and cold, rather like your nobles. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go back to your manors and keep your thirst inside your own borders.
- Agreed. The golems will stand down. The doors stay bolted.
- Very well. You learned what everyone learns sooner or later: stone cannot be drained.

#### Refuses peace
- Not while a single pen stands in your lands. The iron keeps marching.
- Peace? You have had centuries to grow tired of war, and you never have. Neither have our golems.
- No. Immortal or not, you can be buried, and we are very good at digging.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Bleed someone else, [CT_NAME].
- No. The Luchuirp feed no lords but our own families.
- Go and ask your cattle. We are not on the menu.

### Luchuirp → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs. We smelled the envoy before we saw it. Keep your raiders off our roads and we will keep our golems off yours.
- So you are the Ember Banner. Fire does very little to a stone golem, except warm it.
- The Clan of Embers, who tear down what others build. You will find we build very sturdily.

#### Declares war
- Your raiders have burned their last Luchuirp village. The golems are marching on Braduk.
- Bring your axes and your sacred fires. Stone does not burn, and neither do we.
- Bhall fell from the heavens and you fell with her. Now you will learn how far down the mines go.

#### Refuses to talk
- Talk? Orcs talk with axes. So, today, do we.
- No. Go and throw something into Bhall's pit and see if she answers you.
- We have nothing to say to the Clan while your fires are still burning our fields.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Peace with orcs. My grandfather would never believe it.
- Welcome. Your warbands have kept clear of us, and I am grateful, and a little amazed.
- Greetings. If you are here to trade rather than raid, we can do business.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, orc? Our scouts keep finding your scorch marks.
- Speak quickly. The golems have been restless, in their way.
- Ember-folk. You stink of ash and broken promises.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. And it stays traded, not raided back next week.
- Agreed. Simple, honest, and nothing set on fire. I like it.
- Fine. Just do not break it over somebody's head.

#### Thanks for a gift
- For us? An orc giving instead of taking! Thank you.
- Well, well. Thank you. I shall not ask whose village it came from.
- Thanks. The golems approve, and they rarely approve of anything.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is the sort of bargain you make with an axe at your throat, and we see no axe.
- Not a chance. Goblin trinkets for dwarven steel? No.
- No. We will not arm your raiders for a handful of ash.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go home to Braduk and warm yourselves at your goddess's fire.
- Agreed. Our golems stop pounding your camps; your camps stop burning our farms.
- Fine. Peace. Just remember how hard stone hits.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Every scorched Luchuirp field wants an answer, and the golems are giving it.
- Peace? Your war-chiefs would break it before the ink was dry.
- Not yet. Bhall fell once. Her orcs can fall a little further.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Come and take it, orc. Mind the golems.
- No. We did not live through the Age of Ice to pay orcs for the right to breathe.
- Your warlords stole a holy scepter and bolted an axe to it. Steal from someone else.

### Luchuirp → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. You thrived in the very winter that nearly killed us. Forgive us if we are not delighted.
- Wolf-folk from the wastes. We are small, it is true, but we are not prey.
- So you are the pack that ran with the cold while our people hid beneath it. We learned different lessons, I think.

#### Declares war
- You leave your weak to die in the snow and call it strength. Let us see how strong you are against things that cannot freeze.
- Wolves hunt the slow and the small. Our golems are slow, but they are not small.
- The pack has sniffed around our halls long enough. Now it meets iron.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Wolves do not parley; they wait for you to stumble. We will not stumble.
- Howl at the moon, [CT_NAME]. We are not listening.
- Not now. Our golems are busy with your pack.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello, northman. The peace holds and our gates are still on their hinges. Good.
- Welcome. Your hunters bring fine furs, and we make fine blades. A fair match.
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Strange friends we make, the cave-dwellers and the wolves.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want, wolf? You have been circling our border like a pack around a lame deer.
- Speak, and then go back to your snow.
- The Doviello again. Have you come to trade, or to count our sentries?

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. A good hunt for both of us.
- Agreed. Our steel will serve your hunters better than teeth.
- Fine. A fair trade, and no blood spilled. Try it more often.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift, from you? Thank you. I did not think wolves shared the kill.
- Thank you. We will put it to good use, and not leave it lying in the snow.
- Gruff folk, generous after all. Our thanks.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would take the meat and leave us the bones.
- That deal feeds the pack and starves the stranger. No.
- No. We do not trade away the forge for a heap of pelts.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go home to your wastes; the thaw must vex you enough as it is.
- Agreed. Even wolves know when the prey bites back.
- Fine. The golems stand down. Keep your pack on its own side of the hills.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The pack chose this hunt. Now it can finish it.
- Peace? Not while your raiders still carry our people's tools on their belts.
- Not yet. We will leave your war-bands in the snow, the way you leave your weak.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. We are not a lame deer to be culled, wolf.
- Tribute? The pack eats what it kills. Come and kill it, if you can.
- No. We lived through Mulcarn's winter without your help, and we will live through your threats.

### Luchuirp → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim! Keepers of the old holy places. If any of your shrines need mending, our masons would be honoured.
- Well met. They say your monks fight without weapons. Our golems fight without fear. Different virtues, but virtues.
- Greetings, pilgrims. You kept the old knowledge alive through the ice in your chants. We kept ours alive in our workshops.

#### Declares war
- I regret this, truly I do. But your holy places will not shield your cities from iron.
- Peaceful folk, and yet you stand in our way. The golems march, and Kilmorph forgive us.
- You tend to the broken, Elohim. I am sorry to say you will have a great deal of tending to do.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now. Your monks could talk the hammer out of a smith's hand, and we need ours.
- No. Peace from your lips sounds sweet, and that is exactly why we cannot listen yet.
- Not today, [CT_NAME]. Pray to Sirona; we are busy.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend. How fare your shrines? Our masons still offer their hands.
- Ah, [CT_NAME]. A visit from the Elohim always reminds me there is decency left in Erebus.
- Hello! Come, sit. Your monks are welcome at our hearths any day of the year.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, Elohim? Have you come to scold us about our mines as well?
- You keep the holy sites; we keep our patience. Ours is wearing thin.
- Speak. Even pilgrims can wear out their welcome.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair trade with honest folk; my favourite kind.
- Done. May it serve your pilgrims well on the road.
- Gladly. Your word is worth more than most nations' gold.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, truly. Kindness was always the Elohim way.
- How generous. We will build something worthy of it.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. The Luchuirp will remember this.

#### Turns down a deal
- I am sorry, no. Generous souls make hard bargains without meaning to.
- No, friend. Even for the Elohim, that price is too steep.
- We cannot. Good craftsmanship costs what it costs.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, thank Kilmorph. This war never sat right with either of us.
- Agreed, and gladly. Go back to your shrines, and we will go back to our forges.
- Peace. Let your monks tend our wounded as well as yours; we will not turn them away.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your priests pray for peace, but our generals still have work to finish.
- Not now. I will not have holy words undo what our golems have won.
- No. A little longer, and then we can talk properly.

#### Rejects a demand
- No, friend. Not even for the folk who saw the Godslayer handed down.
- Tribute? From you, of all people? No.
- Charity is your calling, Elohim, not ours.

### Luchuirp → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori, who need no gods. Kilmorph pulled our people out from under the ice, so forgive us if we keep her.
- Adventurers, the lot of you! Any Grigori can become anything, we hear. We would love to see one become a tinker.
- Greetings. A people that leads itself; we respect that, so long as you respect our faith.

#### Declares war
- You turned your backs on the gods. We never turned ours on Kilmorph. Now we will see who stands.
- Your adventurers can grow into anything, they say. Let us see one grow into a match for a golem.
- No god watches over the Grigori, by your own choosing. Then nothing will save your walls.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Lead yourselves to a better offer.
- Not today. Your heroes have cost us dearly.
- We have nothing to say, [CT_NAME]. Take your own advice; you always do.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Free folk and honest craft; let us do business.
- Hello! Do any of your adventurers want an apprenticeship? We have openings.
- Greetings, friend. Your independence is admirable, even if we prefer a goddess at our backs.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, Grigori? Another lecture on how little the gods care?
- Speak. And spare us your godless sermons.
- You again. Your wanderers have been poking about in our old ruins.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. No gods required, only honest goods.
- Agreed. Fair is fair, whatever a man believes.
- Fine. Self-made folk know the value of a well-made thing.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you! A gift with no prayers attached; that is a novelty.
- Kind of you. Kilmorph thanks you, even if you will not thank her.
- Thank you. Your adventurers will always find a warm welcome in our halls.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Independence is no excuse for a cheap offer.
- That is not a deal, it is an adventure, and we do not gamble.
- No. You will have to fend for yourselves on this one, as you prefer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go back to leading yourselves; we will go back to our workshops.
- Agreed. Your heroes fought well, and so did our iron.
- Done. Kilmorph wanted no part of this war, and your people never ask the gods for anything anyway.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your creed teaches you to stand alone. Stand alone against the golems a while longer.
- Not yet. Your heroes have one more lesson to learn.
- Peace? When your adventurers stop looting our ruins.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You believe in no gods; believe in this instead: no.
- No. Help yourselves, as you are always telling everyone to.
- Hah. Ask your Luonnotar to pray for it.

### Luchuirp → Hippus

#### First contact
- The horse lords. In old Patria our ancestors' golems ploughed the fields your horses once did. No hard feelings, we hope.
- The Hippus! We hear your companies fight for whoever pays. We pay well; remember that.
- Greetings, riders. Our legs are short, but our golems never tire. A fair race, someday.

#### Declares war
- Your riders once took dwarves in nets to sell to the clown court. That debt has come due.
- Horses tire, Hippus. Golems do not. Ride as fast as you like.
- No more raids on our roads. We are coming for your herds.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go and hire yourself a peace.
- Not a word, [CT_NAME]. You cannot outride what is coming.
- Talk? You would sell this treaty to the next bidder.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome! How fare the herds? Our smiths have a new horseshoe you will like.
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Your companies keep good order these days. We have noticed.
- Greetings, friend. Gold for steel, steel for gold; the oldest friendship there is.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have your riders found another dwarven caravan to rob?
- You again. Our border wardens are weary of chasing your raiders.
- Speak. And keep your horses away from the golems; they spook.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Fair coin for fair work.
- Agreed. Mercenaries understand contracts; that makes you good partners.
- Fine. A deal as solid as a good horseshoe.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Generosity from the steppes; I did not expect it.
- A gift? Kind of you. We will shoe a hundred of your horses for it someday.
- Thank you! Not every rider stops to give.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would charge us mercenary rates and pay us in hay.
- That price would make a raider blush. No.
- No. Our work is worth more than a quick ride past.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Take your riders home and race each other instead.
- Agreed. Our golems could never catch you, and you could never hurt them. A tedious war.
- Very well. Foreign gold is a better measure of a tribe's prowess than our dead, I am told.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You raided our roads, and now our golems stand on yours.
- Not yet. A few more of your camps, and you will ride home thinking.
- Peace? Someone paid you to start this. Let them pay you to end it.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. We do not pay riders to stop riding.
- Tribute? Your companies fight for gold. Earn it.
- No. Your raiders have taken enough from dwarves already.

### Luchuirp → Illians

#### First contact
- The Illians. Mulcarn's ice ground the empire of the Open-Skiers to dust while your White Hand ruled the cold. We remember.
- So the lost men of Letum Frigus are awake again. We spent one long winter under your god's ice. We will not spend another.
- Greetings, if that is what this is. Our golems froze solid in your winter. These ones are better made.

#### Declares war
- Your god buried the cities of Kradh-Ke-zun beneath tons of blue ice. We are here to bury his last servants.
- When the Illians wake, the world sleeps, they say. Not this time. The forges are hot.
- Mulcarn broke our empire. We will break his heirs.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Talk to the glaciers, [CT_NAME]. They listened to you once.
- We have nothing to say to Mulcarn's men. Nothing at all.
- Never, while the cold walks with your armies.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Peace with the Illians. I keep the forge fires high regardless.
- Welcome, I suppose. Our elders still shiver at your banners, but you have kept your word.
- Greetings. Strange times, when a Luchuirp and an Illian can talk without a war between them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want? Your winds are blowing too close to our halls.
- Speak, Illian. You have a cold way about you, and our patience is thin.
- You again. Every time you visit, the frost creeps a little further down our valleys.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Let it warm both our peoples, for once.
- Agreed. Strange, to see an Illian trade honestly.
- Fine. Our forges could use the work.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift? From the heirs of the winter? Thank you. I think.
- Thank you. Our grandfathers would never have believed this.
- Warmly received, which may surprise you. Thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Too cold an offer, even from you.
- That trade would leave us as poor as your god left us. No.
- No. We gave enough to the winter already.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your frozen mountain; we will keep our fires burning.
- Agreed. The golems will thaw out. We will see whether your hearts do.
- Very well. One Age of Ice was enough for everyone.

#### Refuses peace
- No. We waited under the ice for generations. We can wait for your surrender.
