- Not while a single Illian stands on soil that should be green.
- Peace with Mulcarn's men? When the glaciers melt in your own halls.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Your god already took everything the Open-Skiers had. No more.
- No. Not one ingot for the winter.
- Hah. Freeze, [CT_NAME]. Oh, but you already have.

### Luchuirp → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons. We have heard Mammon's whispers before, from a crystal dug out of our own mines. We threw it down a deep shaft.
- So hell has come up for air. Our golems have no souls to tempt, Infernal. Remember that.
- Keep your sulfur off our land and your promises out of our ears, and we will get along as well as stone and fire can.

#### Declares war
- Hell is a forge built to twist souls. Ours are built to make things that cannot be twisted. Let us see which works better.
- Back into the pit with you. The golems will see you all the way down.
- We have no wish to bargain with demons, and every wish to crush them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Every word from a demon has a price, and we are not buying.
- Talk? Go back to Agares and talk to him.
- Nothing, [CT_NAME]. Silence is the only safe answer to hell.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello. Peace with demons; Kilmorph forgive us. Keep it brief.
- Welcome, I suppose. My smiths keep their hammers close. No offence meant, and probably none taken.
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. We have kept our peace, you and I. Let us keep this simple too.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, demon? I could smell you from the gate.
- Speak and go. The forges are cleaner without you in them.
- Your whispers have been reaching our miners. Explain yourself before I stop listening.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done, and read twice, line by line. One learns how hell bargains.
- Agreed. No soul included in the price, I trust? Good.
- Fine. A plain trade. Do not make it into anything more.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from hell. I will have it inspected by someone braver than me. Thank you, I suppose.
- Hm. Thank you. I will keep it well away from the mines.
- Thank you. Forgive me if I do not touch it with my bare hands.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Demons always want a little more than the bargain says.
- That trade is a pretty crystal in the mud: lovely to look at, fatal to touch. No.
- No. We know how Mammon deals, and how his dealings end.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. Stay in your burnt lands and we will stay in our halls.
- Agreed. But the golems stay on the border, facing you.
- Very well. Hell can wait. It always does.

#### Refuses peace
- No peace with the pit. The golems keep walking until your gates are shut for good.
- Peace? You would use it to dig deeper into our world. No.
- Not while your cities stand on Erebus. Back to Agares with you.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not one coin for hell.
- Tribute to demons? Kilmorph would never let us hear the end of it.
- The pit gets nothing from the Luchuirp. Not now, not ever.

### Luchuirp → Khazad

#### First contact
- Cousins! The Khazad stayed below while we walked under open sky, and we paid for it in the Age of Ice. It is good to see you.
- Well met, Khazad. Kilmorph taught both our peoples to dig. We simply forgot for a while, until she taught us again.
- Greetings, cousins of the deep halls. And do not scowl at our golems; there is more craft in them than magic.

#### Declares war
- Cousins or not, you have hoarded long enough. Kilmorph will judge which of her children built better.
- Your gold will not stop a golem, Khazad. Your walls might, for a while.
- You never trusted our enchantments. Now you will learn you were right to fear them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No, cousin. Not until this is settled with hammers.
- Talk to me when you have counted your losses. Dwarves are good at counting.
- Not now. Go back under your mountain and think on what you did.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Cousin! Welcome! How fare the deep halls? Any new names carved in your Rune Hall?
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Come, share a mug. Kilmorph's children should never be strangers.
- Ah, Khazad! Our smiths have been arguing with yours again; it is the best part of the year.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, cousin? Here to grumble about our tricks again?
- Speak. And no grumbling about enchantments; every golem is honest work.
- You have been counting our gold through the wall again, haven't you?

#### Accepts a deal
- Done, cousin. Kilmorph smiles on a fair bargain.
- Agreed. Dwarf to dwarf, as it should be.
- Fine. I will even pretend you did not haggle me down.

#### Thanks for a gift
- For us? A Khazad giving gold away? Carve the day into the Rune Hall!
- Thank you, cousin. Kilmorph sees it, and so do we.
- Generous! I will carve your name on something handsome.

#### Turns down a deal
- No, cousin. I know Khazad accounting; I would lose a finger.
- No. You weighed that offer with a thumb on the scale.
- Hah! You have grown shrewd in your vaults. Not that shrewd.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, cousin. Kilmorph never wanted her children at each other's throats.
- Agreed. Let this end the way old dwarven feuds should, with a pillar of runes and an embrace.
- Peace. Let the runes record that this war was a mistake.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet, cousin. You started this, and we will finish it.
- No. Our golems are at your outer gates, and I will not call them back now.
- Peace? When you return what your raiders carried off.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute, between cousins? No. Not one ingot.
- Hah. Dig for it, Khazad. You are good at that.
- No. We earned every coin under the ice, while you slept through the winter.

### Luchuirp → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates! Centaurs, giants and men under one banner. Would any of your giants care to sit for a golem's likeness?
- Greetings. We hear your realm takes in anyone with something to offer. We have a great deal to offer.
- Well met. A few great cities, finely built, they say. I would dearly love to see them.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements sprawl into our hills like spilled oil. The golems will push them back.
- Centaurs are quick and giants are strong. Golems are tireless and fearless, which counts for more.
- You hide in a hard shell when war comes, Kuriotate. We have built a great many hammers.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Pull back into your shell; we will be knocking.
- Not today. Your centaurs have done us enough harm.
- No talks. Your royal court can wait, like everyone else.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome! What do your lamia mages make of our runework? I would value their opinion.
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Your cities are marvels. Ours are rather good too, you will admit.
- Greetings, friend. If any giant wants honest work, send them our way.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Your settlements keep creeping closer to our hills.
- Speak. And tell your centaurs to stop racing our golems; it upsets the drivers.
- Your court's polite letters are wearing thin, Kuriotate.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Your great cities will put it to fine use.
- Agreed. A clean trade between civilized folk, of whatever shape.
- Fine. The royal treasury and the Luchuirp both come out ahead.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you! Your people are as generous as they are varied.
- A gift? Thank you. Our workshops will make something of it.
- Kind of you. We will send something back, built to last.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even your great cities cannot buy at those prices.
- That is a settlement's price for a city's goods. No.
- No, I am afraid. Fine craft is worth more than that.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Back into your great cities; we have golems to mend.
- Agreed. Your centaurs fought bravely. So did our iron.
- Peace. Your realm welcomes every kind of folk; perhaps someday a few Luchuirp too.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your heartland is close now, and the golems want to see it.
- Not yet. You would only retreat, regroup and come back. Better we finish it.
- Peace? A royal decree cannot stop iron.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not every people bows to your crown.
- Tribute? We are not one of your client states.
- No. Collect taxes from your own settlements.

### Luchuirp → Lanun

#### First contact
- Sea-folk! We have no love for water; golems sink. But we do love trade.
- The Lanun, where every captain is a law unto himself. How do you ever get anything built?
- Greetings, sailors. Keep your hands off our cargo and we will get along famously.

#### Declares war
- Your captains have plundered our ships for the last time. Golems cannot swim, but they walk along the bottom well enough.
- Your ports are built on land, pirate. That is where we fight.
- Enough raiding. The golems are marching on your harbours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A Lanun's word drifts like seaweed.
- Talk? Sail off, [CT_NAME].
- Not now. You would sell our peace to the next ship that passed.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello, captain! What have your ships brought from the far coasts this time?
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your traders keep our workshops full of strange metals.
- Hello, friend. We will keep building, and you keep shipping.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, pirate? More cargo gone missing on your seas?
- Speak. And keep your fingers out of my pockets while you do.
- You again. Your captains have been inspecting our merchant ships rather closely.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. And I will have it in writing, from every captain involved.
- Agreed. A fair trade, even by sea-folk's reckoning.
- Fine. Mind you deliver it, and not to somebody else.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Lanun! I will find out whose ship it fell off later. Thank you.
- Thank you. Generous, for a pirate.
- The sea has been good to us today. Our thanks.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a pirate's price.
- No deal. I would sooner trust the tide.
- No. Your offer is as leaky as an old galley.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to sea with you; we will stay on dry land.
- Agreed. Golems and ships never mixed well anyway.
- Done. May Danalin answer your prayers again someday.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your harbours are close now, and the golems want a look at them.
- Not yet. You would only sail away and come back next spring.
- Peace? Your captains keep no promises. Why should we?

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Plunder someone else.
- Tribute? Raid a merchant if you want gold.
- Hah. Come ashore and take it.

### Luchuirp → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The Ljosalfar. Your forests are lovely; we will try not to cut down too many of them.
- Greetings, elves. The Age of Ice nearly ended both our peoples. You came back from your hidden groves, and we came back from under the ice.
- Well met, Summer Court. Your trees grow slowly, our golems work quickly. We should talk.

#### Declares war
- Your forests cannot stop iron. The golems are coming.
- Your Fellowship kills folk for cutting a sacred tree. We need a great deal of wood, and we are done asking.
- Hide in your groves, elves. Golems do not get lost in the woods.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your songs will not work on us.
- Not now. Our foundries have work to do.
- No talks, [CT_NAME]. Go back to your groves and think.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. How fare your groves? We have kept our charcoal-burners well clear of them.
- Hello! Your archers are a marvel. Our golems are too, in a less graceful way.
- Greetings, friend. Wood and stone, the best of partners.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, elf? Complaints about our smoke again?
- Speak. And no lectures about the trees.
- Your rangers glare at our woodcutters from the branches. Let us have it out.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Fine work from fine folk.
- Agreed. And no trees were harmed, I promise.
- Fine. Elven goods for dwarven goods; a fair trade.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Elven gifts are always beautiful.
- How kind. We will set it somewhere sunlit, where it belongs.
- Thank you, friend. The forest has been good to us today.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Elves think in centuries, and I cannot wait that long for payment.
- No. Too much leaf, not enough gold.
- No. Even the Summer Court must pay a fair price.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. We stop burning your woods, and you stop shooting our miners.
- Agreed. Your groves deserved better than this war.
- Done. Let the trees grow back, and the forges cool.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The golems are not finished yet.
- Not yet. Your archers still nest in the trees above our roads.
- Peace? When your Fellowship stops killing our woodcutters.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not even for the Summer Court.
- Tribute? Grow it yourselves.
- No. Our halls are not your groves, to be harvested at will.

### Luchuirp → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim, children of the sun! Our people waited generations under the ice to walk beneath it again. We understand the devotion.
- Greetings from the Luchuirp. Desert folk, are you? Sand is murder on a golem's joints, but we would gladly visit.
- Well met. They say Lugus values wisdom over law. A good god for a trading partner.

#### Declares war
- Your sun will not melt iron, Malakim. The golems are marching across your sands.
- We have been content to share the light. Now you will learn what crawls up out of the mountain when provoked.
- Bring your Radiant Guard. Our golems do not squint.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not now. Let your sun set on this war first.
- No. Your priests speak of truth, but we will hear none of it while your armies stand on our land.
- Talk to the desert, [CT_NAME]. It answers about as often as we will.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, friend from the sands. Come in out of the light, if you can bear to.
- Hello, [CT_NAME]! Our smiths have made a sundial for your temples. Lugus would approve, we hope.
- Greetings. Your people are honest and your sun is warm. Two things we value highly.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to tell us we spend too long underground?
- Speak, Malakim. Your light is a little harsh today.
- You again. Your vicars have been preaching in our mining towns, and the miners are getting ideas.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Fair trade in the full light of day.
- Agreed. Lugus would call it just, I think.
- Fine. A good, plain bargain, with nothing hidden in the shade.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, friend. A warm gift from a warm land.
- How kind! We will put it somewhere the sun can reach it.
- Thank you. The Malakim are generous, and we will remember it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No, friend. Wisdom would see that this is not fair to us.
- I am sorry. Even under the sun, that price is too high.
- No. Our work is worth more than sand and good wishes.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. Let the sun shine on both our peoples again.
- Agreed. We will go back below the mountains and you back across your sands.
- Peace. This war cast a shadow over us both, and I am glad to see it lift.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. The golems have not reached your temples, and they mean to.
- No. Your light blinded you to what you were starting. Now see it through.
- Peace? When your armies leave our valleys, and not before.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Lugus teaches that the small have as much voice as the great. Hear ours: no.
- Tribute? Ask the sun for it.
- No, Malakim. The Luchuirp do not pay to stand in the light.

### Luchuirp → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels, here in Erebus. You came to fight hell; we found a piece of it once, in a crystal from our own mines. We know what you are up against.
- The Mercurians. Your soldiers are almost as tall as our golems, and nearly as talkative.
- Greetings. You defied the gods themselves to keep fighting demons. We respect stubbornness; we are dwarves.

#### Declares war
- You care nothing for mortal folk, angel. Then you will care nothing for what the golems do to your host.
- Your war with hell is your own affair. Our hills are ours. The golems are coming.
- Even angels bleed, we are told. Golems do not.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You have no patience for talk, and today neither do we.
- Not now. Go and fight a demon, if you need something to do.
- Nothing to say, [CT_NAME]. Our golems are saying it for us.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, angel. Any demons near our borders, you say the word and the golems will come.
- Hello, [CT_NAME]. Our foundries have made you new hammers. Heavy ones.
- Greetings. Your war is a just one, and the Luchuirp are glad to help where we can.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to accuse our miners of digging too close to hell?
- Speak, angel. And mind your tone; you are a guest in our halls.
- Your host keeps marching through our lands without so much as a by-your-leave. Why?

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. May it help you kill a great many demons.
- Agreed. Quickly done, as you like it.
- Fine. Our steel and your fury; a fine match.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from the hosts of heaven, or near enough. Most kind.
- Hm! I did not think angels gave gifts. Thank you.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. The golems will guard it well.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Holy war or not, we still need paying.
- I am sorry. Your crusade cannot be fought on our credit alone.
- No. You ask too much, as angels always do.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to fighting hell, where you belong.
- Agreed. We have no wish to quarrel with the enemies of demons.
- Peace, and good hunting below.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. You struck first and gave no reason; we will finish this.
- No. Your host trampled our farms. It can go home on foot.
- Peace? Ask again when the golems have finished.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not even angels get our gold for free.
- Tribute? Go and plunder hell.
- No. We will help you fight demons, gladly. We will not pay you for the privilege.

### Luchuirp → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. We build things to last forever, and you want everything to end. We will not get on.
- Gate-openers. We have spent long ages making Erebus a little better. Do not dare undo it.
- Greetings, I suppose. You will forgive us for keeping our runes to ourselves.

#### Declares war
- You want to end creation? Start with your own cities. The golems will help.
- We carve runes to make things live. Yours tear holes in the world. Time to close them.
- No more portals, no more summonings. The forges are lit and the golems are marching.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You would only tell us everything ends anyway.
- Talk? Go and stare into one of your planar gates.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. We have a world to save from you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello. Peace holds. Please, not another speech about the end of the world.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Strange to be at ease with you; I keep my hand near my hammer.
- Greetings. Your runecraft is impressive, I admit. Pity about what you use it for.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to tell us our golems will turn to dust in the end?
- Speak. And keep your hands away from my rune-stones.
- You again. Something has been scratching strange signs into our mine walls.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Use it to build something, for once.
- Agreed. Though why you want anything, if the world is ending, I cannot fathom.
- Fine. A fair trade, which is more than the apocalypse will offer.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift? From the Sheaim? Thank you. I will check it for runes.
- Thank you. Perhaps you are not quite so eager for the end after all.
- Hm. Thank you. Our foundries will make something lasting of it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Why pay for anything, if the world is ending? You first.
- No. We do not sell tools to people who want to break the world.
- That trade would hasten your apocalypse and empty our purses. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your gates, and keep them shut.
- Agreed. The world gets a little longer, then. Good.
- Very well. Your end of days can wait a while.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Not until your gates are smashed and your circles scrubbed.
- Peace? You do not want peace. You want the end of everything.
- Not yet. Our golems have more of your temples to take apart.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not one bolt for the end of the world.
- Tribute? Wait for the apocalypse; it will take everything anyway.
- Hah! You want our gold to buy demons with? No.

### Luchuirp → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. You traded part of your souls for long life. Our golems have no souls at all and last longer still.
- Greetings, grey ones. You are hard to see. Our golems may not notice you at all.
- Well met. You keep to your hidden cities and we to our mountain halls. We have that in common.

#### Declares war
- You have faded long enough, Sidar. Let us help you finish the job.
- Shadows cannot stop iron. The golems are marching on your hidden cities.
- You walk unseen through other folk's lands. Walk through ours again and see what happens.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Speak to the fog, [CT_NAME]; you are made of it.
- Not now. Fade away for a while.
- No talks. We cannot even tell where you end and the mist begins.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello, grey friend. You startled me; I did not see you come in.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. It is good to deal with folk who think in ages, as dwarves do.
- Greetings. Our golems do not age either. Perhaps that is why we get along.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, shade? Lurking in our halls again?
- Speak. And stop drifting about; it upsets my apprentices.
- You again. Our miners keep seeing grey shapes in the deep tunnels.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. A trade for the ages, as you like them.
- Agreed. Now, if you could be a little more solid when collecting it.
- Fine. Fair dealing, even from a shadow.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from the grey cities. How unexpected.
- How kind. I was not sure you still cared for things of this world.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. We will keep it somewhere well lit.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You have centuries to haggle; we do not.
- That offer is as thin as a shade. No.
- No. We trade in solid goods, and that is not solid.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your mists, and we will go back to our forges.
- Agreed. A war against shadows is a tiresome business.
- Very well. Fade in peace.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You chose to step into the light. Now stay there.
- Not yet. The golems have yet to find your hidden cities, and they are close.
- Peace? You could simply wait us out. We prefer to finish it now.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. You traded your souls; you will not trade for our gold.
- Tribute to ghosts? No.
- No. Go and haunt someone else.

### Luchuirp → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Svartalfar, the winter court. We have had enough winter for one age, thank you.
- Dark elves. Your court ruled in autumn and winter, they say. Ours is a people of the thaw.
- Greetings. We have heard how you treat your own kin. Do not expect warmth from us.

#### Declares war
- Your kind welcomed the long winter as a sign of your power. Our golems will show you a new season.
- You cast down your own god and hunted the elves who still prayed to Sucellus. You will find no mercy here either.
- No more knives in the dark. The golems do not sleep, and they do not trust.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Diplomacy with the Svartalfar ends with a knife in the back.
- Go and pay Esus for a miracle, [CT_NAME]. You will get nothing from us.
- Not now. We have seen your courtesy before.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Hello. Peace holds, and we have kept our backs to the wall. Out of habit.
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your court is elegant, I will grant you. Speak.
- Greetings. Our dealings have been honest so far. Let us keep them that way.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, dark elf? Another of your dances?
- Speak quickly. The golems do not like your perfume.
- You again. Our scouts keep finding your assassins in strange places.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. And our guards will count the coins.
- Agreed. Remarkably honest, for the winter court.
- Fine. No knives this time, I trust.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Svartalfar? Thank you. Now I worry.
- Thank you. We will check it for poison and then admire it.
- Unusual, but kind. Thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargains have more edges than a dagger.
- That offer is cold as midwinter. No.
- No. The Svartalfar always take more than they give.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to your dark woods, and stay there.
- Agreed. The golems will stand down. Our watch will not.
- Very well. Even winter ends eventually.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your winter is over, and we mean to prove it.
- Peace? Not while your assassins walk our halls.
- Not yet. The golems are only now warming up.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not even if you ask nicely, which you never do.
- Tribute? Take it from the Ljosalfar; you enjoy that.
- No. Winter took enough from us. You will take nothing.

## Malakim

### Malakim → Amurites

#### First contact
- Children of Kylorin, the sun shines on you. It was your archmage who walked into the ice, and after him came the Thaw. We of the desert have not forgotten.
- The Amurites, who love magic above good and evil. Lugus asks only that a thing be true. Let us see whether we can understand each other.
- Welcome, scholars. Our vicars study the light and yours study everything else. There is much we could teach one another.

#### Declares war
- You weigh every art by its power and never by its light. Your schools have studied the dark too long, and the dawn has come for them.
- Your archmages call necromancy a matter for permits and regulations. Lugus calls it a lie against life. We march.
- You cannot argue with the sun, Amurite, however learned your faculties. Your towers will burn in the noon light.

#### Refuses to talk
- Your words are clever, [CT_NAME], but clever is not true. We will not listen yet.
- No. Spells can make a voice sound honest. The sun is not so easily fooled.
- Our answer will come at dawn, and it will not come from a messenger.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Your scholars are welcome in our temples; the light hides nothing from those who seek it honestly.
- Welcome, friend. Has any of your archmages yet measured the warmth of the sun? Ours have tried, and given up in wonder.
- The sun rises on Kylorin's people today. What may the Malakim do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You come again, wrapped in your spells. Take them off, and speak plainly.
- What is it now? Some new experiment that went wrong across our border?
- The shadows lengthen when your envoys enter. Say what you came to say.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair exchange, openly offered. We accept.
- So be it. Even a school needs bread, and even a temple needs books.
- Agreed. May your archmages put it to good and honest use.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift freely given is a small sunrise.
- We are grateful, [CT_NAME]. Your scholars are kinder than their reputation.
- How generous. The Malakim will remember the Amurites in our dawn prayers.

#### Turns down a deal
- Forgive us; when we hold your offer up to the light, too much of it is shadow.
- No. Your bargain is clever, and cleverness is not the same as fairness.
- We must decline. Lugus asks us to weigh each case on its merits, and this one has too few.

#### Agrees to peace
- The war is over. Let your schools return to learning and our people to their prayers.
- Peace, gladly. The sun never wished to set on your towers.
- We accept. May your magic be turned once more toward the light.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your mages still call fire down on our people; the light must answer it.
- No. You offer peace with one hand and a spell in the other.
- The dawn is not yet over your towers. We will speak of peace when it is.

#### Rejects a demand
- You ask for what you have not earned. The sun shines on all, but it does not shine for you alone.
- No. Not every problem can be solved with a demand, scholar.
- Your scholars have studied many things, but they have not studied us. No.

### Malakim → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- A court of masks. Under our sun, faces are worn openly. We will see what yours look like in time.
- The Balseraphs. You laugh a great deal. We wonder what you are hiding beneath it.
- Welcome to the light, masked ones. We hope your eyes are not too sore.

#### Declares war
- Your court is built on illusions and puppet strings. The sun will burn them all away.
- You made slaves into jesters and men into puppets. The light of Lugus comes to cut the strings.
- No mask survives the noon. Your masquerade ends today.

#### Refuses to talk
- We will not hear a masked voice, [CT_NAME].
- No. You lie even when you speak the truth; we do not know how you manage it.
- Your harlequins can dance for someone else. We do not listen.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. We are glad of your friendship, though we would be gladder to see your face.
- Welcome. Your court is a strange place, but you have kept faith with us. Speak.
- The sun rises on Jubilee today. What is it you wish of us?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Ah. The masquerade arrives. What game is it this time?
- Every word you speak has a shadow behind it. Speak quickly, and let us see the shadow.
- Your puppets have been seen in our markets. Explain them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, and witnessed in daylight, so there is no mistaking it.
- We accept. We have read it twice; the sun reveals much.
- Sealed, then. Even a court of fools can strike an honest bargain.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. We will look at it in the sunlight to see what it truly is.
- A gift from the masked court. We are grateful, and we are watchful.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps there is more to your court than laughter.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That offer wears a mask, and we will not take it.
- We decline. The bargain sparkles too much to be honest.
- Not this. Hold it up to the sun yourself, and you will see why.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Take your masks home, and keep them there.
- We accept. Let your court laugh at something other than war.
- Let the fighting end. The sun forgives much, but it remembers.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your court still holds slaves and puppets, and the light is not finished.
- Not yet. Your promises are as false as your painted smiles.
- Peace? Take off your mask and ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand like a jester and expect to be paid like a king. No.
- Your tricks will not work here, [CT_NAME]. The sun shows them all.
- No. Find another audience for your performance.

### Malakim → Bannor

#### First contact
- The Bannor. Your Order values law; the Empyrean values wisdom. Let us hope the two can share a sunrise.
- Greetings, soldiers of Junil. You fought out of the darkness of hell itself. You will find our sun warm.
- Welcome. Your codex is long and our scriptures are short, but we both walk toward the light.

#### Declares war
- Your priesthood judges by its codex. We judge by the case, and in this case, you are wrong.
- Law without wisdom is a cage, Bannor. The light of Lugus will open it.
- You have damned too many who did not deserve it. The sun now judges you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your crusaders would not listen to us; we will not listen to you.
- Not yet, [CT_NAME]. Consult your codex, and we will consult our hearts.
- Obedience is your virtue, not ours. We will speak when we choose.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Your garrisons stand against the darkness and we are grateful.
- Welcome, Bannor. The light shines on both our banners today.
- Our vicars and your priests have argued all morning, and politely. What can we do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What is it, Bannor? Has your codex found a new law we have broken?
- Your Confessors preach in our cities without asking. Speak, and be brief.
- The sun is hot today, and so is our temper. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- A just and open trade. We accept.
- Agreed. May it help your Orders hold back the dark.
- Gladly. Law and wisdom can trade as equals.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. The Bannor are as generous as they are stern.
- You honour us, [CT_NAME]. May Junil and Lugus both smile on it.
- How kind. A gift given without command; that is rare among your people.

#### Turns down a deal
- We cannot accept. Weighed on its own merits, this bargain falls short.
- No. Not every just cause must be paid for by us.
- Forgive us. Your offer is lawful, but it is not wise.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let our faiths return to arguing, and our soldiers to resting.
- We accept. There is enough darkness in the world without our quarrel.
- Let it end. Go back to fighting the orcs; they deserve your zeal more than we do.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. Your crusade came uninvited; it must leave in the full light of day.
- No. Your priesthood has not yet admitted its error.
- Peace? The sun has not finished judging you.

#### Rejects a demand
- The Empyrean gives an equal voice to small and great alike. Our voice says no.
- No. Even the Order cannot command the sun.
- Your codex may permit such demands. Our wisdom does not.

### Malakim → Calabim

#### First contact
- The Calabim. The first of your kind made its second kill on an acolyte of Lugus named Lanthis. We remember his name.
- You hide from the sun and feed on men. We know what you are.
- Greetings, children of the night. Our lands are very bright. You will not be comfortable here.

#### Declares war
- For Lanthis, and for every herd you have bled, the sun is coming.
- Your nobles feed in the dark. We are bringing the dawn.
- Your manors are tombs with windows. We will open every shutter.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We do not speak with the drinkers of blood.
- Not while your herds are penned and bled.
- Ask the sun for a hearing, [CT_NAME], if your Broods dare stand in it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. We are at peace. Do not ask us to like it.
- Welcome, if you can bear the light. What do you want?
- Peace holds between us. Our vicars pray that some day your herds walk free.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The shadow enters our hall. What does it want this time?
- You smell of blood and cold stone. Say your piece.
- What is it now? Your Broods' hunters have been seen near our villages after dark.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Pay in gold, not in lives.
- We accept. Daylight is witness to it.
- Sealed. A clean bargain, which is more than your herds ever get.

#### Thanks for a gift
- We thank you, though we wonder whose blood bought it.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. We will give it to the poor, who need it more.
- Grateful we are, and watchful still.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargains always take more than they give.
- We decline. That offer is as cold as your skin.
- No. We do not trade with those who keep men as cattle.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. The sun withdraws, but it will rise again tomorrow.
- We accept. Keep to your shadows, and keep your herds alive.
- Then the fighting stops. Do not make us regret it.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your herds are not yet free.
- The dawn does not bargain with the night.
- Not yet. Lanthis is not yet avenged.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. We will not feed you, in any manner.
- Demand what you like. The sun gives nothing to the dark.
- Take your demands back to your crypts, and your thirst with them.

### Malakim → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- The Clan of Embers. Your fathers were devout men of many nations before Bhall fell. The sun remembers what you were.
- Children of Braduk. Your goddess was a light once, before Agares whispered to her. Ours never fell.
- Greetings, orcs. You live by fire. We live by the sun. Let us see which burns cleaner.

#### Declares war
- Bhall's fire turned to cruelty when she fell. The sun has come to put it out.
- Your raiders have burned enough of the world. The light comes to judge them.
- You throw captives into your sacred fires. Now face a fire you cannot feed.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words smell of smoke and ash.
- Not while your raiders burn our fields, [CT_NAME].
- We will speak when your fires are cold.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. You have kept the peace. The sun notices.
- Welcome. Your people were once just and merciful, before the fall. Perhaps they can be again.
- Peace holds between the sun and the ember. What do you need?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want, orc? The smoke of your raids still hangs over our border.
- Speak. Then return to your burning city.
- The Clan again. Have you come to threaten us, or merely to boast?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. An honest trade, without an axe at anyone's throat.
- We accept. Use it to build, not to burn.
- Done. Even the Clan can deal fairly, it seems.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from the Clan, freely given. We are surprised and pleased.
- We are grateful, [CT_NAME]. There is still some of Bhall's old goodness in your people.
- Thank you. The sun shines a little brighter on Braduk today.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. This deal is a raid with ink on it.
- We decline. It gives you everything and us ashes.
- Not this, orc. Bring us something honest.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go home to your fires, and keep them burning there.
- We accept. Let the ashes settle and the fields grow back.
- Let the swords rest. Perhaps your people will remember how to be good again.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your raids have not stopped, and neither will we.
- Not yet. The light must reach your burning city first.
- You burn villages and ask for peace in the same breath. No.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand tribute as raiders do. We are not a village to be burned.
- No. Take it from the ashes of your own lands.
- Our gold buys bread for the poor. It will not buy your favour.

### Malakim → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. Our hunters once crossed the frozen wastes too. We found mercy there; you found only the wolf.
- Wolves of the north. You abandon your weak, and we take in strangers. We are very different peoples.
- Greetings. The ice is melting and the sun is rising. Your age is ending, northman.

#### Declares war
- You left your weak to die in the snow. The sun will leave you nowhere to hide.
- The pack hunts the helpless. Now the light hunts the pack.
- You ran free in the heart of winter. Now meet the heart of summer.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Wolves do not parley; they circle.
- Your pack is still on our land, [CT_NAME]. Not now.
- Swear by Camulos all you like. We are not listening.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, northman. The sun shines even on the tundra now. What do you need?
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. You have kept faith with us, and we honour that.
- Peace holds, and the pack has kept to its own hunting grounds. Speak.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want, wolf? Your raiders have crossed our border again.
- Speak. And keep your teeth behind your lips.
- The pack prowls close today. What is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair hunt for both of us.
- We accept. May it feed your people through the next hard winter.
- Settled. Strength can bargain honestly too, it seems.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. We did not know wolves shared their kill.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. Kindness from the north is a rare thing.
- Thank you. May the sun warm your camps tonight.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would take the whole carcass and leave us the bones.
- We decline. That is a wolf's bargain: the strong eat, the rest go hungry.
- No. Bring us something we can honestly accept.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your hunting grounds; the sun will not follow you there.
- We accept. Even a wolf may learn to live in the light.
- It is done. Let your people find warmth now, not war.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The pack has not yet been driven back to the snow.
- Your raiders still carry our people off. How can there be peace?
- You offer peace the way a wolf shows its belly. We do not trust it.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. We are not some straggler left behind by the pack.
- Demand all you like. The sun does not fear wolves.
- Take it from the winter. It gave you everything else.

### Malakim → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim. You tended the broken while the gods made war; our hunters once carried a dying stranger in from the snow. We are kindred, I think.
- Greetings, keepers of the holy places. Wherever your seven firs stand witness, our sun will gladly shine.
- Welcome. Sirona taught wisdom and Lugus teaches truth. Your order and our temples should have much to say to each other.

#### Declares war
- It grieves us. But you guard the holy places as if the light belonged to you alone, and the sun belongs to everyone.
- Your monks carry no weapons. We are sorry that ours must; the truth sometimes demands it.
- Even the keepers of shrines may stand on the wrong side of the dawn. You do now, and we march.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not yet, [CT_NAME]. Your monks could talk a sandstorm into stillness, and we must not be stilled.
- Forgive us. Your words would soften us, and this war must first find its truth.
- Chant for us, as we pray for you. But we will not treat with you yet.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. How fare your shrines? Our vicars would gladly help you reclaim those lost to the ice.
- Welcome, friend. Your pilgrims are always welcome at our wells and in our temples.
- The sun rises gladly on the Elohim. What may we do for those who sheltered mankind through the Age of Dragons?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What is it, Elohim? Have you come to tell us our temple stands on one of your holy sites?
- Speak. Even the witnesses of the Compact can try a host's patience.
- You come with gentle words and stern eyes. Out with it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Between your order and our temples, a fair trade is the least we owe each other.
- We accept gladly. May it carry your pilgrims a little further down the road.
- Gladly done. Few nations bargain as honestly as the Elohim.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you, friend. The Elohim give as the sun gives, asking nothing back.
- We are grateful. We will share it with the poor, as your monks would.
- Thank you, [CT_NAME]. Your order comforted the dying in every age; today it comforts us.

#### Turns down a deal
- We are sorry, friend. Not even for the shrine-keepers can our treasury stretch so far.
- No. Your monks would weigh this bargain and find it wanting, and so do we.
- Forgive us. Kindness on one side does not make a trade fair on both.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, gladly. Sirona and Lugus never meant their children to fight.
- We accept with joy. Let our healers and your monks tend the wounded side by side.
- Let it be so. The sun shines on your shrines again, and on our hearts.

#### Refuses peace
- Not yet. It pains us, but our armies have not reached what they set out for.
- No. You will find us at the shrines when it is over, and not before.
- We cannot. Peace now would leave this war half understood, and the truth half seen.

#### Rejects a demand
- We give freely to those in need, but not to those who demand. You taught the world that, Elohim.
- No, friend. This is not the way your order was founded, and you know it.
- Charity cannot be commanded, not even by the heirs of Immanuel Logos.

### Malakim → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori, who turned from the gods. We will not hold that against you; truth is truth, whoever speaks it.
- Greetings. Your cities shelter any who wish to live their own lives. Ours once sheltered a stranger from the snow. We understand.
- Welcome. You say no god acting on Erebus deserves worship. Stand in our sun a while, and then decide.

#### Declares war
- You say the gods do not care for mortals. The sun is coming to show you otherwise.
- Your adventurers walk without faith. Let us see whether they walk without fear.
- You turned your back on the light. Now it turns its face on you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You trust only yourselves; then trust yourselves to bear this war a while longer.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Your heroes have spilled too much of our blood.
- Your creed refuses help from heaven. Do not expect a hearing from us yet.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. You do not worship the sun, but you are welcome under it.
- Welcome, friend. Your adventurers are always welcome at our wells.
- The sun shines on the godless as warmly as on the faithful. What can we do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to tell us our prayers rise to empty skies?
- Speak, Grigori, and spare us your sermon against the heavens.
- Your wanderers have been prying about in our temples. Explain them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Faith or no faith, a fair trade is a fair trade.
- We accept. Lugus honours honesty wherever it is found, even among those who ignore him.
- Settled. May it serve your free cities well.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Generosity needs no god, it seems.
- You are kind, [CT_NAME]. We will pray for you, whether you wish it or not.
- Thank you. Your people are kinder than your creed sounds.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You teach your people to rely on themselves. Rely on yourselves for a better offer.
- We decline. Weighed honestly, it serves you and not us.
- No. Perhaps one of your adventurers can find a more foolish partner.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Walk without the gods if you must, but walk away from war.
- We accept. Let your heroes rest; they have earned it.
- It is done. The sun forgives even those who never ask it to.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your adventurers still stand on our soil.
- Not yet. Your free cities chose this war freely; they can carry it a little longer.
- You ask nothing of heaven. Ask nothing of us either.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. You say men must stand on their own. Stand, then.
- Ask the Luonnotar's greater god for it. We owe you nothing.
- The light gives to those who seek it, not to those who demand it.

### Malakim → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus. Your riders charged down the warrior mages of Patria in Kylorin's day. The desert would welcome such horsemen.
- Greetings, horse lords. We hear your companies fight for whoever pays. The sun cannot be bought; we hope your word cannot either.
- Welcome. Your plains and our sands are both wide and open. There is room for us both under the sky.

#### Declares war
- Your companies have sold their swords to the shadow. Now they will face the sun.
- You measure honour in foreign gold. We measure it in truth, and you are found wanting.
- Ride hard, Hippus. Our deserts are long and our wells are guarded.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Whoever is paying you for this war may hear our answer on the battlefield.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. A mercenary's word lasts as long as the coin.
- We will speak when your riders leave our oases.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Your herds look well. The sun has been kind to the plains.
- Welcome, friend. Your companies served us honestly, and we have not forgotten.
- The sun shines on the horse lords today. What brings you to our hall?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Is someone paying you to stand here?
- Speak, rider. Your raiders have been watering their horses at our wells without asking.
- The Hippus again. Have you come to sell us a war, or to sell one against us?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. An honest contract, plainly written.
- We accept. Gold honestly earned is no shame.
- It is well. May your herds grow fat on it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from a people who usually ask payment; we are moved.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. Generosity becomes the horse lords.
- Thank you. May your horses never go lame.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a mercenary's price, and we are not hiring.
- We decline. This bargain gallops off in only one direction: yours.
- No. Even in the desert, water costs less than this.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Ride home, and let your companies find honest work.
- We accept. Your riders fought bravely, whatever their pay.
- Let the war end. Let your clans race one another instead of raiding us.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your riders still burn our villages for someone else's gold.
- Not yet. The contract you signed against us is not yet torn.
- Peace? Ask your paymaster first.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. You may sell your swords; you may not sell us your threats.
- Tribute? We are not a caravan to be raided.
- No. Gold is a poor measure of prowess, and a worse reason for a demand.

### Malakim → Illians

#### First contact
- The Illians. In the Shadowed Vale you once pulled the sun itself through the mist, and that light became the faith of the Malakim. Why do you now serve the winter?
- Greetings, men of Letum Frigus. Our people froze under Mulcarn's sky, and we have not forgotten whose god held the frost.
- So the White Hand rises again. The sun has returned, Illian, and it does not intend to leave.

#### Declares war
- You once broke the darkness of the Shadowed Vale with sunlight. Now you would bury the world in ice. The sun comes to take back what it lent you.
- When the Illians awake, the world sleeps, they say. Then let the dawn wake it.
- Mulcarn's age is over. Your glaciers will melt before our armies.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. The winter has nothing to say that the sun wishes to hear.
- Not while your frost lies on our fields, [CT_NAME].
- We will speak when your god's snow has turned to water.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Peace between the sun and the snow. Strange, and yet here we are.
- Welcome. You once brought light where there was none. Perhaps a little of it remains in you.
- The sun shines on your mountain today. We hope it is welcome there.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What does the winter want with us now?
- Speak, Illian. Your cold is creeping into our hall.
- Priests of the White Hand have been seen at our borders. Explain them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even the cold may trade fairly in the light.
- We accept, and we will watch the weather closely.
- So be it. A warm bargain, for once, from a cold people.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from Letum Frigus; we hardly know what to say.
- We are grateful, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps the thaw reaches even your halls.
- Thank you. It is warmer in our hands than we expected.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That bargain is as cold as your god.
- We decline. The winter takes; it does not give.
- No. Bring it back to us in high summer.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Keep your snows on your own mountain.
- We accept. May the sun soften what Mulcarn hardened.
- Then let it end, and let the ice between us melt.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your god's ice still grips our northern lands.
- Not yet. The dawn has not yet reached Letum Frigus.
- Peace with the winter? Not while the sun has strength.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. The sun pays no tribute to the snow.
- You demand like a god, Illian. You are not one yet.
- Nothing. Not a single coin for Mulcarn's cause.

### Malakim → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons, carving cities out of the dirt with your own claws. In all its ages, the sun has never shone on anything so foul.
- The Infernal. Light never reached Agares' pit. It reaches every corner of this world, and it will reach you.
- We know what you are: souls ground down in hell until cruelty became pleasure. We pity what you were. We will destroy what you are.

#### Declares war
- You dragged hell into the daylight. The daylight will drag it back down.
- Your Obsidian Gates will crack in the noon heat. The sun is marching.
- Agares sent you to make Erebus despair. Lugus sends us to make you burn.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Every word a demon speaks is a hook.
- Never, [CT_NAME]. Go and whisper to the Ashen Veil.
- Speak to the dark you came from. The light will not answer you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- We are at peace, and that is all you will have from us. Speak.
- Speak, [CT_NAME], and speak plainly. The sun is listening.
- Welcome, if that is the word. Your servants will wait outside, in the light.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Our hall stinks of sulfur. What do you want?
- Speak, demon, and touch nothing.
- Your Ashen Veil whispers in our villages. You will answer for every word.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, at noon and before witnesses, so nothing can be twisted.
- We accept, and our priests will read it again under the full sun.
- Sealed. And no soul is any part of the price.

#### Thanks for a gift
- We will take it, and leave it in the sun for a week before anyone touches it.
- Thank you. The priests will cleanse it, and then the poor may have it.
- A gift from hell. We will be watching for the hidden price.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Demons always ask more than the bargain says.
- We decline. Nothing that comes out of the pit is ever what it seems.
- No. This offer smells of brimstone.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. Keep to your burnt lands and out of our light.
- We accept. But the sun forgets nothing it has seen.
- It is done. Crawl back to your ashes.

#### Refuses peace
- No peace with hell, not now and not ever.
- No. The sun will not set on this war while a single demon walks Erebus.
- Not while your gates stand open.

#### Rejects a demand
- Nothing for hell. Not one grain of sand.
- No. The light does not kneel to the dark.
- Ask Agares. You will have nothing from us.

### Malakim → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad. You lived so deep beneath the mountains that you hardly noticed the winter. Come up; the sun is worth seeing.
- Greetings, dwarves. Outsiders cheated your forefathers with illusions, we hear. You will find no illusions under our sun.
- Welcome. Your gold glitters in the light almost as brightly as our sands.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults have grown fat while the poor went hungry. The sun is coming to open them.
- You hide in the dark beneath the mountain. We will bring the light down to you.
- Your walls are stout, Khazad, but sunlight finds every crack.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Count your losses in your deep halls; we will speak later.
- Your hammers have spoken enough for both of us. Not now.
- Go back underground. We will send for you when we are ready.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Your merchants are honest, which is more than can be said of most.
- Welcome, friend. Come up into the light a while; the deep halls will keep.
- The sun shines on your mountains today. What can we do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Your merchants have been weighing our gold with a heavy thumb.
- Speak, dwarf. And stop squinting at us as if we were some conjurer's trick.
- You again. Your envoys glare at our priests as though their prayers were illusions.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Plainly weighed and plainly paid.
- We accept. A dwarf's contract and the sun's witness; nothing could be firmer.
- Settled. Your coffers and ours both the fuller for it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift of dwarven gold? We hardly believe our eyes, and they are good eyes.
- How generous, [CT_NAME]. It shines beautifully in the light.
- Thank you. The Khazad are more generous than their legends.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You count very well, Khazad. So do we.
- We decline. That bargain favours the vault, not the temple.
- No. Held up to the light, it is plain how one-sided this is.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back beneath your mountain and leave the surface to the sun.
- We accept. Your walls held, and our faith held. Enough.
- Let it end here. May your halls be warm and your vaults full.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your armies still stand on our sands.
- Not yet. Your gold bought this war, and it cannot buy the peace.
- Peace? When your siege engines leave our walls.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Dig for it, dwarf.
- Your vaults are full enough. Nothing from us.
- Outsiders once cheated your people. Do not become what you hated.

### Malakim → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates! Centaurs, giants and men judged by merit alone. The Empyrean teaches the same.
- Greetings. Your realm grants asylum to the persecuted. Ours once took in a freezing stranger. We understand one another already.
- Welcome. A few great cities and a wide country of settlements, we hear. The sun shines on all of it.

#### Declares war
- Your realm is wide and loosely held. The sun will find every gap in it.
- You welcome every people, and yet you turned your armies on ours. The light will judge that.
- Retreat into your shell, Kuriotate. The sun is patient.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your court's decrees do not move the sun.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Your centaurs still ride across our lands.
- We will speak when your armies are home in their great cities.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Your lamia mages and our vicars had a wonderful argument yesterday.
- Welcome, friend. Your confederation lives what the Empyrean preaches.
- The sun shines on every race of your realm. What can we do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Your settlements are spreading into our deserts.
- Speak, Kuriotate. Your court's courtesy is wearing thin.
- You again. Your centaurs drink at our oases without asking.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Merit for merit, as your realm prefers.
- We accept. May it serve every one of your peoples.
- Gladly. Fair dealing with fair folk.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Your realm is generous to all, it seems.
- You honour us, [CT_NAME]. Your giants and centaurs will be in our prayers.
- A gift from many peoples to one. Thank you.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your realm is wide, but this offer is narrow.
- We decline. Weighed on its merits, it lacks a few.
- No. Even an enlightened realm must bargain fairly.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Your centaurs fought bravely; let them rest.
- We accept. The Empyrean and the Kuriotates were never meant to fight.
- Let the war end. Back to your great cities, with our blessing.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your settlements still hold our people.
- Your shell is not yet cracked. We will wait.
- Peace? The sun has not finished its judgement.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. The Empyrean gives an equal voice to the small and the great; even a great realm cannot command us.
- Demand it from your client states, not from us.
- No. Your realm shelters the poor. It does not get to make them.

### Malakim → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun. You sail by the stars; we cross the sands by the sun. Both of us know what it is to travel where others fear to go.
- Greetings, captains. We hear a Lanun's word drifts with the tide. Ours stands as firm as the noon.
- Welcome. We hear Danalin no longer answers you, and that stranger things rise from the depths instead. Our sun still answers us.

#### Declares war
- Your captains raid our coasts and sell our people to whoever pays. The sun has seen it all.
- The depths have darkened, and so have you. The light comes for your harbours.
- You keep no law but a captain's whim. We bring a sterner one.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A captain's promise is worth less than seawater.
- While your ships still prowl our shores, there is nothing to say.
- Sail away. We will send for you when the tide turns.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, captain. What news from the far islands?
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your traders bring spices to our markets, and we are glad of them.
- The sun shines on the sea as on the sand. What can we do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have your captains lost track of another of our ships?
- Speak, pirate. And keep your hands where we can see them.
- You again. Your Overlords' cultists have been preaching madness in our ports.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Written down, witnessed, and sealed in daylight.
- We accept. May fair winds carry it home.
- Sealed. An honest deal, even from the sea.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the waves! We will treasure it.
- How kind, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps not every captain is a rogue.
- Thank you. We will not ask which ship it came from.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a pirate's bargain.
- We decline. It would sink us faster than any reef.
- No. The tide of this deal flows only one way.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Back to the sea with you, and leave our coasts alone.
- We accept. May Danalin hear your prayers again.
- Let it be so. Let the waves carry trade instead of war.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your ships still burn our harbours.
- Not yet. A Lanun peace lasts until the next sail is sighted.
- Peace? Your captains would not even agree among themselves to keep it.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Raid someone else.
- Tribute? We are not one of your island ports to be plundered.
- Nothing, pirate. Not even a drop of fresh water.

### Malakim → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- The Ljosalfar! Before the light of Lugus came to us, the only elves our people had seen were the dark ones. It gladdens us to meet the fair.
- Greetings, Summer Court. You nearly perished in the Age of Ice, as our people did. Now the sun shines on both of us again.
- Welcome. Your forests are cool and green; our deserts are bright and hot. Between us, Erebus is well kept.

#### Declares war
- Even the fairest elves can turn from the light. Your groves will not hide you.
- We do not wish this. But your court has wronged us, and the sun will answer.
- Your forests cast long shadows. The noon will burn them away.

#### Refuses to talk
- Not yet, [CT_NAME]. Your songs are lovely, but we will not be sung to sleep.
- No. The court of summer has made war on us, and we will not hear it now.
- We will speak when your archers come down from the trees.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. The summer sun loves your forests as it loves our sands.
- Welcome, friend. How fare your groves? Our vicars pray they flourish.
- The sun shines on the Ljosalfar today. What brings you to our hall?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to lecture us about our wells and our woodcutters?
- Speak, elf. Your court's pride fills our hall.
- You again. Your rangers have been shadowing our caravans.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair trade between sun and leaf.
- We accept. May your forests flourish because of it.
- Gladly. Elven craft is worth every coin.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. Your gifts are always beautiful.
- The Summer Court is kind, [CT_NAME]. Our thanks.
- Thank you. We will plant it in the shade, where it will grow.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Elves bargain as if they had forever, and we do not.
- We decline. Your offer is pretty, but it is thin.
- No. Weighed honestly, it serves your groves and not our people.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Let the summer return between us.
- We accept, gladly. Elves and men should not fight while darker things are about.
- Let the arrows rest. Go back to your forests, with our blessing.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your archers still haunt our roads.
- Not yet. The court has not admitted its fault.
- Peace? Not while your rangers hold our wells.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not even for the Summer Court.
- You demand, elf. We do not give to demands.
- Nothing. Grow it yourselves.

### Malakim → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp! Your people waited under the ice for generations to walk beneath the sun again. Be welcome to it; it is warm here.
- Greetings, Open-Skiers. The sun has shone on many wonders, but never on anything quite like your golems.
- Welcome, children of Kilmorph. Our people too were saved in the Age of Ice by a hand from beyond, and we too keep faith with it.

#### Declares war
- Your golems neither feel the sun nor fear it. Your people do, and they will.
- You built wonders, Luchuirp, and then sent them against our people. The light will judge your craft.
- Even stone cracks in the desert heat, and iron grows too hot to touch. Our armies march at noon.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your golems speak loudly enough for you.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. The smoke of your foundries still hangs over our burned towns.
- Go back to your workshop and think on what your machines have done.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Your craftsmen built a fountain in our capital, and the children adore it.
- Welcome, friend. How fare your golems? Has the sand got into their joints again?
- The sun shines gladly on the Open-Skiers. What can the Malakim do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Your golems have been tramping across our fields.
- Speak, dwarf. And keep your machines out of our temples.
- You again. Your miners dig too close to our sacred springs.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Luchuirp craft is worth its price.
- We accept. Fine work deserves fair pay.
- Sealed. Golems for our fields, and prayers for their makers.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A work of art, like everything your people make.
- We are grateful, [CT_NAME]. Kilmorph's children have generous hands.
- Thank you. It will stand in our temple court, where the sun can find it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your golems are fine work, but not that fine.
- We decline. Even your craft has a fair price, and this is not it.
- No. This bargain is as heavy as a golem, and it all sits on our side.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your forges, and let your golems build instead of break.
- We accept. The Open-Skiers should stand under the sun, not against it.
- Let it end. Our people will rebuild, and perhaps yours will help.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems still stand on our sands.
- Not yet. Your iron is in our cities, and the light has not finished with it.
- Peace? When your machines leave our temples.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Kilmorph's children need not beg, and they should not demand.
- Tribute? Build it yourselves; you are very good at that.
- You waited generations under the ice without our help. You will manage without our gold.

### Malakim → Mercurians

#### First contact
- The Mercurians. Our faith came to us out of Arawn's domain, with the elves who fled it, and you defied Arawn's command. We are not so different.
- Greetings, angels of war. You carve your prayers into your own flesh. We sing ours to the sun at dawn.
- Welcome to Erebus. The Compact was meant to keep heaven's soldiers from this world, and yet here you stand. The sun shines on you all the same.

#### Declares war
- You broke the Compact to fight demons. You will not break the Malakim.
- You care nothing for mortals, angel. Then mortals will teach you to.
- Your host has trampled our people in its hunt for hell. The sun forbids it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You never cared to talk to mortals, and today we return the courtesy.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Go and find a demon to strike.
- We will speak when your host leaves our lands and returns to its true war.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Our priests pray daily for your war against the pit.
- Welcome. We are glad to have the hosts of heaven on the side of the light, whatever their manners.
- The sun shines on your host. What do you need of us for the war below?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to accuse us of sheltering demons?
- Speak, angel. Your patience is short, but so is ours today.
- Your soldiers have been rough with our people. Their size is no excuse.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. May it serve you in the war against hell.
- We accept. Quickly done, as you prefer it.
- So be it. Light and wrath, fighting the same darkness.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from an angel is a rare and holy thing.
- We are grateful, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps you care for mortals more than you admit.
- Thank you. We will turn it against the dark, as you would wish.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Holy war or not, the bargain must be fair.
- We decline. You ask too much, as the hosts of heaven always do.
- No. Your cause is just; your offer is not.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to fighting hell; we have no quarrel with that war.
- We accept. Light should not make war on light.
- Let it end. May Arawn forgive us both for this.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your host still burns our villages in its hunt for demons.
- Not yet. You struck first, angel, and you never said why.
- Peace? When you learn that the people you trample are the ones you fight for.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. We give to the poor, not to angels.
- Demand it of hell; it owes you far more than we do.
- Your war does not make our treasury yours. No.

### Malakim → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. You long for the end of the world; we greet each new dawn with a song. We will not understand each other.
- Greetings, gate-openers. The sun has risen on every day since creation began, and it will rise tomorrow too.
- Welcome. Your people came from every nation, gathered for one purpose. We pray you find a better one.

#### Declares war
- You would end creation. We will end your cult first.
- Every gate you open lets in a little more darkness. The sun comes to close them all.
- Your Armageddon will have to wait. The dawn is on the march.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You want only the end, and we want nothing you can offer.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Go and gaze into your gates.
- We do not speak with those who pray for nothingness.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. The world has not ended yet. Is that not a blessing?
- Welcome. Our peace holds and the sun still rises. Speak.
- The sun shines even on your cities. Perhaps it will change your minds about the end.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Another prophecy of doom?
- Speak, Sheaim, and open nothing while you are here.
- Your summoners have been seen near our temples, drawing strange runes. Explain them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Strange that you bargain at all, if all is ending.
- We accept. Use it to live a little, for once.
- Settled. Perhaps you hope for tomorrow after all.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from those who long for the end; we are touched.
- Our thanks, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps a little light has reached you.
- Thank you. We will use it to make tomorrow better, whatever you think of tomorrow.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Why bargain, if everything ends? You first.
- We decline. We do not trade with the apocalypse.
- No. This deal would hasten your doom and ours together.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go home, and keep your gates closed.
- We accept. The world lives a little longer, and so do you.
- Let it be so. Perhaps you will learn to love the dawn.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your gates still stand open.
- Not yet. Your summoners still walk our lands.
- Peace? You do not want peace; you want the end of everything.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not one coin for the end of the world.
- Ask the void you worship. It has nothing either.
- Your prophecies say we will lose everything anyway. Then why give it to you now?

### Malakim → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. You traded portions of your souls for long life. We hope the trade still pleases you.
- Greetings, grey ones. They say the light never glints in your eyes. Our sun will try its best.
- Welcome. You have walked unseen through many lands. In ours, the noon shows everything.

#### Declares war
- You have stood apart from the world for ages. Now the world comes to you.
- The sun burns away every fog. Your hidden cities will be found.
- You hate the undead, yet you cheat death yourselves. The light sees little difference.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words are as thin as mist.
- Go back to your grey cities, [CT_NAME]. We are not listening.
- We will speak when your shadows have left our lands.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. You are welcome in the light, if you can bear it.
- Welcome, friend. Sit in the sun a while; it may warm what is left.
- The sun shines on your hidden cities too, whether they wish it or not. What can we do for you?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, shade? Lurking in our halls again?
- Speak. And stand where the light can find you.
- Your grey watchers have been seen in our temples. Explain them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A solid bargain, even with a shade.
- We accept. May it bring some warmth to your grey cities.
- So be it. Fair dealing, even from the fog.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. A gift from the grey ones; we are moved.
- We are grateful, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps you are not so detached from the world after all.
- Thank you. We will set it in the sun, where you cannot follow.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. This offer is as thin as a shade.
- We decline. It fades the longer we look at it.
- No. Bring us something we can hold up to the light.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your mists, and we will go back to the sun.
- We accept. Go in peace, grey ones, and in the light, if you can.
- Let the war end. The sun will not chase you.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The sun has not finished burning away your fog.
- Your shadows still haunt our lands. No peace while they do.
- Peace? You hardly cared to make this war; you can hardly care to lose it.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Gold is a thing of this world, and you gave up your share of it.
- Immortality was your bargain. Do not come to us to pay for it.
- Nothing. The sun lends no warmth to those who traded it away.

### Malakim → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- The Svartalfar. Before Lugus came to our villages, yours were the only elves our people had ever seen. We have learned better since.
- Greetings, Winter Court. You ruled the cold half of the year. The sun rules all of it.
- Welcome. We hear you cast aside your own god and punished those who kept faith with Sucellus. The sun remembers such things.

#### Declares war
- You hunted your own kin for keeping faith. The light comes for you now.
- The Winter Court ruled while the world froze. Summer has come.
- Your knives work best in the dark. There will be no more dark.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words come with knives behind them.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Buy your miracles from Esus; we are not selling.
- We will speak when your assassins have left our cities.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Greetings, [CT_NAME]. Our peace holds. That surprises us both, I think.
- Welcome. The sun shines even on the Winter Court today.
- Speak, friend. We are listening and, forgive us, watching.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, dark elf? Another plot?
- Speak, and keep your hands where the light can reach them.
- Your assassins have been seen in our temples. Did you think the sun would not notice?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, in daylight, so there is no treachery.
- We accept. Surprising, from your court, but welcome.
- Sealed. Even the Winter Court can bargain fairly.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Thank you. We will check it for poison, and then we will treasure it.
- How kind, [CT_NAME]. Perhaps there is a little summer in you yet.
- Thank you. Unexpected, and kind.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargains have more edges than a dagger.
- We decline. It is as cold as your court.
- No. Hold it up to the light yourself, and you will see why.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your shadowed woods.
- We accept. Even the longest winter ends.
- Let it end. Let the sun shine on your forests too.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your winter is over, and we mean to prove it.
- Not yet. Your knives still find our people.
- Peace? Not while your court plots in the dark.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Not to the Winter Court.
- Pay Esus for it. That is how your miracles work, is it not?
- Nothing. The cold half of the year is over.

## Mercurians

### Mercurians → Amurites

#### First contact
- Mages. Kylorin once closed the portals and drove demons and elementals out of this world. See that his children do not open them again.
- Amurites. You study every branch of magic and forbid none of them. We will be watching which ones you study.
- We are here for the Infernal. Keep your circles clean of summonings and we will have no cause to visit them.

#### Declares war
- Two young mages once called a Balor into my camp to show me their cleverness. I gave them my answer. Here is yours.
- You regulate your necromancers instead of hanging them. That is not law. That is an invitation to hell.
- Your schools have trafficked with the pit long enough. The host is marching on them.

#### Refuses to talk
- I have heard enough clever words from mages, [CT_NAME].
- No. Your tongue is trained in persuasion. My hammer is not.
- Speak to me again when your summoners are in chains.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your battle-mages burned a nest of imps last season. That was well done. Speak.
- Amurite. Your schools have kept to clean magic so far. Be brief.
- You may speak. Your fire has been turned on the right enemy lately.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Mage. I smell sulfur on your envoys. Explain it, and quickly.
- My patience with your archmages ended some time ago. What do you want?
- Speak, and do not raise your hands while you do. I know what Amurite hands can call.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Put it toward war-magic that kills demons, not toward experiments.
- Agreed. Now go. Every hour spent bargaining is an hour hell spends arming.
- Acceptable. Your schools may yet prove useful.

#### Thanks for a gift
- So Kylorin's children remember whose war this is. Good.
- It will be spent against the pit. That is all the thanks you need.
- Some mages, it seems, have wisdom after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Haggle with your colleagues; I have a war to fight.
- You have not proven that your magic serves the light. No.
- Your offer is like your magic: clever, and of no use against a demon.

#### Agrees to peace
- Your schools are spared. Teach your students which doors stay shut.
- Peace. Turn your fire on the Infernal, where it should have been.
- Enough. Hell gains every day we waste on each other.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your summoners are still alive.
- Mercy is for the innocent, mage. Your libraries are not innocent.
- You opened the door. You do not get to close it with a treaty.

#### Rejects a demand
- You want tribute from the host of heaven? Conjure it.
- No. My soldiers need their steel more than your scholars need their stipends.
- I do not waste breath on mages who make demands. That one is your last.

### Mercurians → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- Balseraphs. Your court is crawling with summoned things: imps, djinn and worse. I have killed better for less.
- I came to fight demons, not to watch a circus. Keep your harlequins away from my soldiers.
- A mad court, built on the blood of slaves. Your fate is your own, until it touches hell. Then it is mine.

#### Declares war
- Your summoners have opened too many doors. I am here to close them, and your court with them.
- Laugh, Balseraph. Laugh while my host tears down your masquerade.
- Your puppets cast spells for their masters, and your masters cast spells for hell. Both will burn.

#### Refuses to talk
- I do not trade words with jesters.
- No. Every sentence you speak is a riddle, and I have no time for riddles.
- Do I look amused, [CT_NAME]?

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. You have kept your summoners leashed. For now, that is enough. Speak.
- You may speak. Keep it plain, and keep it short.
- Balseraph. Your harlequins fought imps at my side last season. I have not forgotten. What do you want?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Another of your games?
- If you rhyme at me, this audience is over.
- My patience is razor thin with your court. Your summoned creatures are testing it.

#### Accepts a deal
