- Done. If there is a trick in the wording, my hammer will find it.
- Agreed. Do not make me regret it; that is a game you will lose.
- Acceptable. Now take your masks and go.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The masquerade gives a gift. It will be spent on the war, whatever joke you meant by it.
- Accepted. I will not ask what it cost your slaves.
- So even a mad court can be wise once.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your court serves nothing but its own amusement.
- I do not buy from people who sell souls.
- Your bargain dances like a harlequin. I do not trust things that dance.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Send your summoned things back where they came from, and your court may live.
- Peace. Laugh quietly.
- Enough. There are worse things than you in this world, and I am needed against them.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your summoners still breathe.
- No mercy for a court that buys its power with the blood of slaves.
- The show is over, Balseraph. There is no encore.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute, for a jester? No.
- No. Look for a fool elsewhere; this tent has none to spare.
- You demand gold from the host of heaven? Your madness is worse than I was told.

### Mercurians → Bannor

#### First contact
- Bannor. Your fathers were dragged into hell when Bhall fell, and an angel led them out. You know what we fight.
- Junil's servants keep the Compact behind palace walls. We broke it, and we fight in the open. Remember the difference.
- Soldiers of the Order. Your discipline is good. Turn it on the Infernal and we will get along.

#### Declares war
- You fight chaos with codexes and Confessors. Hell does not read codexes. Stand aside or be crushed.
- Your priesthood decides who is damned. Today, I decide.
- The Order demands obedience. So do I. You chose wrong.

#### Refuses to talk
- I do not negotiate with crusaders who have lost their way.
- No. Your priests talk enough for every nation in Erebus.
- Go back to your Halls, [CT_NAME]. We will speak when your Orders kneel.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your Orders held the line against the demons. That is the only thing I respect. Speak.
- Bannor. You fight well and you fight the right enemy. What do you need?
- Speak. Your crusaders have earned my ear, if not my patience.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have your priests decided I am a heretic?
- Speak. And spare me the sermon.
- Your Confessors have been preaching to my soldiers. That stops today.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. May it arm your Orders against the pit.
- Agreed. Your quartermasters bargain like soldiers. Good.
- Acceptable. Now get back to your war.

#### Thanks for a gift
- It will be spent on the war. The Order understands that.
- Good. Some of you remember where you came from.
- The Order trains its givers as well as its soldiers, it seems. Accepted.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer serves the Order, not the war.
- You have not proven your devotion to our cause. Your priests' approval does not count.
- Your priests wrote this offer, not your soldiers. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Your Orders are needed against the demons, not against me.
- Go. Spend your soldiers' lives on the right enemy.
- Enough. We have wasted enough good soldiers on each other.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your crusade struck at me first. It will end when I say it ends.
- Your priests have damned too many innocents for me to spare their army.
- Not until your Orders stop calling my host a heresy.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Order? Junil can pay his own soldiers.
- No. I take no orders from priests, and no demands from their armies.
- You must not understand the severity of the times. My steel goes to the pit, not to you.

### Mercurians → Calabim

#### First contact
- Vampires. You are not demons, but you are close enough. Stay out of my way.
- Calabim. You keep men as cattle and call it nobility. I have seen hell's pens. Yours are not much different.
- I am here for the Infernal. Do not give me a reason to be here for you.

#### Declares war
- Your Broods feed on the living. My host feeds on nothing. We do not tire, and we do not stop.
- An abomination, the holy nations call you. They are right. I have come to finish what they could not.
- Your herds are going free. Your nobles are going into the ground.

#### Refuses to talk
- Things that drink blood do not get an audience.
- No. Your charm does not work on angels.
- Go back to your crypts, [CT_NAME].

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. We are at peace. Do not mistake that for approval.
- Speak, and keep your thirst to yourself.
- You have kept your Broods away from my soldiers. That is the only reason I am listening.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want, bloodsucker?
- I smell old blood in this tent. Say your piece.
- Your hunters have been feeding near my camps. Explain yourself before I stop listening.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Whatever you paid for it, I do not want to know.
- Agreed. Now go.
- Acceptable. Blood-money still buys swords.

#### Thanks for a gift
- I will spend it on the war, and pray it was not taken from your herds.
- Accepted. You have done one decent thing.
- An undying thing that gives instead of takes. I did not expect to see it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I do not deal in blood.
- Your bargains are as pale as your nobles.
- No. Your Broods serve nothing but their thirst.

#### Agrees to peace
- Your lives, such as they are, have been spared. Use them wisely.
- Peace. Keep your herds alive and your Broods out of my sight.
- Enough. The pit needs me more than your crypts do.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your herds are still in their pens.
- Your Broods have fed for centuries. Their reckoning will not take so long.
- Join your victims, Calabim.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to vampires? Bleed someone else.
- Demand it of your herds. I owe your Broods nothing but a grave.
- No. Not a coin, not a drop.

### Mercurians → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs. Your goddess fell to Agares' whispers, and you fell with her. I know whose work you are.
- The Clan of Embers. Your fathers were good men once. What hell made of them is my concern.
- I have no quarrel with you yet, orc. Do not give me one.

#### Declares war
- Your fires were lit by a fallen goddess. I put out fires.
- Braduk burns because Agares willed it. I will make it stop burning.
- Your sacred flame is a gift from the pit. The host will snuff it out.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your kind talks with axes. I prefer the hammer.
- Go and pray to Bhall. She will not answer either.
- Speak to me when your fires are cold, [CT_NAME].

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. You have kept your raiders away from my camps. Speak quickly.
- Orc. Your warbands killed imps last season. That was useful. What do you want?
- Speak. I do not have long.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want, orc?
- You smell of brimstone and ash. Too close to the enemy. Speak.
- Your raiders burned a village my soldiers were defending. Explain yourself.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Now go back to Braduk.
- Agreed. Do not break it over somebody's head.
- Acceptable. Keep your fires to your own lands.

#### Thanks for a gift
- An orc who gives. The war has made stranger allies.
- Accepted. It will be spent against the pit.
- Accepted. Your fathers were generous men before the fall. Something of them remains.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargain is a raid with a smile.
- No. Your Clan has never served anything but plunder.
- No. I do not arm those who burn villages.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, orc. Do not make me regret it.
- Peace. Turn your axes on the demons that made you.
- Enough. Agares would laugh to see us fight.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your sacred flame still burns.
- Orcs who throw captives into the fire do not get to ask for peace.
- Join your goddess in her fall.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to raiders? No.
- No. Bhall took enough from your people. You take nothing from me.
- Come and take it, orc. You will not like where it takes you.

### Mercurians → Doviello

#### First contact
- Doviello. You swear by Camulos. I have seen his hell, a proving ground where souls learn to love cruelty. Mind what you pray to.
- Wolves of the north. Your savagery may be your own, or it may be something older. I will find out which.
- You fight for strength alone. So do demons. Do not give me cause to confuse the two.

#### Declares war
- The pack has fed on the weak long enough. The host does not feed, and it does not tire.
- Whatever taint runs in your blood, I will bleed it out.
- Camulos trains his demons on souls like yours. I will leave him no more recruits.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Wolves do not get an audience.
- Howl, [CT_NAME]. I hear nothing.
- Come back with your pack's heads bowed, and I will consider it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your pack tore apart a swarm of imps on the tundra. Good. Speak.
- Northman. You fight hard and you fight demons. That is enough for me.
- Speak. Your warriors have earned that much.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What does the wolf want now?
- Your raiders struck my supply lines while I was fighting the pit. Explain that, if you can.
- Your patience and mine are both short, Doviello. Get to it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Use it to hunt demons instead of villages.
- Agreed. Brief, like a good hunt.
- Acceptable. Go back to your pack.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The pack shares its kill. Unexpected. It will go to the war.
- Accepted. You are less savage than your reputation.
- From the wastes, freely given. My soldiers will make use of it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You want the meat and would leave me the bones.
- Your offer is a wolf's offer: all teeth.
- No. Strength is not the same thing as worth.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Take your pack home and point it at the demons.
- Peace. You fought well, for beasts.
- Go. The pit is a better hunting ground than my camps.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The pack chose to hunt the host. Now the pack is hunted.
- You leave your weak to die. I leave nothing of my enemies at all.
- Not yet. Your war-god wants a long war. He will be disappointed by a short and final one.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? The strong take, you say. Try.
- No. Not to wolves.
- Your pack can starve before it eats from my table.

### Mercurians → Elohim

#### First contact
- Elohim. You stood witness when the Compact was signed and the Godslayer was handed to Finner. I stood against it. We will not agree on much.
- Keepers of the holy places. Keep them well. The Infernal will want them.
- You tend the wounded. I make more of them. Each of us has a task.

#### Declares war
- You have made treaties with demons before, Elohim. There is no peace with demons, and none for those who make it.
- Your shrines are sacred to you. My war is sacred to me. You stand in its way.
- I would spare your monks if they stood aside. They will not, will they?

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words are gentle, and gentleness has lost more wars than cowardice.
- Pray, if you like, [CT_NAME]. I do not negotiate.
- Not yet. Your monks can tend the wounded while they wait.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your monks tended my wounded without being asked. I have not forgotten. Speak.
- Elohim. You keep the holy sites out of the hands of the pit's servants. That is useful work. What is it?
- Speak. The keepers of the old shrines may have my ear for a moment.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Another sermon about the Compact?
- Your monks are lecturing my soldiers on mercy. Stop them, or I will.
- Your patience is famous, Elohim. Mine is not. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Your word is good; that is rare enough.
- Agreed. Put the rest toward guarding your shrines from the Infernal.
- Acceptable. Go back to your pilgrims.

#### Thanks for a gift
- It will go to the war. You would not approve, yet you gave it anyway.
- Accepted. Your order has always been generous, even to those it disagrees with.
- The Elohim give without asking. I do not pretend to understand it, but I accept.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Charity does not win wars, and neither does this offer.
- Your bargain is kind. Kindness is not what I need.
- No. Bring me something I can kill demons with.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Making war on monks is a waste of good steel.
- Enough. Guard your shrines. Hell will come for them, and I want them guarded.
- Go. Teach your people to fight demons, if you will teach them nothing else.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You will learn that some wars cannot be prayed away.
- Not until your armies stand down. Gentle words will not end this.
- Peace with you means a soft flank against the pit. Not yet.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand? Your order has forgotten itself.
- No. Your charity is your business. My steel is mine.
- Ask Sirona for it. I run no god's errands any longer.

### Mercurians → Grigori

#### First contact
- Grigori. Your founder counselled Dagda to sign the Compact and wished the gods gone from this world entirely. I would not sign it at all. Two rebels, opposite roads.
- A people who want no gods and no angels. You have an angel at your border now. Get used to it.
- Your heroes lead themselves, they tell me. Lead them against the Infernal and we will have no quarrel.

#### Declares war
- You think mortals can stand alone against hell. I have come to show you how wrong you are.
- Your creed says the gods' war has nothing to do with men. Tell that to the towns the demons burned.
- You turned your backs on heaven's war. Heaven's war has turned to face you.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You want nothing from heaven. You will get nothing from me.
- Your adventurers can find their own way to peace.
- I do not bargain with those who would abandon the field, [CT_NAME].

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your adventurers fight demons well, whatever they believe. Speak.
- Grigori. You keep free cities and you keep them strong. That is enough for me. What is it?
- Speak. You are godless, but you are not useless.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have you come to tell me the gods are not worth my blood?
- Speak, and spare me your philosophy.
- Your cities keep sheltering deserters from my host. That ends.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Your heroes will put it to better use than most.
- Agreed. Self-reliance has its uses.
- Acceptable. Keep your adventurers sharp; I may need them.

#### Thanks for a gift
- You want nothing from heaven, yet you give to its soldiers. I will not refuse it.
- Accepted. It will kill demons whether you believe in them or not.
- You give without being asked. Your creed taught you better than I thought.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Stand on your own, as you like to, and find another buyer.
- Your offer assumes I need you. I do not.
- No. Free men can make free offers elsewhere.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go and lead yourselves; lead yourselves away from me.
- Peace. Your adventurers fought well. Point them at the pit next time.
- Go. Two rebels against heaven at each other's throats is exactly what hell would want.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You chose to stand alone. Stand.
- Not yet. Your heroes are still in my way.
- When you understand that this war belongs to everyone, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute from heaven's soldiers to those who reject heaven? No.
- You want no help from above. You will get none.
- No. Go and ask the greater god your Luonnotar pray to.

### Mercurians → Hippus

#### First contact
- Hippus. Your riders hunted mages and helped drive the demons out when Patria fell. I could use horsemen like that again.
- Horse lords. You sell your swords, I hear. I am buying, if the target is hell.
- Your clans raid each other for sport. Find a better enemy. I can show you one.

#### Declares war
- Whoever paid you to cross me paid too little.
- Your companies took gold from the wrong side. The host has come to collect.
- Ride as fast as you like. My soldiers are patient, and hell is waiting for both of us.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go and find someone to pay for your peace.
- You will hear nothing from me until your companies are broken.
- I do not bargain with mercenaries in the middle of a battle, [CT_NAME].

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your riders cut down a demon column on the plains. Good. Speak.
- Horse lord. Your companies keep their contracts. That is more than most can say.
- Speak. Riders who fight demons have earned a hearing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Who is paying you this time?
- Your riders were seen escorting cultists. Explain it.
- My patience runs out faster than your horses. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Fair pay for fair fighting.
- Agreed. Now ride.
- Acceptable. Your gold will buy steel for the pit.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A mercenary who gives freely. The war has done stranger things.
- Accepted, and spent on the right enemy.
- Good. Your clans may yet be worth more than their price.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a mercenary's price, and I do not pay mercenary prices.
- Your offer is quick and slippery, like your raiders.
- No. Show me dead demons, and then we will talk about gold.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go and sell your swords to someone who fights the pit.
- Peace. Your riders are too useful to waste on me.
- Ride home. Next time, ask whom you are fighting before you take the coin.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your contract against me runs until I tear it up.
- Not yet. Someone paid you to fight me. I want to know who, and I want them to watch.
- You raid for sport. I do not fight for sport, and I do not stop halfway.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Earn it, as mercenaries do.
- No. Gold is a poor measure of anything that matters.
- I pay soldiers. I do not pay threats.

### Mercurians → Illians

#### First contact
- Illians. Your god broke the Compact and froze the world. I broke it too, to fight the pit. Do not imagine that makes us alike.
- The men of Letum Frigus. You would make yourself a god, I hear. I have seen what gods do. One more is not welcome.
- Mulcarn's priests. Your winter is over. Do not try to bring it back while I walk this world.

#### Declares war
- Your god broke the Compact for conquest. I broke it for war against hell. Only one of us was right.
- You would climb into godhood. I have thrown down things far nearer to it than you.
- When the Illians awake, the world sleeps. I do not sleep.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go and pray to your frozen god.
- I have nothing to say to the White Hand, [CT_NAME].
- Not while your frost lies on the fields.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your frost killed a demon host in the passes. That is the only warm thing I know of you. Speak.
- Illian. We are at peace. Do not ask for more.
- Speak. The cold has its uses against the pit.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What does the winter want now?
- Speak, Illian. Your ambition is showing.
- Priests of the White Hand have been seen near my camps. Explain them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Cold coin buys warm steel.
- Agreed. Go back to your mountain.
- Acceptable. Mulcarn's heirs can be useful after all.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Even the winter gives, it seems. It will be spent on the war.
- Accepted. You are less cold than your god.
- Unexpected. My soldiers will be warmer for it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That offer is as cold as your god.
- Your bargain serves your ascension. I do not.
- No. I will not fund a would-be god.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your ice, and keep your ambitions on your own mountain.
- Peace. Hell is the greater enemy, greater even than the winter.
- Your mountain is left standing. Do not make me climb it again.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your ambition must be broken before it grows.
- Not yet. The world has had enough of your winter.
- Mulcarn's breach killed more than any demon. His heirs get no peace from me.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to a would-be god? No.
- You are not divine yet. Offerings can wait.
- No. Freeze if you must, but not on my coin.

### Mercurians → Infernal

#### First contact
- So. The pit has crawled out into the daylight. Good. I no longer have to go down to find you.
- Infernal. I have spent ages in your hell, killing your kind in their own fires. Here, at least, the air is clean.
- You came to drag mortals into the pit. I came to drag you back into it. Let us not pretend this ends any other way.

#### Declares war
- This is the war I broke the Compact to fight. There is no declaration. There is only the hammer.
- Every Balor I have strangled howled as it died. You will howl too.
- I extinguish fire. You are made of nothing else.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Every word out of hell is a lie with teeth.
- I do not speak to demons. I end them.
- Talk? Go back to Agares and talk to him, while you still can.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. That we are not at war is an accident I intend to correct. Speak quickly.
- I hear you. Do not mistake that for anything more.
- Say what you came to say, demon. The truce will not outlast my patience.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The stench of brimstone fills my tent. What do you want?
- Speak, and pray to Agares that I let you finish.
- You dare open talks with me? My hammer is still wet with your kind.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Every coin of it will go to killing your servants.
- Agreed. And I will read every word of it in daylight, twice.
- Acceptable. Hell pays for its own destruction. Fitting.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from hell. It will be melted down and forged into weapons against you.
- I accept, and I will turn it on your armies.
- Whatever you hope to buy with this, you have not bought it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. There is no good deal to be made with demons.
- I do not bargain with the pit.
- Your offer reeks of sulfur. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- A pause, not a peace. Use it to count your dead.
- Enough, for now. My host needs rest before it finishes you.
- Peace? Call it a breath between blows.

#### Refuses peace
- No. There will be no peace while a single demon walks Erebus.
- Never. I did not defy the gods themselves to sign treaties with hell.
- Go back to the fire. I will follow you there.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to hell? I would sooner carve another prayer into my flesh.
- Not one coin. Not one soul.
- You make demands of me? I have strangled Balors for less.

### Mercurians → Khazad

#### First contact
- Khazad. You dig deep. Mammon's hell lies somewhere below; if you break into it, send word, and I will come.
- Dwarves. You distrust magic and summoners. So do I. That is a start.
- Your siege engines are the best in Erebus, they tell me. There are walls in hell that need breaking.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are full and your mines are deep, and neither will save you.
- You hoard gold while the world burns. The host has come to spend it.
- Your walls are stout, dwarf. I have broken stouter in hell.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Count your losses and come back.
- I do not haggle, [CT_NAME], least of all with dwarves.
- Go back under your mountain. I will find you there.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your engineers cracked a demon stronghold that had held against me. Speak.
- Dwarf. No illusions and no tricks in your halls. I value that.
- Speak. Your hammers are honest, and so, mostly, is your word.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have your miners dug up something they should have left buried?
- Speak, dwarf, and do not haggle.
- Your merchants sold steel to the Ashen Veil. Explain that, if you can.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Dwarven steel kills demons as well as any.
- Agreed. You drive a hard bargain. Good; so does hell.
- Acceptable. Have it delivered to my front lines.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Dwarven gold, freely given. I did not think I would see it.
- Accepted. It will become weapons, which you of all people will approve.
- Out of the deep halls and into the war. It will be spent where it matters.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I know how a dwarf counts.
- Your price is a peacetime price. There is no peacetime.
- No. Even dwarven gold is not worth that much of my time.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your halls, and dig carefully.
- Peace. Your walls held. Point your engines at hell next time.
- Go. Your siege craft is wasted on me.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your vaults paid for this war; they can pay for its end.
- Not yet. Your gates still stand.
- Peace? When your engines fall silent.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You are richer than I will ever be.
- No. Dig for it.
- Not a coin. Your vaults are full enough.

### Mercurians → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- Kuriotates. You take in anyone with something to offer. So do I. Offer me soldiers.
- Centaurs, giants, lamia. Your realm is crowded with strange folk. See that none of them trades with demons.
- Your borders are wide and loosely held. Hell probes for exactly such borders. Watch them.

#### Declares war
- Your borders are porous and your settlements thin. Hell found the gaps, and so have I.
- Your lamia wield powers I have not yet judged. The host has come to judge them.
- Retreat into your shell, Kuriotate. I have cracked harder shells than yours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your court can send its letters to someone else.
- I do not negotiate with confederations. Too many voices.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Your centaurs still stand in my path.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your centaurs rode down a demon warband. Well done. Speak.
- Kuriotate. Your realm shelters those who fled the Infernal. That has value. What is it?
- Speak. Your court is polite. Be brief as well.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Your settlements keep sheltering cultists.
- Speak, and spare me the courtly flourishes.
- Your lamia were seen near an Infernal gate. Explain it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Your many peoples will fight the better for it.
- Agreed. Merit for merit.
- Acceptable. Send your centaurs to the front.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Many peoples gave this. It will arm one cause.
- Accepted. Your realm understands what this war needs.
- Good. Your court is wiser than most.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer is as loose as your borders.
- That is a bargain for courtiers, and I am not one.
- No. Bring me something worth the time it costs.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Pull back into your great cities and guard them well.
- Peace. Your centaurs are better spent on demons.
- Go. Your confederation has bled enough for one war.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your shell is still whole, and I am not done with it.
- Not yet. Your settlements still shelter my enemies.
- When your lamia answer for their magic, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Collect it from your own settlements.
- No. Your royal treasury is deep enough.
- I owe your realm nothing but a warning: hell is coming.

### Mercurians → Lanun

#### First contact
- Lanun. Something answers your prayers from the deep now, and it is not Danalin. Mind what you let up onto the land.
- Sea captains. Your word is said to be fleeting. Mine is not. Remember that when we bargain.
- I fight demons, not pirates. Keep your ships out of my way and we will rarely meet.

#### Declares war
- Your Overlords' cultists drown men and raise them as thralls. That is the pit's work, whatever lies under the waves.
- Your ships carried cultists and summoners across the sea for gold. You will carry no more.
- Something rises from your depths that does not belong in this world. I am here to put it back.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. A captain's word drifts with the tide.
- Sail off, [CT_NAME]. I am not listening.
- Pirates get no parley from the host.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your ships ferried my soldiers when I needed them. Speak.
- Captain. You have kept your Drown away from my camps. What is it?
- Speak. Your fleets have their uses.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now, pirate?
- Your ships ran cargo to the Ashen Veil. Explain it.
- Speak, sailor, and keep your knives sheathed.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Deliver it to the front, not to the highest bidder.
- Agreed. Hold to it longer than a Lanun usually does.
- Acceptable. Now sail.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from a pirate. I will not ask whose it was.
- Accepted. Wherever it was taken from, it will be spent against the pit.
- A captain who gives. The sea is full of surprises.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a smuggler's price.
- Your offer is as slippery as your decks.
- No. I do not buy what was stolen.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to sea, and keep your Drown in the deep.
- Peace. Your fleets are better used ferrying soldiers to the front.
- Go. Danalin may hear you again, if you stop listening to what replaced him.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your Overlords' thralls still walk the shore.
- Not yet. Your harbours still shelter cultists.
- A Lanun peace lasts until the next tide. I will wait for a better one.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Plunder someone else.
- No. Pirates get nothing from me but steel.
- Come ashore and take it, captain.

### Mercurians → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- Ljosalfar. Demons have set your forests burning before. They will again. When they do, I will be there.
- Elves of the summer court. You lived through the death of your god. I turned my back on mine. We both know what is lost when heaven fails.
- Your archers are good and your groves are vulnerable. Fire is the pit's favourite weapon.

#### Declares war
- Your Fellowship kills men for cutting a tree and does nothing while demons walk. Your priorities offend me.
- Hide in your forests, elves. The host does not tire of searching.
- Your court has chosen the wrong side of this war. I will not wait for spring to correct it.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your songs are wasted on me.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Come down from the trees, and then we may talk.
- I do not negotiate with archers in the branches.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your archers stood with my soldiers against a Balor. Speak.
- Elf. Your forests have stayed clean of the pit. Keep them so. What is it?
- Speak. The summer court has earned that much.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Complaints about my soldiers cutting firewood?
- Speak, elf, and spare me the poetry.
- Your rangers shadow my columns. Explain it.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Elven bows kill demons.
- Agreed. Your groves will be the safer for it.
- Acceptable. Go back to your forests.

#### Thanks for a gift
- An elven gift: beautiful, and useful. It will go to the war.
- Accepted. The summer court is wiser than I was told.
- Good. Your groves will be guarded the better for it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Elves bargain as though there were all the time in the world. There is not.
- Your offer is graceful and useless.
- No. Hell will not wait for your court to make up its mind.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Guard your forests; the pit loves to burn them.
- Peace. Your archers are better aimed at demons.
- Go. The trees have suffered enough.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your court has not yet answered for its choices.
- Not yet. Your archers still nest above my roads.
- When your forests are clean of my enemies, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Grow it.
- No. The summer court can feed itself.
- I give nothing to those who hide from the war.

### Mercurians → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- Luchuirp. Your golems have no souls for hell to whisper to. I envy you that.
- Your mines once brought up a crystal full of Mammon's whispers. Dig carefully, dwarf. Hell is closer below than you think.
- Golem-makers. Build me soldiers that neither fear nor tire, and we will get along.

#### Declares war
- Your golems are fine work. They will make fine rubble.
- You build tireless things. My host is tireless too, and it has marched through hell.
- Kilmorph's children have sheltered the wrong guests. I have come to evict them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back to your workshop.
- Hiding behind iron and asking for talks? No.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Your golems are still standing.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your golems held a pass against a demon horde without flinching. Speak.
- Dwarf. Your foundries arm half my host. What do you need?
- Speak. Kilmorph's children have been useful allies.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? More complaints about my soldiers in your tunnels?
- Speak, dwarf, and be brief. I have no time for long explanations of gearwork.
- Your miners keep digging toward things that should stay buried. I want it stopped.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Build me more of those golems.
- Agreed. Fine craftsmanship. It will be put to hard use.
- Acceptable. Deliver it to the front.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Forge-work, freely given. It will be broken on demon skulls, as it deserves.
- Accepted. Your craft does you credit.
- Good. Kilmorph's children understand what this war requires.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your workmanship is fine, but your price is finer.
- Ornaments do not kill demons. No.
- No. Bring me golems, not bargains.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Your golems are wasted on me. Send them against the pit.
- Peace. Go back to your forges and keep them hot.
- Go. Kilmorph would not thank either of us for this war.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your golems still stand in my way.
- Not yet. Iron can be broken, and I have not finished breaking it.
- When your foundries are cold, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Build it.
- No. Your forges can make whatever you need.
- I owe dwarves nothing but steel, and they make their own.

### Mercurians → Malakim

#### First contact
- Malakim. Your faith in Lugus came out of Arawn's domain, with the elves who fled it. I served Arawn once, and I left him too. We are both deserters, of a kind.
- People of the sun. Your light is welcome against the pit. Keep it burning.
- Desert folk. You took in a stranger from the snow, and gained a god by it. I hope you choose your guests as wisely now.

#### Declares war
- Your light is bright, but it is not a weapon. Mine is.
- Truth, your priests say. Here is one: you stood in my way.
- The sun cannot save you from a host that has marched through hell.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your vicars talk too much already.
- Not now, [CT_NAME]. Light has no need to speak.
- I do not bargain with those who shield my enemies.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your Radiant Guard stood beside my host and did not break. Speak.
- Malakim. Your light burns demons nearly as well as my hammer. What is it?
- Speak. The children of the sun have earned my ear.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Has your sun shown you something it did not like?
- Speak, and spare me the talk of dawns.
- Your vicars have been preaching patience to my soldiers. That stops.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. May it burn bright against the pit.
- Agreed. An honest people make an honest bargain.
- Acceptable. Send it to the front at first light.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The children of the sun give generously. It will serve the war.
- Accepted. Your people are as generous as they are bright.
- Good. Some mortals see clearly after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer is warm and empty.
- I do not need prayers. I need steel.
- No. Light does not pay soldiers.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Light should not make war on light. Go back to your sun.
- Peace. Your Radiant Guard is wasted on me.
- Go. Arawn's deserters should not be fighting each other.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your armies have not yet learned.
- Not yet. The dawn can wait a little longer.
- When your sun has set on this war, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? The sun gives freely, they say. Go and ask it.
- No. Your temples have gold enough.
- I give nothing to those who demand it, however bright their banners.

### Mercurians → Sheaim

#### First contact
- Sheaim. You open gates into hell and call it scholarship. I know what comes through those gates. I kill it.
- You want the world to end. I want hell to end. Only one of us will get what we want.
- Gate-openers. Every portal you tear in creation brings me a little closer to your door.

#### Declares war
- Your planar gates are open wounds in the world. I am here to cauterize them.
- You long for the end. I will give you yours, and leave the world standing.
- Your summoners have called their last demon. The host is coming to close every gate you made.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Every word you speak is a summoning.
- I do not speak with those who pray for the end of creation.
- Go back to your gates, [CT_NAME]. I will be along shortly.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. We are not at war. That surprises me more than you. Speak.
- Speak, and keep your hands still while you do; I know what your gestures summon.
- I am listening, for now. Your gates have stayed closed. Keep them so.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Another prophecy of doom?
- Speak, and quickly. I smell the pit on your robes.
- Your summoners opened another gate near my camp. Explain it, or do not bother speaking.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Use it for anything but summoning.
- Agreed. Though why the end of the world needs gold, I cannot guess.
- Acceptable. I will be watching what you do with it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The gate-openers give a gift. It will be spent closing gates.
- Accepted. Do not expect me to thank you for it.
- Strange, that those who long for the end give gifts. Perhaps you hope to be spared.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. I do not arm the apocalypse.
- Your offer smells of the void.
- No. Why would the end of the world need my coin?

#### Agrees to peace
- A pause. Close your gates while it lasts.
- Enough, for now. Creation lives a little longer.
- Go. The end of days can wait; my war against hell cannot.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your gates are still open.
- Not while one of your summoners still breathes.
- You want the end. I am glad to give it to you.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? To hasten the end of the world? No.
- Not a coin for your Armageddon.
- Your gates have made you bold, Sheaim. They will not make you safe.

### Mercurians → Sidar

#### First contact
- Sidar. You traded pieces of your souls to live forever. I have seen where traded souls end up. Be careful.
- Shades. You walk unseen. So do demons, sometimes. Do not make me mistake you for one.
- You hunt the undead, I hear. Then we are not enemies. Not yet.

#### Declares war
- You stand aside from every war. No one stands aside from this one.
- Half a soul is still a soul. I can still send it where it belongs.
- Your hidden cities shelter things I hunt. The host is coming to find them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words are fog.
- Shadows get no answer, [CT_NAME].
- Not now. Fade, while you still can.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your shades cut down a nest of the undead near my camps. Good. Speak.
- Grey one. You are hard to see and harder to trust, but you have kept faith. What is it?
- Speak. There is something cold about you, but you are not my enemy.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Have your shades been creeping through my camp again?
- Speak, and stand where I can see you.
- I do not like being watched, Sidar. Explain your spies.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. Solid coin, from a shade.
- Agreed. Use your share against the dead.
- Acceptable. Fade back to your cities.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The grey ones remember the living. Unexpected. It will go to the war.
- Accepted. Perhaps you still care for this world.
- Good. Even half a soul can be generous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your offer is as insubstantial as you are.
- You have eternity to haggle. I do not.
- No. Bring me something I can hold.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Return to your hidden cities and your endless patience.
- Peace. Hunt the undead, and leave my soldiers alone.
- Go. A war against shadows wastes good steel.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You chose to step out of the fog. Stay out of it.
- Not yet. Your shades still stalk my host.
- When you remember that you have something left to lose, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You have eternity to earn it.
- No. Shades have no need of gold.
- I owe nothing to those who sold their souls for time.

### Mercurians → Svartalfar

#### First contact
- Svartalfar. You threw down your own god and took Esus in his place. I turned from the gods too, but I did not hunt those who kept faith.
- The winter court. Your treachery is legendary. Keep it away from my host.
- Dark elves. Your quarrel with your cousins means nothing to me. Demons mean everything. Stay out of my way.

#### Declares war
- You punished your own kind for keeping faith. That is the pit's justice, and I have come to end it.
- Your knives work in the dark. My hammer works anywhere.
- Your court ruled while the world froze. Your rule ends now.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your words come with a knife behind them.
- I do not bargain with assassins, [CT_NAME].
- Go and buy a miracle from Esus. You will get none from me.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- [CT_NAME]. Your Shadowriders killed a coven of the Ashen Veil in their beds. That was useful. Speak.
- Speak. I will listen, with my back to the wall.
- Dark elf. You have kept your word so far, which surprises me. What is it?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What now? Another plot?
- Speak, and keep your hands where I can see them.
- Your assassins were found in my camp. Explain yourself, or do not bother.

#### Accepts a deal
- Done. If there is poison in it, I will find you.
- Agreed. Remarkably straightforward, for your court.
- Acceptable. Now go back to your shadows.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the winter court. I will check it for blades.
- Accepted. Whatever you meant by it, it serves the war now.
- Unexpected. Whatever you want in return, you will not get it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your bargains have hidden edges.
- I do not deal with those who pay for their miracles.
- No. Too cold, and too clever.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Take your plots back to your dark woods.
- Peace. Hell is worse than you, barely.
- Go. Point your knives at the pit for once.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your court has not yet paid for its treachery.
- Not yet. Your assassins still walk my camps.
- When the winter court learns honesty, ask again. I expect a long war.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Pay Esus for it, as you pay for everything.
- No. Not to traitors.
- Not a coin. Your court has knives enough to take what it wants; try them on me.

## Sheaim

### Sheaim → Amurites

#### First contact
- Children of Kylorin, at last. Your father ended one winter; we intend to end everything else. Shall we compare our studies?
- The Amurites, who license their necromancers like fishmongers. The Sheaim keep no such ledgers, and our magic is the richer for it.
- Your schools draw gifted minds from every corner of Erebus. So do our gates, though our students seldom ask to leave.

#### Declares war
- Your archmages squabble over footnotes while the world burns down to its last page. We have come to turn it for you.
- Kylorin's blood runs strong in your mages. Let us see whether it boils as readily as it casts.
- Your laws forbid the darker spheres. We have come to teach your schools everything they refused to learn.

#### Refuses to talk
- Send your envoy to a committee, Amurite. Perhaps it will reach a verdict before your last academy falls.
- No. Your battle mages may argue terms with our summonings, and those do not adjourn.
- We do not treat with a faculty in session. Return when your headmasters have finished dying.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, the scholars. Have you come to borrow from our grimoires, or only to admit you envy them?
- Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Your mages and ours understand one another far better than your priests would like.
- Our libraries are open to the Amurites, for now. Knowledge is the one harvest worth gathering before the end.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Speak quickly, Amurite. Our gates have opinions about lectures, and they are not patient ones.
- You lock away the very arts that will end this world, and you call it prudence. State your business.
- Another of Kylorin's heirs come to scold us? He turned on his own pupils once. We know whose lessons were the truer ones.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair exchange between scholars, written in ink that will burn with everything else.
- Done. Take it back to your academies and let them study it, while there is still time to study anything.
- These terms would pass even your examining boards. Agreed.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Amurites, freely given? Your archmages must be distracted by some feud. We accept, gratefully.
- Your generosity is noted. When the sky falls, we will see that it falls on your schools last.
- How courteous. Kylorin's children were always better mannered than Kylorin's pupils.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even an Amurite apprentice could find the flaw in this bargain, and we are no apprentices.
- Rework your sums, scholar. That offer would not pass the most junior of your examiners.
- We decline. Your terms are as swollen as your bureaucracy.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Return to your seminars and your feuds; the end will reach your schools in its own season.
- Enough. Your siege-mages have earned a rest, and our rituals need tending more than this war does.
- Let it end. There is no wisdom in two great houses of magic burning each other before the true fire comes.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace? Your arcane might has not yet impressed us. Bring more fire, Amurite, or bring your surrender.
- No. Your mages are only now learning what our spells can do to them, and the lesson is far from over.
- You would table a motion for peace? Denied, by the vote of every gate we hold open.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute from the Sheaim? Petition your council of archmages; perhaps it will rule on the matter in a century or two.
- You mistake us for students who owe you tuition. We owe the Amurites nothing.
- No. Keep your demands for the lesser colleges that still fear you.

### Sheaim → Balseraphs

#### First contact
- The court of Jubilee. We have looked into it before, through a certain enchanted mirror. Your masque has not changed.
- Laughter, puppets and chains. You are nearly as mad as this world deserves, Balseraph, and we mean that kindly.
- We have met before, you and we, though your court's memory is a crowded place. Some of our blood still dances in your halls.

#### Declares war
- The circus is over. We will strike the tents, and then the world beneath them.
- Your harlequins have juggled long enough. Let us see how they caper in balefire.
- Every jest has an ending, Balseraph. We have come to deliver the last one.

#### Refuses to talk
- No more riddles and rhymes. We will not be talked into your next trap.
- Keep your puppets on their strings and your envoys at home. The Sheaim are not your audience.
- We remember what became of the last agent we sent to your court. There will be no next one.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, the masquerade. Which face speaks for Jubilee today?
- We enjoy your court, [CT_NAME]. It is the only place in Erebus where the end of the world would be met with applause.
- Welcome, Balseraph. Your freaks and our summonings would make a splendid parade into oblivion.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Spare us the verse. What does the court of fools want this time?
- Your mimics have been studying our mages. We noticed. State your business before we stop finding it amusing.
- We have screams enough of our own here, jester. We do not need yours. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair bargain, even by a madman's measure. Done.
- So be it. Do keep your word on this; we know you like to keep it in odd shapes.
- Agreed. Let both our ledgers burn in the same fire, someday.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from Jubilee with no hook in it? We will search it for one, and then thank you properly.
- Generous, Balseraph. Your taskmasters will be the last to be whipped into the abyss.
- How delightful. We shall applaud, since that seems to be the custom at your court.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We know your fondness for tricks of language, and this offer is one of them.
- Not today, harlequin. Your bargain wears too many masks.
- Find another fool for your court, Balseraph; you seem to collect them. We decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well, the curtain falls on this act. Keep your harlequins on your side of the stage.
- Peace. We have learned that wars with madmen never end the way anyone planned.
- Enough. Let your court laugh about it; ours will be busy with grander ruin.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The play is not finished, and your city is the next scene.
- Peace? Your court would only spend it rehearsing its next betrayal. We will finish this.
- Beg in rhyme if you like. The answer will still be fire.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for a clown? We already paid your court once, and it cost us our finest spy.
- What a jest. Even your own courtiers will not dare to laugh at this one.
- No. Pull your own strings, Balseraph.

### Sheaim → Bannor

#### First contact
- The Bannor, who once walked out of hell. How sad, to cling so hard to a world that is already dying.
- So you are Junil's crusaders. You march against the apocalypse, and we are the apocalypse. We will have much to discuss.
- The Bannor, led out of hell by an angel. You escaped Agares's pit; some of us escaped other pits. Only one of us learned anything there.

#### Declares war
- Your priests keep a list of the damned. We keep one too, and the Bannor have always been at the top of it.
- Let us end the pretense, crusader. You were raised to fight the end of the world, and the end has come for you.
- March out your Orders and your Families, Bannor. Your Law will burn the same as any other parchment.

#### Refuses to talk
- No envoy from the Halls of Sabathiel will be received here. Pray to Junil instead; he may even listen.
- We know what a Bannor truce is worth: a pause to sharpen swords. We will not talk.
- Speak to us of Law once more and we will open a gate in the middle of your chapel.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- A Bannor at our door who is not carrying a torch? Remarkable. What do you want?
- We are as civil as two enemies of fate can be, [CT_NAME]. Say your piece.
- Even the Order and the Sheaim may share a table, so long as nobody says grace.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Confessors have been burning our acolytes again. Speak, before we answer in kind.
- Ah, the zealot. Have you come to read us our sins? It will be a very long reading.
- Mind your sword hand, crusader, and we will mind our runes. Now, what is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even crusaders must eat until the end comes.
- Done. Do not tell your priesthood where it came from.
- We accept. Let it be written in your Halls that the Sheaim kept their word.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Bannor charity? Your priests must be sleeping. We accept it before they wake.
- Charity from the Order. We will remember it, and perhaps burn your garrison towns a little more gently.
- How pious. Your Confessors would be horrified, which makes it all the sweeter.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms are as rigid as your drill, and twice as tiresome.
- Junil asks for unquestioning obedience. We question everything, beginning with this offer. No.
- Unacceptable. Take it back to your estate-holders and let them haggle with each other.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, for now. Go home to your fortress farms; you will need them when the sky falls.
- We will stand down. Tell your priests the Sheaim showed mercy, and watch them refuse to believe it.
- Enough. Your Orders bleed bravely, but the end needs no hurrying from you.

#### Refuses peace
- Peace with the Bannor? You would only call it an intermission in your Crusade.
- No. You climbed out of hell once, crusader. We are sending you back.
- Your priests would never forgive themselves a truce with us, and we will not offer them the temptation.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Halls of Sabathiel? We would sooner pay it to Agares himself.
- The Order may demand obedience of its own flock. We are not among its sheep.
- No. Add this refusal to your list of our sins; it will be in good company.

### Sheaim → Calabim

#### First contact
- Os-Gabella's brood. She grew weary of creation long ago, as did we. Has she told you?
- The Calabim, who keep people as cattle. A tidy arrangement, until the end comes and the herds are gone.
- Your Grand Broods feast while the world dwindles. Tell us, vampire, what will you drink when there is nothing left?

#### Declares war
- Your herds are wasted on you, Calabim. We have better uses for them, and for you.
- You have cheated death for centuries. We have come to collect it, with interest.
- We are coming for your estate farms. The cattle will scarcely notice the change of masters.

#### Refuses to talk
- Talk with a leech while its teeth are still in us? No.
- Your courtiers may whisper and charm all they like. Not one of them will cross our threshold.
- No. Save your guile for your bloodpets; it has no purchase here.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Calabim. You at least understand that people are a resource to be spent.
- Ah, the nobility of the night. Our rites and your feasts are not so different, in the end.
- Sit, [CT_NAME]. You will be truly disappointed when the end arrives, and we find that rather endearing.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Wipe your mouth before you address us, vampire.
- What does the parasite want now? Be brief; our patience is shorter than your lifespan.
- We know you hunger for our people. Speak, and keep your fangs where we can see them.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Blood for gold, gold for blood; it all ends in the same fire.
- Done. Your Broods drive a fair bargain, for leeches.
- Take what you need and feed well on it, while there is still a world to feed on.

#### Thanks for a gift
- How gracious of the Grand Broods. We will remember this when the sky turns red.
- Freely given? You must have fed very well this season, vampire. Our thanks.
- Our thanks. Your herds will be among the last to burn.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would bleed us dry with terms like these.
- Charm your bloodpets with that offer; we are not so easily drained.
- That offer has the patience of someone with centuries to spare. We do not. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well, peace. Go back to your feasting; let the end find you sated.
- Enough. You have centuries to brood over this war, and we have rites to finish.
- Let it be peace. There is no sense in two dark powers bleeding each other for the priests' amusement.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your cities are full of cattle, and we have pens of our own to fill.
- Peace with a vampire lasts until the next hunger. We will not sign.
- You have lived long enough to recognise a lost war. We will wait for you to admit it.

#### Rejects a demand
- Feed elsewhere, Calabim. The Sheaim do not bleed on request.
- A tithe? We are not one of your herds.
- No. Os-Gabella herself was never given what she demanded of the world, and her brood will fare no better.

### Sheaim → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs of the Ember Banner. Bhall fell and burned Braduk, and you are what her fire left behind. We find that promising.
- The Clan. You remember the day fire rained from heaven. We mean to make it rain again.
- Ah, the children of Braduk the Burning. We have long admired your goddess's last great act.

#### Declares war
- You love fire, orc. Then we will give you more of it than Braduk ever held.
- Your tribes burn villages. We burn worlds. Let us show you the difference.
- Raise your Ember Banner, Clan. It will make a fine torch for your own pyre.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not parley with raiders. Bring your axe or go home.
- No talk. Your warlords understand only the blade, and that is what you will get.
- Save your bellowing for the sacred pit, orc. The Sheaim will hear you when you come to us in chains.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Clan. Few understand the beauty of a burning city as well as you do.
- Ah, our fiery friends. What do the orcs of Braduk want from the Sheaim?
- Axes sheathed, for once? Come, warm yourselves at our fires; they burn hotter than your sacred pit.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You smell of smoke and blood. Speak, and do not drip on our runes.
- The Clan raids our borders, then comes to talk? Be quick, orc.
- What now, savage? Our fires burn hotter than your sacred pit, and our patience burns shorter.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Burn something worthwhile with it.
- Done. Orcs bargain more honestly than the Bannor ever did, we will grant you that.
- Struck. Both our peoples know where this world is going.

#### Thanks for a gift
- The Clan, giving instead of taking? Our thanks, and our astonishment.
- Bhall's children are generous today. We will see your axes well fed at the end.
- Good. When the last fire comes, we will make sure you have a fine view of it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even an orc should know that offer is an insult.
- We decline. Take your plunder to Orthus's tribes; perhaps they will want it.
- Your offer is as crude as a war-axe bolted to a priest's sceptre. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough. Go back to your raiding, Clan, but raid someone else.
- Peace. Burn the Bannor instead; they have earned it far more than we have.
- We will stop. Your fire and ours should not be wasted on each other.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You lit this blaze, orc, and we will see it burn to the last ember.
- Peace? Your warlords would break it before the smoke cleared over Braduk.
- Not yet. Bhall did not stop halfway when she fell, and neither will we.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for orcs? Take it, if your axes can reach.
- No. The Sheaim do not pay raiders to go away; we make them go away.
- You want our gold? Bhall gave your people fire, orc, not wit.

### Sheaim → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello, wolves of the wastes. You survived the Age of Ice by eating your weak. Admirable, in its way.
- You ran free through Mulcarn's winter and then helped Kylorin end it. Do you miss the cold yet, wolf?
- Some among us have walked the burning fields of Camulos's hell, savage. Your war god's realm is not the glory you imagine.

#### Declares war
- The pack culls its weak, does it not? Then we have come to cull the pack.
- You worship strength. Let us show you a strength that ends worlds.
- Howl while you can, Doviello. When the world ends, the wolves starve with everyone else.

#### Refuses to talk
- We do not bargain with beasts in the middle of a hunt.
- No. A wolf speaks of peace only when it is bleeding, and you are not bleeding enough.
- You leave your wounded in the snow, Doviello. Do not expect us to stop and tend to you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Doviello. Your people know the world is cruel; we only plan to finish what it started.
- Come in out of the wind. The Sheaim respect any people who survived Mulcarn's winter on their own terms.
- What does the pack want, [CT_NAME]? Speak plainly; we know your kind dislikes clever words.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You reek of raw meat and the hunt. Speak, and leave your wolves outside.
- Another snarl from the north. Say what you came to say, beastman.
- Your raiders test our borders as wolves test a herd. We are not a herd. What do you want?

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Drag it back to your pack and fight over it as you please.
- Done. The strong trade with the strong.
- Done, wolf. Spend it on whatever passes for a feast in your halls.

#### Thanks for a gift
- So the wolves share the kill after all. You must have hunted well. Our thanks.
- Good. It seems even Camulos's children can share the kill.
- Perhaps your pack will be spared the first wave of the end, Doviello. We are grateful.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a wolf trying to steal the carcass while pretending to share it.
- Your terms are as raw as your meat. No.
- Not enough. Come back when you have something worth gnawing on.

#### Agrees to peace
- Enough, Doviello. Go back to your hunting grounds and lick your wounds.
- Peace. Even wolves know when to break off a hunt that costs too much.
- We will stand down. Turn your teeth on the Illians; you know their scent better than ours.

#### Refuses peace
- No. In your own law the weak are left to die. We are only following it.
- Peace? You taught the world yourselves that the wounded are left behind.
- Not while your packs still circle our cities.

#### Rejects a demand
- The Sheaim do not throw meat to wolves.
- No. Take it by strength, as your custom demands, if you can.
- You demand from us? The pack has grown far too bold, and its leader far too careless.

### Sheaim → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim, keepers of holy places. Tell us, how many shrines will you keep when there is no world left to hold them?
- You witnessed the Compact being made. We intend to witness everything it protected come undone.
- So you are the monks who tend the sacred sites. We tend sites of our own, for very different purposes.

#### Declares war
- Your shrines are sacred to the gods. We are going to break them, one by one, and you will watch.
- You comforted the dying in the Age of Dragons. You are about to be very busy again.
- The Elohim guard the world's holy places. The Sheaim have come to desecrate them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No, monk. Your gentle words will not close our gates.
- We will not hear the keepers of the shrines. You would only beg for them.
- Your order's patience is famous. Practise it now.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Elohim. Your kindness is pointless, but strangely pleasant.
- Peace be with you, as your monks say. We will make an exception to our plans for you, for a while.
- The Elohim are always welcome here, to look upon what they cannot save.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Spare us the sermon on suffering. We know more of it than any of your monks.
- What now, keeper? Have we trampled another of your holy groves?
- You preach care and shelter, and beneath it we hear only fear. Speak your fear, then.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Tend it as carefully as you tend your shrines.
- Done. Your monks drive an honest bargain; it is almost a shame.
- It costs us nothing we will need at the end, keeper. Agreed.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Elohim, to the very ones who will end you. Your teachings are remarkable.
- Our thanks. You truly do tend to everyone, even the damned.
- How kind. For this, the seven firs of the Compact will be among the last things to burn.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even a monk should know to ask a fairer price.
- Charity is your virtue, keeper, not ours. We decline.
- Unacceptable. Take your offer back to your abbey and meditate on it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go back to your pilgrims and your shrines, while they still stand.
- Very well. You sheltered the dying in every age; go and shelter your own.
- Peace, monk. Your warriors fight well for men who carry no weapons.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your shrines are still standing. That will not do.
- Peace with the keepers of the holy places? Not while a single altar of yours remains.
- You signed a peace with demons once and they smiled. We are smiling now.

#### Rejects a demand
- The Sheaim give nothing to the caretakers of the gods' leftovers.
- No. Pray to Sirona for it; she may even answer.
- A demand? How unlike a monk. The answer is still no.

### Sheaim → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori, who turned from the gods. We too reject the gods' plans for this world, only more thoroughly.
- The Grigori, who serve no god. You would free men from the gods. We would free them from creation itself.
- So you are the haven for those who doubt. Doubt is the first step, Grigori. The Sheaim are the last.

#### Declares war
- Your adventurers are brave. They will be brave all the way into the abyss.
- You hoped to let men build a world of their own. We have come to end it before they finish.
- No god will come to save you, Grigori. You made very sure of that yourselves.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Lead yourselves out of this war, as your creed instructs.
- Your heroes will have to earn their peace the hard way. We are not talking.
- Your creed refuses help from on high. Refuse our mercy as well; it was never on offer.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Grigori. We share a contempt for the gods, if little else.
- Ah, the free thinkers. What do you want from the Sheaim, [CT_NAME]?
- Your people know this world was a poor gift. We merely intend to return it.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You preach that men should lead themselves. Then lead yourself out of our sight.
- What now, unbeliever? Has another of your adventurers fallen through one of our gates?
- The Grigori trust no gods and no masters. Trust this, then: our patience is gone.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Heaven gave neither of us anything; let us at least give each other this.
- Done. Your merchants are as practical as your temples are empty.
- Take it, and spend it on your adventurers; they will need every coin.

#### Thanks for a gift
- No god's blessing on it, and no priest's hook in it. Refreshing. Our thanks.
- Generous, Grigori. When the end comes, at least your gods will not disappoint you.
- Our thanks. We will not pray for you; you would not want us to.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You refuse divine boons; we refuse this bargain. Fair is fair.
- That is a bargain only a true believer would take, and we believe in nothing. No.
- Not enough, Grigori. Your heroes have taught you to ask for too much.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace, then. Go and improve what you have been given, while you still have it.
- So be it. Your champions have earned this without any god's help.
- Enough. We have no quarrel with those who would leave the gods to rot.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You wait for the doors of the true heaven to open, Grigori. We intend to break them down.
- Peace? Your heroes are only beginning to understand what they face.
- The Grigori need no gods, and they will find no mercy either. The war goes on.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Lead yourselves, as your creed demands, and earn your own wealth.
- Tribute? Your creed teaches men to ask nothing of higher powers. Heed it.
- You refused the gods' gifts, Grigori. Refusing ours should come easily to you.

### Sheaim → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus, whose riders hunted mages for Kylorin. We are mages too, and much harder to ride down.
- Horse lords and sellswords. Tell us, what does it cost to hire a Hippus company for the end of the world?
- You charged down Patria's warrior mages while the portals were being closed. We open portals. Think on that.

#### Declares war
- Your forefathers rode down Patria's mages. Their heirs will meet ours, and our fire.
- Saddle up, Hippus. There is no corner of the plains where the end will not find you.
- Your contracts are cancelled, horse lord. All of them, forever.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Gallop back to your camps; we have nothing to say to you.
- A mercenary's peace is only a contract awaiting a better bid. We will not talk.
- Not now. Your riders still smell of our burning fields.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Hippus. Our gold is as good as anyone's, should your companies be for hire.
- Come, [CT_NAME]. We have use for riders who never ask where the road ends.
- Ah, the horse lords. Your lances would ride well beside our summonings.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your horses trample our borders and then you come to talk? Be quick.
- What does the sellsword want? Name your price and go.
- Speak, Hippus, before your herds foul our sacred grounds any further.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. A fair price, as mercenaries reckon such things.
- Done. Your people know the worth of gold. So do we, for a little while yet.
- Ride home with it, horse lord, before it loses its meaning.

#### Thanks for a gift
- No price attached? From the Hippus? You surprise us, and we thank you.
- Our thanks. Perhaps one day we will hire your riders for the last charge of all.
- Generous, horse lord. The Sheaim will remember which clan brought it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a mercenary's price, and we are not desperate.
- Even your raiders would refuse a contract this poor. No.
- Too dear, Hippus. Haggle with the Kuriotates; they are used to paying you.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Your riders have earned their rest, and their pay.
- Go back to your herds and your hills, horse lord. Peace.
- Enough. We would rather hire your companies than bury them.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your riders broke Patria's mages once; that debt has never been paid.
- Peace? You would only sell your lances to our enemies the next morning.
- When the plains are burning, ask again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? You are mercenaries, Hippus. Work for it.
- No. The Sheaim do not pay riders to stay home.
- Your price for leaving us in peace is too high. We will take the war instead.

### Sheaim → Illians

#### First contact
- The lost men of Letum Frigus. You dream of a world asleep beneath the ice; we dream of it gone entirely.
- The Illians, whose lord would become a god. We would end the world that any god might rule.
- Mulcarn's old faithful. The Winter King is gone, and still you go looking for another.

#### Declares war
- Your winter will not save you. Ice burns well enough, with the right spell.
- When the Illians wake, the world sleeps. We have come to make certain neither of you wakes again.
- You mean to climb into the heavens, Illian. We will be waiting at the top with fire.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back to your frozen ruins and your ghosts.
- We will not speak with the White Hand. Mulcarn's priests had their age, and wasted it.
- Silence, Illian. Your voice is as cold as your future.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Illian. Your winter and our fire want the same thing: an end to this tiresome spring.
- Ah, the frozen ones. What brings you down from the broken mountain?
- Sit with us, [CT_NAME]. We have never met a people so eager to put the world to sleep, and we approve.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your ambition is louder than the north wind, Illian. Speak over it if you can.
- What does the White Hand want? Be quick; the cold you carry chills our braziers.
- You plan to make gods. We plan to make gods irrelevant. Speak, and then leave.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Even the ice must trade, it seems.
- Done. Carry it back to Letum Frigus.
- It is yours. May it warm your halls, if anything can.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Winter, being generous? We did not know it could. Our thanks, Illian.
- Generous, Illian. When your ascent to godhood fails, we will remember you kindly.
- How unexpected. Mulcarn's heirs have a warm hand after all.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That bargain is as barren as your tundra.
- Your terms are cold comfort indeed. We decline.
- Not enough, Illian. The ice has numbed your sense of value.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your glaciers and your dreams of godhood.
- Very well. Let ice and fire pause, and see which outlasts the other.
- Enough. We would rather watch your ambitions fail on their own.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your ice has not yet melted from our lands.
- Peace? You would only use it to finish your climb to heaven.
- Not while one snowflake of yours still falls on our cities.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute for the White Hand? Mulcarn is gone, and that custom went with him.
- No. You mean to become a god; conjure it from the snow yourself.
- You demand from us? The cold has addled your wits, Illian.

### Sheaim → Infernal

#### First contact
- Hell's legions walk in Erebus at last. Rites much like ours thinned the walls you came through; do not forget it.
- Welcome to creation, demon. Enjoy it while it lasts. We certainly do not intend to follow you back.
- So hell has come up for air. Some of us spent centuries down there, and we do not miss it.

#### Declares war
- We opened the way to end the world, not to hand it to Agares. Back into the pit, demon.
- Your master wants souls to torment forever. We want no souls left at all. Our goals were never the same.
- You think the end of the world belongs to hell? It belongs to the Sheaim.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We have bargained with hell before, and we remember the price.
- Not a word, demon. Every one of your contracts has teeth.
- Go and claw at your dirt, demon. The pit gets no hearing here.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Infernal. Our gates and your legions make good neighbours, for now.
- Ah, our friends from below. What does hell want from the Sheaim today?
- Come, [CT_NAME]. We have more in common than either of us will admit before the priests.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Speak quickly, demon. Some of us remember hell's hospitality all too well.
- You bring the stink of brimstone into our halls. What do you want?
- Your demons have been eyeing our cities like a butcher eyes a carcass. Speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. And yes, we read every clause; we know hell's habits.
- Done. A bargain with hell, sealed on our terms for once.
- Done. Spend it carving another city out of the dirt.

#### Thanks for a gift
- From hell, a gift? There is always a price. We will pay it later, gladly.
- Our thanks, demon. Agares is unusually generous today.
- How unlike your kind, to give without taking. We are suspicious, and grateful.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We have read enough infernal contracts to smell a trap.
- Hell bargains badly when it cannot burn the other party. We decline.
- Even the merchants of Mammon's city would laugh at that offer. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Hell can wait for us a little longer.
- Go back to carving your cities from the dirt, demon. We will not stop you.
- Enough. There will be souls enough for everyone when the end comes.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The Sheaim will never kneel to hell again.
- Peace with the pit? We would rather burn.
- Your legions are still on our side of the walls. Peace can wait until they are not.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to hell? Some of us already paid, in centuries of screaming.
- No. Take it up with Agares; he owes us more than we owe you.
- Hell gets nothing from the Sheaim. Not this time, not ever again.

### Sheaim → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad. You slept through Mulcarn's winter in your holes under the hill. You will not sleep through the end.
- Dwarves, who distrust all magic. You will distrust us most of all, and rightly.
- So you are the gold-counters of the deep halls. Count carefully, dwarf; there is not much time left.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are deep, dwarf. The end of the world goes deeper.
- Seal your great stone doors. They could not keep out the truth before, and they will not keep out us.
- Your gold will melt as easily as anyone's when the sky catches fire.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Go back underground and wait there.
- We do not haggle with dwarves while their siege engines are aimed at our walls.
- Not a word, Khazad. Let your stone walls speak for you, while they stand.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, dwarf. We will not trick you with illusions; we prefer to be honest about the end of the world.
- Ah, the Khazad. Your coffers are full, we trust? Good. Spend them while they still mean something.
- Come in, [CT_NAME]. Mind the runes on the floor; some of them are still active.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- What do you want, dwarf? Be brief; we know you hate wasting time on outsiders.
- Your hammers ring all night along our border. Speak.
- The Khazad climb out of their halls to complain? Say it, then.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Count it twice if you must.
- Done. Your appraisers are as sharp as your axes.
- Agreed. Lock it in your vaults until the end.

#### Thanks for a gift
- Gold, freely given, from the Khazad? We must mark the date.
- Our thanks, dwarf. We will not ask what it cost you; we know how dwarves feel about cost.
- Generous. Kilmorph would be proud, or horrified.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We learned from your own history, dwarf: a bad bargain agreed to is still a bad bargain.
- Did you expect us to take a merchant's first offer? No.
- Not good enough, Khazad. We know exactly how deep your coffers go.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Go back to your halls and your ledgers.
- Peace. Your stout hammers have earned it.
- Enough. Neither of us gains anything by bleeding on stone.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your vaults are not yet empty.
- Peace? Not while your walls still stand.
- You hid underground through one age, dwarf. You will hide there again, until the end.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Khazad? You have more gold than you can count, and you count everything.
- No. Dwarves demanding gold from others? This is truly a strange age.
- Nothing, dwarf. Not a single coin, and certainly not an illusion of one.

### Sheaim → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates. Centaurs, giants and men gathered into a few great cities. A fine collection to be ended all at once.
- You never age, they say, Kuriotate. How fortunate; you will live to see the very end of things.
- Every outcast race of Erebus shelters under your banner. Convenient. They will all be in one place.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements are scattered and your borders porous. We will walk straight in.
- Draw back into your shell, Kuriotate. Shells crack.
- You have gathered every exile and stray of this world under your banner. We will end them all together.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your diplomats may wait at the border with everyone else.
- We will not talk with the confederation. Go home to your core cities while they stand.
- Not now. Your outlying lands still have too much left to burn.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Kuriotate. Your centaurs are a wonder; we would hate to see them end before their time.
- Ah, the great cities. What brings the confederation to the Sheaim?
- Be welcome, [CT_NAME]. You gather the strange and the outcast. So do we.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your lamia have been prying at our wards. Speak quickly.
- What do you want, Kuriotate? Your courtesy is wasted on us.
- Speak, and keep your centaurs on their own side of the border.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your royal administration drives a fair bargain.
- Done. May your settlements prosper, briefly.
- We accept. Let your settlements carry it far and fast; time is short.

#### Thanks for a gift
- From the confederation, a gift? Our thanks, to you and to your centaurs.
- Generous, Kuriotate. Your wisdom is no mere legend.
- Gratefully received. The centaurs may be spared the first fires.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your administrators ask too much.
- We decline. Not even your royal bureaucrats could justify those terms.
- Offer that to one of your client states. We are not one.

#### Agrees to peace
- Peace. Return to your great cities.
- Very well. Your shell held; we will look for its cracks another day.
- Enough. Your centaurs fight well, and the end can take them later.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your outlying settlements are still standing.
- Peace? Behind that young face you are cold enough to understand why we refuse.
- We have only taken the edges of your sprawl. Ask again when we reach the core.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. You already rule more than any child should, Kuriotate.
- Tribute? The Kuriotates must think us one of their protectorates.
- The Sheaim are no client state of yours, Kuriotate.

### Sheaim → Lanun

#### First contact
