- Send another envoy and we will send him back as a puppet. You of all people should appreciate it.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, Jubilee. Your festivals are the only revels in Erebus that rival our own.
- Welcome, Balseraph. Your court and ours are the two great theatres of this world. Shall we compare notes?
- [CT_NAME]. Your freaks are delightful. Do send us one; we will return it improved.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Spare us the verse, fool. What do you want?
- Your taskmasters have been taking slaves along our borders. We take slaves too, but only our own. Speak.
- Your puppets crept into our court last month. We cut their strings. Now, what is it?

#### Accepts a deal
- A fair bargain, even from a fool's court. Agreed.
- We accept, and we shall read every clause twice. Your court is so fond of loopholes.
- Done. Your jesters may sing of it; ours will poison the singers if the tune is poor.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Laughing Court, and not even a trap in it? We are almost disappointed.
- How charming. We will hang it in our hall, beside the masks of our enemies.
- Our thanks, Balseraph. Your madness has excellent taste.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a jester's bargain, and we are not laughing.
- Your terms twist like a contortionist at a fair. We decline.
- Even Esus would not ask that price for that miracle.

#### Agrees to peace
- The show ends, then. Take your harlequins home.
- Peace. Your court has amused us longer than most.
- Very well. Let us both return to our intrigues; open war is so unsubtle.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You have not yet learned to fear us, and we will not stop until you do.
- Your court mocks every treaty it signs. We will not give it the satisfaction.
- Peace? The masque has one more act, Balseraph, and you are in it.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? The Winter Court does not pay jesters.
- No. Juggle for it.
- Your threat was almost funny. Almost. You are no longer amusing.

### Svartalfar → Bannor

#### First contact
- The Bannor. Crusaders of Junil, who see sin in every shadow. You will find a great many shadows in our forests.
- Soldiers of Junil. Your priests decide who is damned; we assume we were damned long before you found us.
- So you are the Order's sword. We have broken finer swords than yours, and kept the pieces.

#### Declares war
- Your priests wanted a crusade, Bannor. We have decided to oblige them.
- The Order demands unquestioning obedience. We demand only that you die quietly.
- Every farm a castle, every city a garrison. How diligent. We will simply poison the wells.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your Confessors cannot absolve you of this war.
- We do not speak with crusaders. They hear only their own priests.
- Keep your sermons for your troops, Bannor. They will need them.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Ah, crusader. We are at peace, and you have not yet tried to burn us. How refreshing.
- Welcome, Bannor. Your discipline is admirable, though we prefer our soldiers quieter.
- [CT_NAME]. Your Order and our court rarely agree, but we both value an enemy's silence.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Confessors preached against Esus in our cities. They were found without their tongues. Speak.
- What does the Order want? To save us? Save yourself the effort.
- Speak, crusader. Your fervour is tedious, and our patience is short.

#### Accepts a deal
- Even zealots can do business, it seems. Agreed.
- Done. Do not tell your priests where you got it.
- We accept. Law has its uses, so long as we are the ones who write it.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Order? Your priests must be appalled. Our thanks.
- How generous. Your Confessors must have been looking the other way.
- We accept, Bannor. Pity is the virtue we most enjoy in our enemies.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms are as rigid as your Law and half as clever.
- Junil may ask for unquestioning obedience. We question everything, and this most of all.
- We decline. Take that offer back to your estate-holders; they enjoy being fleeced.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go and crusade against someone else.
- Peace. Your soldiers fought well, for fanatics.
- Enough. Go home to your fortress farms and count your scars.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your Crusade must be broken, not paused.
- Not while your Orders still march under our trees.
- Peace? Your priests would call it a truce and preach about it every spring.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Order? Esus does not tithe to Junil.
- No. Your priests have a whole palace full of tribute; they need none of ours.
- We are not your penitents, crusader, and we never will be.

### Svartalfar → Calabim

#### First contact
- The Calabim. A noble house ruling over cattle. We understand each other perfectly.
- Vampires. You keep your herds fat and docile; we keep ours frightened. We should compare our yields.
- The Grand Broods. Such old blood, and such indifferent manners.

#### Declares war
- Your herds are wasted on your Broods. We will take them, and then we will take you.
- We have tired of your fangs, vampire. Ours are sharper, and they are made of steel.
- Even the undying can be poisoned, Calabim. Shall we find out how?

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your charm does not work on elves.
- Talk to a leech? Not while it is still attached to our throat.
- Your courtiers will find our doors locked and our knives drawn.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Calabim. Your court is nearly as refined as ours.
- [CT_NAME]. Our nobles admire yours. They admire the bite less.
- Ah, the lords of the night. Have you brought something rare, or someone?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Broods have been hunting in our forests. That is our privilege, not yours.
- What does the leech want? Be brief; we have guests and would like them to stay alive.
- Speak, vampire, and keep your teeth away from our servants.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Blood is cheap; gold is not.
- Done. A noble bargain between noble houses.
- We accept. Feed well on it, and do not come back hungry.

#### Thanks for a gift
- How gracious of the Grand Broods. We will taste it for poison, as you would taste it for blood.
- A gift from the vampires. We are touched, though not, we trust, bitten.
- Our thanks. Elves once stole a grimoire from your libraries; it is pleasant to be given something instead.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You would drain us dry with those terms.
- Your Broods bargain like they feed: greedily. We decline.
- Not for that price. We have centuries too, vampire, and we can wait you out.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Return to your estates and your feasts.
- Peace. Let the priests wait a little longer to celebrate our ruin.
- Enough. Go back to your bloodpets; we will go back to our webs.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your herds will look so much better under our banner.
- No. Your Broods would sign with one hand and feed with the other.
- Not yet, Calabim. Your estate farms are only half burned.

#### Rejects a demand
- Feed elsewhere, vampire. The Svartalfar do not bleed on request.
- No. We are not one of your herds.
- You would extort the Winter Court? Even Os-Gabella would laugh at the presumption.

### Svartalfar → Clan of Embers

#### First contact
- Orcs. Once you were devout men of Braduk, they say, before your goddess fell on you. How far you have come down.
- The Clan of Embers. Your goddess fell from heaven in flames. Ours merely stopped answering, and we replaced him. Neater.
- So these are the tribes of the Ember Banner. Brutes with a flag. It is a start.

#### Declares war
- Your axes are loud, orc. Our knives are not.
- Your camps will make fine kindling. You do love a fire, so we will give you one.
- You raid our borders like beasts, so we will hunt you like beasts, from the trees, at night.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We do not parley with savages who still eat by their sacred pit.
- Your warlords murder their own priestesses at the holy fire. Why would we trust them with a treaty?
- Bellow your terms at the barbarians, orc. They are the only ones who will listen.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, orc. You have kept your axes sheathed near our forests. We are almost impressed.
- [CT_NAME]. Your Clan has been useful to us against the Bannor. Do keep it up.
- Ah, the Ember Banner. What do the children of Braduk want from their betters today?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- You smell of smoke and charred meat, orc. Speak before we have you washed.
- Your raiders have been setting fire to our woods. Fire spreads, orc, and so does our displeasure. Speak.
- Speak, savage, and keep your torches well away from our trees.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Buy yourselves a better axe; that one is chipped.
- Done. Orcs bargain honestly; it is so rare that we hardly know what to do with it.
- We accept. Carry it home to Braduk the Burning and throw it on the pile.

#### Thanks for a gift
- An orc, giving gifts. We will have to tell the court; they will not believe it.
- Our thanks, orc. Your people may have a future after all, if you keep learning from your betters.
- How generous. Bhall's children have finally learned something besides burning.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. We have seen better offers carved on a goblin's club.
- An axe-head bolted to a sceptre is not a crown, and that offer is not a bargain. We decline.
- Take your plunder to Orthus's tribes, orc. They might value it.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go back to your fires and your sacrifices.
- Peace. Burn the Bannor instead; we will watch from a pleasant distance.
- Enough. Your tribes have bled enough for one season, and we have run short of arrows.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your tribes still breed faster than we can kill them, and we intend to catch up.
- Not while your torches still glow beneath our trees.
- Peace? Not until your camps burn the way Braduk burned on the day your goddess fell.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to orcs? Come and take it, if you can find us in the dark.
- No. Your axes cannot reach what they cannot see.
- You demand from us? The fire has finally cooked your brains, orc.

### Svartalfar → Doviello

#### First contact
- The Doviello. You ran free in the heart of Mulcarn's winter while our court ruled through it. We are both a little sorry it ended, are we not?
- Wolves of the north. You leave your weak to die in the snow. Our court is crueller, but far better dressed.
- So the pack has come south. You helped Kylorin end the winter, we hear. That was careless of you.

#### Declares war
- The wolf is cunning, they say. The spider is patient. Come into our web, Doviello.
- You cull the weak from your pack. Allow us to help.
- Your raiders hunt in packs. Our assassins hunt alone, and they never need a second try.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Wolves do not keep bargains, and we do not waste ours on wolves.
- Howl at the moon, beastman. It may answer you; we will not.
- Circle our cities all season if you like. Our walls do not tire, and our archers do not sleep.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Doviello. You understand that kindness is a weakness. We find you refreshing.
- [CT_NAME]. The winter suited us both, did it not? Sit, and let us speak of the cold old days.
- Ah, the wolves. Have you come to hunt beside us, or only to sniff at our borders?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your hunters have been tracking our scouts. A few of them even came home. Speak.
- What does the pack want? Be brief; you smell of wet fur and old blood.
- Stop growling, beastman. It is unbecoming in a guest. Now speak.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Carry it off in your jaws, wolf.
- Done. Strength bows to cunning in the end, however loudly it growls.
- We accept. Spend it on whatever your people call a feast.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the wolves. You must have killed something very large.
- Our thanks, Doviello. Even a wolf can learn to bring tribute to the den.
- How unexpected. Does the pack share its kill with outsiders now? Camulos would be scandalized.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That is a wolf's bargain: all teeth and no meat.
- Hunt down a better offer, wolf, and bring it back still warm. We decline.
- Your terms stink like a wolf's den.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go and lick your wounds in the snow.
- Peace. Turn your teeth on the Illians instead; they have never forgiven you for the thaw.
- Enough. The hunt is over, wolf, and you were not the hunter.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You leave your wounded behind, Doviello. So do we.
- Peace? The pack has not yet lost enough to understand its place.
- Not while a single wolf of yours still stalks beneath our trees.

#### Rejects a demand
- You demand tribute? The pack forgets whose forest it is standing in.
- No. Wolves eat what they kill, not what they beg for.
- We do not throw scraps to dogs, however loudly they howl.

### Svartalfar → Elohim

#### First contact
- The Elohim. Sucellus set your order to tend his holy places, and then he died. We declared him gone; you are still sweeping his floors.
- Keepers of shrines and secrets. You know where Finner lies, do you not? We would pay handsomely to know.
- Monks who carry no weapons. How brave, and how very short-lived.

#### Declares war
- Your shrines hold secrets you have no right to keep. We have come for them.
- You tend the sacred sites of a dead god. Let us show you just how dead.
- Your monks carry no weapons. That will make this so much quicker.

#### Refuses to talk
- No, monk. Your gentle words are wasted on the Winter Court.
- No, keeper. You would only beg us to spare your shrines.
- You once signed a peace with demons, and paid for it. We will not make your mistake by signing one with you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Elohim. Your kindness is so sincere it is almost exotic.
- [CT_NAME]. Your monks visit our cities without trying to convert anyone. We find that oddly restful.
- Ah, the keepers. How fare the seven firs of the Compact? We hear they are lovely in winter.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your monks pray for our souls in our own marketplaces. It is embarrassing. Speak.
- Spare us the sermon on suffering, keeper. We have caused more of it than your order has ever tended.
- What does the shrine-keeper want? Be quick, before we grow curious about your relics.

#### Accepts a deal
- Your order bargains honestly. It must be exhausting. Agreed.
- Done. Tend it well, keeper, as you tend everything.
- We accept. Even the Winter Court can make an exception for saints.

#### Thanks for a gift
- How kind. Your charity reaches even us. We will try not to take advantage. Much.
- A gift from the Elohim. We are touched, monk, and only slightly suspicious.
- Our thanks. Sucellus chose his servants well, for all the good it did him.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Even a monk should bargain harder than that.
- Your order gives everything away, keeper. We give nothing away, least of all a bargain. No.
- Your terms are as plain as your robes, and about as valuable.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go back to your pilgrims and your relics.
- Peace. Your warrior monks fight remarkably well with empty hands.
- Enough. We will leave your shrines alone, for now. Do not mistake that for reverence.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your shrines still have secrets in them.
- Not while your monks still stand guard over what we want.
- Peace? Not until we know where Finner was laid to rest, and what lies beside him.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to monks? Pray for it.
- No. Your order needs no gold; you have told the world so for ages.
- The Winter Court gives nothing to beggars, holy or otherwise.

### Svartalfar → Grigori

#### First contact
- The Grigori. You turned your backs on the gods; we simply changed ours when the old one failed. We are more practical.
- A people with no gods and no masters. We will have to find something else to threaten you with.
- Your adventurers are famous, Grigori. Our assassins have been eager to meet them.

#### Declares war
- Your adventurers will make handsome trophies for our halls.
- You refused the protection of the gods, Grigori. Now refuse our knives, if you can.
- You shelter every runaway and doubter in Erebus. We have come to collect a few of ours.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You have no gods to plead for you, and we have no ears for pleading.
- We will not talk with a people who listen to no one.
- Your heroes have not yet earned a parley. Send us a few more and we will see.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Grigori. Your doubters make such interesting conversation.
- [CT_NAME]. You trust no gods. Wise. Trust no elves either, and we will get along famously.
- Ah, the free cities. Are your Luonnotar guests still preaching about the god above the gods? How quaint.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your adventurers keep wandering into our forests. Some wander out again. Speak.
- The godless at our door, demanding an audience. Your independence is admirable; your manners are not.
- Speak, Grigori, and spare us the lecture about servitude. We are the ones who keep slaves.

#### Accepts a deal
- A practical bargain between practical peoples. Agreed.
- Done. Spend it on your adventurers; they seem to need new boots every season.
- We accept. Your merchants answer to no god, so at least they will not tithe our gold away.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from those who answer to no god. At least we know whom to thank: you.
- Esus would have charged you dearly for such a miracle. You gave it freely. How very Grigori.
- Our thanks. You owe the gods nothing and us even less, yet here it is.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your adventurers have made you bold, and boldness is expensive.
- The gods ignored half the counsel that made the Compact. We will ignore all of this offer. No.
- That is a bargain only a believer would accept, and we believe in very little.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go and improve what you have been given, as your creed says.
- Peace. Your adventurers fought like heroes, and we have several of their bodies to prove it.
- Enough. Neither of us went to war for a god, so neither of us needs to keep fighting for one.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your heroes still live, and we have promised their heads to our court.
- Peace? Your people lead themselves. Lead yourselves to defeat first, and we will talk.
- Not yet. Your cities still shelter too many of our runaways.

#### Rejects a demand
- No. Your creed teaches men to rely on themselves. Do so.
- You turned away the gifts of the gods, Grigori. Ours are no easier to come by.
- Tribute from the Winter Court? You turned down heaven itself, Grigori. Turn this down too; you have the practice.

### Svartalfar → Hippus

#### First contact
- The Hippus. Sellswords on horseback. Name your price; the Winter Court pays well and asks no questions.
- Horse lords. Your clans raided one another for generations. We admire a people that knows how to betray its own.
- Your riders hunted Patria's mages for Kylorin. We have mages of our own, so do try to stay on good terms.

#### Declares war
- Your companies took our enemies' gold. We will make them regret the contract.
- Ride, Hippus. Our arrows fly faster than your horses.
- A mercenary's loyalty lasts until the better bid. We have made one: your death.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. We do not negotiate with hired swords; we hire them.
- Gallop home, horse lord. Your saddle is the only throne you will keep.
- Your offer to talk is like your loyalty: for sale. We are not buying today.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Hippus. Is your company free this season? We have work, and it pays.
- [CT_NAME]. Your riders are the finest in Erebus. We would hate to see them on the wrong side.
- Ah, the horse lords. The gold is waiting, if your lances are.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your herds have been trampling our gardens. Speak.
- What does the sellsword want? Remember who paid you last, and who will pay you next.
- Speak, horse lord. Your mercenaries rode against us last season; we recognized the saddles.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Hired steel at an honest price; the other clans will be furious.
- Done. Your contracts are honest, if nothing else about you is.
- We accept. Ride home with it before someone outbids us.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Hippus. We kept looking for the terms of payment.
- Our thanks. Perhaps we will hire your company for something special. Something quiet.
- How generous, horse lord. Your rivals in the other clans will be so jealous.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Hired lances charge hired prices, and we are not that eager.
- No. A contract that poor would start a feud between your own clans.
- Haggle with the Kuriotates, horse lord; they are used to paying dearly for riders.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go back to your herds and your hills.
- Peace. Your lances are worth more to us hired than dead.
- Enough. Your contract with our enemies has surely run out by now.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You sold your lances to our enemies, and that bill is not yet paid.
- Peace? You would sell it to the highest bidder before the ink dried.
- Not yet. No one outruns the Hippus, they say. We intend to test it.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? We hire Hippus, horse lord. We do not keep them as pets.
- No. The Winter Court hires riders; it does not pay them to stay home.
- Your price for staying in your saddles is too high, horse lord. Ride at us, then.

### Svartalfar → Illians

#### First contact
- The Illians. When the winter came and spring never followed, the crown of the elves stayed with our court. We have always been grateful to your god.
- Men of Letum Frigus. You would bring back the long winter. We would gladly hold your cloak while you do it.
- So the White Hand rises again. The Winter Court remembers Mulcarn fondly.

#### Declares war
- Winter belongs to our court, Illian, not to your upstart lord.
- You would make yourself a god of winter, Illian. There is only one Winter Court, and it does not kneel.
- You would be a god, Illian. We have discarded gods before; a mortal will be easier.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You already speak like a god, and we do not bargain with gods.
- The White Hand may wait outside in the snow. It should feel at home there.
- We will not bargain with a would-be god. They always want worship written into the terms.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Illian. Winter suits us both.
- [CT_NAME]. When your winter comes, remember who welcomed it first.
- Ah, the frozen ones. Have you brought the cold with you? How thoughtful.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your ambitions are growing tiresome, Illian. Speak.
- What does the White Hand want? Be brief; even we find you chilly.
- Speak, Illian, and remember that your godhood is not yet a fact.

#### Accepts a deal
- A cold bargain, but a fair one. Agreed.
- Done. Carry it back to your broken mountain.
- We accept. May the first snow come early this year.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the north. Our thanks; the cold so rarely gives anything back.
- How generous. You know how to court an ally.
- When the snows return, we will remember who brought this.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That bargain is as bare as the ice around your broken mountain.
- Even winter has its price, Illian, and this is not it. We decline.
- Your terms are cold comfort, and we have warmer offers.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Winter should not make war on winter.
- Peace. Go and finish your ascent; we will watch with interest.
- Enough. Let the snow settle between us.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You must be reminded that you are not yet a god.
- Not while your snows still bury our forests.
- Peace? We would rather see your ambition frozen solid.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Mulcarn is gone, Illian, and you are not him.
- No. Conjure it from the ice, if you are as divine as you claim.
- The Winter Court pays no tribute to winter's would-be heirs.

### Svartalfar → Infernal

#### First contact
- Demons in Erebus. How exciting. Do try not to scorch the tapestries.
- The legions of the pit. Our court has dealt with many devils before; most of them wore elven faces.
- So the walls of creation have cracked and hell has sent an envoy. The Winter Court is rarely impressed, but you have our attention.

#### Declares war
- Your legions are loud and hot and stupid. We are none of those things.
- Back into the pit, demon. Erebus belongs to the clever, not the merely cruel.
- You torment souls for an eternity. We prefer to do it efficiently, and then move on.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Hell's contracts have teeth, and ours have poison. Neither of us would sign.
- We do not bargain with brimstone while it is still burning our forests.
- We will not parley with a thing that had to claw its way into this world.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Infernal. Our court and yours share a certain taste in suffering.
- [CT_NAME]. You make a delightful neighbour. Nothing grows near your cities, and nobody visits.
- Ah, hell's envoy. What has Agares sent us today?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- The stench of sulphur reached us long before you did. Speak.
- Your underlings obey you out of terror. Ours obey us out of terror and good taste. What do you want?
- Speak, demon, and keep your claws off the furniture.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Our scribes combed it for loopholes and found only yours.
- Done. A bargain with the pit, on our terms for once.
- We accept. Spend it on brimstone, or whatever demons buy.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from hell. We will look very carefully for the hook.
- Our thanks, demon. We will count our fingers afterwards.
- A demon who gives without taking. We will wait for the other hoof to fall.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Hell's terms are always one-sided, and so are ours. We cannot both win.
- Even Esus charges less for a miracle. We decline.
- That offer reeks worse than you do.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go back to your ashen fields.
- Peace. There are fatter souls than elves for you to harvest, demon.
- Enough. We would rather watch you devour the Bannor than spend our arrows on you.

#### Refuses peace
- No. You are not yet back in the pit where you belong.
- Not while your legions still stand in our forests.
- Peace? You would only spend it gathering more souls to burn.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to hell? Collect it yourself, if you dare come into the dark.
- No. The Winter Court pays no one, least of all the damned.
- We will give you nothing but cold, demon. Let us see how you like it.

### Svartalfar → Khazad

#### First contact
- The Khazad. Your people were cheated once by smooth strangers bearing illusions. Do not worry. Ours are far better.
- Dwarves and their gold. We have heard about your vaults; our thieves speak of little else.
- You hid beneath the hills through the long winter while we ruled above it. Hello, neighbour.

#### Declares war
- Your vaults are deep, dwarf, and our thieves are patient.
- You distrust all magic. You are about to learn why.
- Seal your stone doors if you like. We came in through the cracks long ago.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your siege engines still point at our trees.
- We will not haggle in a war, dwarf. Count your dead instead; you love to count.
- Go back underground. We will talk when you have counted your losses twice.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Khazad. We promise the gold we pay you is real. This time.
- [CT_NAME]. Your stonework is splendid. We could almost envy it.
- Ah, the dwarves. Your coffers are full, we trust? Good. We prefer to trade with the wealthy.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your miners keep complaining about our thieves. Prove it. Now, speak.
- What does the dwarf want? Be brief; your suspicion is wearing on us.
- Look us in the eye when you speak, Khazad. We know you suspect we are an illusion.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Weigh it on your own scales; we know you trust no others.
- Done. Trade is quicker than robbing your vaults, though far less fun.
- We accept. Your appraisers are almost as sharp as our thieves.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A dwarf, parting with gold of free will? The court will want this carved somewhere.
- Our thanks. We will not tell our thieves; they would be insulted.
- How generous. Your ancestors in the Rune Halls must be turning in their stone.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You learned to drive a hard bargain after your people were cheated. Too hard, dwarf.
- A dwarf's first offer is always a test. We decline it, as you expected.
- Your terms are as heavy as your gold and twice as dull.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go back to your halls and count something.
- Peace. Your hammers hit hard; we admit to bruises.
- Enough. Stone does not bleed, dwarf, and our arrows are blunted on it.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your vaults are still full, and we have only begun to empty them.
- Not while your walls still stand between us and your gold.
- Peace? You would carve it into a pillar as a victory. We will not oblige.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to dwarves? You have more gold than sense already.
- No. Dig for it.
- We do not pay, dwarf. We take. You of all people should remember how that feels.

### Svartalfar → Kuriotates

#### First contact
- The Kuriotates. You rule centaurs and lamia and never age a day. Your court is almost as strange as ours.
- Your borders are wide and porous. Our agents thank you for the convenience.
- Every outcast race of Erebus under one banner. How generous of you, and how very vulnerable.

#### Declares war
- Your settlements are scattered and lightly held. We will pluck them one by one.
- Retreat into your shell, Kuriotate. Our knives are thin enough to slip between the plates.
- You play a cruel game of patience, Kuriotate. Ours is crueller.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Send your envoys home; we have petitioners enough.
- We will not talk with a confederation that cannot hold its own borders.
- Not now. That hiss has crept into your voice again, and we prefer to wait until it passes.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Kuriotate. Centaurs, lamia, giants: your court is as varied as a menagerie, and as dangerous.
- [CT_NAME]. Your centaurs are magnificent. Do they ever tire of serving the throne?
- Ah, the great cities. Still young, Kuriotate? You never change.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Two of your lamia were caught studying our wards. They are studying our dungeons now. Speak.
- Your asylum laws shelter our deserters. We would like them back, preferably in pieces. Speak.
- Speak, Kuriotate. Your charm is wasted on the Winter Court; charm is our native tongue.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your clerks are so efficient that we may steal a few.
- Done. Our regards to you, and to the cold thing that watches from behind your young eyes.
- We accept. Spread it thin across your settlements, as you spread your armies.

#### Thanks for a gift
- How gracious of you. We will send you a toy in return.
- Our thanks. Your famous openness to outsiders extends even to us.
- A gift from the great cities. Our thanks; even the lamia smiled as they delivered it.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your clerks have overreached, Kuriotate; tell them so.
- Not even your client states would accept those terms. We are not one of them.
- You win every game of strategy, we hear. Not this one. We decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Crawl back into your core cities; we have learned the shape of your defences.
- Peace. Your centaurs fought well; it would be a pity to make rugs of them all.
- Enough. Return to your great cities and your long childhood.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your settlements still sprawl across our hunting grounds.
- Not yet. You are patient; we are more patient, and far less kind.
- Peace? You would only use it to draw your borders across our forests again.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Your settlements may pay you tithes; our forests do not.
- No. Spoiled children should not be rewarded for tantrums, however old they are.
- The Winter Court does not pay for the privilege of your company, Kuriotate.

### Svartalfar → Lanun

#### First contact
- The Lanun. Pirates with a flexible sense of honour. We will get along splendidly.
- Your god Danalin has gone quiet, we hear. Ours did too, once. We replaced him. You might consider it.
- A captain's word, they say, is somewhat fleeting. So is ours. Let us agree to distrust one another, and profit.

#### Declares war
- Your ships rule the waves. Our assassins rule the dark. Your captains do have to sleep ashore sometimes.
- We will burn your harbours, captain, and let the sea keep what floats.
- Every captain rules his own ship, they say. We will see how many of you still have one by winter.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You would only rob our envoy and sell him back to us.
- We do not parley with corsairs while their raiders are still on our coast.
- Your word turns with the tide. We will wait for low water.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, captain. Your crews and our agents have so much in common.
- [CT_NAME]. Have you come to trade, or to steal politely? Either is acceptable here.
- Ah, the Lanun. The things rising from your depths these days; we would love to hear about them.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your corsairs burned three of our fishing villages. We are counting. Speak.
- What does the pirate want? Keep your hand off your sword; ours are already drawn.
- Speak, captain. Danalin no longer listens to you, and we barely do.

#### Accepts a deal
- By the law of the sea, whatever it is this week. Agreed.
- Done. A fair trade between thieves.
- We accept. Fair winds, captain, and may they blow you far from our shores.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Lanun? Did you steal it first? Of course you did. Our thanks.
- Our thanks, captain. The Winter Court will remember your ship's name.
- How generous. Your Overlords' dreamers will have something pleasant to babble about.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Did you mistake us for a merchant galley riding low in the water?
- That offer would embarrass a harbour pickpocket. We decline.
- Not good enough, captain. Even your cabin boys would mutiny over a share that small.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Back to your waves.
- Peace. The sea is wide; go and rob somebody else.
- Enough. Your captains have learned that our shores bite.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your harbours still stand.
- Peace? A Lanun treaty lasts as long as the tide is in.
- Not while your sails still crowd our horizon.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to pirates? Your ships cannot sail into our forests, captain.
- No. Your captains outrank your governors, we hear. They do not outrank us.
- We pay no toll to any captain, however loud.

### Svartalfar → Ljosalfar

#### First contact
- Cousins. The Summer Court crawls out of its hidden groves at last. Did you think we had forgotten the war the ice interrupted?
- Still mourning Sucellus, Ljosalfar? Or have you found yourselves a new god of the wild and are too proud to admit we were right?
- The rite of spring was never performed, cousin. The crown never came back to you, and it never will.

#### Declares war
- The ice separated us before we could finish. The ice is gone. Shall we resume?
- Your court had its summer. Ours has come to claim the rest of the year.
- You refused to stop praying to a dead god. We have come to send you to him.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Our war with the Summer Court began before the ice, and words did not end it then.
- We will hear the Seelie court when it kneels to the crown it lost.
- Talk, cousin? We said everything at the last rite of autumn, and you were not listening.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Cousin. How lovely to see you. We trust your stay will be comfortable.
- [CT_NAME]. We are at peace, and it is so pleasant to pretend we enjoy it.
- Welcome, Ljosalfar. Shall we sit by the window and pretend we are still one people?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your druids have been preaching in our forests again. We hanged them from the oldest trees. Now, what is it?
- Speak, cousin, and spare us the tears for Sucellus.
- What does the Summer Court want? Your season ended long ago.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed, cousin. Do not imagine this means we have forgiven you.
- Done. It is almost like the old days, when the crown passed between us without bloodshed.
- We accept. The trees need never know we traded with you.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Summer Court? How gracious. We will have it searched for thorns.
- Our thanks, cousin. You were always the generous one. It is why you lost.
- How sweet. You still believe kindness will bring the spring back.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. The Summer Court always asked for half of everything. We are done with halves.
- We decline, cousin. You always did overvalue your trees.
- That offer is as naive as your faith.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well, cousin. Go back to your groves; we will finish this some other winter.
- Peace. Let us return to the old game of pretending to love one another.
- Enough. The elves have bled enough for one age, and the humans are laughing at us both.

#### Refuses peace
- No. The war the ice interrupted is not finished.
- Peace? You would only use it to pray for a spring that is never coming.
- Not while a single Seelie banner still flies.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the Summer Court? Your season ended an age ago.
- No. We do not pay those we should have finished during the winter.
- You would presume to deny the Winter Court everything else and then demand its gold? No, cousin.

### Svartalfar → Luchuirp

#### First contact
- The Luchuirp. Little artificers and their obedient clay. We do envy a servant who cannot betray you.
- Heirs of the Open-Skiers. Your empire trusted its golems, and the ice took it anyway. You might trust a little less.
- Golem-makers. How wonderful. Our court has always wanted a servant who cannot be bribed.

#### Declares war
- Your golems are mindless, artificer. We suspect your generals are not much better.
- We will take your workshops and keep the golems. They will not even notice the change of masters.
- The ice ground your empire into the mountains once. We are far less patient than ice.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Send your golems to talk; at least they will not whine.
- We do not negotiate with tinkers while their clockwork is marching on our forests.
- Not now, little one. Go and wind something.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Luchuirp. Your golems are exquisite. We would pay well for one that pours wine.
- [CT_NAME]. You came back into the sun after an age beneath the ice. We know how sweet it is to outlast a winter.
- Ah, the artificers. What marvels have you brought us from your forges?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your golems keep trampling our gardens. Speak.
- Speak, tinker. Your little clay soldiers do not frighten us.
- What do the Open-Skiers want now, their empire back? It is buried under the ice, and there it stays.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Clockwork at a fair price; our court will have new toys this winter.
- Done. We will take good care of it, until we take it apart to see how it works.
- We accept. Graoin's heirs bargain carefully, we will give you that.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Luchuirp. Fine work; our smiths will weep with envy.
- Our thanks, little one. You are kinder than your golems are clever.
- How generous. Kilmorph taught you more than digging, it seems.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That offer has as many hidden gears as one of your golems.
- Even a golem would know it was being cheated. We decline.
- Your offer is clever, little artificer, but clever is not the same as generous. No.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go and mend your golems.
- Peace. Your clay soldiers fought with admirable stupidity.
- Enough. Take your golems home and let them stand in the sun you longed for.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your forges are still turning out soldiers.
- Not while your golems still trample our forests.
- Peace? You hid beneath the ice for an age. You can hide a little longer.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Build it yourself, artificer; you love building things.
- No. Dig for it, as your goddess taught you.
- The Winter Court does not pay tinkers to stop tinkering.

### Svartalfar → Malakim

#### First contact
- The Malakim. Your hunters once knew no elves but us. Then they found a stranger dying in the snow and spared the stranger's life. A charming mistake.
- Desert folk of Lugus. Your sun is very bright. We prefer the long night.
- Your Empyrean gives every nation an equal voice. How generous. We will be sure to speak loudly.

#### Declares war
- Your sun cannot reach into our forests, Malakim.
- Your forefathers learned what the Svartalfar are. Their descendants are about to remember.
- The light of Lugus casts long shadows. We live in them.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your Empyrean may deliberate on this war for an age, if it likes.
- We will not talk beneath your glaring sun.
- Not now. Your Radiant Guard is still burning our forests.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Malakim. Do stand in the shade; you look parched.
- [CT_NAME]. Your Empyrean's fairness is so earnest. We find it adorable.
- Ah, the desert folk. Have you come to trade, or to preach?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your Vicars have been preaching in our cities. We sent them home sunburned from the inside. Speak.
- Speak quickly, desert envoy. Our patience evaporates faster than your water.
- Speak, Malakim, and step out of the light; you glitter unpleasantly.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Your judges would weigh it as even; we weighed it as profitable.
- Done. Load it on your camels and hurry home before the sun cooks it.
- We accept. Desert traders surprise us now and then.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the desert. Our thanks; we did not know sand could be generous.
- How kind. Your people were always merciful to strangers. It is your great weakness.
- Our thanks, Malakim. The Winter Court remembers its debts, if not always fondly.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. That offer is as dry as your desert.
- Bring it before your Empyrean judges, Malakim; even they would rule against you.
- Your terms are as harsh as your sun, and far less warm. We decline.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go back to your oases.
- Peace. Your Radiant Guard fights with tiresome conviction.
- Enough. The sun and the night may keep their own hours.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your temples still shine, and we find the glare offensive.
- Not while your sun still beats down on our forests.
- Peace? The desert still has cities in it.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute? Ask Lugus.
- No. The Empyrean gives small nations a voice. Here is ours: no.
- The Winter Court gives nothing to the sun but shade.

### Svartalfar → Mercurians

#### First contact
- Angels who broke the Compact. How delightfully rebellious. We may have misjudged your kind.
- You disobeyed your own lords to keep fighting. The Winter Court knows a thing or two about defying the old order.
- The rebel host has come down to Erebus. You care little for mortals, we hear. We care little for angels. A promising start.

#### Declares war
- You came to kill demons, angel. We are not demons, but we can be every bit as unpleasant.
- Your host has never fought a war in the dark. Let us teach you.
- Holy wrath carved into your arms will not stop a poisoned blade.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. Your hammer has said enough for both of us.
- We do not parley with fanatics, mortal or divine.
- Not now, angel. Go and pray in blood somewhere else.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, angel. Our court is no friend of the hells; we simply dislike competition.
- [CT_NAME]. Your host is so single-minded. We find that very useful in a neighbour.
- Ah, the rebel host. Carving any new prayers today?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your soldiers keep mistaking our people for demons. It is flattering, but tiresome. Speak.
- What does the rebel host want? Be brief; you are not built for conversation.
- Speak, angel, and keep your judgments to yourself.

#### Accepts a deal
- Even angels need coin, it seems. Agreed.
- Done. Spend it on your endless war.
- We accept. May it buy you many dead demons.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from an angel. Our court will be insufferable about it for a century.
- Our thanks. Arawn's former servants are kinder than their master.
- How unexpected. You care so little for mortals; perhaps elves are different.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your host asks for more than it gives.
- We decline. Not even angels are worth that price.
- Your terms are as harsh as your faces, and nowhere near as handsome.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go and hunt your demons.
- Peace. We would much rather you spent your wrath on the pit.
- Enough. Your war is with the hells, and we have no wish to stand in its way.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your host still mistakes us for its enemies, so we have decided to become them.
- Peace? You broke the Compact itself. Why would you keep a treaty with us?
- Not while your hammers still fall in our forests.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the rebel host? Ask Arawn.
- No. Angels should not need gold; ask your hammer for some.
- The Winter Court bows to no angel, fallen or otherwise.

### Svartalfar → Sheaim

#### First contact
- The Sheaim. A cult gathered from every nation's discontented, working to end the world. Do wait until after our next festival.
- Gate-openers. Your Armageddon is ambitious. Our ambitions are smaller: we merely want to rule what you would destroy.
- So you are the ones who want everything to end. How dreary. The Winter Court prefers eternity.

#### Declares war
- We rather like the world, Sheaim. It has so much in it to own.
- Your gates let horrors in. Our knives let lives out. Let us see which works faster.
- The end of the world is not yours to schedule.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. You would only try to talk us into the abyss.
- We will not bargain with those who want nothing to remain.
- Go and pray to the void, cultist. It is the only one listening to you.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Sheaim. Your rituals are so dramatic; we do love a show.
- [CT_NAME]. Our court has always admired a good apocalypse, from a safe distance.
- Ah, the end of the world, visiting in person. How are your preparations coming along?

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your gates have been spewing horrors near our forests. Speak.
- What does the apocalypse want today? Be brief; we have a future to plan, even if you do not.
- Speak, cultist, and keep your meteors to yourself.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. Though why you want wealth when you plan to end the world, we cannot imagine.
- Done. A bargain until the end of time, or until your Armageddon, whichever comes first.
- We accept. Spend it on something that will burn prettily.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sheaim. We will have it searched for curses.
- Our thanks. You give generously, for a people who expect nothing to last.
- How kind. We will keep it, for as long as there is something to keep it in.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. You offer us things you mean to turn to ash, cultist.
- Your bargain smells of brimstone and despair. We decline.
- Your terms are as bleak as your future.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Go and chant at your gates; we will draw the curtains.
- Peace. We will need someone to blame when the meteors fall.
- Enough. Your summonings have trampled enough of our gardens.

#### Refuses peace
- No. Your gates are still open, and we intend to close them with your bodies.
- Not while your summonings still stalk our forests.
- Peace? So that you can finish your rituals undisturbed? We think not.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to the apocalypse? What would you even spend it on?
- No. You will only burn it anyway.
- The Winter Court will outlast your Armageddon, and so will its treasury.

### Svartalfar → Sidar

#### First contact
- The Sidar. Shades who traded their souls for eternity. We merely traded our god. A smaller price.
- Grey ones. You walk unseen through other people's cities. So do our assassins; perhaps they have met.
- So you are the people who feel nothing. A pity. Cruelty is wasted on you.

#### Declares war
- We hear you are very hard to kill, shade. We have always enjoyed a challenge.
- Our spies have found your hidden cities, shade. Fog does not hide from those who live in shadow.
- You watch the world from the shadows. The shadows belong to us.

#### Refuses to talk
- No. There is nothing to say to a ghost.
- We will not bargain with those who do not even want anything.
- Not now, shade. Drift away.

#### Greeting (friendly)
- Welcome, Sidar. You are so restful. Nothing we say upsets you.
- [CT_NAME]. You know so much. Do share some of it; we will make it worth your while.
- Ah, the Grey. We barely noticed you come in, and we mean that as the highest compliment.

#### Greeting (hostile)
- Your shades have been drifting through our court, reading our letters. Speak.
- What do the ghosts want? Be brief, before you fade.
- Speak, shade. Our threats do not frighten you, so we will have to rely on our knives.

#### Accepts a deal
- Agreed. It will outlast us both, no doubt; well, it will outlast us.
- Done. A bargain with no greed on the other side; our merchants hardly know what to do with themselves.
- We accept. Add it to your eternal library.

#### Thanks for a gift
- A gift from the Sidar. We are flattered you noticed us.
- Our thanks, shade. Generosity without feeling; how efficient.
- How kind. We will try to remember it as long as you will, though we doubt we can.

#### Turns down a deal
- No. Your terms are as pale as your skin.
- You have eternity, shade. Spend a little of it on a better offer. We decline.
- Not even ghosts get that bargain from the Winter Court.

#### Agrees to peace
- Very well. Fade away.
- Peace. You are too hard to kill to be worth the effort.
- Enough. We have better things to do than chase fog through the trees.

#### Refuses peace
- No. We have not yet found out quite how hard you are to kill.
- Not while your shades still haunt our forests.
- Peace? A treaty with ghosts would bind only one side, and it would be ours.

#### Rejects a demand
- Tribute to ghosts? What would you buy with it, a soul?
- No. You gave up greed with your soul, or so you say. Live by it.
- You would presume to demand from the Winter Court? You have finally found something to feel: disappointment.
